News.title: Police settle debate on November 5 firework rules including 'curfew' penalties
News.content:
Police settle debate on November 5 firework rules including 'curfew' penalties

With celebrations taking place on November 5 many people are already preparing for their firework displays

View 3 Images Police have clarified the rules on fireworks, including age limits and bans on throwing fireworks into streets or public spaces (Image: francesco riccardo iacomino/Getty)

November 5 is annually celebrated across the UK and is known as fireworks - or more commonly - Bonfire Night. Police have settled the debate over firework rules and penalties that some people could incur.

‌



‌



On Ask The Police, a website administered by police forces around the UK, someone asked: "What are the rules relating to fireworks?" The experts listed the rules and noted that, across four nights of the year, curfews are in place with slight differences due to the event. The Police said it is an offence to:

‌



Possess adult fireworks (all fireworks except category 1 fireworks - party poppers, sparklers, throwdowns etc) in a public place by anyone under the age of 18;

Possess category 4 fireworks (professional display fireworks) by anyone other than a fireworks professional;

Supply adult fireworks to those under 18;

Throw or cast or fire any firework in or into any highway, street, thoroughfare or public space (this would include throwing or firing from a private place into a public place, street, highway etc);

To light any fire or discharge any firearm or firework (without lawful authority or excuse) within 50 feet of the centre of a highway which consists of or comprises a carriageway, and as a consequence, the highway is damaged.

‌



What are the four firework categories?

View 3 Images Bonfire Night is marked across the UK on November 5, with fireworks displays lighting up the sky (Image: Getty)

Category one: ‘Throwdown fireworks’ including firecrackers, bangers and party poppers

‘Throwdown fireworks’ including firecrackers, bangers and party poppers Categories two and three : ‘Adult fireworks’ available in shops

: ‘Adult fireworks’ available in shops Category four: Professional display fireworks available from specialist suppliers

Is there a curfew for fireworks?

There is a curfew on the use of adult fireworks between 11 pm and 7 am, except on:

‌



Bonfire Night (when the curfew is between midnight and 7 am)

New Year's Eve (when the curfew is between 1 am and 7 am)

Chinese New Year (when the curfew is between 1 am and 7 am)

Diwali Night (when the curfew is between 1 am and 7 am)

Police say there are penalties for setting off fireworks outside the curfew hours, including up to six months in prison and a hefty fine of up to £5,000 - or even unlimited depending on the severity and specific regulations being enforced). They also warn that residents could be committing an offence if they use fireworks to cause a nuisance.

‌



Jail and an on-the-spot fine

Gov.uk confirms that if you, for example, set off fireworks past the Bonfire Night curfew, where the cut-off is midnight, you could find yourself in trouble. It urges people to check with their local council to find out about any local rules for setting off fireworks.

It states that you can only buy fireworks (including sparklers) from registered sellers for private use on these dates:

‌



October 15 to November 10

December 26 to 31

3 days before Diwali and Chinese New Year

View 3 Images Police warn that breaking the fireworks curfew can lead to penalties, including fines and up to six months in prison (Image: Getty)

‌



It adds: "At other times, you can only buy fireworks from licensed shops. You can be fined an unlimited amount and imprisoned for up to 6 months for selling or using fireworks illegally. You could also get an on-the-spot fine of £90."

Why do we celebrate Guy Fawkes Day?

Guy Fawkes Day (Bonfire Night) is a British event held on November 5. It marks the failed Gunpowder Plot of 1605, when a group led by Robert Catesby planned to blow up the Houses of Parliament and kill King James I. According to Britannica, the Gunpowder Plot conspirators, led by Robert, were "zealous Roman Catholics enraged at King James I for refusing to grant greater religious tolerance to Catholics."

‌



The plot was discovered, and Guy Fawkes was caught the night before with the explosives. The plotters were killed or captured and later executed. Parliament then made November 5 a national day of thanksgiving, first celebrated in 1606.

Remember...

Traditionally, straw figures of Guy Fawkes were thrown onto the bonfire. In the days before Guy Fawkes Day, children carried these figures - known as “Guys” - around the streets and asked passers-by for “a penny for the guy,” often chanting rhymes linked to the event. The best-known one dates back to the 18th century. You may know it...

Remember, remember, the fifth of November Gunpowder treason and plot We see no reason Why Gunpowder treason Should ever be forgot….

News.title: Russell Brand's wife tells rape trial couple broke up as 'it was clear' monogamy was 'difficult for him'
News.content:
Russell Brand's wife tells rape trial couple broke up as 'it was clear' monogamy was 'difficult for him'

Brand's latest appearance in court comes after he delivered hours worth of evidence on Wednesday, during which he admitted longtime friends wouldn't 'touch me with a barge pole'

View 5 Images Brand has arrived at court for another day of his trial (Image: Getty Images)

Giving evidence in court today, Russell Brand's wife explained that the couple broke up when she was "very aware" of her now-husband's promiscuity.

Laura Gallacher spoke at her husband's rape and sexual assault trial the day after he said he has focused on recalling events "at the expense of my marriage". Laura Gallacher appeared at Southwark Crown Court after arriving with her ex-comedian husband, where she went into detail about her and Brand's sex life.

She said he was “very caring” and they always have sex “at my pace”. She also spoke of when they started dating in 2007. Ms Gallacher said: “I was not experienced, I had only had one partner before Russell. I felt entirely cared for and looked after by Russell.”

View 5 Images Laura Gallacher will be giving evidence today (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

She told jurors Brand “respected my view” if she said she did not want to do something. Ms Gallacher said they broke up in summer 2007 when she was “very aware” of Russell Brand’s promiscuity. She said: “I wasn’t interested in having a relationship with him if he was sleeping with other people. I was invested, we both had told each other we loved each other but it was clear it was difficult for him to be monogamous.”

She said they got back together again as a couple in 2015 and married in 2017. Asked for her view of her husband’s character, Ms Gallacher said: “Russell, my husband, is caring, he is kind, he is a wonderful father to our children. He is amazingly attentive husband. He has got an eye for detail I’ve never known before. The way he treats me is to really know me, I feel very seen by him in every way. I love him very much.”

View 5 Images Ms Gallacher will give evidence the day after her husband (Image: Getty Images)

As his wife gave evidnece, Brand could be seen smiling broadly at points, having shown little emotion during the course of his trial so far. He let out an audible laugh when she told the court: “We do have many friends and there are colleagues, and we are grateful for those people.”

The former comedian, whose wife has been present in court for most of the trial, said on Wednesday it has been "deeply traumatic" since the allegations were made against him, adding that he has focused on recalling events "at the expense of my marriage, my children and my health".

Brand has pleaded not guilty to three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault, and one allegation of indecent assault, relating to six women between 1999 and 2009.

View 5 Images Gallacher told the court about hers and Brand's sex life (Image: Ian Vogler / Daily Mirror)

Speaking at Southwark Crown Court on Wednesday in response to questions from prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones KC in relation to alleged inconsistencies in his prepared statement to police and what he has told the jury with regard to one of the complainants, Brand said: "Ms Karmy-Jones, I completely agree."

"Since these events occurred there's been escalating recollection. Its been a deeply traumatic episode of my life. I've focused on at the expense of my marriage, my children and health.

"I ask your forgiveness, well not your forgiveness. I recognise that this recollection includes small details that are inconsistent and I acknowledge that." The court also heard today from Elia Alvarez Diaz, a ballet dancer who dated Russell Brand for three years in the 1990s. She said their relationship ended because he cheated on her repeatedly.

View 5 Images The court also heard from Brand's ex-girlfriends (Image: Getty Images)

Ms Diaz said Brand was well-liked when they studied together at drama school, and was a “complex character” who could be “exciting to be with”.

‌



She said in a statement: “He was promiscuous and unfaithful. We had many arguments.” She said the relationship “failed as I could no longer trust him to be faithful”. A second ex-girlfriend, Amanda Alguero Alejos, told the court in a statement that Russell Brand had also repeatedly cheated on her.

She said: “He was undoubtedly promiscuous, never in front of me and never when I was around. That was not what mattered to me at the time.”

Article continues below

She recalled women “circling” around Brand “like birds”, even when they were out as a couple.

News.title: Ebola warning as deadly virus ‘could reach UK and spread like Covid’
News.content:
Ebola warning as deadly virus ‘could reach UK and spread like Covid’

Dr Jean Kaseya, director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has warned that the rare undibugyo strain of Ebola currently sweeping Africa could spread to the UK

View Image Health workers clean equipment inside a Ebola treatment camp in Butembo, Congo (Image: AP Photo/Sebastien Kitsa Musayi)

A top health expert has warned that Ebola could reach the UK and spread like Covid if countries across the world do not take action.

‌



‌



There are now more than 10,000 cases and nearly 5,000 people have died from the deadly Bundibugyo strain of Ebola across four African countries.

‌



The rapid spread of the horrific disease has now been likened to the start of the Covid-19 pandemic, which began in China before killing millions worldwide.

‌



Dr Jean Kaseya, director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said: “We shouldn’t forget that at the beginning of Covid, many countries said there was zero risk of being affected, but a few months later, they became the hotspot.”

He added: “We don’t want to see the UK and other countries become the hotspot.”

The outbreak, which began in May has turned into the largest and deadliest Ebola crisis ever seen in the Democratic Republic of Congo, surpassing the epidemic there in 2018-2020.

‌



The disease has now spread to Kenya, which reported its first case earlier this month and now has nine cases after a man died in Nairobi following a visit to Congo.

⁠Nigeria became the fourth African country to report an Ebola case last week. Meanwhile in France a doctor who had returned from DR Congo in June was infected with the disease.

‌



It is essential that countries around the world need to take coordinated action to tackle the spreading virus, The Guardian reported.

“We want all countries to know that they are not safe if they don’t take appropriate measures,” he said.

‌



“Each country, not only in the African region, but all continents, must now increase the preparedness level and the possibility for treatment.

“It is the first time three African regions have been affected [by Ebola]. The geographic extension of this outbreak is unprecedented,” he said.

Article continues below

Dr Jean Kaseya, head of Africa CDC, which is holding a meeting today discussing the escalating worldwide threat, has called on African nations to step up their responses to the now international crisis, saying this week: “Ebola is crossing borders. Our response must move faster, with stronger coordination, greater solidarity and decisive political leadership."

But while tens of thousands of people have been infected and thousands more are dead, a significant number of people have recovered. At least 2,600 patients have recovered from the disease in Congo though.

News.title: New Lidl £8 'atmospheric' spheres similar to £45 Next version out Thursday
News.content:
New Lidl £8 'atmospheric' spheres similar to £45 Next version out Thursday

The new Special Buy range coming out next week features a collection of festive decorations

View 3 Images Shoppers can enjoy 'atmospheric lighting' for under £10 at Lidl (Image: Getty)

Lidl is bringing out a new set of 'atmospheric' spheres ahead of Christmas, for anyone keen to start decorating their home early. The supermarket is launching a new range of festive decorations next week as part of its upcoming weekly Special Buy refresh.

‌



‌



From Sunday, November 8, customers will be able to get their hands on the store's new Livarno LED Decorative Spheres. A set of three costs £7.99 and is described as "atmospheric" in Lidl's product description online. They also look similar to a pricier version available at Next.

‌



The Livarno light-up spheres are battery-operated, so they can be placed anywhere in the house without needing to be near a plug socket. Lidl says the decorative spheres are "made from high-quality glass with warm white light". Other key features include:

‌



Six-hour timer with automatic daily repetition

Simply switch on at your desired time of day and start the timer

Can also be switched on and off manually

For indoor use only

The Lidl Livarno set of three LED decorative spheres could be viewed as a budget-friendly alternative to a Laura Ashley set at Next for anyone who loves its look but wants to avoid the premium price tag. Next says: "This charming Set of Three Laura Ashley Crackled Glass Lit Ornaments casts a warm, inviting glow that transforms any mantel or tabletop into a cosy winter retreat. When illuminated, each ornament reveals an intricate forest scene straight from a snow-dusted fairy tale."

View 3 Images Livarno LED Decorative Spheres (Image: Lidl)

‌



Both options provide a nearly identical setup for seasonal decorating, featuring three gold, crackled-glass globes that emit a warm white glow. They also share the exact same sizing footprint, measuring 10cm, 12cm, and 15cm in diameter, meaning they will occupy the same amount of space on a mantelpiece or dining table.

Despite their visual similarities, there is a difference in cost. The Lidl set is priced at just £7.99, while the Next version costs £45, saving shoppers around £37.

‌



Lidl also includes all nine necessary batteries in the box. On the other hand, the Next set requires you to purchase eight batteries separately, which adds another hidden cost to an already expensive item. The Lidl globes come with a built-in six-hour automatic daily timer to save battery life.

View 3 Images Next's Set of Three Laura Ashley Crackled Glass Lit Ornament (Image: Next)

Article continues below

One compromise shoppers will make by choosing the cheaper option is the level of design detail. When illuminated, the Next spheres display an intricate, hidden woodland forest scene within the glass.

The Lidl spheres do not have this silhouette and simply emit a classic, textured glow. However, because they achieve the exact same warm, festive atmosphere from across the room, the Lidl set is easily the smarter buy for a budget-conscious shopper.

News.title: Inside Britain's most festive pub as bar transforms into Christmas wonderland
News.content:
Christmas may be two months away, but one Cambridge pub has wasted no time getting into the festive spirit.

The Empress has already spent two weeks transforming itself into a festive grotto, with thousands of pounds worth of decorations covering almost every inch of the venue. From Christmas jumpers fixed to the walls to tinsel wrapped around the lights, the traditional boozer has once again gone all-out for its annual festive makeover.

Baubles hang from the ceiling, twinkling lights fill the bar and one part of the pub has even been transformed into a colourful candy cane and gingerbread wonderland.

The huge decorating job has become an annual tradition at The Empress, with regulars pitching in alongside staff to get everything ready. And despite the decorations going up in October, they will not be coming down in a hurry, with the festive display expected to remain in place until the middle of January.

The tradition was first started by former landlord Dave Utting, who died in 2022, and has since been continued in his memory.

News.title: Fireman's urgent alert to parents as certain Halloween costumes can 'go up in flames'
News.content:
Fireman's urgent alert to parents as certain Halloween costumes can 'go up in flames'

A fireman has issued an urgent alert to parents as certain Halloween costumes can "go up in flames". He recently named the outfits you want to avoid during spooky season

View Image An urgent alert has been issued about Halloween costumes (stock image) (Image: RyanJLane via Getty Images)

A fireman has issued an urgent alert to parents as they start thinking about Halloween costumes. The big event will take place this weekend, but there are some things you need to be aware of, as there's some expert advice that you may not have come across regarding costumes.

‌



‌



It turns out, when it comes to parenting choices, there's some things you need to know about picking out costumes as some can pose hidden dangers. According to the fire service, certain outfits need to be avoided at all costs or they could "go up in flames" when put in a risky situation.

‌



This isn't the first time such an alert has been issued either. Previously, it was shown how quickly some costumes can catch fire.

‌



A fireman from County Durham and Darlington Fire and Rescue Service recently appeared in a video to offer advice. There's some information you should really be aware of.

What is his advice?

He said: "Hi everybody. So, leading up to Halloween, I'm guessing loads of people out there are going to be dressing up, you're going to be going door to door on Halloween.

"Before we do that, I just want to give you a little bit of advice around Halloween costumes. Did you know that many Halloween costumes can be highly flammable?

‌



"This is because many of them are classed as toys, so they are less fire resistant than normal clothes. Make sure you always check the label for a UKCA or CE mark. This tells us that this is safe to use."

‌



He added: "Unfortunately, there is a number of items out there people use as Halloween costumes but they in fact aren't, and they haven't been tested. So that's telling me that this is safe to use and it is flame retardant."

Ensure our latest headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as a Preferred Source in your Google search settings.

‌



Key information for parents

In the video, the fireman holds up a child's costume to explain what people need to know. Naturally, all costumes should be checked to ensure they're as safe as possible.

However, parents should look out for a few things when buying their children's costumes. Always ensure you buy them from reputable retailers and look for UKCA or CE marks on labels to ensure they meet British and European standards.

‌



You should also keep costumed children and long fabrics far away from candles, open fires and Jack-O'-Lanterns. Instead of using candles around the home to light pumpkins, you could also use battery-powered LED lights or torches.

There are some simple changes you could make to help boost safety at this time of year. They can make a big difference.

Article continues below

It should also be noted that you should show your children what to do in an extreme emergency. Teach children what to do if their clothes accidentally catch fire. The stop, drop and roll method is handy knowledge to have.

As well as this, it's wise to choose face paint or makeup instead of restrictive masks. This should enable you to have a safer Halloween.

News.title: ‘Gentle' and 'loving’ grandad killed in three-car crash as Storm Boelo battered Scotland
News.content:
‘Gentle' and 'loving’ grandad killed in three-car crash as Storm Boelo battered Scotland

Jim McCollum, 84, was one of two people killed in a three-car collision in Bathgate, West Lothian, with his heartbroken family paying tribute

View 3 Images Jim McCollum, 84, was one of two people killed in a three-car collision in Bathgate, West Lothian. (Image: Police Scotland )

An 84-year-old grandad who was one of two people killed in a horror three-car crash during Storm Boelo has been named.

‌



‌



Jim McCollum was the driver of a blue Peugeot 208 that collided with a white BMW and blue Citroen Saxo on the B708 Lower Bathville road, in Bathgate, West Lothian, at around 12.15pm on Sunday.

‌



He died at the scene along with Arran Callander, 20, the driver of the BMW.

‌



The passenger of the BMW, a 19-year-old man, was taken to hospital for treatment, and the occupants of the Citroen, a 20-year-old man and a 23-year-old woman, were assessed by paramedics at the scene.

View 3 Images Arran Callander was killed in the crash (Image: Facebook)

Yemenia Airways jet left with massive dent and cracked windscreen after hailstorm READ MORE :

In a statement released by Police Scotland, Jim's family said: “Jim was a gentle and loving husband, father and grandfather and will be deeply missed by his heartbroken family. The family wishes to thank the emergency services who attended the scene of the crash.”

‌



The tragedy unfolded as an amber weather warning for Storm Boelo was in place until Sunday evening across most of Scotland, reported the Daily Record.

Images taken from the scene show a large cordon in place as officers scour the crash site. The road was closed to allow crash investigation work to take place and cops are appealing for anyone with information to come forward.

‌



Arran's sister, Angela, led the tributes to the young man who was described as "one of a kind".

View 3 Images Emergency services at the scene

‌



She said: "You will be so missed by so many. It's not sunk in. I want to see you again. It's like I'm dreaming. Thinking of everyone affected by the crash, Love you so much, forever and always. Fly high."

Many other people have also spoken fondly of Arran, with Amelie Johansen writing: "I'm never going to get my head around this. My longest friend. The memories we’ve shared along with all the laughs we’ve had will always be at the front of my mind.

‌



"I'll never forget your one liners. You had everyone laughing. You really were one of a kind, Arran. None of this feels real and I don't think it ever will. The grief that has come with this is unbearable. Until we meet again, Arran. I love you loads."

While Katie Cummings said: "Thoughts to Arran's family. He was always lovely when he came into my work," and Ashley Forrest shared: "Heartbreaking for all involved, thinking of A and his family. Such a lovely young man."

Article continues below

Other messages included from Lauren Cawley who said: "Lost for words. Rest easy, Arran. Absolutely gutted," Caitlin Logan wrote: "Rest easy Arran. Young life taken far too soon" and Cole Mckillop penned: "Rest easy Arran forever childhood best mates."
