Sports.content:
Naomi Osaka, seeded No 7 and playing before home fans in Japan, was knocked out of the Pan Pacific Open on Thursday by teenager Mia Pohankova.

Slovakia's Pohankova, who turned 18 a week ago and was a wild-card entry in Japan, upset Osaka 6-3 7-5 to advance to the quarter-finals.

Pohankova will face Alycia Parks in the last eight.

Pohankova, the 2025 junior singles champion at Wimbledon, stunned Osaka, who was coming off a win over Jasmine Paolini in the first round in Tokyo.

In other round-of-16 matches on Thursday, Parks defeated Kimberly Birrell 6-3 6-1, and Leylah Fernandez defeated No 5 Elise Mertens 6-2 7-6 (8-6).

In a late match, top-ranked Elena Rybakina will face Yulina Putintseva. Both were born in Russia but represent Kazakhstan.

Second-seeded Maja Chwalinska and No. 4 Belinda Bencic pulled out of the tournament earlier with injuries. Chwalinska has an injured left thigh and Bencic has a right-ankle injury.

Sports.title: Wolff explains Antonelli turnaround after tears
Sports.content:
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff says it is "extremely satisfying" to see Kimi Antonelli's turnaround from last year as the Italian looks to secure the 2026 Formula 1 world title this weekend in Mexico.

A top nine in this Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix for Antonelli will ensure he becomes the sport's youngest world champion at 20 years old - breaking Sebastian Vettel's record by three years.

Antonelli joined Mercedes last year and struggled for the majority of his rookie season after a huge amount of excitement prior to his Formula 1 debut.

Wolff recalls the 2025 Belgian Grand Prix as a particular low moment when Antonelli was in tears after being eliminated in Q1.

"The many people that said last year after nine races without points, he shouldn't be in a Mercedes," said Wolff.

"People in other teams that said, he shouldn't even be in Formula 1, the tears in Spa, in parc ferme. And all of that now is extremely satisfying to see what he's able to deliver, how he's working with the team, with Bono [Antonelli's engineer Peter Bonnington] and yielding the results. But it wasn't an easy road.

"So, I'm happy that, 99.9 per cent, he still needs to finish the race in Mexico. So, it's either going to be a big tequila party or if it's not a tequila party, then it's going to be Caipirinha the weekend afterwards."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater gives his verdict on the on United States GP, as a dominant win for Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli leaves the Italian needing just two points from the Mexico GP to claim an historic first world title

Antonelli has won nine races this season and consistently had the upper hand on Mercedes team-mate George Russell throughout the year.

Wolff thinks the new 2026 cars, which provided a reset for the field, has benefitted Antonelli and is mystified how the Italian has hit back so strongly after last year.

"I think maybe it was to his benefit that the regulations were all new. When last year he came in and those cars existed, those cars existed for four years. The other drivers were used to it," he said.

"And all new for everyone this year. And he just made it stick with his easiness, with his mindset, with his easiness of approaching things.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff says that Kimi Antonelli's performance at the United States Grand Prix was 'exceptional'.

"In Austin, he came to my office before getting ready, before getting dressed and just sat down on the sofa and said, 'I'm going to enjoy this one. And isn't it funny? I'm not thinking at all about the championship'.

"I said, 'well, exactly stick to that attitude. You have the best job in the world. Don't forget that.' So he has also the right mindset.

"It's been 30 or more years that I've tried to understand racing drivers' brains and I still don't know what has happened over the winter.

"His ability to process and deliver something that's outstanding, which we didn't see coming. But credit to him, credit to his engineers, to his environment, his family that he's delivered in that way."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martin Brundle sits down with Andrea Kimi Antonelli to discuss his career so far at Mercedes

Antonelli looking to win championship 'in style'

Antonelli's win last weekend in Austin was somewhat of a surprise after Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the previous two Formula 1 races.

Several F1 championships have been won without the champion finishing on the podium in that race, but Antonelli is keen to "finish on a high".

"The perfect way would be to finish off in style and enjoy the rest of the season," he told Sky Sports F1.

"I'm very well aware it's very close but the mindset hasn't changed. I want to finish the season on a high in order to have high hopes in 2027.

"First we focus and worry about finishing this [season] well and we will see."

Formula 1 2026 remaining races Mexico This weekend Qatar November 27-29 Brazil November 6-8 Abu Dhabi December 4-6 Las Vegas November 20-22

Antonelli admits his success has been a "good surprise" but Mercedes have played a pivotal role in his quick development over the last 18 months.

"I'm very lucky because I have a very good group of people around me. In the team, I have my father, who always comes, then my performance coach," he said.

"I just have a great group of people around me that help me to be more relaxed and not worry about these kinds of things. They help me to block out the noise, and that's also what's been allowing me to enjoy the weekend and perform."

Sports.title: Kayla Allen: From self-taught boxer to star prospect
Sports.content:
Kayla Allen only started boxing a few years ago, teaching herself with YouTube videos and throwing punches in her garden.

Her rapid ascent since then has been astonishing. She made it all the way to the GB squad and has now become the first woman to sign with Zuffa Boxing. She will have her second fight on Sky Sports on November 7.

"Any fight I go into, whether it's the first debut, the second fight or a world title fight, everyone's getting dealt with the same," she told Sky Sports.

"It's always been exciting, it's never been boring. So for me it's not about being someone else, it's about being myself, and the best Kayla beats anybody on the night."

After originally pursuing ambitions in football, Allen started trying to box at home during the pandemic lockdown.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Allen stopped Edina Kiss in an impressive pro debut at Zuffa Boxing 11

"I learned how to box in my back garden as an 18-year-old girl. I watched videos on YouTube, how to throw a jab, watched Mayweather, Mike Tyson, AJ, I just studied the sport and then went down to the local boxing gym, did a couple of white-collar fights and now we're here," Allen said.

"I've always believed in myself. Whenever I first started, no matter what I do I always go: 'I'm going to be the best at this'. So whatever that means I don't know, but that's just my mindset. No matter what I do I'm always the best at it and I'll be the best at boxing."

Her first amateur tournament was the Golden Girl, a large international competition in Sweden. She won it.

Allen performed well in the national championships and was soon on the GB squad, an astonishing ascent.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Here is everything you need to know about Zuffa Boxing's first female fighter Kayla Allen

"Within six months I was on England and then within eight months I was on GB. That's work, credit to my coaches and credit to myself, and the GB system and the England system to allow me to get to where I needed to be. It's a blessing. I'm glad to be here and it's a good opportunity," she said.

It led her now to her breakthrough move into professional boxing, becoming Zuffa's first female signing.

"Where's the girls at? I'm here now, so let's go!" she said. "It helps other females coming through, that nothing's impossible."

She promises: "Explosive, knockouts, just explosive energy, I'm going to bring ferocity to the ring… When I step into that ring it's game on for me.

"It's creating my own legacy, one of one, and creating my own name for female boxing.

"It started in a unique way and it'll finish in a unique way as well. I do everything my own way."

Sports.title: Boyd questions Rangers' title credentials after Hearts draw
Sports.content:
Olwethu Makhanya scored an 89th minute equaliser against Hearts after Rangers has taken an early lead; it ended the Ibrox side's winning league run at nine games; they remain four points behind leaders Celtic with the Jambos a further four back

Rangers remain four points behind Celtic after their draw at Hearts

"If you're going to win a league, there has to be periods in games where you dominate that game... Rangers don't do that."

Sky Sports' Kris Boyd is concerned about his former club's "disjointed" performance in their 2-2 draw with Premiership title rivals Hearts.

Derek McInnes was booed loudly by the home support as he emerged from the tunnel for his first match back since leaving for Ibrox in June.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kris Boyd believes Rangers will be delighted to leave Tynecastle with a draw after being outplayed for long spells by Hearts.

However, his team silenced a pumped-up home crowd when Kevin Kelsy scored a 16th-minute opener after a lapse from Laurent Mendy.

Hearts turned the game round with goals from Claudio Braga and Calvin Miller early in the second half. But Olwethu Makhanya's 89th-minute header rescued a late draw to keep Rangers four points behind leaders Celtic, who dropped points against Dundee United.

"They've stolen a point because, especially that second half, it's got to be better," said Boyd after watching the game at Tynecastle.

"If you're going to win a league, there has to be periods in games where you dominate that game.

"When you're suffering, put together a few passes that frustrate the opposition. Trust me, there is nothing worse than chasing a team that keep the ball for a period of time. Rangers don't do that."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch highlights from the Scottish Premiership match between Hearts and Rangers.

The result halted the Ibrox side's winning Premiership run at nine games, while Hearts extended their unbeaten home record to 26 games.

"Rangers don't have players that get on the ball and make six or seven passes to then drag the opposition out.

"Can [Ryan] Naderi run? Of course. Can Kelsey run? Yes. Can [Djeidi] Gassama run? Yes. Can [Minsu] Kim run? Of course they can run. They can run at speed when they want to do it.

"Hearts are a pressing team. They'll get after you. There's gaps in behind. But everything's just so rushed for Rangers.

"Rangers really struggled to deal with Hearts. Emmanuel Fernandez, he looked so at unease with the Hearts attacking players. The amount of times that he caused problems for his own team-mates, again.

"Everything just seems disjointed."

Sports.title: Time and owners not on Moyes’ side as he tries to end Everton trophy drought
Sports.content:
A European challenge plus a concerted effort to end a trophy drought that will soon stretch into a 32nd year were Everton’s stated aims for this season, although that was before the club’s owners turned the taps off in the transfer market and announced they were looking to sell up. An abrupt change of direction and ambition from The Friedkin Group (TFG) has not altered the demands on David Moyes, however. It is as you were for the Everton manager, regardless of the tools at his disposal.

Newcastle’s visit to Hill Dickinson Stadium in the Carabao Cup fourth round on Thursday – when they will be backed by 7,732 fans after Everton allocated their opponents 15% of the ground – is timely on several counts. It is, first and foremost, an opportunity for Moyes’s team to advance in a competition that Everton have never won and edge closer to realising one stated aim for the campaign. It is also a chance to restore positivity after consecutive defeats against Chelsea and Arsenal, Everton’s only losses of the season.

This will be the first of two games in a row between the sides, with Everton going to St James’ Park in the league on Monday. Newcastle serve as a potent reminder of the League Cup’s power to lift a club out of trophy torment, in their case 56 years, with victory in the 2025 final.

Newcastle, though, had Alexander Isak leading the line at Wembley in 2025. Everton have Thierno Barry and no alternative striker as a result of the calamitous end to the summer transfer window when TFG first signalled the change in the club’s financial landscape by accepting a £35m bid from Nottingham Forest for Harrison Armstrong. The young midfielder’s form and value have continued to improve in the following weeks, just as the Evertonians who protested against his sale during the draw at Bournemouth knew they would.

Barry started his second season in English football encouragingly, with four goals in the first two games. But as the misses have racked up from the 24-year-old French forward – he leads the way in the Premier League this season with 12 big chances missed – so Everton have looked disheartened at times and their performances have dipped.

It is not all on Barry, of course. Brennan Johnson and Jack Grealish need to contribute much more from out wide than they have this season. Moyes’s sparing use of Hayden Hackney, Tyrique George and Tyler Dibling has also invited criticism that his resources, while extremely limited, are not being maximised. Jordan Pickford’s recent form has been an added, uncharacteristic cause for concern.

“We need to start picking up results,” James Tarkowski, the club captain, said. “Even though we won against Ipswich, it feels, not like a slump, but it feels like we need to work our way out of this. It’s a big game on Thursday in the cup.”

Moyes gave a fine speech when receiving a tribute award from the Football Writers’ Association North in Manchester on Sunday night. In a wide-ranging analysis of a managerial career spanning more than 1,200 games, he spoke of the importance of working for owners with resolve and foresight, his desire for more British coaches to work abroad and his envy at the trophy collections of other long-serving peers such as Sir Alex Ferguson, Arsène Wenger and José Mourinho.

The unadulterated joy that he and West Ham got from winning the Europa Conference League in 2023 – ending that club’s 43-year wait for a major trophy – is a feeling that Moyes longs to experience again with Everton. But time and TFG are not on his side.

The 63‑year‑old Scot’s contract expires at the end of this season and talks over an extension have been kicked repeatedly down the road. Moyes has restored stability on the pitch while TFG has stabilised Everton’s finances off it, but is a manager’s contract and long-term planning on the owner’s agenda now it is trying to sell the club in a difficult market?

View image in fullscreen David Moyes’ contract expires at the end of this season. Photograph: Silvina Brodersohn/CameraSport/Getty Images

Moyes has quickly – though not as quickly as fans would like – constructed a team that could challenge for Europe with quality additions in attack, at right-back, and with a lot of luck with injuries. Everton made a £25m profit in the last transfer window and are the lowest net spenders in the Premier League over the past five years. Yet it seems highly unlikely that a wantaway owner would invest in the squad as required in January.

“Look, it’s never going to be easy,” Moyes said last month when dissecting Everton’s damaging end to the transfer window. “You know what happens in these situations, there’s only one person who tends to get called out at the end of it. You know what I mean?” That may be true but there is realism regarding Everton’s latest predicament, along with a recognition of how important a win over Newcastle could be.

Sports.title: Liverpool beat Chelsea on penalties yet again to secure Carabao Cup progress
Sports.content:
Chelsea must have been resigned to their fate as soon as the shootout arrived at Anfield. Four times they had faced Liverpool on penalties previously and four times they had lost. Number five was confirmed when Wesley Fofana’s wild effort sailed high into the Kop and sent Andoni Iraola’s side into a Carabao Cup quarter-final against his old club Bournemouth.

Fofana was not the only culprit as Chelsea’s catalogue of penalty misery against Liverpool gained a new chapter alongside the 2007 Champions League semi-final, the 2019 Uefa Super Cup final and the FA and League Cup finals of 2022.

Emmanuel Emegha had the chance to win it for Xabi Alonso’s side in sudden death but was denied superbly by Giorgi Mamardashvili. Liverpool fluffed their lines with victory in sight too, Kostas Tsimikas blazing over and ruining the chance to reprise his match-winning role at Wembley four years ago. Ryan Gravenberch and Valentin Barco also failed to convert.

It fell to Joe Gomez of all people to edge Liverpool ahead with the first shootout penalty of his Anfield career. The long-serving defender, who has never scored for Liverpool, found the top corner of Mike Penders’s goal in convincing style. Fofana could not repeat the trick and finally, after Morgan Rogers and Cody Gakpo had both scored penalties in normal time, the two adversaries were separated. It was another painful result for Alonso, fresh from the home defeat against Tottenham on Saturday, although the Chelsea display was an improvement.

The Chelsea manager said: “For sure it is not the outcome we wanted or expected but once you go to penalties there has to be a sad side. We played with courage, the game was close with not many chances for both sides. It is a small setback because it is probably the least important competition for us. As soon as we leave Anfield our focus will be on a very important game [against Manchester United] on Saturday.”

If, as Alonso claimed, the Carabao Cup is not a priority for Chelsea this season then his decision to again overlook the merits of Estêvão, who was left kicking his heels on the bench all evening, was mystifying. With João Pedro injured and Cole Palmer suspended Chelsea started with Danny Welbeck in attack and the former Liverpool captain Jordan Henderson operating in an advanced midfield role. Liverpool contained them relatively comfortably.

View image in fullscreen Andoni Iraola embraces his goalkeeper Giorgi Mamardashvili. Photograph: Michael Regan/Getty Images

The Premier League rivals served up a fast-paced, committed cup tie that was lacking goalmouth incident before they exchanged penalties in the space of four minutes. Chelsea were awarded the first when Moisés Caicedo was released inside the Liverpool area by a cleverly disguised pass from Malo Gusto and clipped from behind by Gravenberch. The boos for Henderson intensified as he carried the ball to the spot with a wry smile on his face and handed it to Rogers, who sent Mamardashvili the wrong way with an emphatic penalty kick.

Liverpool soon had a spot-kick of their own when Caicedo and Fofana challenged Virgil van Dijk at a Tsimikas corner and the ball struck the Chelsea defender’s raised hand. Gakpo converted confidently into the bottom corner. The referee, Darren England, called both penalties instantly and correctly, showing officials do not always have to rely on video assistance. The game benefited as a spectacle from the absence of a video assistant referee, although Iraola might well have disagreed had Rogers scored after appearing to control Pedro Neto’s chip with his arm. Mamardashvili’s save meant that controversy was avoided.

Penders, keen to atone for his costly error against Spurs, took centre stage for Chelsea when saving a flying header from Ronald Araújo at close range. The Liverpool defender had been supplied by a fine cross from Gomez and, with two defenders pushed forwards, Rogers almost punished them on the counterattack. Gomez, however, worked tirelessly to chase back and block the forward’s eventual shot. Penders also saved impressively from Bradley Barcola when the France international cut inside from the right and his low shot was deflected towards the bottom corner.
