Rogers was involved in several promising openings for Chelsea as Alonso’s team – improved more than Liverpool by their substitutes – finished strongly. Marco Palestra had the best of them when released by the England forward’s perfectly weighted pass but Mamardashvili produced an excellent save low to his right. Wirtz also had a late chance to seal victory but his attempt from Gakpo’s knock-down struck Levi Colwill and was eventually cleared. And so to penalties, and a familiar feeling for the side from Stamford Bridge.

Iraola said: “I’m pleased for the players because they put in a big effort tonight. I can feel [togetherness within the squad] and I’m happy to feel it because it is very important. The players are feeling support from the crowd and now we have another big one on Sunday [against Arsenal] so let’s try to finish this four in a row in the best way.”

Sports.title: Tottenham’s season has finally taken off. How far up the table can they go?
Sports.content:
In reality, it was only three points. All Tottenham took from their 2-0 win at Chelsea last Saturday evening was a helpful boost in the Premier League standings. But it feels far more significant than that.

This is a fixture Tottenham almost never win. In their 34 previous visits to Chelsea in the Premier League, they had won only once. It was their first win to nil at Stamford Bridge in any competition since December 1986, nearly 40 years ago. Winning at Chelsea is huge. Plenty of Spurs fans have only ever seen this happen once before, in April 2018 under Mauricio Pochettino, when their team was a formidable force.

Tottenham went into the game in the relegation zone with just one win this season – against promoted Coventry – after back-to-back 17th-place finishes, and with noteworthy absentees from their best team. Few supporters would have expected this result, and they are well within their rights to enjoy it.

The real reason this felt so seismic, though, is that it could be a turning point for a team that has veered terribly off course over the past two years. At great expense this summer, Tottenham bought into Roberto De Zerbi’s ideas, spending vast amounts to transform the team. Results in the early part of this season hinted that the new players would take a while to gel. Spurs took until the 86th minute of their fifth match, at which point they were already 3-0 down to Aston Villa, to score their first league goal of the season.

Since the international break that followed that defeat, though, Spurs have put in much-improved displays. They drew 1-1 at Manchester United, though they really deserved to win, and then secured their first win of the season against Coventry. All of their goals in that 3-1 win were scored from outside the box and generated only 0.86 expected goals. They probably deserved the win, but it was not the most convincing display.

However, in much more daunting surroundings away to Chelsea, they produced when it mattered most. Spurs kept the ball effectively, ending with 68.9% possession, and although they did not create many clear cut chances, winning through a freak Mike Penders own goal and a wonderful and surely unrepeatable individual goal from Mathys Tel after a 45-metre ball carry, they got into dangerous positions frequently. Their 0.74 xG did not tell the story of their dominance.

It was no coincidence that this was the first game that £85m summer signing Mateus Fernandes started at the base of their midfield. He is precisely the kind of press-resistant midfielder needed to play De Zerbi’s football but for several reasons, ranging from injuries and sharpness to the very recent birth of his first child, he had not started in his preferred position.

On Saturday, everything went through him and he proved he is most effective in a deeper midfield role. He was in his favoured position at Stamford Bridge alongside fellow expensive summer signing Sandro Tonali as Spurs’ new midfield pair finally played together for the first time.

Fernandes was exceptional. He had more touches than any other player has had away from home in a Premier League game this season (124). He also led the way for tackles (five) and completed 92.2% of his 102 passes. He was constantly getting himself and Spurs out of difficult situations. His total of 89 touches under pressure from an opponent was the fifth-highest by a player in a Premier League game this season and his 48 touches while under high pressure (meaning an opponent was within two metres of him) inside his own half was the highest total by anyone in the competition.

Most impressively, his pass completion rate while under pressure from an opponent was 91.2%. He also progressed play well. He played 27 line-breaking passes, the 12th most by anyone in a Premier League game this season. Crucially, 21 of those were made while under pressure, which nobody else in the division has been able to top all season. And Fernandes did it away to Chelsea.

If Tottenham needed unlocking to fulfil De Zerbi’s wishes, Fernandes may well be the key. He made it possible for Spurs to bait Chelsea’s press and play through them, getting the ball from back to front consistently and reliably – something Spurs have not done for a long time.

In truth, their work in the final third showed how much there is left to do. Their 58 final-third entries for just 0.74 xG is one of the worst ratios by any team in a Premier League game this season. But the consistency with which they reached attacking positions hints at what this team can achieve. Nobody in the squad has more than one league goal this season, so they need Dominic Solanke, Omar Marmoush, Sávio, Mohammed Kudus and Tel to find their shooting boots.

“We are improving a lot,” De Zerbi said after the win. “We are improving in the mentality in the group, in the relationships between the players and on the pitch.” This improvement is happening just in time for Spurs to hit a favourable run. Using the average Opta Power Rating of each team’s next five opponents, Spurs have the “easiest” run of every team in the Premier League.

They face Crystal Palace (home), Leeds (away), Ipswich (home), Sunderland (away) and Fulham (home). On the basis of their performance at Chelsea, Spurs should be hopeful of winning all of those matches. But, having won their last two games, stringing together five more wins would mean a seven-game winning run – something only Aston Villa managed in the whole of last season.

Spurs are still only three points off the relegation zone and are not out of trouble, but they are also – very suddenly – just two points off the top six. There is every reason for them to be looking up the table rather than down. Their next five matches are important, though, because they then face a difficult run, with games against Arsenal, Liverpool, Brighton, Bournemouth and Manchester City to come.

After such a positive performance at Stamford Bridge, it’s time for Spurs to start thinking about what they can achieve this season rather than worrying about whether they can escape another relegation battle. It’s also important to remember that it was only one win, and things could very quickly come crashing down. At least they have shown there are foundations to build upon and they have it within them to do exactly what De Zerbi wants.

This is an article by Opta Analyst

Sports.title: Arsenal’s Slegers hails ‘role model’ Russo after historic hat-trick sinks Benfica
Sports.content:
Alessia Russo wrote herself into the history books once more as she became the highest English goalscorer in the Women’s Champions League. Her hat-trick gave Arsenal a vital 3-0 win against Benfica to send the Gunners up to second in the league phase table.

“I’m so happy. I think we’ve found a nice dynamic as well with the last two games,” Russo’s manager, Renée Slegers, said. “She’s one of the leaders and she does it her way. She cares for everyone around her and connects well with her teammates. She leads the way as a role model, doing the right things consistently.”

It was a statement performance from the 27-year-old who has shaken off the early-season cobwebs. Her three goals at Meadow Park on Wednesday took her tally up to 10 in her past seven appearances for club and country, hitting a rich vein of form just when Arsenal have needed her most.

It is safe to say Arsenal’s season has yet to fully burst into life. Struggles in front of goal and unforced errors have defined the opening two months but the gritty north London derby win on Saturday did feel like it could be a springboard for momentum.

There was no less pressure coming into this Champions League match against Benfica, another must-win game with Arsenal’s European form mirroring their domestic struggles. A last-ditch win against HB Køge and a heartbreaking draw against Paris FC (in which they surrendered a two‑goal lead) left them fifth in the league phase table before kick-off, with Barcelona and OL Lyonnes looming.

Slegers made three changes to freshen things up. Ona Batlle returned to her more natural right‑back role while the summer signings Élisa De Almeida and Géraldine Reuteler made their full debuts.

Ivan Baptista’s Benfica arrived in confident form on the back of consecutive wins domestically. Slegers was keen to highlight their strong identity pre-match, having had first‑hand experience of their resilience in last year’s league phase. So it proved once more in a first half in which Arsenal dominated, but struggled to break through against a well-structured opposition.

View image in fullscreen The Arsenal head coach, Renée Slegers, has eased pressure on herself with back-to-back wins over Spurs and Benfica. Photograph: David Cliff/EPA

It was the visitors, in fact, who had the best opportunity of the first half hour. Frøya Dorsin was left beating the turf in frustration after spurning a glorious opportunity to catch out a stranded Misa Rodríguez with a lob. It was a moment that jolted Arsenal into life as they upped the tempo and began to rain pressure on Benfica’s goal. First Olivia Smith set up Russo for a low shot that went narrowly wide before Smith herself forced Lena Pauels into a fine save.

Arsenal found their breakthrough just before half-time when Russo produced a sublime finish after a well‑worked move down the left.

It was like a switch had flipped for Arsenal after the break as they exuded confidence, zipping the ball around the turf with increasing ease. Smith looked more and more comfortable in her central role while Caitlin Foord came alive down the left, the latter denied a clear shot by a superb last-ditch challenge.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The conductor behind them all was Russo as she pressed and stretched the play to her tune. The captain on the night was at the heart of things once more as the hosts doubled their lead, rising high to glance home a corner. She completed her hat-trick shortly afterwards, converting from the spot after Foord was brought down by Catarina Amado.

Quick Guide Roundup: Chelsea roll past Roma, Bayern and Real draw Show Chelsea maintained their strong start to this year’s Women’s Champions League campaign as second-half goals from Ellie Carpenter [pictured, centre] and Kadeisha Buchanan secured a 2-0 win over Roma at Plough Lane. After a goalless first half, substitute Carpenter combined with Wieke Kaptein to open the scoring in the 51st minute. The Australian made a powerful run, found Kaptein and then met her cross from the right with a low shot which took a deflection off Roma defender Winonah Heatley before going in. Central defender Buchanan wrapped up the win in the 89th minute, heading home to ensure a second win in three European matches for Sonia Bompastor’s unbeaten team. Roma were left to rue chances missed by Maya Doms and Alayah Pilgrim as they extended their scoreless Champions League start to three games. 'I’m pleased with the fact we scored really early in the second half. We could probably have killed the game a little bit earlier,' said the Chelsea head coach, Sonia Bompastor. 'It’s important for us in these games to be able to be clinical and ruthless as early as possible. But we find different ways to impose ourselves in the game and to score goals. So it’s good.' Bayern Munich fought back from two goals down to draw 2-2 against Real Madrid and preserve their unbeaten home record in the pre-knockout phase. Last season’s semi-finalists have now not lost any of their 17 home games in the group stage or league phase thanks to Momoko Tanikawa's second-half equaliser. Athenea del Castillo pounced from Linda Caicedo’s cross in the seventh minute, before Lineth Beerensteyn headed in from close range to double Madrid’s lead midway through the first half. Edna Imade nodded in to reduce the deficit on the half-hour and Tanikawa levelled soon after the restart, before Sophie Proost hit the post for Bayern in stoppage time. Eight-time champions Lyonnes cruised to an emphatic 6-0 home victory over Internazionale, with Marie-Antoinette Katoto scoring twice before Lily Yohannes made it three on the hour mark. Vicki Bècho came off the bench shortly after and hit a hat-trick as the French giants went top of the table on goal difference. Swiss side Servette claimed a historic maiden Champions League win at the ninth attempt as they brushed aside OH Leuven 5-1 in Geneva. Paola Hernández and Gloria Marinelli both struck twice to leave the Belgian champions winless so far in this season’s league phase. Press Association Photograph: Andrew Redington/Getty Images Europe Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

It was a finish that marked the 200th goal of Slegers’s tenure and one that further eases the pressure on the head coach. With every minute that passed the hosts looked increasingly like themselves and could have added more to their tally.

“It looks like there is something off our shoulders,” Slegers said. “We were playing like us tonight and I am so happy. The players enjoyed themselves – they connected, they expressed themselves and they played with intensity. We backed the last performance up. We need to do it again at the weekend.”

There will no doubt be sterner tests to come in Europe, more immediately away to Barcelona in a fortnight’s time, but this was a victory that signified something more important than just climbing up the Champions League table.

Sports.title: Rulli’s heroics earn Manchester City shootout success against Brighton
Sports.content:
After Jérémy Doku’s second-half substitute appearance transformed Manchester City into a high-octane proposition, the smart money was on the momentum continuing into a victorious penalty shootout.

So it proved as Enzo Maresca’s men triumphed 4-3, Gerónimo Rulli the hero: his save from Lewis Dunk’s fifth spot-kick was decisive, the Argentinean also having repelled Yasin Ayari’s fourth effort.

While Jason Steele kept out Mateo Kovacic’s attempt, City progressed after Brighton twice took the lead – via Malick Yalcouyé and Georginio Rutter – before being pegged back by Kovacic and Vitor Reis.

Maresca was left beaming: “Since I’m here we never practised penalties,” said the City manager. “It always happens that the one that scored in the 90 minutes [Kovacic] misses the penalty. I am very happy.”

Of Doku, he said: “He made an impact. This is the reason they are there. Jérémy and the rest – to try to do their best, if they start from the beginning or if they come in from the bench try to make an impact.”

The tie might have gone either way, so the lottery of penalties felt apt to decide who went through before Saturday’s rematch back here in the league. City will now play League One Bradford in the quarter-finals.

“I watched all [Brighton’s] Premier League games and since the first day they always go front foot, man to man, so they’re going to be exactly the same on Saturday,” Maresca said.

His opposite number spoke of vengeance. “We lost in a shootout. We had enough chances to win the game – they had the luck today. We have to reset. We have a great chance on Saturday to take revenge,” said Fabian Hürzeler.

Quick Guide Carabao Cup quarter-final draw Show Fleetwood v Everton or Newcastle Manchester City v Bradford City Crystal Palace v Sunderland Liverpool v Bournemouth Ties will take place during the week commencing 14 December Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Brighton will stay up in the area. “Not sleeping in your own bed is not an advantage,” said the manager. “But we’ll go there with full energy and ready to go on Saturday.”

When Yalcouyé opened the scoring there was the proverbial hint of offside about the forward as his shot pinged off Rulli and in.

With no video assistant referee in the Carabao Cup the goal stood, though it was soon cancelled out by Kovacic: Phil Foden fed him and, from the edge of the penalty area, he threaded the ball beyond Steele low into the left corner.

View image in fullscreen Georginio Rutter fires Brighton into a second-half lead. Photograph: Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty Images

For the second half Maresca introduced Rayan Aït-Nouri and Ryan McAidoo for Ayyoub Bouaddi and Floyd Samba. Instantly, though, City conceded: Brighton slipped through the lines with ease, and Jaouen Hadjam’s cross was slid in by Rutter.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The forward’s grin went wide in celebration and the Seagulls were heading through, while City were going out. Aït-Nouri, skipping down the left, tried to do something about this, but his ball over was aimless.

At least there was pace in this foray, which those in blue sometimes lacked. But, also, Maresca’s team had become sloppy – a long-range Rayan Cherki pass that ended in Steele’s gloves was emblematic.

Olivier Boscagli’s corner that dipped viciously close to Rulli’s goalline was far more dangerous, so just after the hour Maresca introduced a first big gun – Doku, for Allan – this coming after Rutter ran in and went close to a second, underlining Brighton’s ascendancy.

When Doku played Aït-Nouri in through the left, it was a rare City attack and showed the value of having the Belgian now able to affect the game.

At this point, though, the decision to allow his star quintet the night off was backfiring for Maresca. City lacked control and were toothless. Doku, again, cut through Brighton but there were no runners to prosper from his delivery infield.

Hürzeler’s men tried to squeeze time and snaffle the ball whenever City attempted to move them about, but then came a first passage in which City camped in Brighton territory. Suddenly, those in green were having to answer questions. Foden’s burst that drew a free-kick from Rutter near the 18-yard line presaged one they could not answer. Cherki blasted at goal, Reis stuck out a boot, Steele was wrongfooted, and it was 2-2. Doku had lit up City, his presence terrorising Brighton’s defence and turning the tie.

“They are in a brilliant moment, scoring goals, many goals every game and winning, so we knew it was a tough game in terms of defending in the right way,” Maresca said. “We could have probably done something better defensively, but we started just three months ago [together]. The game was chaotic but we controlled it quite good.”

Sports.title: A three-year-old soccer prodigy went viral. The adults have already let him down
Sports.content:
There is real tragedy in this week’s story of the three-year-old Florida boy whose parents claimed he was so good at soccer that police were called to do what opposing defenders couldn’t. But it doesn’t lie where the outrage cycle wants you to think. It’s broader, implicates more people, and to me, is far more depressing.

You may have seen the video by now. Here was a toddler with fabulous soccer talent, running end-to-end and scoring goal after goal against opponents who have seemingly just found their feet. The cameraman, later identified as the child’s father, loudly and proudly cheers his son on. Way to go, kid.

Then, an abrupt cut to the parents speaking with two police officers from the Orlando suburb of Winter Park. “They called the police on a three-year-old, because he’s too good,” one of the parents says. An officer responds: “They’re wanting you guys to head out, OK?” The parents ask: “You’re confused too, right?”

In the final shot, his mother says: “This is the biggest part of it. We’re trying to put a show on in front of these people. It’s all on [TikTok] Live. There’s thousands of people watching this. He’s famous. There’s thousands of people watching this.”

The story quickly became national news. It was easy to see why. It appeared to take in so many flawed aspects of America: the commoditization of youth sports, overbearing parents, police called for seemingly minor infractions, a social media pile-on and race relations (the child and his parents are Black, the majority of the other children and their parents in the clip were white). Celebrities quickly weighed in to give the story even more life, among them US international Alex Freeman and children’s edutainer Ms Rachel. Civil rights attorney Ben Crump threw his hat in the ring.

But the story is more complicated than the viral video suggested. Police dispatch records, 911 calls and body-camera footage obtained and reviewed by the Guardian offer a fuller picture of what happened on Saturday morning. The organizer, who is also Black, acknowledged that the boy was unusually talented but told officers he had been pushing other children and that his parents had become argumentative. The organizer said he had been rotating players to ensure everyone got a turn, and that the parents had argued with other families. That approach was consistent with i9 Sports’ stated philosophy, which emphasizes fun, inclusion and equal playing time regardless of ability. In a 911 call obtained by the Guardian, the organizer complained of an allegedly disruptive parent who was following him around, calling him names and livestreaming their confrontation. He also referred to the family’s large Instagram following in remarks captured on body-camera footage. The parents offered a sharply different account, insisting that their son was being unfairly singled out because of his ability. Officers, who had not witnessed the dispute, treated it as a civil matter and discussed arranging a refund. No arrests were made.

When the scenes in Winter Park first landed on my feeds on Saturday night, my initial reaction was largely in line with the popular discourse. But even as I learned more, a shot near the end has continued to haunt me. The camera’s edge catches a glimpse of the youngster, visibly confused, already overwhelmed. He couldn’t have known that he’d become a main character of this week’s internet. An audience of mere thousands was about to seem tiny.

Neil Postman got famous arguing that modern media amounts to “amusing ourselves to death”. A few generations on, that phrase is showing its age. Not for its core messaging, but for the implication that amusement is the point. Platforms ensnare users with endless scrolling, fueled by algorithms to extract every penny from one’s pocket and every second from one’s existence. Even if this was the worst day of this kid’s life (or, at least, his worst day so far), that wasn’t the point. The idea that this is an incident with plenty of nuance to consider is immaterial. It was engagement fodder, fresh and meaty ragebait for the ravenous masses to consume and proliferate.

View image in fullscreen Body-worn camera footage of police in Winter Park, Florida, responding to a call of a disturbance at a park on Sunday. Photograph: Winter Park PD

At this point, it’s worth acknowledging that even if the initial video had accurately conveyed the reason for the police’s summoning – which, understandably, the parents couldn’t immediately discern – we may have ended up in the same place. There are countless stories of parents crossing lines at youth sports events, including some that were more worthy of law enforcement. That aspect of this all has largely fallen on deaf ears.

The livestream raises another question, too: what about the other children playing that morning, whose images may have been broadcast to thousands of strangers without their parents ever consenting to such exposure? That point would seem salient enough, and is worth a closer look.

So quickly has this story gone viral that most of us have overlooked one crucial detail: the player involved at the heart of all this is three years old. A toddler. By any criteria, the boy is far too young to be platformed like this, whether by his parents or by the various companies that have leapt on to the story: Jay-Z’s sports and entertainment agency Roc Nation has offered to fly the boy to Spain for “an impactful athletic experience”.

Our culture has ignored any teachable moments from the hype trains that pushed LeBron James, Tiger Woods and Freddy Adu front and center well before they turned 18. Countless parents aspire to turn their children into the next viral sensation, as if that’s a healthy and wise idea. Three-year-olds often can’t keep within the lines of their coloring books, much less understand the ramifications of a grift.

As of Wednesday, the young athlete has nearly 900,000 followers on Instagram and 1.2 million on TikTok. One especially ghoulish post from Monday shows his likeness thrown into a dozen different AI-generated “ads” to position the toddler as a spokesperson for cereal, sugary drinks and athletic gear.

He’s clearly not making these posts himself. It’s hard to imagine he’s asking to become another in an endless and tired trend of athletes turned influencers. Yet his profile has two links: an email address for inquiries – introducing this winter’s hot toy, My Little Inbox – and a GoFundMe to “support [his] soccer journey”, with a claim that this is all about “protecting [his] passion for soccer”. As of Wednesday night, the fundraiser had raised more than $49,000, comfortably surpassing its $30,000 goal.

Hopefully he can soon enjoy the anonymity that nearly every other three-year-old enjoys. To grow up as a child rather than as a commodity. To continue playing sports because he loves them, not because there’s a buck to be made.

But maybe that window has already slammed shut. There were too many clicks to be generated, too much engagement to be had. In this case, across the board, the grownups and their machines have let him down. The question now is whether they’ll allow him to be a child again.

Sports.title: European football: Bayern ease to Cup victory after Kompany leaves hospital
Sports.content:
Bayern Munich sailed to a 6-1 win over second-tier Magdeburg in the DFB-Pokal after their head coach, Vincent Kompany, was discharged from hospital earlier on Wednesday.

Kompany’s assistant, Aaron Danks, was in the dugout for Bayern for the last-32 tie, while Harry Kane was rested. The Ballon d’Or winner received a guard of honour from his teammates before kick-off in front of 75,000 fans at the Allianz Arena.

Bayern had no difficulty without their star striker, with Michael Olise opening the scoring and adding a second-half penalty. Ismael Saibari, Alphonso Davies, Nathaniel Brown and teenager David Santos Daiber also got on the scoresheet, with Mateusz Zukowski striking for the visitors.

The German Cup holders received good news pre-match, with Kompany able to return home five days after collapsing at training on Friday. The Bayern Munich sporting director, Max Eberl, revealed that the Belgian had been suffering from meningeal irritation.

“We have identified the cause: it is a case of meningeal irritation, which is what triggered the incident last Friday,” Eberl said. “He has now been allowed to go home, where he can continue his rehabilitation … [which] means rest and medication. I am very, very confident that he will be back on the touchline at 100% very soon.”

Olise tapped in from an excellent Saibari assist after 10 minutes but the unfancied visitors levelled five minutes later through Zukowski. Olise then set up Saibari midway through the opening half and added a third from the spot early in the second half before smiling and pointing to Kane, Bayern’s regular penalty taker, on the bench.

View image in fullscreen Michael Olise scored from the penalty spot in Harry Kane’s absence. Photograph: Kai Pfaffenbach/Reuters

The teenage forward Lennart Karl set up goals for Davies and Brown, before Santos Daiber added more gloss to the victory with a stoppage-time goal. “We’re also winning for him of course,” Brown said of Kompany. “It’s really good that he’s back home now. He should get some rest, but hopefully we’ll see him again soon.”

“We’re very pleased that [Vincent] is getting better,” said Danks, who will continue to lead the team while Kompany recovers. “But he needs to rest, spend time with his family and continue to get better. He’s doing better and is on the road to recovery. We’ll simply try to do our best and prepare for the game on Saturday.”

Elsewhere, Bayer Leverkusen came from two goals down to win 5-2 against 2. Bundesliga promotion-chasers Nuremberg, with defender Edmond Tapsoba netting twice and Patrik Schick, Jonas Hofmann and Lucas Vázquez also on target.

Deniz Undav’s 90th-minute strike earned Stuttgart a 1-0 win over 10-man Paderborn, while Freiburg also won in stoppage time. The Japan forward Keisuke Goto scored twice in the final 15 minutes to turn a 2-1 deficit into a 3-2 victory over Wolfsburg.

Second-tier Dynamo Dresden upset Schalke 2-0, and Holstein Kiel eliminated Hoffenheim 4-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw to reach the last 16.

There was a huge upset across the border in Poland, as defending league champions Lech Poznan were beaten 1-0 by fourth-tier Siarka Tarnobrzeg in a Cup tie that kicked off at 12.30pm on Wednesday.

Lech held Sunderland to a 1-1 draw in the Europa League last week and beat Legia Warsaw on Sunday to go top of the Polish top-flight – but they were brought down to earth by Arkadiusz Kasia’s second-half header.

Inter sink Venezia, Milan beaten by Bologna

Internazionale returned to the Serie A summit with a nervy 2-0 win at bottom side Venezia, while Bologna won 4-2 at San Siro to inflict a first league defeat of the season on Milan.

Champions Inter drew level with Lazio on 25 points at the top before a hotly anticipated Milan derby on Saturday. Ruben Amorim’s side lost their unbeaten streak after Alphadjo Cisse’s double was not enough to avoid defeat, as Samuel Mbangula’s hat-trick sealed a 4-2 win for the visitors.

Venezia have picked up just three points all season, but earned them with a shock win over Napoli on new coach Davide Nicola’s debut. Another shock result looked possible on Wednesday until they were undone by two late own goals, with Matías Moreno and Redouane Halhal diverting crosses into their own net.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

At San Siro, a lengthy injury list restricted Amorim’s options, and the Milan coach also left Christian Pulisic and Luka Modric on the bench. Mbangula, making his full debut for Bologna, swept home the opener inside eight minutes, but the visitors were soon pegged back when an Arthur Theate error gifted Cissé a simple finish.

View image in fullscreen Bologna’s Samuel Mbangula is surrounded by teammates and coaches after scoring his third goal against Milan. Photograph: Spada/LaPresse/Shutterstock

The teenager struck again in the 27th minute, volleying home a Fikayo Tomori cross, but the game was turned on its head once again in the space of two second-half minutes. Davide Bartesaghi turned a free-kick into his own net before Mbangula struck again just after the hour mark. The 22-year-old sealed victory four minutes from time, beating Mike Maignan after a breakaway.

Juventus’s shaky start continued with a 2-0 defeat away to Genoa. Kingsley Ehizibue struck early before Tommaso Baldanzi doubled Genoa’s lead in the 28th minute. Luciano Spalletti’s inconsistent side have not won back-to-back league games since the opening two weeks of the season, and face Napoli next.

With head coach Massimiliano Allegri suspended after being sent off during the 3-3 draw with Roma, Napoli enjoyed their biggest win of the season, winning 4-1 at Monza to go sixth in the table, above Juve on goal difference.

Rasmus Højlund’s early opener was cancelled out by Gustavo Varela’s header just before the break, but Napoli pulled away in the second half as Matteo Politano, Rafa Marín and substitute Kevin De Bruyne all scored. Elsewhere, Adrián Bernabé saw his penalty saved as struggling Parma and Udinese played out a 0-0 draw.

Copa del Rey games postponed after rail crash

All 24 Copa del Rey matches scheduled for Wednesday evening have been postponed as a mark of respect following the devastating rail incident in Spain.

A high-speed train crashed into the rear of another train on Wednesday morning and derailed two cars in the province of Toledo, with at least 68 people killed.

La Liga clubs Alavés, Celta Vigo, Levante, Real Betis and Valencia were due to get their domestic cup campaigns under way, but all of Wednesday’s fixtures will now be played at later dates.

Real Madrid, Barcelona and Atlético Madrid are not due to enter until the last 32 in December, but all three issued statements expressing sadness and deepest condolences.

Sports.title: ‘This isn’t supposed to happen’: giant-slaying Fleetwood revels in fairytale Arsenal win
Sports.content:
On a wet and windy night on the north-west coast of England, a League Two side sensationally knocked the Premier League champions out of the Carabao Cup. But this is not just a fairytale story of giant-slaying: Fleetwood Town and Arsenal have an unlikely history that stretches back long before Tuesday night’s game.

Arsenal played at their iconic Highbury stadium until 2006, and Fleetwood’s ground has the same title, being named after Highbury Avenue, the adjoining street.

Fleetwood also play in red shirts with white sleeves in the style of the classic Arsenal kit. Nobody is exactly sure why, but according to Ray Curtis, a barman in the town’s King’s Arms: “Fleetwood’s first ever kit, the home kit, was given to them by Arsenal.”

And in the 2000s, not long after Patrick Vieira captained Arsenal, Fleetwood boasted a namesake star: a Brazilian striker called Magno Vieira.

At the 5,300-capacity Highbury on Wednesday morning, the floodlights that Fleetwood had hired for the occasion were being packed away. “It’s back to reality, back to being a League Two team, that’s our normal,” said Zsofia Wright, the ticket office and retail manager.

View image in fullscreen Television equipment is removed from the Highbury stadium on Wednesday after the match between teams 84 places apart in the football pyramid. Photograph: Colin McPherson/The Guardian

On Tuesday, the excitement and anticipation started early. “We started getting what team had turned up, who’d flown in, and the whispers started, and it’s like, ‘oh, they’ve gone quite strong’,” Wright said.

“So we were all planning to just enjoy the occasion. And then obviously, we went 1-0 up and everyone was kind of looking at each other, like this isn’t supposed to be happening.”

She said it was back to reality when Arsenal equalised except that “the clock kept on going and the score didn’t change”.

View image in fullscreen Chris Newman came to the club shop to pick up some souvenir programmes. Photograph: Colin McPherson/The Guardian

Wright said everyone was on the pitch after the dramatic penalty shootout that saw the Premier League champions and Champions League finalists ousted from the competition. The next stop for players, fans and management was the stadium bar.

“Just incredible,” Wright said. “We were here till about half one last night. It was brilliant, amazing.”

“The atmosphere was crazy,” said Chris Newman, 33, who was at the match with his son. He returned to the club shop on Wednesday to pick up two souvenir programmes. “Everything happened so quick,” he said. “I just didn’t expect it at all.”

The shop has done a roaring trade over the past 36 hours, with half-and-half Fleetwood and Arsenal scarves proving especially popular. One buyer with a London accent said: “I’m a Spurs fan, it’s brilliant.”

Wright said the town was abuzz the morning after: “Bars, pubs that are struggling, they were open till God knows what time yesterday. We just hope it can continue throughout the season, just hope that attendances start to pick up, and get consistency back again through the gates.”

The club’s nicknames – the Cod Army, the Fishermen, the Cods and the Trawlermen – all derive from the Lancashire town’s fishing industry.

Sharon Brooks, who was visiting a fishmonger by the harbour, said: “We thought it’d be three, four or five nil, but they did so well to get a draw and then win on penalties, and five brilliant penalties. It’s nice for a town like Fleetwood, and [against the] Premier League winners last season, they just surprised you didn’t they?”

Her 12-year-old son, Ryan, who is an Arsenal fan, said: “Even though I wanted [Arsenal] to win it, I’m pleased for them.”

View image in fullscreen Sharon Brooks with her Arsenal-supporting son, Ryan, who said he was still pleased his local team won. Photograph: Colin McPherson/The Guardian

View image in fullscreen Donald Maclean in the King’s Arms in Fleetwood town centre. He said such a result ‘had never been heard of before’. Photograph: Colin McPherson/The Guardian

In the King’s Arms, everyone was eagerly awaiting Wednesday night’s draw, which will decide who Fleetwood plays next.

Donald Maclean, who missed the game because he was on duty at a nursing home, said: “I saw the goals this morning and I was delighted, over the moon, imagine Fleetwood taking down the Gunners! Never been heard of before, so yes, we’re all delighted about it. Brilliant!”

The Cod Army’s victory has delighted fans partly because it was so unexpected – Fleetwood sit 84 places below Arsenal in the football league pyramid.

Michael Houton said he had thought the result impossible “because Arsenal shouldn’t have got beaten should they? Not against Fleetwood.”

View image in fullscreen Fleetwood Town’s club shop has been doing a roaring trade in half-and-half scarves. Photograph: Colin McPherson/The Guardian

Paul Dagger was so pessimistic about his team’s chances that he had staked £200 at half-time on Arsenal to win at odds of 10/7. “Gyökeres [of Arsenal] scored within five minutes of the start,” he said. “I thought, oh here we go, money’s coming in now. You live and learn.”

Fleetwood fans hope it will be the start of something bigger than just a victory for lovers of the game. “The town needs it,” Dagger said. “As you can see, it’s full of charity shops and vape shops.”

View image in fullscreen ‘I think it’s fantastic for the town,’ said Paul Dagger. Photograph: Colin McPherson/The Guardian

View image in fullscreen Garry Gill said other teams would now be ‘frightened’ of coming to play Fleetwood. Photograph: Colin McPherson/The Guardian

Garry Gill, a retired crane operator, said: “I am a Fleetwood fan and I think it’s fantastic for the town. It’s going to bring coin.

“If they play with the determination they did last night, any team that comes to play now is going to be frightened. And normally, that’s not the case, they think it’s an easy win.”

Jim Buckley said: “It’s magic. We’re a Mickey Mouse town of 25,000 people, there’s no train station. I mean at the Emirates, they can fit three towns the size of this town in there.”

He was not far out – Arsenal’s stadium can hold 60,000 fans.

The drinkers in the King’s Arms said the travelling Arsenal fans had had a good day out despite the embarrassing defeat.

Dagger said: “Two pound twenty a pint in here, two pound fifty a pint over the way. They couldn’t believe it, they were going, facking ‘ell, it’s eight quid where we are.”

View image in fullscreen Bethany Taylor, right, at the Shark Chippy near Fleetwood harbour. She said she was expecting defeat until she heard the roar of the crowd at the final whistle. Photograph: Colin McPherson/The Guardian

Back near the harbour, at the Shark Chippy, there was a lunchtime rush. Dishing up cod and chips, Bethany Taylor said she lived near the ground and could tell the result from the roar of the crowd and the flares. “It was good, brilliant,” she added. “We weren’t expecting it.”

“It’s an incredible result isn’t it?” said her colleague Louisa Smith.

But do they think Fleetwood can lift the Carabao Cup? “It’d be a struggle, but hopefully they will,” Smith said. “We wish them luck.”

Sports.title: Wrexham slapped with EFL punishment after fielding two ineligible players
Sports.content:
Wrexham slapped with EFL punishment after fielding two ineligible players

Wrexham have been fined £75,000 for fielding ineligible players on two occasions this season.

The EFL have sanctioned the Championship club, with £25,000 of their fine suspended.



3 Callum O'Hare is one of two ineligible players fielded by Wrexham Credit: Getty

It relates to summer signings Issa Kabore and Callum O'Hare, who were included in matchday squads without the proper paperwork being completed.

Kabore came off the bench in a 2-1 home defeat to Birmingham City on August 28.

The full-back had signed permanently from Manchester City the previous day following his loan spell last season.



However, the Home Office 'right to work' documents required for Kabore to feature had not been uploaded correctly.

Meanwhile, O'Hare was an unused substitute in Wrexham's 3-0 away win over Millwall on September 2.



Similarly to Kabore, the midfielder's documentation had not been uploaded in time for him to be registered for the match at The Den.

O'Hare completed a deadline day switch from Sheffield United on September 1, penning a three-year deal with the Red Dragons.



In a statement, Wrexham said: "We can confirm that Wrexham AFC has reached an Agreed Decision with the EFL concerning two breaches relating to player eligibility."

They added: "The club is taking the appropriate steps to prevent such issues occurring in the future."

It is understood Wrexham are planning to hire a club secretary to avoid similar issues arising in the future.

3 Kabore's documents were not uploaded correctly before a match against Birmingham Credit: Shutterstock Editorial



Phil Parkinson's side made seven permanent signings during the summer transfer window.

Of those, four were completed after the start of the Championship season, including deals for Kabore and O'Hare.

The Red Dragons spent around £33.5million bolstering their squad following last season's play-off near miss.

Wrexham finished seventh on their return to the second-tier, missing out on a post-season berth by just two points.



After 12 matches of the current campaign, they sit 17th in the table, six points above the relegation zone.

Meanwhile, they are an equal amount adrift of the play-offs, which have now extended to eighth place.

3 Parkinson's side are currently 17th in the Championship Credit: Getty

Wrexham travel to Bramall Lane this weekend to face Sheffield United on Friday, October 30.



The match is scheduled to kick-off at 8pm, live on talkSPORT 2.

Sports.title: Rio Ferdinand: Cristiano Ronaldo is obsessed – he will know anything bad you’ve said about him
Sports.content:
Rio Ferdinand: Cristiano Ronaldo is obsessed – he will know anything bad you’ve said about him

Cristiano Ronaldo is aware of everything negative said about him - it's the reason why he is obsessed with being the best.

That's the view of his ex-Manchester United teammate Rio Ferdinand, who has declared the 41-year-old is constantly looking to prove his critics wrong.

3 Ferdinand and Ronaldo spent six trophy-laden years together at Old Trafford Credit: AFP

Ronaldo, who is in the twilight of his career, is closing in on becoming the first player in history to score 1,000 goals.

Into the final year of his contract at Al Nassr, the veteran forward is just 19 goals shy of reaching the stunning milestone.

But while his place in history has already been sealed, having won five Ballon d'Or awards and as many Champions League titles, he hasn't been without his critics.

Who has criticised Cristiano Ronaldo?

And as ex-teammate Gary Neville and Liverpool icon Jamie Carragher have found out, you'll be shunned if you speak negatively about him.

He famously snubbed Neville during his second spell at United - blanking him as he greeted Louis Saha and Jamie Redknapp before the Red Devils faced West Ham.

Just months before Neville criticised Ronaldo's conduct by walking down the tunnel early and refusing to come on against Tottenham - Carragher was given the same treatment after suggesting he should have been sold that summer.

He was also denied a handshake by Ronaldo, who greeted Neville and Roy Keane, during Sky Sports' coverage of United vs Liverpool.

And speaking on the Sports Breakfast Show, Ferdinand, who won nine trophies alongside Ronaldo during their six-year spell together at the Theatre of Dreams, has insisted he never forgets those that talk ill of him.

And the former defender declared that Portugal's record goalscorer uses criticism as fuel to be the best at everything he does.

What has Rio Ferdinand said about Cristiano Ronaldo?

After co-host Ally McCoist suggested Ronaldo will be obsessed to reach the 1,000 goal mark, Ferdinand said: "Yeah, he will be obsessed [with getting 1,000 goals], and I think that's the key word that you put alongside him.

3 Ronaldo deliberately blanked Neville in October 2022 after his ex-teammate criticised him over his conduct during the 2-0 win over Spurs Credit: Sky Sports

3 The five-time Ballon d'Or winner also refused to acknowledge Carragher on live TV Credit: Sky Sports

"You can talk about ability and goalscorer and all that, the guy is obsessed with being in the best condition, with being the best, with scoring the most goals, with putting his imprint in the game to be legendary.

"He's just obsessed with all these things, he will know that if you've said something about him that's a little bit out of shape or whatever - that something will get his way to him.

"He'll find it and he'll pick at it and he'll use that as fuel, and sometimes people can point him and use that as a stick to beat him with.

"But he's not Cristiano Ronaldo without those traits, those obsessive traits to continually fight against any negative comments, any negative spirit that comes around him.

"He uses that and I think any young player, you look at and you go, 'How are you going to make it?'

"It's not just about being a great footballer, you've got to find things that turn you on mentally, that stimulate you to become the best every day and that's what he does."

Sports.title: Chelsea fans will turn on Xabi Alonso if weird treatment of star player continues
Sports.content:
Chelsea fans will turn on Xabi Alonso if weird treatment of star player continues

Chelsea fans and pundits alike have been left baffled by Xabi Alonso's treatment of Estevao.

The Blues boss left the Brazil winger on the bench as his side crashed out of the Carabao Cup in a penalty shootout defeat to Liverpool on Wednesday night.

2 Estevao scored six goals in 33 matches during an exciting debut campaign before suffering a long-term injury Credit: Getty

Despite becoming a fan favourite during his first season at Stamford Bridge, Estevao has played just 148 minutes of competitive football under Alonso.

The 19-year-old is yet to start in the Premier League this season, appearing only as a substitute and playing back-up to Pedro Neto at right-wing-back.

He was left out of the Chelsea starting XI in favour of Geovany Quenda - another 19-year-old with significantly less top-flight experience - for the 2-0 defeat to Tottenham.

And he was snubbed completely at Anfield despite right-sided forward Cole Palmer being suspended.

With Estevao expected to become one of football's biggest stars, the whole situation has made fans question whether there is something going on behind the scenes.

There are also fears the highly-rated teenager could become unsettled and look to leave the club.

Explaining the Estevao decision at Liverpool, Alonso said: "I understand his situation and that he could be happier for sure.

“Every player wants to play, wants to be part of the team. We have had some intense games, and there will be moments for everything.

“I'm sure that Estevao will have his moment. It's my responsibility and we need to deal with that.”

talkSPORT verdict: Chelsea fans will turn

Ex-Premier League stars Jamie O'Hara and Jermaine Pennant warned Alonso that his treatment of Estevao risks making him unpopular among the Chelsea faithful.

2 Could Estevao look to leave Chelsea if his playing opportunities do not improve?

O'Hara said: "That's a bad situation there for Chelsea, because I genuinely think he is a star in the making.

"And if you're playing Neto and you've got Cole Palmer, okay, but to not use Estevao at all, not even feature, it's almost a bit embarrassing, right?

"Come on, he's a Brazilian star in the making and you're just pieing him off.

"And I think that's actually going to come back and bite Alonso in the backside. I think Chelsea fans will be like, 'Hold on a minute'."

Pennant added: "That could be one of the Achilles' heels for Alonso, if he does not start using him.

"If he's getting results, you can be like, okay, fair enough, you're picking a winning team.

"But if you're going away with losses and he's not featuring, when he can be a difference, that's when they [the fans] will start turning."

Sports.title: Top five greatest midfield trios in Premier League history
Sports.content:
Great midfielders are the lifeblood of any Premier League team - and every so often they join forces to become truly unstoppable.

A combination of creators and runners to destroyers and goalscorers; the top-flight has boasted some of the best in the business.



6 talkSPORT's Mount Rushmore looks at the most influential and iconic things in sport, with presenter Max Scott selecting five (four is just not enough) in each topic Credit: Alamy

The rise of the 4-3-3 and 4-2-3-1 formations in English football has meant the midfield trio is now the norm for most elite clubs.

And talkSPORT's Max Scott has whittled down his list of the best in his weekly series, Mount Rushmore or Less, where four isn't enough.

Whilst there are four of the most influential presidents in American history on the iconic sculpture, in this case we need a fifth pick.



1. Arsenal: Robert Pires, Patrick Vieira and Gilberto Silva

Premier League Starts Together: 44

Record: 31 Wins, 11 Draws, 2 Losses

Win Rate: 70.5%

Points Per Game (PPG): 2.36

"First up for me, it's three of the midfielders from Arsenal's Invincibles, title-winning squad in 2003-04," Scott explained.

"Let's start with Robert Pires, somebody who I think lived in the shadow of Thierry Henry a little bit. I don't necessarily think he minded that, but in that title-winning season, that invincible title-winning season, he scored 14 goals and got nine assists.



"Gilberto Silva, the invisible wall, one of those unsung heroes with that defensive capability to break up play and technically gifted as well.

"Then, one of my favourite midfielders in Premier League history is Patrick Vieira - In terms of my living memory, he was the first midfielder I saw that had the physical dominance and prowess to absolutely dominate opponents, but then the technicality, or the technical ability, and the grace with the ball moving forward, some magnificent flicks in his link-up play with the amazing players around him, most notably Thierry Henry, was a sight to behold.



"So I know Arsenal at the time didn't always just exclusively play with a midfield three, but from that invincible winning squad, that midfield three was unbelievable."

6 Gilberto and Vieira were a force to be reckoned with in Wenger's central pivot, with Pires starring on the left Credit: Getty

2. Man City - Rodri, Kevin De Bruyne and Bernardo Silva

Premier League Starts Together: 56

Record: 41 Wins, 8 Draws, 7 Losses

Win Rate: 73.2%

Points Per Game (PPG): 2.34

The tactical backbone of Pep Guardiola's record-breaking City side, which helped claim a historic four-in-a-row Premier League title run.

Rodri controlled the tempo at the base of the midfield, while Bernardo Silva's press resistance and tactical flexibility to play multiple positions allowed De Bruyne to pick up pockets of space to devastating effect.



"A midfield trio which is arguably the most complete midfield trio we've seen in recent Premier League history," Scott surmised.

"Rodri, Kevin De Bruyne and Bernardo Silva, not David Silva. I'm more of a Bernardo fan. Why? They won four consecutive Premier League titles; never been done before.

"If I'm putting in the Arsenal-Invincibles midfield trio, I have to put in this Man City midfield trio that did what no one has ever done before, and I tell you what, I don't think it will ever be done again.

"All magnificent players in their own right, they are part of the foundations of what Manchester City have become in recent years."



6 De Bruyne, Rodri and Bernardo formed the foundation for Man City's 2022–23 Treble campaign. Credit: Getty

What is Mount Rushmore? The faces of George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt and Abraham Lincoln are carved into the stone in South Dakota, chosen for their representation of the most important events in the United States' history. As a result, fans use the idea to create their own version to list the most influential or iconic games and people that define their selected categories. Here, though, talkSPORT argues five is not enough, so more or less this is Mount Rushmore.

3. Man United: Paul Scholes, Ryan Giggs and Roy Keane

Premier League Starts Together: 112

Record: 74 Wins, 24 Draws, 14 Losses

Win Rate: 66.1%

Points Per Game (PPG): 2.20

Scott continued: "Up next is a Manchester United midfield trio, which I acknowledge usually played in a four.

"It's Ryan Giggs, Paul Scholes, Roy Keane. So it means Becks, Sir David... I'm leaving you out, I'm afraid, because you went off to the Galacticos and you left Manchester United.

"So I have to pick those three players that played together for 12 years in that time, won 12 major trophies; everything that you could possibly want to win, including a Champions League.



"Roy Keane, one of the greatest ever central midfielders, a standard bearer, a tone setter for Sir Alex Ferguson during his most successful period at the Football Club and represented a brand of football which we don't see these days, where football was definitely a contact sport and not full of this sort of wet white behaviour of everyone rolling around on the floor like prima donnas.

"And he's taken that attitude into his life as a pundit, and he's much adored and rightly so for that.

"Paul Scholes, I think in some ways, was quite underrated - one of the best passers that the world has ever seen of a football.

"A wand of a right foot and could do everything and scored some absolute screamers - one of the greatest to ever play in the Premier League and then Ryan Giggs.



"He played almost a thousand games for Manchester United, scored 168 goals, 268 assists in the Premier League alone, one of the greats.

"The fact that he played to the age of 40 and he was still effective right to the very end, that for me is Premier League heritage."

6 Scholes, Keane and Giggs won six Premier League titles while part of the same squad at Old Trafford Credit: Getty

4. Chelsea: Frank Lampard, Michael Essien & Claude Makelele

Premier League Starts Together: 39

Record: 27 Wins, 10 Draws, 2 Losses

Win Rate: 69.2%

Points Per Game (PPG): 2.33

This Chelsea trio suffered only two defeats in 39 league matches when all three were on the pitch in the 2005/06 title-winning season.



Scott told talkSPORT: "Frank Lampard, 177 Premier League goals, 119 Premier League assists - the greatest ever goal-scoring midfielder that this country has ever seen.

"Makelele, centre defensive midfielder, one of the first of that breed that became famous and hugely well paid for playing a defensive role; that CDM became known as the Makelele role.

"He's got a legacy, and the people that follow Rodri, for example, all these great players playing since CDM, I think, is largely down to Claude Makelele. Think of N'Golo Kante and the rich history that Rory Jennings will bang on about Chelsea in terms of having midfielders.

"For me it starts with Claude Makelele, and then there's Michael Essien - Ghanaian phenomenon who had an unbelievable engine.



"He had an unbelievable right boat on him, and so together as a trio they were magnificent, and they typify what Chelsea became under Roman Abramovich.

"I know Frank Lampard was there before, but that brutal winning mentality under Jose Mourinho and Roman Abramovich, wow!"

6 Lampard, Makelele and Essien formed one of the most physically dominant 4-3-3 midfields in Premier League history Credit: AFP

Mount Rushmore of less. Liverpool: Gini Wijnaldum, Fabinho and Jordan Henderson

Premier League Starts Together: 34

Record: 26 Wins, 6 Draws, 2 Losses

Win Rate: 76.5%

Points Per Game (PPG): 2.47

Jurgen Klopp’s first-choice engine-room trio did the unsung work behind Mohamed Salah, Roberto Firmino, and Sadio Mané.



Wijnaldum, Fabinho and then-Reds captain Henderson were Liverpool's midfield combination that started their 2019 Champions League final win over Tottenham in Madrid.

In fact, their only two league defeats when starting together the following season, as Klopp's men won the title, came after clinching the trophy (against Man City and Arsenal in July 2020).

Scott said: "As great players that they are, they don't have that stardust blockbuster name.

"But what they did do is provide the support and the backbone for one of the most entertaining sides we've seen in recent Premier League history.



6 Wijnaldum, Henderson and Fabinho were three of the quintessential Klopp midfielders Credit: AFP

"You think about Mane, Firmino, Salah, but behind them, you've got the dogged pressing and winning the ball back and leadership and standards of Jordan Henderson, Wijnaldum and Fabinho.

"They won the Champions League in 2019. Then they broke the dominance of City by winning the Premier League in 2020.

"While we rave about the front three, and rightly so, they were magnificent to watch as a forward three; behind them are the kind of unsung heroes of those three midfielders.



"And so for me, they have to be mentioned in the list of midfield trio greats in Premier League history. Hats off to you boys."

The Bantams - who reached the final of the competition in 2013 - have been handed a massive giant-killing opportunity as they prepare to take on last year's winners at the Etihad Stadium.



4 Fleetwood, meanwhile, are back at home and have another Premier League opponent coming to Highbury Stadium Credit: Getty

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo beats Lionel Messi to win inaugural award
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo has beaten Lionel Messi and a host of football legends to win the inaugural Ballon d'Or 'BOAT' award.

In a brand new category introduced for this year's edition, Ronaldo has been awarded the prize which crowns the greatest Ballon d’Or winner of all time.

4 Cristiano Ronaldo's 2008 Ballon d'Or triumph has been ranked above all others Credit: AFP

While Harry Kane enjoyed an historic triumph in the main category, the Portuguese icon was among ten legendary players nominated for the Ballon d'Or of All Time [BOAT] award.

This pitted previous multiple-time winners of the award against each other in a fan vote.

With Ronaldo a five-time recipient of the individual prize, he was up against some greats of the game, including generational rival Messi.

Also in the running were the Netherlands' Marco van Basten and France's Michel Platini - each with three Ballon d'Or crowns - plus Barcelona icon Johan Cruyff, who also won a trio of golden balls.

Brazil 2002 World Cup winner Ronaldo Nazario, Germany great Franz Beckenbauer, Newcastle and Liverpool icon Kevin Keegan, Real Madrid legend Alfredo Di Stefano and Germany's Karl-Heinz Rummenigge completed the list of contenders.

But it was Portugal's Ronaldo who triumphed in the all-time category, adding yet another individual award to his huge collection.

Ronaldo scoops prestigious prize

After a fan vote, Ronaldo's 2008 Ballon d'Or season finished first, with eight-time winner Messi's 2012 season coming in second.

The Al Nassr forward also took third-place for his 2017 award - the last time he won football's ultimate individual prize.

Ronaldo claimed the first Ballon d'Or of his career in 2008, seeing off Messi and former Liverpool star Fernando Torres after a standout campaign with Manchester United.

In the 2007/08 season, the football megastar scored 42 goals in all competitions to help Sir Alex Ferguson's side to Premier League and Champions League glory.

4 Messi and Ronaldo share 13 Ballons d'Or between them - but only one has won the 'BOAT' award Credit: Getty Images - Getty

4 Ronaldo scored a staggering 31 Premier League goals in his Ballon d'Or-winning 2007/08 campaign Credit: Getty

It was this triumph which truly catapulted Ronaldo into contention as one of the world's greatest footballers.

He certainly never looked back after that, with a move to Real Madrid for a then world-record £80million fee coming a year later in 2009.

Ronaldo went on to spend nine years with the Spanish giants, winning the Champions League four times and going on to establish himself as one of football's all-time greats.

His exploits saw him scoop four more Ballon d'Or awards while at the Bernabeu - in 2013, 2014, 2016 and 2017.

Ronaldo's rivalry with Messi reached its peak during his time in Spain, with the pair starring on opposite sides of the El Clasico rivalry and going head-to-head in the race to be crowned the world's best player.

Wit the Barcelona icon boasting three more Ballon d'Or crowns, Ronaldo will take delight in beating him in his BOAT triumph.

4 Now in his forties, Ronaldo continues to chase records Credit: Getty

The Man United great has made no secret of his drive to be regarded as the greatest footballer of all time, and has openly voiced his belief of this before.

He remains motivated by individual records even in the latter stages of his career, most notably his desire to reach 1,000 career goals.

Ronaldo is closing in on the unprecedented milestone, currently sitting at an incredible 981 strikes in 1,340 professional games.

Sports.title: Vincent Kompany discharged from hospital as cause of terrifying collapse confirmed
Sports.content:
Vincent Kompany discharged from hospital as cause of terrifying collapse confirmed

Vincent Kompany has been discharged from hospital after his terrifying collapse at Bayern Munich's training ground.

The 40-year-old was airlifted to hospital last Friday with medical staff working tirelessly to try and discover what the cause of Kompany's health scare was.

3 Kompany was in hospital for five days Credit: AFP

It's been revealed that Manchester City legend Kompany was diagnosed with meningeal irritation.

The mengines are the membranes surrounding the brain and spinal chord which, when irritated, can trigger painful muscle spasms.

Bayern sporting director Max Eberl confirmed the news as he also revealed he expects Kompany to be back on the touchline soon, although the Belgian will not be rushed back.

Cause of Kompany health scare confirmed

Eberl told German publication ARD: “I think this is the biggest and best news for all of us. They have found what it is.

“It’s meningeal irritation that caused this incident last Friday.

“He has now been allowed to go home, where he can continue his rehabilitation. In his case, rehabilitation means rest and medication.

“I am very, very confident that he will soon be back on the sidelines, operating at 100 per cent.

“[He will get] all the time he needs – we’ve said that all along. That is why, from the very beginning, we spoke in terms of weeks.”

It's reported that Kompany fell unconscious and experienced convulsions while also dislocating his shoulder when he collapsed.

Kompany's assistant Aaron Danks took charge of Bayern for their win over Freiburg last Sunday, as well as their DFB-Pokal clash at home to Magdeburg.

3 Kompany has won five trophies as Bayern boss Credit: Getty

Former Burnley and Anderlecht boss Kompany has been in the Bayern hotseat since 2024, leading them to two Bundesliga titles and three domestic cups.

He has played a role in developing Harry Kane's game even further, culminating in the England captain winning the Ballon d'Or on Monday.

In his acceptance speech, Kane issued a well-wishing message to Kompany while also paying tribute to his Bayern teammates.

Kane said: “The way you guys push me, the way we compete, me against (Dayot Upamecano) in training every week, it makes me a better player, makes me want to improve.

“To Vinny (Kompany), I think he's at home or still in the hospital — wishing you very well and hope this has given you a bit of energy.”

Kompany's final game before his collapse saw the Bundesliga champions play out an entertaining 2-2 draw at home to Arsenal in the Champions League two days prior.

3 Harry Kane sent a heartfelt message to Kompany in his Ballon d'Or winner's speech Credit: Getty

Bayern are top of the Bundesliga with 17 points from seven matches, ahead of Borussia Dortmund on goal difference.

However, the two sides face off in the latest edition of Der Klassiker on Saturday at the Allianz Arena.

As for their European exploits, Bayern are 14th in the table with five points from three games with their next outing seeing them travel to Atletico Madrid on Tuesday night.

Sports.title: Ivan Toney's trial over assault at exclusive London nightclub will start in 20 MONTHS - putting England star's Euro 2028 prospects at risk
Sports.content:
England international Ivan Toney’s assault trial will not be heard for another 20 months – and will potentially rule him out of Euro 2028.

Toney, who was in this summer's World Cup squad, appeared at Southwark Crown Court for a pre-trial hearing on Thursday morning and pleaded not guilty to assault occasioning actual bodily harm.

The 30-year-old is accused of headbutting and punching Saber Da Silva at the 100 Wardour Street nightclub in Soho on December 6 2025.

Toney’s defence do not dispute that he caused injury but they claim he acted in self-defence.

The trial will begin on June 12, 2028 - three days into the European Championships, which are being held in the United Kingdom and Ireland - and is expected to last three to four days.

Toney arrived at Southwark Crown Court at 9:10 on Thursday morning, flanked by a six-man entourage, wearing a black button-up cardigan with a white shirt, black tie and grey trousers.
