Sports.title: Tyson Fury and wife Paris both break down in tears as they recount how he 'didn't want to live' in deep depression amid his alcohol and drug addiction in new Netflix documentary trailer
Sports.content:
A tearful Paris Fury has revealed how she was left 'scared' over husband Tyson's alarming health decline, with the heavyweight superstar opening up on his paralysing drink and drug addiction in a new documentary.

Tyson, 38, saw his life spiral out of control after reaching the pinnacle of boxing following his heavyweight title triumph over arch rival Wladimir Klitschko in 2015.

The Gypsy King, speaking in Netflix's new documentary Tyson Fury, confessed how he had lost his 'whole point of existence' after his win in Dusseldorf, leading to a crippling addiction to alcohol and cocaine.

In the documentary trailer, Tyson says: 'All I wanted to was beat Klitschko. It was an obsession for me.

'I'd achieved all my childhood dreams, but my whole point of existence had been taken away. I didn't want to live.'

Tyson and Paris Fury both broke down in tears as they recounted his troubling addiction past

Fury revealed how he had lost his whole point of existence after winning the heavyweight title

Fury fulfilled a career-long obsession after beating Wladimir Klitschko in 2015

Tyson's wife and childhood sweetheart Paris, could only watch on as her husband's life unravelled, and was emotional as she recounted the traumatising episode.

'Straight after [the Klitschko fight], Tyson said to me "this is as good as it is ever going to get". I didn't understand at the time what he meant,' she says.

'The Tyson I knew was gone and I was so scared.'

The documentary, which charts Tyson's incredible rise to heavyweight champion of the world, tells how he grew up surrounded by strong male figures - where discussing emotions was off limits.

'Growing up in my family, there was no emotion shown. They were all hard nuts. Like 50cent said: "Show no love, love will get you killed."'

Fury fought back from his addiction problems to make his boxing comeback in 2018, before triumphing over Deontay Wilder in a sensational heavyweight trilogy against the big-hitting American - where he won the WBC title.

The Gypsy King sought to unify the heavyweight division against the all-conquering Oleksandr Usyk, but twice fell short in a pair of thrilling contests against the Ukrainian.

Netflix cameras have documented the lives of the Fury family since 2023. The latest series centred on Fury's decision to come out of retirement, plus the family's move from Morecambe to the Isle of Wight.

The streaming giant will broadcast Fury's mega-fight against Anthony Joshua in Cardiff on December 11.

Sports.title: Former Chelsea star Marc Cucurella's WAG narrowly avoids being caught in Spain's deadly train crash which has killed at least 68
Sports.content:
Former Chelsea star Marc Cucurella's WAG narrowly avoids being caught in Spain's deadly train crash which has killed at least 68

Marc Cucurella's partner Claudia Rodriguez admitted that she was in 'shock' after revealing that she was on the train that followed Spain's deadly crash which has already claimed 68 lives.

The horrifying high-speed rail accident saw one train strike another, stationary, train on the outskirts of Toledo amid a failure to communicate about the obstruction from central command.

The country has been plunged into mourning as the death toll rises, with at least a further 100 people suffering injuries in the wake of the crash.

Many high-profile footballers in Spain and abroad have shared their sympathies in the aftermath, but Claudia Rodriguez shared hers as she revealed how close she came to travelling on the line that day.

In a story posted on Instagram, the long-time girlfriend of the Real Madrid star claimed that she had been 'on the way to Malaga on the train behind', offering all of her 'support to the victims' families and friends'.

'Guys I'm fine, my train hasn't been affected at all because there was a lot of distance from the train that has suffered the accident,' she explained in a longer post.

'We just had to turn around and go back to Madrid since it was the same route.

Marc Cucurella's partner Claudia Rodriguez revealed that she had been on the train behind the one involved in Spain's fatal crash

Their family moved to Madrid following the defender's summer transfer from Chelsea (Source: Instagram/Claudia Rodriguez)

Spain has been plunged into three days of official warning after the horrifying crash which saw a high-speed train collide with a stationary one

'I was removed from everything. To think that if it happened later it would have happened to my train but please, nothing compared to what the people who did go on that train would have happened (heart emoji) All my strength again for those families (prayer hands emoji).'

Rodriguez went on to share her support for a call to give blood in Madrid, where her family is now based following their move from Chelsea over the summer.

The Spanish Football Federation confirmed that 24 Copa del Rey matches would be postponed this week as a 'mark of respect' after the crash.

A number of LaLiga sides had been due to play on Wednesday evening, with revised dates and times for the fixtures planned by the RFEF.

'The entire Spanish football community stands united in grief over this tragedy and has made itself available to the authorities to assist the victims of this devastating accident,' a statement from the federation added.

Three days of official mourning have begun in the country just months after the year's first fatal train crash which, like the most recent, involved a collision between one high-speed Renfe train and another from rival rail operator Iryo.

More than 540 people were travelling on the two trains when the force of the crash sent two carriages skidding down a nearby slope, amplifying the damage. The crash is believed to rank as one of the most fatal in the country's history of railways.

Among the footballers to share thoughtful messages of support in a challenging time was Ballon d'Or candidate Lamine Yamal.

'My solidarity and support to all the families of the victims and those affected by the Urda disaster,' he shared. 'All support and strength to everyone.'

Sports.title: Hero driver who bravely dragged British rival from horror fireball crash opens up on their unique friendship... and reveals he was gifted a Rolex as a thank you for 'giving me more time'
Sports.content:
Almost two months on from British driver Ollie Millroy's miraculous rescue from a fireball crash, he's opened up on the horrific incident with the hero who saved him.

Millroy, 36, had been racing in a China GT event at Shanghai International Circuit in September when two cars smashed into his Ferrari while navigating a bend.

In video footage of the incident, Millroy's vehicle was seen spiralling off the track while aggressive flames and huge plumes of smoke billowed above it.

Rival Dutch driver Loek Hartog, 23, pulled up beside the wreckage, jumped out and tried to free the stricken driver before scrambling to find a fire extinguisher to put out the blaze. Hartog and track staff pulled Millroy away from the fireball, saving his life.

Millroy, who is married to wife Fern with three children, broke his hand, five ribs and severely damaged his lungs but Hartog's quick thinking and bravery prevented the horrific accident from being fatal.

Millroy and Hartog have met three times since the incident and the Brit even surprised his rescuer at his birthday party, giving him a special Rolex watch engraved with the words: 'Thank you Loek.'

Ollie Millroy (left) gave his rescuer, Loek Hartog (right) an engraved Rolex watch

A British driver almost lost his life after a horrific crash China GT event sent his vehicle up in flames but Hartog saved him

Hartog told The Guardian: 'It was really special and they gave me a very special gift, because I gave them more time.'

He explained how he felt in the hours after hauling Millroy from the wreckage, adding: 'That was really emotional for me. I couldn’t sleep because I was overloaded and then Wiep, my partner, sent me a picture of Fern, the kids and Ollie at Disneyland. She was like: "You did it for them". That really struck me.

'Lots of people told me the marshals are not allowed to cross the guardrails on their own, which makes total sense on paper. But once something like this happens in front of you, I cannot believe you’re telling people to go against their feeling.

'If your gut tells you to do something, it should be your cue to act. We should mandate rules that are more human.'

Understandably, the gratitude felt by Millroy and his family is boundless, with the Brit adding: 'Thank you again Loek and don’t change. I know you won’t. This is in your nature and you’re an inspiration to all of us in sport and life in general. Fern and I now think about life differently because you really put everything into perspective.'

Millroy and Hartog shared the pictures of the Rolex watch gift on Instagram, with Hartog writing: 'Ollie and I met in circumstances neither of us could ever have imagined. One day after my birthday, he and Fern secretly flew from Dubai to Amsterdam, completely surprised me with lunch, and we spent the afternoon catching up on everything that has happened since and, more importantly, talking about what we can actually do with it all going forward.

'Somewhere along the way, Ollie, Fern, Wiep and I also just became friends. And then, as if them being there wasn’t enough, they gave me this.

'I still don’t really have the right reaction for someone handing me a Rolex across a table. I hope the first photo says enough. It is an incredibly special gift that I’ll keep and cherish forever.

The watch was given to the Dutch driver by Millroy after he flew out to surprise him

Millroy, pictured with his wife Fern, has three children and came so close to losing his life

'But the thing I’m probably most grateful for is something you can’t really photograph. On 5 September, Ollie was somebody I barely knew. Then we were sitting together in Amsterdam talking like we know each other for years. Life is weird. In this case, in a pretty beautiful way.'

Millroy is still recovering and in significant discomfort, so much so that he can't sleep, having tried to wean himself off heavier pain killers.

But the crash has not deterred the Brit from wanting to race again or encouraging his son Mylo to pursue his passion, having already started competing in karting.

In the aftermath of the crash, Millroy emotionally reflected on Hartog's heroism from his hospital bed, writing: 'I am still alive entirely thanks to one man. Loek Hartog stopped instantly with no flag marshals or fire crews in sight, and risked his own life to get me out of the car.

'I don't remember anything between 30 seconds before the crash and 1 hour after it, but I will remember his incredible act of bravery for the rest of my life.

'One day I will tell our three kids this story and Loek will be the biggest superhero in history in their eyes too.

'I'm laying here tonight with 5 broken ribs, broken collar bone, broken hand and finger and a bruised lung, but it could have been much worse.

Millroy's wife was amazed to see him alive after his fireball crash in Shanghai

'Thank you Loek. I owe you my life for your selfless act today.'

Hartog, meanwhile, posted on his own social media: 'When I saw a car turning into a huge fireball far ahead, there wasn't really a decision to make.

'From what I had seen, I genuinely believed the driver might not be able to get out by himself. I stopped, got out and went towards the car. There was never a moment of doubt.

'It was scary. There were moments where I didn't know I would actually be able to get Ollie out. But this isn't about what I did, and I'm sure many people in the same position would have reacted exactly the same way.'

Millroy's wife Fern added: 'I still can't believe he's alive, purely down to our real life superhero Loek Hartog.'

Sports.title: Carlos Tevez reveals he 'wanted to kill Gary Neville' in new claims about Sir Alex Ferguson breaking a promise - and sparking his infamous move to Man City from Man United
Sports.content:
Former Manchester United forward Carlos Tevez has claimed Sir Alex Ferguson broke a promise to him before he left the club to join arch rivals Manchester City - and that the fallout of his move had made him 'want to kill' Gary Neville.

Tevez infamously made the switch from United, where he was on loan, to City in 2009. He would go on to win the Premier League for a third time, and hold a banner reading 'RIP Fergie' during the 2012 title celebrations.

The former forward would later try and explain his actions, but has now revealed that Ferguson is responsible for the reason why he left the club.

Tevez was appearing on the Rio Ferdinand Presents channel, and said: 'They spoke to me (before) the two-year loan. After, if you play well, (we) pay the contract after one year.

'Fergie told me, “Carlos, now I'm going to pay out your contract and you're going to stay in Manchester". The team went to a pre-season. I remember this conversation with Fergie. He said “I’m going to pay for Berbatov but you, don't worry, I'm going to buy you and we'll do your contract.'

That didn't transpire, though, and United refused to pay the fee that would have his deal made permanent. He stayed at the club for another year before leaving.

Carlos Tevez (left) has suggested a broken promise from Sir Alex Ferguson (right) led to his Manchester United departure

The Argentine star notoriously held up a banner proclaiming 'RIP Fergie' after winning the title

The move also brought conflict between Tevez and his former United team-mate Gary Neville

'For me, the people understand,' Tevez said of the United fans, who have been split on their view of him since he departed. 'They don’t understand about Fergie speaking to me, or behind the scenes. What happened between Fergie and me, I think people don't understand that.'

He added: 'I think that Ferguson had, from the day we talked, up to six months to keep his word. And he didn't. On the contrary, he started leaving me on the bench. In my head, he started pushing me aside so he could bring down what I was worth. And that's what hurt me the most.'

The move across town, despite Man City's then-status as the under-achieving neighbours, ruffled feathers at his former club, with Tevez recollecting that one former team-mate - Neville - was especially critical.

'We went to play against you - you wanted to kill Gary Neville?' Ferdinand recalled, with Tevez agreeing that he had 'wanted to fight'.

Another opponent who felt his ire during that first ire was Rafael, but as Tevez noted, he was just 'aggressive (and) young'.

'But it is on the pitch,' he stressed. 'Gary Neville, in the press.'

Ferdinand recalled that he had seen Tevez's anger at the defender 'in his eyes' after believing that Neville had been 'speaking too much' about his former team-mate's departure.

'Gary, he said that I didn't respect Ferguson,' Tevez added. 'He didn't understand me. He didn't understand the situation.'

Amid the lingering bad blood, Ferdinand also noted that the situation had 'killed' Man United.

Tevez would leave United for arch rivals Manchester City in 2009 and win another league title

While the club would go on to win the Premier League title at the end of the 2012-13 season, they have not won the league since.

But it seems Tevez, who is now a manager and was most recently in charge of Talleres in his native Argentina, still has a soft spot for the Red Devils, despite all that went on after his departure.

'For me it was hard, Rio,' he added. 'It was hard because I felt like I'd given my heart to United. And I didn't feel the same.

'I didn't feel the same because, if you remember, we won the Champions League. We won the league and, and then, to bring down my price, they brought in a player and I carried on the same way for the first months. The second months, let's say, of the second year. But by the second, the second month, I didn't want to know any more.'

He added: 'I had a great time at United. The other team, City, for me, was like a revenge. I didn't get back what I gave.'

Sports.title: Vincent Kompany is discharged from hospital as Bayern Munich reveal manager's 'meningeal irritation' diagnosis after 'dislocating his shoulder' in collapse at training ground
Sports.content:
Vincent Kompany is discharged from hospital as Bayern Munich reveal manager's 'meningeal irritation' diagnosis after 'dislocating his shoulder' in collapse at training ground

Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany has been discharged from hospital as the club revealed a meningeal irritation was the cause of his collapse at their training ground last week.

The Manchester City legend has been absent from the touchline since taking charge of Bayern's Champions League draw against Arsenal last week, after collapsing at the training ground five days ago.

Bayern sporting director Max Eberl provided an update on Kompany's health to German television ahead of their DFB-Pokal tie against Magdeburg.

Eberl revealed Kompany has now been discharged from hospital to continue his recovery at home and that doctors had identified the cause of his collapse.

'I think that's the biggest and best news for all of us,' Eberl told ARD.

'They have found what it is, it is meningeal irritation that caused this incident last Friday.

Bayern Munich have confirmed meningitis was the cause of Vincent Kompany's collapse after he was discharged from hospital

'But he was allowed to go home now and can do his rehab there.

'For him, rehab means rest and medication. And then I'm very, very sure that he'll be back on the sidelines at 100 percent very soon.'

If left untreated meningeal irritation can become meningitis.

The meninges are the membranes around the brain and spinal cord.

BILD had reported earlier in the day that doctors had earlier ruled out significant conditions including a heart attack or stroke as being behind his collapse last week.

The German outlet had reported that Kompany suffered a dislocated shoulder when he collapsed while watching Bayern's Under-23 side and reportedly suffered from seizures.

The 40-year-old was then quickly airlifted to hospital via rescue ambulance.

Early reports suggested that Kompany was recovering from a viral infection that caused problems with old scar tissue in his hip, leaving him in pain and with difficulties climbing stairs.

There had also been some concern over Kompany's 'workaholic' work ethic from club insiders, with some thought to be worried that he was getting too little sleep.

Kompany will continue his recovery at home and is expected to remain off work for weeks

Other concerns included irregular eating habits, and that he has been barely exercising, drinking excessive amounts of coffee, and taking on too much work.

Eberl, however, reiterated that Kompany's illness had been the cause of his collapse rather than his workload.

'This is an illness, and that must be kept completely separate,' Eberl said.

'This has nothing to do with the pressure we face in the Bundesliga.'

Bayern have reiterated that Kompany will be given the time he needs to recover with his assistant Aaron Danks taking charge of the first team in the meantime.

Danks worked as Kompany's assistant at Anderlecht before deputising for Dean Smith and Steven Gerrard at Aston Villa and Michael Carrick at Middlesbrough.

He then reunited with Kompany at Bayern and is shouldering the responsibility at one of the world's biggest clubs until the manager is fit to return, which could still be weeks.

Without Kompany at the helm, Danks will oversee fixtures against Borussia Dortmund, Atletico Madrid and Mainz.

But the Bundesliga serial champions have started the season strong and sit at the summit of the domestic top flight.

Shortly after winning the Ballon d'Or, Kompany's player Harry Kane was optimistic when he stressed that his manager was 'on the mend'.

Kane said: 'He actually phoned me, phoned me bright and early at 9am (Monday). I was just out of bed thankfully, so I was able to answer it. But no, he just wanted to wish me all the best, good luck.

'I asked him how he was doing, he said he feels good, he feels like he's on the mend. I know he's the type of character who just wants to be back with the team already.

'He wants to be out on the training field with us, on the bench with us. But it's important that he rests, you know? He's been going through a bit of a tough time with his health recently, and we can hopefully cover it, the staff can cover it.

'Obviously, he's not there, but, you know, it will be massive for me to go back to Munich and see him, all the staff, all my team-mates. I've spoken about how much this [award] is theirs as well as it is mine. So just to celebrate them a little bit will be special.'

Sports.title: 'Bournemouth is incredible - in summer it feels like I'm back in Brazil!': EVANILSON on taking down Man United and AC Milan, Marco Rose's 'high expectations', leaving home at 13 and drawing his late mother every day
Sports.content:
'Bournemouth is incredible - in summer it feels like I'm back in Brazil!': EVANILSON on taking down Man United and AC Milan, Marco Rose's 'high expectations', leaving home at 13 and drawing his late mother every day

A storm was swirling around Old Trafford, Senne Lammens had been left behind and the angle had all but closed.

Evanilson has been drawing perfect lines since he was a child in Fortaleza in Brazil’s Northeast region, pausing cartoons on the television to copy them on to paper. Last Sunday he drew one more – arcing violently into the Manchester United net.

'When I thought about going past the goalkeeper, I just took a chance,' he tells Daily Mail Sport. 'It was very windy, too. Maybe the wind helped, but I went for the perfect angle there. I managed to score that goal, which was very difficult, but it was beautiful.'

The goal in question capped a 3-0 win, Bournemouth's fourth in a row without conceding and the third time in four seasons they’d won at Old Trafford by that scoreline. Three days earlier, Evanilson's flicked header led to the penalty that kickstarted a 3-0 win over AC Milan in the Europa League.

In 2008, Bournemouth began a season in the fourth tier with a 17-point deduction. Now they are in Europe for the first time, at a stadium that holds about 12,400, in red and black stripes borrowed from Milan more than 50 years ago.

'For our club, for all the players, beating two world giants is always very special,' says Evanilson, 27. 'A very important week for us. I think we're quite confident for the rest of the season. It helped us a lot.'

Evanilson goes around Manchester United goalkeeper Senne Lammens...

...arcs an audacious effort into the top corner to make it 3-0 to Bournemouth...

...and celebrates another milestone win for the club in what was surely the greatest week in its history

The strike at Old Trafford was Evanilson's fourth in five games, a week after his 100th career goal against Sunderland. Asked to give it a mark out of five, he goes further.

'For me, this is one of the most beautiful,' he says. 'Even more so because of the size of the game, against United, away from home, at Old Trafford. That pushes the score even higher.'

The week could get better still. Carlo Ancelotti names his Brazil squad on Thursday, and Evanilson, whose two caps for his country came in 2024, has never been called up by the Italian. With Chelsea No9 Joao Pedro injured, Brentford’s Igor Thiago out of form and Richarlison out of favour at Tottenham, will this be Evanilson’s time?

'Of course, I'm always thinking about the national team,’ he says. ‘I think it's the hunger of every player, to always be wearing the biggest shirt of all national teams. My expectation is high. I hope to be able to be there. If not, keep working, keep doing my part. Who knows, one day.'

Not long ago, a week like this looked a distant prospect. Andoni Iraola left in the summer after taking Bournemouth to sixth place and a first European qualification. His successor, Marco Rose, took seven league games to get his first win, after a 5-1 defeat at Chelsea on October 10 left his side 17th.

Under Rose, Evanilson presses from the front and has at times dropped behind another striker. He has four goals and four assists in 11 games in the Premier League and Europa League.

'For me, there's no such thing as a lost ball,' he says. 'I'm always running, making movements up front. I work for the team. The manager has fitted us well into this team, and now we know what he really wants from us. He wants mobility up front, he wants us to press high. It's no coincidence that we won these last four games, and won well, without conceding.'

Iraola, now at Liverpool, taught Evanilson about life in the Premier League after he joined for a club-record £40million from Porto two years ago.

Andoni Iraola, now at Liverpool, taught Evanilson about life in the Premier League after he joined for a club-record £40million from Porto two years ago

Marco Rose, Iraola's successor, has set Evanilson a target of 15 to 20 goals this season

Evanilson reacts to Justin Kluivert opening the scoring against AC Milan last week, kickstarting a historic 3-0 win for the Cherries

'He helped me a lot to adapt to English football, which is totally different,' says Evanilson. 'With this intensity, he helped me a lot with pressing, with making movements to try to break down my opponent. He's Spanish, and I don't speak fluent English, but he spoke to me in Spanish. I'm very grateful to him.'

Rose has needed time too.

'At the start it's always difficult, even for him, to adapt to English football,' Evanilson says. 'In some games he tells us to do certain things and we don't do them, and we suffer for it. He knows what he's doing, he plans the games very well, and the intensity on the pitch is also very similar to Iraola's. He trusts me a lot.'

The German has said Evanilson can score 15 to 20 goals this season, after 18 in his first two campaigns combined.

'The expectation he has is very high,' says Evanilson. 'I'm sure more chances will keep coming. I have to be there, I have to be focused to convert them.'

Evanilson’s compatriot Rayan also scored at Old Trafford, his first league goal of the season. The 20-year-old joined from Vasco da Gama in January in a deal worth an initial £24.7m and started for Brazil at the World Cup.

'I already knew the quality he had as a player, but I didn't know him as a person,' says Evanilson. 'He's an impeccable lad, a good guy. We're always together here at the club. He's a player with a lot of strength, explosiveness, and he also has that nose for goal. Since he arrived, I've tried to help him so he could adapt faster.'

At Porto, Evanilson was the one being helped. Having joined for around £8m in 2020 from Fluminense, he spent much of his first year in Portugal with the B team. Pepe, the former Real Madrid centre back, kept him going.

Legendary former Real Madrid centre back Pepe (centre) was the guiding light for Evanilson (left) when his Porto career took a while to get going

But eventually the striker found his place and scored 60 goals in 154 Porto appearances, earning him his move to the Premier League

'Love him, love him,' he says of Pepe. 'He was always talking to me. He'd say: "Calm down, your time will come, the coach really likes you." Sometimes I'd get sad. I'd been signed and I was playing for Porto B.'

Porto won the league and cup double the following season, and Evanilson scored 21 goals in all competitions. Two years later he was on his way to England.

Bournemouth is a very long way from home, but he had learned about distance long before, leaving Fortaleza for Fluminense in Rio de Janeiro – 1,600 miles and a day and a half’s drive away at the opposite tip of Brazil.

'It's very hard for us to leave the Northeast,' he says. 'When I left there at 13, I was a kid, I left on my own. Sometimes I wanted to go back.

'And my mother told me all the time: "If you want to be a footballer, you have to face reality, you have to keep going. You're a good player, but this part off the pitch, you have to overcome it."'

Jose Neto, the coach who took him to Rio, has said the boy promised to draw his mother, Madalena, every day to ease the homesickness. She died suddenly in 2017 when Evanilson was in the Fluminense youth academy, and he thought about giving up football.

'I'd like her to be living all of this that I've been through, from when I left Fortaleza to where I am now,' he says. 'I'm sure she's proud. The only thing I'd really like is for her to be able to be here, living it and watching me play in the Premier League.'

The drawing never stopped. These days he does it with his daughter, Maria Alice.

Bournemouth team-mate and compatriot Rayan has nailed down a place in the Brazil starting XI - now Evanilson wants to follow suit

Evanilson moved more than 1,600 miles from his home city of Fortaleza to join the Fluminense academy in Rio de Janeiro

'Whenever I'm at home with her, we try to do some drawing,' he says. 'It makes me relax, it makes me forget some problems. And it's really nice to know that she likes it too.'

Home in Bournemouth also means Ola Brasil, a small shop on Wimborne Road whose owner delivered rice, beans, chicken and farofa, a toasted cassava flour, to the family's hotel when they arrived.

'That food every Brazilian loves, when you go a while without eating it, you even feel weak,' he says.

It is the only place he can find Brazilian-style Maria biscuits.

'I always buy them,' he says. 'My one-year-old son only eats these Maria biscuits. He's crazy about them.'

He has always lived by the sea, in Fortaleza, Rio, Porto and now Dorset, where the water is a bit different.

‘It’s impossible to go in because of the cold water. Very, very cold,’ he says.

The sea he grew up with is in Brazil’s Northeast, a region of nine states along the Atlantic. Fortaleza, with about 2.6million people, is its biggest city. Evanilson still goes back with his family.

Evanilson has two Brazil caps to his name, and is hoping to win his first call-up under Carlo Ancelotti this week

‘In summer (Bournemouth) is incredible, it gets up to 35 degrees, and it’s nice. Sometimes, in summer, you can feel like you’re in Brazil, in our Northeast’

‘Our Northeast is incredible, very beautiful,’ he says. ‘Even though it’s very hot, it’s very beautiful, it’s perfect, it has beautiful beaches. I loved living there. Whenever I go to Fortaleza, I always want to be on the beach. Even the water temperature helps you relax.

‘The town here is very good too. In summer, it’s a really hot town. Lots of people from other cities in England come to spend the summer here. The beaches are always full, the streets packed, and the heat here is similar too.’

On the hottest days, the distance to his homeland shrinks.

‘In summer it’s incredible, it gets up to 35°C, and it’s nice. Sometimes, in summer, you can feel like you’re in Brazil, in our Northeast.’

Sports.title: Jordan Henderson smirks as he trolls Anfield boo-boys on return with Chelsea - and argues with ex-Liverpool team-mate Virgil van Dijk
Sports.content:
Jordan Henderson laughed off his haters on his return to Anfield on Wednesday night. Liverpool legend Henderson, 36, played the full 90 minutes of the Carabao Cup last-16 tie as Chelsea lost 6-5 on penalties, although the veteran did score his spot kick. It capped what must have been a strange night for the midfielder as he went back to the club where he made 492 appearances and won eight trophies over a 12-year period. Henderson left to join Saudi Arabian side Al-Ettifaq in the summer of 2023. Despite his long service, Henderson received a vociferous reception as a Chelsea player, with the home faithful booing him every time he touched the ball. And, after the Blues were awarded a penalty in the first half when Ryan Gravenberch fouled Moises Caicedo, that atmosphere escalated further. Henderson picked up the ball and walked towards the penalty spot as if he was going to take the spot kick. Hendo smirking at Liverpool fans in a Chelsea shirt. Never thought we'd see the daypic.twitter.com/Fac2gSbe5x — Dom✨ (@footy_road) October 28, 2026 Jordan Henderson was seen smirking after receiving a hostile reception from Liverpool fans The former Liverpool captain also argued with his former team-mate Virgil van Dijk at one point As he did so, Henderson was loudly jeered and he allowed himself a wry smile and laugh as he looked back towards the crowd. Henderson ultimately handed the ball over to Morgan Rogers, who made no mistake from the spot. The hostile reception may have been in part motivated by the midfielder's desire to contest several decisions with Liverpool's players and referee Darren England, along with the fact he is now representing Chelsea. At one point early in the first half, both Henderson and his former team-mate Virgil van Dijk fought their case in one discussion with England. As they walked away, the pair shouted at each other from afar in what must have been a strange sight for Liverpool supporters to witness. Henderson did later appear to applaud the crowd after the game when he was also seen laughing and joking with van Dijk. Meanwhile, at the end of last season, Henderson, who has similarly played for Ajax and Brentford in recent years, returned to Anfield for the first time with the Bees. On that occasion, he received a warm reception and then a standing ovation when he was substituted in the second half. Speaking after that game, he wrote on social media: 'I'd like to thank the Liverpool fans for the reception they gave me yesterday. 'It meant a lot to me going back to Anfield and being able to say thank you for everything you gave me in my 12 years at the club. It's a feeling that I'll never forget. 'To be able to be there to see my two brothers, Mo [Salah] and Robbo [Andy Robertson], say goodbye and get the send-off they deserve was also special. 'We spent some amazing times together that I will cherish forever. I wish you both all the very best in your next chapters.'

Sports.title: Ballon d'Or 2026 RESULTS: Harry Kane wins big award as top 10 announced after controversy
Sports.content:
Harry Kane was crowned the best player in the world on Monday evening as he won the Ballon d'Or at a star-studded ceremony in London

England captain Harry Kane has been crowned the world’s best footballer at the 2026 Ballon d’Or awards.

The eyes of the footballing world descended on the West End tonight as the London Palladium hosted the prestigious ceremony.

And Three Lions and Bayern Munich striker Kane won the top award, becoming the first English player since Michael Owen in 2001 to do so.

Former Tottenham forward Kane said: “I am almost speechless. Being here in London has made it extra special.

“Made it a good omen for me tonight. Thank you to everyone who voted for me. I can imagine it was tough this year.”

Kane spearheaded Bayern's Bundesliga title and England's run to the World Cup semi-final in North America, and beat off competition from the likes of France forward Kylian Mbappe and Spain youngster Lamine Yamal to win the award.

London City Lionesses and Spain star Alexia Putellas, meanwhile, won the women's prize.

Sports.title: Sir Kevin Sinfield surprised by Rob Burrow's children after being left 'grumpy'
Sports.content:
Sir Kevin Sinfield surprised by Rob Burrow's children after being left 'grumpy'

Sir Kevin Sinfield received a reality check while raising money in honour of the late Rob Burrow

View 3 Images Sir Kevin Sinfield spoke movingly about Rob Burrow's children (Image: The Good, The Bad, The Rugby)

Sir Kevin Sinfield was left extremely emotional after completing yet another harsh charity run and feeling "grumpy." However, a surprise from Rob Burrow's children, along with their mother and Prince William, brought him right back to reality.

‌



‌



As he recalled the moment, the ex-rugby league star highlighted the courage and strength of his late friend's family as they continue life without Rob. Sinfield commended Burrow's children - Macy, 14, Maya, 10, and Jackson, seven - stating that they should never have had to handle the heartbreak of watching their dad succumb to motor neurone disease (MND) at just 41 years old.

‌



During an appearance on The Good, The Bad and The Rugby podcast, the ex-Leeds Rhinos star described a particularly gruelling charity run that took a lot of his strength.

‌



He had been anticipating nothing more than a hot bath following the finale of his 7-in-7 ultra-marathon challenge. However, he was informed he would need to wait five minutes before crossing the finish line.

Rob Burrow's dad Geoff passes away as tributes pour in for MND campaigner READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Sinfield, who has generated £13m through remarkable fundraising endeavours in tribute to Burrow, acknowledged he had grown weary and irritable as he got close to the end at Wakefield Trinity's ground and wasn't pleased about the postponement.

‌



But the explanation for the hold-up quickly emerged when he stepped onto the pitch and discovered the main stand filled with people waiting to greet him, led by the Burrow family. He explained: "All I want to do is get in a hot bath, right. It's rained and it's not been a great day. I'm tired, a bit grumpy.

"You can almost see the finish line and I'm sort of thinking about the bath. And then get a phone call saying, 'You've gotta wait five minutes.' I'm like, 'Wait five minutes, why? What's going on? What's happened? Why are we waiting five minutes, we're gonna be late.'"

‌



View 3 Images Sinfield raises money in honour of the late Rob Burrow (Image: George Wood/Getty Images)

Sinfield revealed his initial bewilderment upon reaching the stadium to find the usual welcoming party absent. He added: "Well we turned up at the ground and, typically, there's normally a few people outside to greet us. There's nobody there - 'What is going on?'

‌



"Then the guy who plans all our routes, Tristan - he's a top guy - comes running out from pitchside and says - because we've all stopped looking round because I know where the changing rooms are and I go to have my bath - And he says, 'You're in here!'

"And then I look up and I see - first of all, I saw Sally Nugent (BBC reporter), and then I saw Prince William and Princess Catherine. And then Rob's kids. And Rob's mum, sister. It couldn't have been a better combination of people."

‌



View 3 Images The former team-mates captured hearts across the nation (Image: George Wood/Getty Images)

Growing more emotional, Sinfield said: "Just a really, really nice moment for a whole host of reasons. But up until turning that corner, walking on the grass, yeah, I was a little bit grumpy.

Article continues below

"Saying, 'Who's made us late here?' Well yeah, we had a decent excuse and it couldn't have been a better combination of people. Clearly the royalty are massively important, but for Rob's kids to be there, it was pretty special. It shouldn't have been that way for them."

Sports.title: Would Man Utd benefit from having Roy Keane? Have your say as  ex-captain denied return
Sports.content:
Would Man Utd benefit from having Roy Keane? Have your say as ex-captain denied return

Roy Keane was earmarked by Ole Gunnar Solskjaer to be his No.2 had he returned to Manchester United in January - but he lost out to Michael Carrick

View Image Roy Keane left Man Utd in 2005 and has never returned

Roy Keane could've been sat in the Manchester United dugout had events turned out differently.

‌



‌



The Irishman was lined up to be Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's assistant had the Norwegian got the job on an interim basis in January. Instead Michael Carrick won that battle, excelled initially, got the job permanently and the rest is history.

‌



Keane continues to commentate from the sidelines, be that in the Sky Sports studio or on podcasts alongside Gary Neville. But for years the question has been asked as to whether such an elite leader, one of the club's greats, could bring something to the table in Manchester.

‌



A serial winner during his time at Old Trafford, Keane was perfect for his era. A driver of standards in a way few others were, and plenty feel this current squad need some home truths and someone to set the level.

Conversely, some feel that Keane's methods and take on the game hasn't moved on as much as it should to align with the modern day player. His values can be perceived as old school; he endured an acrimonious exit from the club in 2005 and he's ultimately not been a coach for a number of years - so would he prove an asset or a hindrance?

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso admits Carabao Cup 'least important tournament' as Chelsea lose at Liverpool
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso admits Carabao Cup 'least important tournament' as Chelsea lose at Liverpool

Chelsea's Carabao Cup hopes ended at Liverpool on Wednesday night but Xabi Alonso conceded it was their least important trophy of the season

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso didn't shy away from admitting the Carabao Cup was the least of his priorities

Xabi Alonso openly admitted the Carabao Cup was the "least important competition" for Chelsea after they were dumped out in the fourth round.

‌



‌



The Blues headed to Anfield and, after the game finished 1-1 after 90 minutes, were beaten on penalties. Wesley Fofana was the man to miss in sudden death as the defender blazed his effort into the Kop.

‌



It ends Chelsea's first chance of landing silverware this season, but Alonso appeared unbothered by the opportunity passing them by and was open enough to admit that the Carabao Cup was the least desirable of the tournaments available to him.

‌



There's no doubt that the competition carries the least prestige and top teams can often juggle their line-ups to rest players in a way they wouldn't even in an FA Cup encounter. However, managers do usually emphasise their desire to win every trophy on offer, but Alonso told his team to "move on" after his honest admission.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



He said: “It’s a small setback in this competition. It’s probably the least important competition for us in the year, so we need to move on. And as soon as we leave Anfield, our focus is Saturday’s Premier League [game]. This is the main and the most important thing.”

Alonso never won the Carabao Cup, which has gone through a host of name changes, during his time as a player in England. Chelsea themselves have only won the competition on five occasions, the last of those coming more than a decade ago in 2015 back when Jose Mourinho was manager.

‌



Alonso is still looking for consistency as Chelsea boss having started with a bang, only to see that momentum die off. At the weekend they suffered a rare home defeat to Tottenham, who secured only their second win in the league this season.

View 2 Images Wesley Fofana's missed penalty settled the shootout

‌



As a result Alonso, was looking for a reaction from his side and, despite their loss, he believes he got the desired performance. “Well for sure the outcome is not what we wanted. It is not what we expected before the game," he said. "You know once you reach the penalties, there's going to be a sad side. This is us in that case.

“But I would say that the game we have played to a very good competitive level, good performance. We showed an improvement, I would say. That's what we wanted."

Sports.title: 'I had to resuscitate a burglar I caught in my house - I nearly killed him'
Sports.content:
'I had to resuscitate a burglar I caught in my house - I nearly killed him'

The famous Premier League hardman had quite the welcome for a burglar who entered his home

View 2 Images Duncan Ferguson opened up about a terrifying ordeal he once experienced (Image: YouTube/The Overlap)

Few players in Premier League history struck fear into opponents quite like Duncan Ferguson - and one unlucky intruder learned that reality the hard way.

As two of Ferguson's old clubs, Everton and Newcastle, prepare to square off in the Carabao Cup on Thursday night, the current Glentoran boss has lifted the lid on the night his fearsome reputation almost took an irreversible turn.

Two intruders broke into the Scottish striker's home in January 2001 whilst his wife and six-month-old daughter were inside and one encountered the full fury of the Toffees icon. He has disclosed that the confrontation ended with him performing CPR on the burglar, terrified that he had killed the individual.

Ferguson, who was 29 at the time, recounted the chilling encounter with one of the two intruders on the BBC podcast Tony Bellew Is Angry. He claimed: "I'm lying on the couch. I heard something. I put my trainers on. I had no top on, I was ripped back then and I could see two shadows coming through the conservatory. I was quite calm.

Michael Carrick could be sacked within hours if Man Utd board follow regular blueprint READ MORE :

"I unloaded, I really did. I really followed in to the point where I thought I'd killed him, I really did. I had to try and resuscitate him then. So you go from a point of unloading on the fella to helping him. It happened in a matter of seconds."

The perpetrators behind the break-in, Michael Pratt and Barry Dawson, admitted their guilt and were handed 15-month prison sentences. Dawson required three days of hospital treatment following injuries inflicted by Ferguson.

The pair had tried to make off with bottles of champagne, a framed picture and CDs. Judge Anthony Procter told Dawson and Pratt at their sentencing: "There is no way you can be called hardened criminals but we are dealing with a burglary at night when the house was occupied.

"Mr Ferguson may give the impression of being a hard man, but it is clear he was shaken by this incident, primarily for the effects on his wife and young child."

Despite listing the property for sale following the frightening ordeal, Ferguson faced a second attempted burglary at his £2million Formby residence two years on.

Sports.title: Liverpool dump out Chelsea on penalties as former favourites face up to new realities
Sports.content:
Liverpool dump out Chelsea on penalties as former favourites face up to new realities

LIVERPOOL 1-1 (Pens: 6-5) CHELSEA: The two Premier League heavyweights couldn't be separated after 90 minutes with Wesley Fofana missing the decisive spot kick

View 4 Images Liverpool got the better of Chelsea on penalties

Liverpool knocked Chelsea out of the Carabao Cup on penalties with Wesley Fofana missing the decisive spot kick in sudden death.

‌



‌



Valentin Barco was the first man to miss in the shootout and his miss presented Kostas Tsimikas with the chance to put the Reds through, but he blazed his effort into the Kop. Jordan Henderson would score the tenth penalty on his return to Anfield to send it into sudden death.

‌



Ryan Gravenberch and Emanuel Emegha missed successive penalties, the latter having the chance to send Chelsea into the next round. But it was Chelsea defender Fofana who fired over, leading to huge celebrations at Anfield.

‌



It was a night of spot kicks with Morgan Rogers opening the scoring in front of the travelling fans, but the Chelsea lead would last a matter of minutes before Liverpool themselves were awarded a penalty. Cody Gakpo scoring emphatically just before half-time.

The Reds went into the shootout having lost their last two, which had major consequences. One of those against Crystal Palace in the Community Shield and the other against PSG in the Champions League.

Andoni Iraola made six changes to his team, but gradually drip fed his quality from the bench. Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola all emerging in the second-half.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



The opening goal of the game came courtesy of a penalty, which was awarded following a reckless challenge from Ryan Gravenberch on Moises Caicedo. Ex-Red Jordan Henderson held the ball for long periods as huge jeers rained down from the Anfield crowd, but he handed it off to Rogers, who confidently converted.

Chelsea's lead though only last three minutes as a Wesley Fofana handball from a corner presented Liverpool with the chance to level. Gakpo scoring in front of the Kop.

‌



Bar the two strikes from the spot in was a first-half lacking in goal mouth action, with neither goalkeeper being regularly called into action.

Wirtz began the evening on the bench but with the game still in the balance Iraola turned to the German just before the hour mark. Mike Penders produced a huge save to deny a Ronald Araujo header, with Rogers racing up the opposite side of the pitch seconds later, only to see his effort blocked.

‌



View 4 Images Wesley Fofana fired into the stands in sudden death

The Chelsea record signing was instrumental in creating a change for Marco Palestra, but the full-back's effort was well saved by Giorgi Mamardashvili. Not long after and a huge block from Levi Colwill denied Wirtz from close range, but neither side was able to find the goal that would've decided the game inside 90 minutes.

‌



REDS ON A ROLL

Liverpool have now enjoyed five wins on the bounce dating back to their Manchester City loss with Iraola looking like he's getting on a roll after his summer switch.

In that time the Merseysiders have shown all sides to them - they quashed the Brighton momentum at the weekend, overcame the challenge that is Brentford away and showcased their powers of recovery against Villarreal in the Champions League.

‌



Getting the better of Chelsea is their latest scalp, and even if the Blues are by no means the side of old, they are still a rival who needed to be dispatched if Liverpool wanted to keep alive their hopes of winning the season's first trophy - which they have done.

View 4 Images Morgan Rogers opened the scoring on the night from the spot

‌



Given Iraola's exploits at Bournemouth plenty was expected, but it has been a slower start than he perhaps would've liked. Nothing quite keeps people happy or builds confidence like winning games and Liverpool are getting into good habits.

HENDO'S FROSTY RETURN

He was the man who captained Liverpool to their first ever Premier League title, completing a comeback from a man who was once deemed surplus to requirement to one who would lead one of their greatest teams. And yet Henderson still felt the backlash from those who once chanted his name.

‌



The midfielder returned to English football with Brentford, but few would've thought at his age that a move to a heavyweight club remained on the cards. Still, Chelsea came calling in the summer.

Henderson enjoyed a sensational period at Anfield under Klopp, also winning the Champions League, but his decision to leave for Saudi Arabia back in 2023 certainly didn't sit well with everyone. This was a player who championed certain causes, which weren't even legal in the Middle East, and there was clearly a financial motive behind his move.

‌



View 4 Images Cody Gakpo levelled shortly before half-time

His reception at Liverpool serves as a reminder that no player's legacy is guaranteed by what they do whilst playing for a club. How they choose to leave and where they go next can often prove defining.

‌



REDS IN BLUE

In a different world perhaps Caicedo and Romeo Lavia would both be playing for Liverpool. But in the summer of 2023 both men, who had been on Jurgen Klopp's radar, chose to move to Stamford Bridge.

The Reds actually had a then British-record bid accepted by Brighton as they looked to go after Caicedo, having also been linked with Lavia, then at Southampton, for much of the summer. Caicedo made it known he wanted to move to Chelsea, and eventually got his wish.

‌



Liverpool were denied the chance to pivot to Lavia with Chelsea, in the midst of another major spending spree, signed him too. Injuries have plagued Lavia but he's finally fit and Caicedo has shown that he's been worth the money. The two lined up in midfield together against Liverpool, who had youngster Trey Nyoni and Gravenberch to oppose them.

Caicedo's well-timed run into the box saw him scythed down by Gravenberch, which led to the opening goal, but it wasn't a night where you thought the two midfields were £140m apart.

Sports.title: Roy Keane denied Man Utd return by Michael Carrick call as role lined up for ex-captain
Sports.content:
Roy Keane denied Man Utd return by Michael Carrick call as role lined up for ex-captain

Roy Keane could've landed back at Manchester United if Ole Gunnar Solskjaer had been named as interim boss, with the Irishman lined up as his assistant

View 2 Images Roy Keane was in line to be Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's assistant if the Norwegian took charge in Manchester (Image: Dave Shopland/Shutterstock)

Roy Keane could've secured a return to Manchester United had they overlooked Michael Carrick at the start of the year.

‌



‌



Carrick was up against Ole Gunnar Solskjaer as the Old Trafford hierarchy looked to fill the void left by Ruben Amorim's departure in January. Carrick had worked under Solskjaer during his stint at the club.

‌



And it was the ex-Middlesbrough boss who got the nod, but had Solskjaer been given the gig then he would've looked to bring in Keane as his assistant, according to The Sun.

‌



During Solskjaer's previous spell in charge of United, he had Mike Phelan his assistant, but remained close with Keane and has made no secret of his admiration for him and his opinions. He previously said: “I keep in touch with Roy and have been at his house for a cup of tea. I always listen to Roy and his opinions. I value them very highly. I know Roy did an interview saying there are many people that claim to be his friends."

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Keane managed Sunderland and Ipswich but has also spent time as a No.2, working underneath Martin O’Neill at Ireland and Nottingham Forest and with Paul Lambert at Aston Villa.

The Irishman won seven Premier League titles, four FA Cups and the Champions League in a 12-year spell at Old Trafford, but endured a high-profile exit in late 2005 following a clash with Sir Alex Ferguson. Keane has previously commented that the Scot's presence at the club may hamper any return.

‌



Carrick ultimately won the race to lead United last term and his stunning interim spell saw him land the job on a permanent basis, keeping ex-England coach Steve Holland as his main lieutenant.

View 2 Images Roy Keane and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer have retained a strong bond (Image: Instagram/ Roy Keane)

‌



Keane had been critical of Carrick's appointment when it first happened and said on the Stick To Football podcast: "His wife can always come in [if Carrick doesn't do well], cause she's got a bit of a big mouth sometimes. She's probably doing the team talk."

The comment stemmed from a feud in 2014, when Keane criticised Carrick's performance in a Champions League defeat to Olympiacos.

Carrick's wife Lisa Roughhead posted on Twitter: "Roy Keane what a ****, says anything to provoke a reaction." She later deleted the tweet and posted an apology.
