Sports.title: F1 newcomers Tsolov, Mini and Slater among eight drivers to run in practice on Friday | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Eight teams will give practice outings to inexperienced drivers at this weekend’s Mexican Grand Prix.

Three of them – Red Bull junior driver Nikola Tsolov, Alpine’s Gabriele Mini and Audi’s Freddie Slater – will make their debuts in an official F1 test session. Tsolov will drive for Red Bull’s second F1 team, Racing Bulls.

Teams must give four opportunities to inexperienced drivers – two in each of their cars – in first practice sessions over the course of the year.

Among the others driving this weekend is Luke Browning. Williams has entered him for a fifth session this year after he completed no laps when he appeared for them at the Circuit de Catalunya.

Also in action this weekend are Leonardo Fornaroli and Jak Crawford, making their fourth appearances for McLaren and Aston Martin respectively. McLaren recently confirmed Fornaroli, the 2025 Formula 2 champion, will drive for its new WEC Hypercar team.

Ayumu Iwasa will also make his fourth appearance this year, and third for Red Bull. He has also previously driven for Racing Bulls. Ryo Hirakawa will appear for the third time in a Haas this season.

More than half the teams will have completed their obligation to run drivers on four occasions after next week’s Brazilian Grand Prix. Unlike in previous years, none of the remaining rounds are sprint events, meaning they theoretically have more opportunities to run their junior drivers. But with doubt continuing to hang over whether the final races in the Middle East will go ahead, teams appear to be ensuring they do not fail to fulfil their practice quotas should they be cancelled.

Sports.title: New contract to keep Perez racing for Cadillac until at least 2029 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Cadillac has announced a new contract with Sergio Perez, days before he starts his 300th grand prix at home in Mexico.

Perez will remain at the team until at least 2029 under his new, long-term deal.

He joined the F1 newcomers last year ahead of their debut this season.

“Building a competitive team in F1 is a long-term journey, and securing Checo’s talent and leadership gives us the continuity and commitment we need to build on the strong foundation established in our first year,” said CEO Dan Towriss. “Together, we are focused on the next phase of our journey, pushing the team forward and making progress up the grid.”

Cadillac is yet to confirm the identity of Perez’s team mate for next year. The team are yet to score a point, Perez having achieved a best finish of 14th, current team mate Valtteri Bottas 13th.

“Building a Formula 1 team from the ground up takes time, relentless work and patience, but the progress we are making together is incredibly rewarding,” said Perez. “There is still a lot of work ahead of us and I am fully committed for the next three years.”

Perez has experienced disappointment with multi-year contracts before. In 2019 he agreed a three-year deal to stay at Lawrence Stroll’s Racing Point team, before it became Aston Martin. However Stroll dropped Perez at the end of the following season and replaced him with Sebastian Vettel.

During his fourth year at Red Bull the team extended his contract by two years, then dropped him at the end of the season. He sat out the 2025 campaign before returning to F1 with Cadillac.

Sports.title: Antonelli’s coronation, Mexico’s optional turn one and more Mexican GP talking points | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The world championship outcome may be a foregone conclusion but there are plenty of other talking points of note at this weekend’s Mexican Grand Prix.

All over bar the shouting

There could hardly be less doubt over the destination of this year’s world drivers’ championship. Yes, theoretically there are still three drivers in the hunt, but the two who aren’t Andrea Kimi Antonelli realistically need him not to score in the next four consecutive races to still be in with a shot come the final round.

On top of that, consider that at least one of the remaining rounds might not go ahead anyway. In which case even this flimsy conjecture is moot, and the championship is already Antonelli’s.

But if, as seems almost certain, he does win the title this weekend, what a venue to do it at. If the remodelled Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez has one thing going for it, it’s the joyous theatre of F1 fever which greets drivers in the stadium at the end of the race.

Optional turn one

The opening trio of corners on the Mexico City track has been a trouble spot since Hermann Tilke’s designers reworked the layout for the race’s return in 2015. The tight corner configuration and generous run-off area make it easy for drivers to abuse track limits at this point on the track.

Last year’s start was a particularly egregious example as multiple drivers arguably benefitted from cutting the corner. Max Verstappen’s approach to it gave every indication he never intended to stay within the track’s boundaries.

Will race control take note and put stricter measures in place? There was little sign this was a priority in Austin last weekend, where track limits have long been a problem.

Debutants Slater and Mini join the rookies

At least two drivers will make their debuts in an F1 practice session this weekend. Audi’s promising rookie Freddie Slater, who finished second in Formula 3 this year, will take over Gabriel Bortoleto’s car for first practice. Alpine’s Gabriele Mini will be in Franco Colapinto’s car.

Several of the regular practice session drivers will also appear: Frederik Vesti at Mercedes, Luke Browning at Williams and Ryo Hirakawa at Haas. Some teams are yet to confirm their plans.

Mexico versus Lawson

Liam Lawson was at the centre of a bizarre incident last year when he had the misfortune to encounter two marshals on track. Incredibly, Mexico’s automobile club accused the blameless driver of being responsible for the oversight.

The FIA later made it clear Lawson had done nothing wrong. Hopefully there is no repeat of either administrative slip-up this year.

Perez hits 300

Last year’s Mexican Grand Prix was the first without a home driver since the event returned to the calendar. But Sergio Perez is back on the grid this year and will mark his 300th start in front of his home crowd.

Expect the usual huge cheers for the Guadalajaran. However the hope of a points finish looks as remote as ever. Indeed, the combination of high cooling demands and several heavy braking points could aggravate one of Cadillac’s most obvious weaknesses.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury Documentary Launches on Netflix Today Ahead of Joshua Fight
Sports.content:
Netflix releases TYSON FURY today, tracing the heavyweight’s rise through boxing and examining his personal struggles before he faces Anthony Joshua on December 11.

Lucy Wilcox directs the feature-length documentary. Fury, his wife Paris and father John give interviews alongside previously unseen footage from his life and career.

Tyson Fury’s Career and Family Life

The film follows Fury from childhood into the heavyweight ranks, revisiting the victories and setbacks that shaped his career. His family contributes its accounts of the experiences behind those performances.

Mental health, addiction and the loss of a child are among the subjects covered. The documentary also examines Fury’s views on masculinity, his family relationships and the support he has relied on throughout his career.

Paris and John bring their perspectives to a film that explores the personal pressures accompanying Fury’s success in the ring.

Fury vs Joshua: December 11 Date and Netflix Broadcast

Fury and Joshua step into opposite corners on Friday, December 11, 2026, at Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales. Netflix will broadcast their first professional meeting globally to all members at no additional cost.

The remaining bouts have yet to be announced.

At their September 30 press conference, Fury spoke about the years spent waiting to get Joshua into the ring.

“I’m looking forward to the challenge. It’s been 10 years in the making,” Fury said.

“The rise has been phenomenal from both fighters. We’ve both had our ups and downs. Finally, we arrive at this moment.”

Fury also praised his British rival: “He’s been a role model and a poster boy for British boxing for years.”

Joshua welcomed the occasion and said their exchanges would drive him through extra rounds in the gym.

“I feel fresh. I feel very excited about this opportunity to work again,” Joshua said.

Sports.title: David Benavidez Ready To Put Oleksandr Usyk First
Sports.content:
David Benavidez is risking his shot at Oleksandr Usyk by messing around with Jai Opetaia or Artur Beterbiev beforehand. Jumping straight up to heavyweight makes total sense, especially since he already sounds open to flipping the script.

Talking about skipping straight to Usyk sounds a whole lot less like fearless ambition and a whole lot more like self-preservation.

Benavidez knows that the road running through Jai Opetaia and Artur Beterbiev is not a tune-up run. It is an absolute danger. If he actually believed he could steamroll both men, he would happily take their scalps, build an undeniable mountain of momentum, and walk into a showdown with Usyk as a massive multi-division attraction.

Bypassing them exposes the reality: he knows the risk of getting derailed before cashing that mega check is sky-high.

“If they want me to go up … I don’t give a f***,” Benavidez stated in the interview. “I want to fight. I want to fight the best people. And if I got to go up there and fight for the lineal belt with no belts, I’ll do that … I just want to fight the best in the world. I want my respect, and I’m going to get it one way or another,” said Benavidez to Fight Hub TV about moving up to heavyweight to face Usyk.

That sounds like someone ready to sign for Usyk the moment pen meets paper. He never locked himself into clearing out Opetaia or Beterbiev before taking that leap.

If he takes an L against either one, the Usyk lottery ticket instantly turns to dust. Usyk is not going to look twice at a defeated Benavidez trying to pick up the pieces, not when he can command massive money elsewhere.

Opetaia has the exact southpaw movement, discipline, and sharp counterpunching to turn Benavidez into a frustrated stalker swinging at fresh air while eating clean leather all night. Beterbiev brings brutal inside violence and technical craft that makes trading in the pocket pure trouble.

Both matchups carry a high probability of stripping Benavidez of his spotless record and shredding his market value.

Benavidez already wasted years chasing Canelo Alvarez, only to come away empty-handed. Now that he is finally free from that waste of time, he ought to recognize the danger of waiting around for the stars to align.

Usyk is clearly the legacy crown he wants.

“Usyk has more accolades than Canelo, in my opinion,” Benavidez noted. “Once I beat him, there’s no denying me my spot in the history of boxing.”

Admitting he would train “like I’m scared for my life” shows he respects the mountain in front of him. Taking Usyk immediately carries risk, but it locks down the biggest prize while Benavidez’s zero remains intact.

Sports.title: Chrisean Rock vs Morgan Victory In Smack Fighting Championships Main Event
Sports.content:
While some of the elite level boxers continue to disappoint their fans with overpricing themselves, and dehydration clauses, a new wave of combat sport is scooping up the casual fans, and some of the traditional boxing fans.

On Friday night November 20th reality TV star turned boxer Chrisean Rock will face Morgan Victory. The action is set to take place at Harrah’s Philadelphia Casino, and it will air live on Triller TV.

This event is unique because of the unconventional format. For this collection of contests, half of the card is boxing, and the other half of the event card will be smack fighting matches.

Unlike traditional boxing, smack fighting is an open-hand fast pace type of bout. The fighters use custom designed gloves that are made for open hand strikes.

The architect of the Smack Fighting Championships is the CEO Damon Feldman. The Broomall, Pennsylvania native is a former boxer who had a record of (9-0, 4 KOs).

Unfortunately, his professional boxing career was derailed due to injury. Now Feldman has put together an event that is both unique and entertaining.

Chrisean Rock (1-0, 1 KO) has dedicated herself to the sweet science, and she plans to take another successful step in her boxing journey. Her opponent Morgan Victory was also victorious in her boxing debut and she’s ready to play the role of the spoiler.

The night of November 20th promises to be a groundbreaking night of entertainment. Naughty By Nature rapper Treach, and two-division boxing world champion Danny “Swift” Garcia will be the guest hosts for the event.

Sports.title: Will Golden Boy Pay Shakur Stevenson’s Price?
Sports.content:
Oscar De La Hoya is making a play to sign Shakur Stevenson, but his pitch reveals Golden Boy’s real priority: staging a William Zepeda rematch. While De La Hoya sees big business in a second meeting, he has yet to outline what he would actually put on the table to secure Stevenson’s signature.

“I would love to promote a Shakur Stevenson. He’s arguably the best fighter pound-for-pound in the world. Who doesn’t want to promote him? I know what to do with him,” De La Hoya said to the media.

De La Hoya is either dreaming or running a pure promotional bluff, because the economics make zero sense.

If Dana White and Zuffa walked away from Shakur over demands of 15 million per outing, there is no world where Golden Boy can satisfy that appetite. Golden Boy operates on a standard broadcast model with DAZN. To justify a 15 to 20 million guarantee, a fighter has to generate massive pay-per-view buys, fill a football stadium, or carry commercial sponsorships at an astronomical level.

Shakur does none of that.

His pure boxing skill is undeniable, but his safety-first style has never translated into commercial box office power. Casual fans simply refuse to pay premium pay-per-view prices to watch twelve rounds of tactical potshotting and resetting. If Golden Boy put Shakur on pay-per-view against anyone other than a megastar like Gervonta Davis, the buy rate would be catastrophic. Even a rematch with William Zepeda is nowhere near big enough to cover those kinds of purses.

So what is Oscar actually doing? Most likely, De La Hoya is using Shakur’s free agency to generate free press and build up Zepeda’s profile. By publicly offering to sign Shakur and insisting Zepeda is the man who pushed him to the brink, Oscar gets the benefit of elite association without having to cut the check.

“What excites me is that who gave Shakur his toughest fight? William Zepeda, who’s getting better, who is becoming a complete fighter,” De La Hoya claimed. “So will we see that fight happen again? I would love to see it because Zepeda right now is a punching machine that now has the wit, the experience, the power, and the punch output is through the roof.”

If Oscar truly believes he can deliver 15 million purses on DAZN pay-per-view with Shakur at the top of the bill, he is setting Golden Boy up to take a massive financial bath. In reality, once real contract numbers replace public soundbites, the gap between what Shakur expects and what Golden Boy can afford will stop any deal dead in its tracks.

Money talks, yet De La Hoya skipped the finances entirely. He talked up his promotional track record, but stopped short of floating purse guarantees, a schedule, or a debut matchup.

Shakur benefits from having another major player chasing him openly. Golden Boy gets to chase a generational star while building buzz around Zepeda. De La Hoya put his cards on the table. Now, Golden Boy needs to back up the talk with a genuine contract offer.

Sports.title: Vergil Ortiz Jr. Scrambles To Sell Shot Keith Thurman
Sports.content:
Vergil Ortiz Jr. wants everyone to treat Keith Thurman like a live dog ahead of their December 5 matchup, yet cracked wise about Sebastian Fundora’s towering reach along the trail. Joking around will not scrub away the harsh reality of that loss. Thurman looked completely spent against Fundora, leaving Ortiz to convince paying customers that a victory here actually counts for something meaningful.

Here lies the messy reality of selling this event. Ortiz must puff up Thurman because blasting out a shot fighter earns him zero credit.

“People are overlooking Thurman because he got stopped by a world champion who can tie his shoes standing up,” Ortiz remarked during promotional duties.

Fundora’s freakish height definitely created problems. The sixth-round stoppage proved Thurman lacked answers once his punches fell short. He absorbed steady damage with zero response.

His prior appearance, a third-round stoppage over Brock Jarvis, provided a highlight reel against soft opposition. It never proved the former unified champion could still hang with the division’s best, which made the harsh lesson against Fundora predictable.

The sport leans on this familiar strategy. Promoters match a surging contender against a faded name coasting on reputation. The veteran cashes a check on past glory, and the rising star gets a marquee notch on his resume. Fans see right through it.

“I just want to be in exciting fights. That’s the point of boxing. I want to be remembered as a guy who never said no to a fight,” Ortiz stated.

Taking every challenge is commendable, but that attitude fails to justify Thurman as pay-per-view headliner material. Crowds clamoring for clashes with Jaron Ennis or Fundora get handed a guy Fundora already battered into submission.

“I don’t go in with the mentality to get someone out right away. I’ll feel him out and download information. Obviously I’m familiar with Thurman, but we’re not gonna take anyone lightly,” Ortiz explained.

Ortiz walks right into a classic situation. Score a swift knockout, and critics declare Thurman washed up. Grind out a distance win, and people will point out Fundora did the job much faster.

Thurman desperately needed an honest tune-up to give this clash real credibility. Without that foundation, Ortiz is left doing all the heavy lifting at the podium.

Sports.title: David Benavidez Claims He Never Needed Canelo Alvarez After Wasting Years Chasing Him
Sports.content:
David Benavidez claims he never needed Canelo Alvarez. Spending his absolute prime sitting by the phone waiting for him proves otherwise. If Benavidez genuinely believed those words years ago, he would have jumped to 175 pounds long before his career lost precious runway.

“Everybody’s like, ‘Oh, well, he doesn’t have Canelo. He’s not going to do nothing.’ Like I said, ‘I don’t need Canelo,’” Benavidez said to the media. The quote is empty considering how many prime years disappeared while he stalked Alvarez at super middleweight.

Benavidez addressed the Alvarez obsession during a group interview, claiming zero bitterness remains. In his mind, having their names linked decades from now simply cements their status as kings of this era.

“I’m enjoying this moment, bro. I’ve worked my whole life for this. And I’m just enjoying this,” Benavidez said. “There’s great fights available for me. I didn’t need to go that route. I wanted to because I wanted to show the world who I am. But that wasn’t given to me. I still made my greatness elsewhere.”

Wanting Alvarez in the ring made financial sense. Alvarez holds the keys to the biggest paydays in the sport, and beating him would have transformed Benavidez into a global superstar overnight. Moving up meant abandoning the specific payday he chased relentlessly.

Patience extracted a massive toll. Every single calendar year spent chasing Alvarez stole time away from conquering light heavyweight, not to mention eventual plans for cruiserweight.

Benavidez made his 175-pound debut in June 2024, beating Oleksandr Gvozdyk on points to collect the interim WBC light heavyweight belt. That jump instantly paid off. He walked away with a victory over a former world champion plus a direct route toward undisputed glory.

The WBC quickly confirmed his status as mandatory challenger. His entire future stopped depending on whether Alvarez felt like picking up the phone.

Moving up sooner would not have guaranteed a packed schedule. Big fights require painful network negotiations, purse splits, endless politics. Cruiserweight success is never guaranteed for a former super middleweight.

Starting that journey earlier would have bought him real development time. He could have established dominance across multiple divisions, ignited natural rivalries, given fight fans reasons to watch him without mentioning Alvarez.

Benavidez remains entirely confident about his legacy. When asked what moving through divisions proves, his answer was direct: “That I will be a Hall of Fame fighter.”

He also turned his attention toward inspiring younger kids dealing with doubt. He reflected on growing up as an overweight kid written off by peers, aiming to turn his rise into proof that dedication works.

That backstory connects with general fans. Combined with his brutal pressure style in the ring, it gives him an authentic identity capable of selling arenas without riding on Alvarez’s coattails.

Benavidez earned the right to enjoy his recent run. Claiming he never needed Canelo simply makes that endless pursuit look foolish in hindsight. Massive opportunities sat waiting for him all along, and grabbing them years ago would have put him way ahead of where he sits today.

Sports.title: Osleys Iglesias Targets Canelo Alvarez-Christian Mbilli Winner
Sports.content:
Osleys Iglesias has his sights set on a massive unification clash with whoever walks away victorious from Saturday’s battle between Canelo Alvarez and Christian Mbilli. The unbeaten IBF super middleweight champion wants the WBC crown, though his shot at that prize largely hinges on the final result in Riyadh.

“Whoever wins, though, I want to fight him,” Iglesias said to The Ring. The unbeaten Cuban made his first IBF title defense on October 8, stopping Oliver Zaren in the seventh round in Quebec City. He now wants another champion rather than another challenger.

The hard-hitting Cuban notched his first IBF defense on October 8 by halting Oliver Zaren in the seventh round in Quebec City. Now, he wants belts instead of contenders.

Sitting at 16-0 with 15 knockouts, Iglesias is pulling for a Canelo victory on October 31, yet he insists he is ready for either man. He sees Saturday’s headliner as an even matchup, crediting Alvarez’s ring craft while respecting Mbilli’s nonstop aggression. Regardless of who prevails, his target remains unchanged.

“Hopefully Canelo wins; it will be the most interesting outcome for the division. Whoever wins, though, I want to fight him. For me, it doesn’t really matter. God willing, the winner will face me. I’m ready; that great opportunity will come, and from there I will win that fight,” Iglesias said to The Ring.

Luring Canelo into the ring presents the steeper climb. Iglesias stands tall, punches with concussive force from the southpaw stance, and brings real tactical versatility. If he elects to box from range behind a disciplined right jab, Alvarez could struggle to work his way inside effectively.

Behind that lead hand, Iglesias can neutralize Canelo’s offense, wear him down, and guide him straight into heavy left hands. Alvarez would have to close distance and target the ribs without eating clean counters. Against someone with Iglesias’ knockout ratio, stepping into range is dangerous business.

The Cuban possesses the pedigree to execute that long-range game plan. Eye of the Tiger lists him with 184 wins across 200 amateur contests, a run highlighted by triumphs over David Morrell Jr. and Gleb Bakshi. His pro record is relatively brief, but his technical schooling runs deep.

That seasoned background proves he can stick to a smart boxing blueprint instead of hunting for one punch. Alvarez would certainly have to respect those skills when mapping out his future schedule.

Mbilli represents the far more realistic option for Iglesias. Mbilli’s relentless engine would spark a wild clash of styles, handing the Cuban clean targets as the French puncher charges in. That brings plenty of peril for Mbilli as well, yet an Iglesias-Mbilli showdown feels much easier to make than Canelo voluntarily accepting such a dangerous fight.

Iglesias took care of business in his initial defense and stated his claim. Nothing guarantees him the victor of Saturday’s bout. If Canelo claims the WBC strap, Iglesias may discover that getting the Mexican superstar to sign the contract is much tougher than figuring out how to box him.

Sports.title: Has Boxing Made Waiting More Profitable Than Fighting?
Sports.content:
A fighter collects the biggest paycheck of his life, and boxing pays for it for the next twelve months. The money lands in the bank, the entourage celebrates, and the division goes on ice. Once an inflated check becomes the baseline, regular title defenses suddenly look like bad investments.

Oscar De La Hoya called out this trend, pointing out that too many top fighters now sit around waiting for what he termed the ultimate purse. He hit on an uncomfortable reality. A packed stadium show might generate headlines for forty-eight hours, but it leaves behind a barren schedule when the headliner disappears until another lottery ticket surfaces.

Taking a massive purse makes plenty of personal sense. A fighter walks away with security, leverage, and a shiny target on his back. Taking a dangerous fight for ordinary money suddenly looks foolish to his handlers. A loss wrecks his market value. A rough night hurts his bargaining position. Inactivity turns into the safest play on the board.

The trouble starts when every recognized name adopts that same corporate logic. Legitimate contenders get bypassed because they represent too much risk for the return. Solid, respectable paydays get treated like personal insults. The only bout worth taking is one against an opponent who will not push back.

Fighters forget that extraordinary money usually comes from extraordinary circumstances. A blood feud, an undisputed clash, or an eager backer with deep pockets creates an artificial economy that standard pay-per-view cards cannot duplicate. When fighters confuse a unique financial windfall with their permanent market rate, every future negotiation stalls before anyone even signs a contract.

Nobody argues that athletes in a brutal trade should risk their health for pocket change. Fighters take real physical damage, and securing their future is the goal of the sport. Promoters, networks, and sanctioning bodies also share blame for dragging out talks.

Yet the sport still suffers the damage. Belts sit idle, contenders get frozen out, and divisions grind to a halt. When the star finally agrees to return, fans get fed an overmatched tune-up disguised as a necessary prelude to the meaningful bout somewhere down the road.

Supporters get tired of following mandatory rotations, press conference callouts, and endless contract leaks that lead nowhere. Hardcore fans want action, not accounting lessons. When staying active requires another state-funded fortune to lure a champion out of his living room, people simply tune out.

High pay does not demand total inactivity. Naoya Inoue proved that by stepping into the ring four times in 2025. He proved that an elite attraction can handle a relentless schedule without sitting out a year between appearances.

Massive purses make big events happen, but they poison the water when their main legacy is an impossible asking price and a dormant champion. Boxing needs its stars to earn well, but the sport only survives when fighters actually fight. If the business continues rewarding long absences, fans will find another sport to follow.

Ghana News.title: Spain Ambassador visits Ghana’s amputee football team ahead of 2026 World Cup
Ghana News.content:
The Spanish Ambassador to Ghana, His Excellency Ángel Lossada Torres-Quevedo, has visited Ghana’s national amputee football team, the Black Challenge, ahead of the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico.

The ambassador met with all 15 players and members of the technical team at the Mendiata Hotel in Accra, where he offered words of encouragement ahead of the team’s departure for the tournament.

Addressing the players, Lossada Torres-Quevedo expressed his support for Ghana, while emphasising the importance of promoting the rights of persons with disabilities through sport.

“For me, you are allies. If, at the end of the World Cup, I am in the camp of the Spanish side, if there is a final like that, but I will be on your side in this process,” he said.

“At the end of the day, sport is important, but the rights of persons with disabilities are more important. You are already very good, and I wish you all the best.”

President of the Ghana Amputee Football Association, Foster Kwarteng, also expressed gratitude to the ambassador for his continued support for disability sports in the country.

“We want to thank you for always attending to disabled sports. What you’ve done for the National Paralympic Committee and persons with disabilities, I personally cannot thank you enough. You’ve always opened your doors to us, and I thank you for that,” Kwarteng said.

The Black Challenge have been drawn in Group D alongside Colombia, Angola and Iraq for the tournament in Mexico.

Ghana will be aiming to make history by winning the global title, having established themselves as a dominant force in African amputee football with back-to-back Africa Cup of Nations triumphs.

Ghana News.title: SanlamAllianz in Ghana launches “PROUD Moments 2.0” to celebrate everyday heroes

SanlamAllianz, one of Ghana's leading providers of Life and General insurance, has announced the return of PROUD Moments, a campaign that celebrates the achievements of everyday Ghanaians. The campaign is now open for its second edition, with entries closing on 13th November 2026.

Built around a simple question, "Who or what makes you proud?", PROUD Moments invites Ghanaians to celebrate themselves and their own achievements, as well asrecognise people whose actions, sacrifices, resilience or support have made a meaningful difference. The campaign affords people an opportunity to celebrate a parent, teacher, mentor, friend, partner, colleague, or even the nominee's own personal triumph.

How to Participate

Participants can nominate themselves or someone else by posting a video on Instagram telling the story behind the nomination. Entries should mention @sanlamallianzghana and use the hashtag #PROUDMomentsGH. The deadline for entries is 13th November 2026.

Selected honourees will be celebrated at a grand ceremony at the SanlamAllianz office and win a #PROUDBOX containing items worth GHS 5,000.00.

Building on a Successful First Edition

The campaign follows a well-received first edition, themed "Your Achievement Deserves Protection," which honoured 10 individuals who overcame some life's toughest challenges to achieve greatness. The event took place on Saturday, 4th October, 2025, at the Achimota Mall in Accra, with award-winning actor and comedian Clemento Suarez as MC.

It drew hundreds of guests, including Mr. Tawiah Ben-Ahmed, CEO/Country Lead of Sanlam Allianz Life Insurance Ghana LTD, and Mrs. Mabel Nana Nyarkoa Porbley, Managing Director and CEO of Sanlam Allianz General Insurance Ghana LTD. Award-winning dancer Endurance Grand also performed.

The highlight was the "Walk of Fame," inspired by the Hollywood Walk of Fame. Honourees, accompanied by their loved ones, walked a blue path lined with their photos as staff and guests cheered. Each received a bouquet of flowers, a personalised citation recognising their effort and dedication, and a SanlamAllianz gift box.

Celebrating the People Behind the Milestones

“We often celebrate major milestones but overlook the small achievements that matter just as much,” said Helen Aryee, Head: Marketing & Brand Awareness, Sanlam Allianz Life Insurance Ghana LTD. “PROUD Moments reminds us that every story matters. We invite Ghanaians to share their own proud moments or celebrate the heroes in their lives, because every achievement deserves recognition, and every unsung hero deserves more than a private ‘thank you.’”

Mr. William Noi Mensah, Executive for Strategy, Analytics, Marketing Communications and Brand at Sanlam Allianz General Insurance Ghana LTD, noted that the campaign reflects the Group's commitment to reimagining how insurance connects with people. "For too long, insurance communication has centered on risks and uncertainties. With PROUD Moments, we're taking a different approach by celebrating the achievements, victories and everyday successes that bring meaning to people's lives. As Africa's largest insurance group, we believe these moments deserve both recognition and protection, giving Ghanaians the confidence to keep striving for more while we help safeguard what matters most."

With the deadline approaching of 13th November 2026., Ghanaians are encouraged to share their Proud Moments and give someone the recognition they deserve.

Share your story on your socials, mention @sanlamallianzghana, use #PROUDMomentsGH and you could see your Proud Moment celebrated this year.

SanlamAllianz is one of Ghana's leading insurance brands, offering life and general insurance solutions through Sanlam Allianz Life Insurance Ghana LTD and Sanlam Allianz General Insurance Ghana LTD.

We provide affordable, tailored insurance solutions to individuals, businesses, groups and the inclusive market. We help customers prepare for life’s planned and unexpected moments.

As part of the SanlamAllianz Group, with a presence across 25 African countries, we leverage strong regional expertise and innovative solutions to create sustainable value for our customers, partners, employees and communities.

Our purpose is to empower generations to be financially confident, secure and prosperous. This purpose is underpinned by our core values of Integrity, Care, Innovation and Collaboration, which guide how we serve our customers and conduct our business.

Through our brand promise, Live with Confidence, we remain committed to enabling Ghanaians to protect what matters, plan for the future and achieve greater financial confidence.

Ghana News.title: Ghanaians are not angry enough about galamsey – Awula Serwah
Ghana News.content:
Massive lake pits caused by galamsey flood an abandoned cocoa farm in the Western Region of Ghana. Image by Edem Srem. Ghana, 2022.

The Executive Director of Eco-Conscious Citizens, Awula Serwah, says Ghanaians are not angry enough about the destruction caused by illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey.

She says she wishes the public would express greater anger and organise themselves to compel political leaders to take decisive action to end the menace.

Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Thursday, October 29, during a discussion on the effects of illegal mining on the country, she stressed that her call was not for violence but for peaceful civic action that would generate the political will needed to tackle the problem.

"All I see is that Ghanaians are not angry enough; we are not angry enough. As you rightly said, when we eat our food, do we know where it comes from? The kenkey, do you know that corn absorbs poison?" she quizzed.

Ms Serwah said Ghanaians must move beyond expressing concerns and organise activities that would put pressure on leaders to take concrete steps to stop illegal mining.

"Ghanaians are being taken for a ride, and we are not angry enough. When I say we are not angry, I don't advocate violence, but we are not angry enough. A sit-down demonstration to say that you cannot continue poisoning us; stop this galamsey," she added.

She argued that stronger public mobilisation was necessary to ensure that the fight against galamsey translates into meaningful results.

Ghana News.title: PETROSOL’s CEO urges Ghana to turn economic stability into sustainable growth
Ghana News.content:
Chief Executive Officer of PETROSOL Platinum Energy PLC, Michael Bozumbil

The Chief Executive Officer of PETROSOL Platinum Energy PLC, Michael Bozumbil, has called on the Government of Ghana to protect the country’s economic recovery through consistent policies, prudent public spending and deliberate support for indigenous businesses.

Delivering the keynote address at the 50th Annual General Meeting (AGM) of the Ghana National Chamber of Commerce and Industry (GNCCI), held on Wednesday, 28 October 2026, at the Ghana Shippers’ House in Ridge, Accra, Mr Bozumbil said improving economic indicators were encouraging, but should be seen as signs of recovery, not proof that the economy had fully recovered.

Speaking on the theme, “From Stability to Growth: Promoting a Resilient and Future-Ready Private Sector,” he compared economic recovery to a patient whose condition has stabilized but who still needs treatment and monitoring. He explained that the real strength of the economy is reflected in businesses that create jobs, generate income and contribute to national development.

“The first few years of economic stability simply mean that the economic recovery process has started. It does not mean that the economy has fully recovered and that we can return to business as usual.”

A call for policy discipline and stronger local businesses

Mr Bozumbil urged government to maintain a predictable policy environment, prepare realistic budgets, spend within its means and build financial buffers to withstand future shocks. He commended the government for signing up to the International Monetary Fund’s Policy Coordination Instrument (PCI), despite not seeking funding from the Fund, and cautioned against decisions that could reverse the gains made ahead of the 2028 elections.

He called for stronger support for credible Ghanaian businesses through transparent procurement, effective local-content policies and access to long-term finance. He also encouraged policymakers to listen more closely to indigenous entrepreneurs, who understand the day-to-day realities of operating businesses in Ghana. In his view, stronger local companies are essential to sustainable jobs, national competitiveness and dependable tax revenue.

Practical lessons for future-ready businesses

Mr Bozumbil identified purpose, quality, credible relationships, financial discipline and continuous improvement as key principles that have helped PETROSOL build resilience. He stressed that businesses must honour their commitments to employees, customers, suppliers and partners, manage cash flow carefully, invest in staff training and adapt to changing market conditions.

He encouraged businesses to strengthen their balance sheets before expanding, improve governance and financial records to attract investment, and treat compliance and recognized standards as competitive advantages. He also urged companies to consider diversification in response to changing markets, including opportunities in solar energy and electric-vehicle charging, where commercial viability and infrastructure readiness must be carefully assessed.

Investing in people was another key priority. He highlighted the importance of developing young talent and creating more opportunities for women in leadership, citing PETROSOL’s Women Network and Next Energy Talent initiatives. He also emphasized that businesses should grow with their dealers, distributors, suppliers and small contractors, rather than at their expense.

Three proposals for the GNCCI

As the Chamber marked its 50th AGM, Mr Bozumbil proposed a capital-readiness programme to help small and medium-sized enterprises prepare for investment; a standards and certification support desk to help businesses meet recognized requirements; and evidence-based advocacy informed by regular data on borrowing costs, regulatory bottlenecks, tax changes, logistics costs and delays in government payments.

He encouraged GNCCI members to participate actively in the Chamber’s work and mentor emerging entrepreneurs, reflecting on the Chamber’s role in recognising his own journey, from being named Young Entrepreneur of the Year in 2016 at the Chamber Business Awards held in 2017 to receiving the Chamber Businessman of the Year award in 2024.

Turning stability into opportunity

Mr Bozumbil concluded that economic stability presents an opportunity that must be protected through preparedness, responsible leadership and collective effort. He paid tribute to PETROSOL’s young, skilled and dedicated employees, crediting their diligence and pursuit of excellence for the company’s progress.

“A resilient business is not one that never faces a storm. It is one that prepares before the storm comes and is ready to move when conditions improve.” He stated emphatically.

His address reaffirmed PETROSOL Platinum Energy PLC’s commitment to quality, responsible business practices, people development and the growth of a resilient indigenous private sector capable of contributing to Ghana’s long-term development and sustainable growth.

Ghana News.title: Audacious Indian jailbreak saga ends with 17 prisoners recaptured
Ghana News.content:
A fake medical emergency, an audacious jailbreak and a 36-hour search operation that ended with 17 prisoners being recaptured.

Those are the highlights of a story from India's Tamil Nadu state that has captured headlines across the country.

It began on Monday night after 17 men escaped from a prison in Theni district in the southern state after overpowering guards, and ended almost two days later with police catching them in batches.

The incident has drawn attention to overcrowding in Indian prisons. Police say the Theni prison was housing 334 inmates against a capacity of 200, leaving authorities unable to maintain control once chaos broke out.

The state police said it has suspended nine staff at the prison for alleged negligence in connection with the incident.

All the men who escaped were undertrials - inmates on trial or awaiting one - and 18 of them were in one cell at the prison in Thekkampatti in Theni.

On Monday night at 2230 local time (17:00 GMT), one of the prisoners acted like he was going through a seizure. The other cellmates shouted for help and a jail official responded. He was soon overpowered by the prisoners, police said.

The prisoners then got out of the cell, reportedly attacked two other jail guards and took away keys which they used to open the main gate and flee. While 17 escaped, one returned to the prison immediately.

Several prison personnel were injured in the attack.

Police sources told BBC Tamil that they were examining the possibility of collusion between some prison officials and the escaped men.

Sandeep Rathore, Director General of Police for Prisons in Tamil Nadu, said in a press briefing that the jailbreak was caused by "human error".

"There was a clear breach of security protocol as the prisoners managed to pass through a three-tier barrier manned by security personnel," he said.

At the time of the incident, only four guards were on duty, far below the staffing required to maintain the prescribed 1:6 guard-to-inmate ratio recommended by the state - which should have worked out to 34 guards against the approved strength of 200 prisoners.

The police then launched a manhunt, calling forces from across the state.

"Advanced technology, drone surveillance, CCTV footage analysis, and the tireless efforts of police personnel played a crucial role," the department said in a statement on X.

Four men were arrested at a bus station in a nearby village, and the fifth was caught while he was travelling in a tuk-tuk.

A drone search of a forest near the prison led to eight more escaped prisoners being caught. Videos of the arrests showed the men obeying police instructions even as they did not answer questions from reporters who were also seen at the scene.

Two more were captured with the help of drone surveillance, police said, while the last two men surrendered on Wednesday.

News agency PTI reported that all 17 recaptured prisoners have been moved to high-security correctional prisons.

Rathore told media that all prisons across the state would be audited to check if rules were being followed.

The incident evoked memories of one of the biggest jailbreaks in Tamil Nadu in 1995 when 43 suspected militants escaped from a special camp after digging a 153-foot-long tunnel beneath a historic fort. Some of them were never recaptured.

While the investigation is going on, the incident has sparked a conversation on overcrowding in Indian prisons. The National Crime Records Bureau's last Prison Statistics India report from 2023 showed a national occupancy rate of 120.1%.

Data shows that undertrial prisoners - individuals who are detained while they await police investigation or court trials - make up more than 73% of India's total prison population. Human rights groups and legal experts have also raised concerns about delays in investigations and trials that lead to people languishing for years behind bars.

Ghana News.title: NAIMOS begins community engagements in galamsey-prone areas
Ghana News.content:
The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) has begun a series of community engagements in illegal mining-prone areas as part of efforts to strengthen collaboration with stakeholders and complement ongoing enforcement operations.

The initiative is aimed at building public confidence, addressing local concerns, improving intelligence sharing and encouraging collective responsibility in the fight against illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey.

In a statement issued on Thursday, October 29, NAIMOS explained that the engagements would bring together traditional authorities, local government officials, opinion leaders and other stakeholders to address the environmental and livelihood challenges associated with illegal mining.

The Secretariat emphasised that the initiative would not replace ongoing enforcement operations but would complement existing measures to tackle the menace.

According to NAIMOS, the programme forms part of a broader and coordinated strategy being implemented by the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, in line with President John Dramani Mahama's vision of intensifying the fight against illegal mining.

The community engagements are being led by the Director of Operations at NAIMOS, Colonel K. S. Appiah, alongside a team from the Secretariat, working closely with traditional authorities and opinion leaders in selected communities.

The Secretariat believes that strengthening cooperation with local communities will help improve intelligence gathering and promote a more sustainable approach to addressing illegal mining activities.

NAIMOS reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining decisive enforcement operations while deepening partnerships with communities and relevant institutions.

The statement, signed by the Spokesperson for NAIMOS, Paa Kwesi Schandorf, stressed that sustained collaboration among stakeholders remains essential to achieving a coordinated and lasting solution to illegal mining across the country.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.content:
The French striker is at the centre of a controversy after a video emerged showing him appearing to make fun of former Chinese leader Mao.

Share Mbappe, Real Madrid and La Liga face long road to redemption in China on social media

Kylian Mbappe, Real Madrid and La Liga have apologised for the French striker’s comments about Mao Zedong, but the damage to their reputation in China will not be easily or quickly repaired, experts say.

The France captain, one of the best footballers on the planet, is at the centre of a controversy after a video emerged this week of him appearing to make fun of former leader Mao.

Mbappe talked about being amused by an internet meme of his face digitally altered onto “some guy, think he’s a Chinese dictator”.

Mao remains officially revered as the hero of the communist revolution and founder of the People’s Republic of China.

He is blamed by historians for millions of deaths, but publicly mocking him is taboo, and Mbappe’s remarks saw him become the latest foreign sports figure or entity to infuriate Beijing.

Leading Chinese brands cut ties with the 27-year-old, and Spanish top-flight matches will be pulled from state television broadcaster CCTV’s schedule.

Chinese state media and social media users lined up to lambast Mbappe, although they were left in the dark about what exactly he said.

China is the world’s second-biggest economy and most lucrative market. Within two days, as the video, purportedly filmed in April, circulated online, the striker, his club Real Madrid and La Liga apologised.

A spokesman for China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the government took Mbappe’s apology “seriously”.

‘Very damaging incident’

So is that the end of the matter?

“Viewed from a calm, objective and emotion-free standpoint, this is clearly a very damaging incident,” Yan Qiang, a veteran sports commentator, told the AFP news agency.



“It causes serious damage to the image of La Liga and Real Madrid in China.

“In the age of the mobile internet, things blow up on social media quickly and emotions run high.

“An apology does not necessarily mean the end of the story.

“It’s better to have an apology than no apology at all, but it’s definitely not the end of the story.”

The furore and the fallout are not an unfamiliar tale.

Various overseas sports leagues or players have found themselves in hot water for comments on topics that are politically sensitive to China.

China effectively cut ties with the National Basketball Association (NBA) in the United States in 2019 after then-Houston Rockets general manager Daryl Morey tweeted his support for Hong Kong protesters.

NBA executives said Morey had the right to freedom of expression. In contrast, La Liga immediately distanced itself from what Mbappe said.

Basketball is among the most popular sports in China along with football. However, Morey’s remark saw the NBA wiped from CCTV for more than a year.

NBA preseason matches returned to China only last year.

Australian National University lecturer Debby Chan called the NBA case – and now Mbappe’s – an illustration of China’s consumer nationalism, where online sentiment and state media converge into “a spiral of outrage”.

NBA commissioner Adam Silver said the league lost “hundreds of millions of dollars” over the split.

No way back for Mbappe, Real Madrid and La Liga?

Spanish football also has a lot to lose.

A source within La Liga told AFP that China and the US alone finance the “majority” of international broadcasting rights, which were valued at 748 million euros ($834m) for the 2024-25 season.

According to the Real Madrid-affiliated newspaper Marca, the Madrid club generates 10 to 15 percent of its jersey and other merchandise sales in China.

Real Madrid also counts Chinese companies among its main sponsors, with Hisense, sports betting firm Kaiyun Sports and Linglong Tire all featuring prominently.

Adam Zhang, founder of the Beijing-based Key-Solution Sports Consulting, said showing fast and heartfelt remorse was the first step.

“This will influence the decision on whether to continue the broadcast ban and, if so, for how long,” he told AFP.

Sports commentator Yan cast doubt on whether the reputation of Mbappe, whose face has adorned drink bottles and advertising campaigns in China, can ever fully recover.

“Judging by commercial sponsorships and big ad campaigns he appeared in during the World Cup, he has a huge influence in China,” he said.



“If that influence can’t be sustained, there can be no talk of commercial interests, and La Liga and Real Madrid will definitely be badly affected.”

Yan said it was “genuinely hard to predict” what happens next.

“In the short term, I’m certainly not optimistic,” he added.

“If they want to repair their image and the relationship, their future actions and behaviour will be key.”

World.title: Trump demands Alaska candidates be removed over alleged ballot scheme
World.content:
A New York Times investigation links Democratic operatives to a namesake candidate in Alaska’s Senate race.

Share Trump demands Alaska candidates be removed over alleged ballot scheme on social media

US President Donald Trump has called for the removal and prosecution of two candidates in Alaska’s Senate race, accusing Democrats of orchestrating a scheme to mislead voters.

Trump’s demand on Wednesday followed a New York Times investigation into efforts by people linked to Democrat Mary Peltola’s campaign to recruit candidates who could draw support from Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, including a retired teacher with the same name.

The November 3 vote could help determine control of the US Senate, Congress’s upper chamber.

In Truth Social posts on Wednesday, Trump accused Peltola and Daniel J Sullivan Jr of election fraud and called for both to be removed from the ballot and prosecuted.

He described the alleged operation as “Voter Fraud at the Highest Level” and accused Democrats of lying under oath.

The Times noted that recruiting candidates to split an opponent’s vote – a practice known as ballot stacking – is generally legal and has been used by both parties in Alaska.

The two Sullivans are among four candidates in Alaska’s ranked-choice election.

Voters rank candidates by preference, with votes transferred if a first choice is eliminated. The ballot identifies the sitting senator as an incumbent Republican.

His namesake says he entered the race independently.

The Times reported that the effort began in 2025, when a Peltola aide was asked to identify Alaskans named Dan Sullivan.

Citing interviews and messages, it said Peltola advisers and officials from the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, which supports Democratic Senate candidates, discussed ways to reshape the ballot.



The newspaper identified Democratic operative Jerid Kurtz as a recruiter who approached potential candidates, sometimes under an assumed name.

It also reported that another Democrat withdrew after an approach from Kurtz, opening a place for Republican Gerald Heikes, who said he too had been encouraged to run.

Peltola’s former campaign manager, Elisa Rios, told the Times that Peltola knew about the operation but did not participate directly.

Rios later sought to withdraw her statements and the newspaper said other evidence supported its reporting.

Peltola’s campaign and the Democratic campaign committee denied recruiting candidates. Her campaign said political threats from Washington would not stop her candidacy.

Senator Sullivan accused Peltola of deceiving voters on Fox News on Wednesday.

Recruiting candidates to divide an opponent’s support is generally legal, the Times noted, and both major parties have used such tactics in Alaska.

The state’s Supreme Court upheld the retired teacher’s right to stand in June.

Trump’s Justice Department, the federal government’s legal arm, sued Alaska last week, seeking to delay certification if Senator Sullivan loses and votes for his namesake could have affected the outcome.

Alaska has asked the court to dismiss the case, arguing that it lacks legal grounds.

World.title: Osaka says she’ll return stronger after latest low, Tokyo exit to Pohankova
World.content:
Four-time Grand Slam champ Naomi Osaka loses 6-3, 7-5 to 18-year-old Slovak Mia Pohankova, ranked 144 in the world.

Share Osaka says she’ll return stronger after latest low, Tokyo exit to Pohankova on social media

Former world number one Naomi Osaka said she would “keep attempting” to get back to her Grand Slam-winning best after her season ended with a second-round exit in Japan on Thursday.

The four-time Grand Slam champion lost 6-3, 7-5 to 18-year-old Slovak Mia Pohankova, ranked 144 in the world, at the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo.

Osaka has not won a title this year and has not reached a Grand Slam final since she returned to tennis after a 15-month break following the birth of her daughter Shai in 2023.

The 29-year-old, now ranked 18 in the world, said she was “at peace” with herself and feeling good about her game.

“Obviously when I play a slam, it’s in my mind to challenge for it,” she said.

“Unfortunately, I haven’t been in that position yet, and I’m going to keep attempting it.

“But if you’re asking me how I think my tennis is, I think it’s pretty good.”

Osaka was appearing at the Pan Pacific Open for the first time in four years.

She came out onto the court wearing a red kimono-style gown with a long frilly train.

She said she chose the colour as a contrast to the blue crane-pattern outfit she wore in her opening match this week.

Osaka said she had more outfits lined up for the Tokyo crowd but “unfortunately” would not have a chance to wear them after exiting the tournament.

Osaka is known for grabbing headlines with her flamboyant custom-made outfits.

She channelled NBA fashion trailblazer Allen Iverson at the US Open and wore an audacious “jellyfish-inspired” outfit in Australia.



She also drew on her Japanese heritage with a kimono-inspired white dress at Wimbledon.

“There are so many things that go on in my mind, and it was just a creative outlet,” she said.

“All the other sports are allowed to do that, and tennis is more subdued and restrained.”

Osaka started the match with an ace, but former junior Wimbledon champion Pohankova soon turned the tables on her.

The Slovak, who said she grew up watching Osaka, broke her opponent three times to take the first set and kept the momentum going to win the match.

Pohankova hit seven aces, and Osaka said it was “tricky to play someone that I know nothing about”.

“It is a little difficult, but I also remember when I was in her position and I was playing players that I watched on TV,” Osaka said.

“I guess age catches up to you eventually.”

Canada’s Leylah Fernandez progressed to the quarterfinals after beating number five seed Elise Mertens of Belgium 6-2, 7-6 (10/8).

World.title: Infantino criticism lands Jordan FA chief judicial review with AFC
World.content:
Jordan Football Association chief Prince Ali bin Hussein said he will cooperate with any Asian Football Confederation (AFC) judicial review after he accused FIFA President Gianni Infantino of taking over last week’s AFC Congress for political purposes.

AFC President Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa had endorsed Infantino for re-election at the continental body’s extraordinary congress in Tokyo.

Following the meeting, Prince Ali alleged delegates had not been allowed to speak, question or debate matters and described the final day of the congress as “pure politics at the behest of Gianni Infantino”.

The AFC said on Tuesday that neither Prince Ali nor any other member association’s representatives had requested to speak and that allegations involving coercion, threats or bribery should be supported by credible evidence.

It added that it would refer Prince Ali’s statements to its judicial bodies.

“I respect the AFC and its judicial bodies and will cooperate fully with any process,” Prince Ali said in a post on X late on Wednesday.

“As the FIFA Statutes provide, the Jordan Football Association will cast its vote in the FIFA presidential election independently.”

He said his earlier post about the congress was intended to explain the FIFA presidential voting process and highlight the importance of transparency in football governance.

“Its final sentence states a principle the whole football family shares: no election should be open to coercion, threats or bribery. I stand by that principle. It was a statement of principle, not an allegation against any person,” he said.



“Where concerns arise, the proper place for them is the competent bodies.”

Prince Ali, who has been a vocal critic of FIFA’s leadership, said he would make no further comment while the matter remained under consideration.

Infantino, who has led FIFA since 2016, is seeking re-election in March after apologising for his abandoned proposal to sell a stake in FIFA competitions.

The AFC’s endorsement marked a sharp shift from its position three months earlier, when it accused FIFA of a “fundamental breach of trust” over the abandoned proposal.
