World.title: Messi and Inter Miami fail to fire as late goal earns Cincinnati a draw
World.content:
Inter Miami’s 2-2 draw sees them slip to third in the Eastern Conference after New England beat the New York Red Bulls 3-2.

Share Messi and Inter Miami fail to fire as late goal earns Cincinnati a draw on social media

Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami stumbled to a costly 2-2 draw with Cincinnati in a Major League Soccer (MLS) game that sprang to life only after half-time and included four superb goals.

Miami took the lead on Wednesday night with a Luis Suarez strike on the hour mark, but conceded two in quick succession before grabbing back a late equaliser from substitute Riquelme Fillipi to ensure the spoils were shared.

The draw was a setback in Miami’s pursuit of the Eastern Conference’s second seed, as the star-studded side lost ground on the New England Revolution, who beat the New York Red Bulls 3-2.

Despite the heartbreak of Fillipi’s late strike, the point could prove valuable for Cincinnati, who sit on the cusp of the automatic playoff places, but are currently headed for the wild card round and could yet miss out entirely with two games remaining.

In a low-key first half, Miami controlled possession and comprehensively outpassed Cincinnati, but were unable to pierce through.

That changed in the 61st minute, as Rodrigo De Paul picked up the ball in the middle of the park, in acres of space, and played it wide to Casemiro.

The Brazilian played it first time with the outside of his boot to Suarez, lurking just inside the box.

The Uruguayan veteran took one touch, swivelled and perfectly curled the ball into the far top corner, where it crashed down and in off the crossbar.

But Cincinnati rallied, and in the 80th minute Frenchman Kenji Mboma Dem scored with another beautiful curling effort to the far post.



He picked up the ball wide right, ran at multiple defenders with a flurry of stepovers, then cut inside to score.

Just six minutes later, Cincinnati silenced Miami’s Nu Stadium by taking the lead.

Defender Samuel Gidi received a pass on the edge of the box and wrapped his left foot around the ball, sending it past Dayne St Clair.

With Messi heavily man-marked and unable to get a shot away, De Paul sprayed a wide pass to young Brazilian attacker Fillipi, who cut back to the corner of the box and bent it through two defenders and into the far side of the goal.

Both sides had even later chances to win the game, with Suarez blasting his at the goalkeeper before Evander’s shot was blocked by a defender at close range as the referee waved away handball appeals.

Inter Miami play New England on Sunday, sitting two points back and needing either a win or a draw to keep their hopes of second place alive.

Nashville SC are top and clinched the Supporters’ Shield last weekend for the first time in the club’s history.

World.title: Israel’s opposition may not be able to form a government, but it still could control Parliament.
World.content:
For decades, Israel’s Arab parties have been relegated to the margins of Israeli political life, often sitting on the sidelines while Jewish parties assembled a governing coalition in Parliament and picked a prime minister.

Heading into Israel’s pivotal election on Tuesday, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned his supporters that the Arabs were “trying to steal the election,” though electoral officials said there were no reports of widespread irregularities. He repeatedly invoked the specter of Arab voters to galvanize his right-wing base, vowing to keep them out of power.

Mr. Netanyahu’s leading rival, Gadi Eisenkot, largely declined to answer whether he would partner with Arab parties if necessary to topple the Netanyahu government, though he said none met his conditions as potential allies.

But record turnout on Tuesday by supporters of the Arab parties looks to deliver them their largest vote totals in generations, possibly since Israel’s establishment 78 years ago.

Now, the Arab minority represents a political reality that cannot be ignored.

Turnout in the Arab community, which represents about 20 percent of Israeli citizens, appears to have translated into a stunning windfall of parliamentary seats — potentially as many as 19 combined between the two leading parties, Raam and the Joint List alliance. The Arab parties have 10 seats in the outgoing Parliament.

Israel’s future could turn in part on whether Mr. Eisenkot decides to take the political risks of partnering with them. Without their support, Mr. Eisenkot and his alliance will almost certainly fall short of the 61-seat majority required in the 120-seat Parliament to form a new government and end Mr. Netanyahu’s hold on power. Mr. Netanyahu’s alliance also looks to fall short of 61 seats.

Many Israeli Jews have long objected to building a governing coalition that relies on Arab party backing for a majority. Some say a Jewish state should be ruled exclusively by Jews. Some cite national security reasons, questioning whether Arab leaders who see themselves as part of the wider Palestinian people can be entrusted with crucial matters of state.

Those objections became even more acute after the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, attacks on Israel and the subsequent rightward shift in Israeli politics. Both Raam and some members of the Joint List condemned the assault, although they have also been highly critical of how Israel has conducted its war against Hamas in Gaza.

The Arab parties for many years were themselves reluctant to join governments that oversaw the Israeli occupation of the West Bank and Gaza. And turnout among Arab Israelis has traditionally been lower than Jewish turnout, reflecting doubts about their ability to influence national decision-making.

Raam, a socially conservative party with roots in Islamist politics, has achieved some acceptance in Israel’s mainstream by putting less emphasis on the cause of Palestinian statehood. But the Joint List, an alliance of three smaller parties that includes a joint Jewish-Arab leftist faction and a Palestinian nationalist faction, is seen as more antagonistic toward Zionism.

Initial election results show that the Joint List will be the significantly larger of the two in Parliament.

“Netanyahu knows that without the Arab parties, there’s no majority to unseat him. That’s why he incites against us,” said Yousef Jabareen, the leader of the Joint List alliance in an interview. “The opposition should reject that incitement.”

He added: “The ball is now in Eisenkot’s court. Whoever wants to remove Netanyahu and change his policies — we are ready to cooperate to topple his government.”

Political analysts say the Joint List would be more likely to support Eisenkot from outside the governing coalition, for instance by agreeing to block any no-confidence votes. There is some precedent for this: In the 1990s, then Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin relied on Arab lawmakers to prevent the collapse of his own minority government.

Arab citizens, some of whom view themselves as both Israeli and Palestinian, experience a tension that can cut to the heart of daily life. Unlike Palestinians in the West Bank — who live under Israeli military rule — Arab Israelis can vote, and some have held high office, including on the country’s Supreme Court.

But they largely live in separate cities and towns from Jewish Israelis and retain tight familial and historical bonds with Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza. Many view themselves as second-class citizens in the Jewish state, saying they face discrimination in housing as well as neglect in receiving public services.

Before this year, the largest electoral success recorded by Arab parties was in 2020, when they secured 15 seats. And the first — and so far, only — time an independent Arab party joined the Israeli governing coalition was in 2021, when Mansour Abbas, the leader of Raam, joined Mr. Netanyahu’s rivals to unseat him in favor of a short-lived government.

Mr. Abbas has since worked to make his party more acceptable to Israeli Jews. He has recognized Israel’s Jewish character as a fact of life and publicly considered integrating Arabs into the country’s mandatory national service, in particular community service.

In a bold move during the election campaign, he named Jewish lawmaker Yoav Segalovitz — a former senior police officer and centrist Zionist — as the number two on the Raam candidate list.

But if exit polls and initial results are correct, Raam’s support would not be enough to give Mr. Eisenkot’s bloc a parliamentary majority. He would also have to rely on the Joint List to topple Mr. Netanyahu. While political analysts say that Mr. Eisenkot might be willing to bring Raam onboard, he would struggle to keep his bloc with him if he made common cause with the Joint List, even if he wanted to, because this could provoke too much political blowback from many Jewish voters.

“There’s a shift in Arab politics, an attempt to get closer to the Jewish Zionist mainstream. It’s just that the other side is not willing to do so,” said Thair Abu Rass, an expert on Israel’s Arab politics. “There’s no partner on the Jewish side to create an alternative reality.”

World.title: The crash comes months after a fatal accident involving the same train operators.
World.content:
Pinned

A high-speed passenger train rear-ended another in Spain on Wednesday morning near the central city of Toledo, killing at least 68 people and injuring dozens more, officials said, in one of the deadliest train crashes in Spanish history.

The accident happened after traffic control operators told a high-speed train to continue its journey when another train was stopped farther along the tracks, Spain’s transportation minister, Óscar Puente, said. He called the operators’ instruction “inexplicable.”

The deadly crash was the second this year involving the same two rail operators; the first, in January, killed 46 people. The latest accident, and its timing months after the previous crash, was likely to deepen doubts about the security of Spain’s once-vaunted rail system.

In Spanish news reports, passengers described an awful impact that tossed people from a dining car, broke limbs and piled passengers atop one another. People crawled out of windows and others were carried by fellow passengers into a nearby field on makeshift stretchers. Local workers, who had heard the crash, rushed to help and guide survivors to safety.

The crash came about a month ahead of national election in Spain, and it had the potential to become an issue in an already bitter campaign about the competence of the left-wing government of Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez.

Spain’s rail authority, the Adif, said the trains involved were a “Renfe train and another from the Iryo company,” both covering the route between Madrid, the capital, and the southern city of Seville. Renfe is the national rail provider.

Mr. Sánchez visited the scene of the crash, saying that Spanish rail’s security systems clearly needed to be reinforced. “If there has been negligence, it will come to light,” he said. “If there have been failures in the safety system, we will respond with the utmost firmness.” He declared three days of official mourning.

The conservative opposition leader, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, voiced his own concern.

“I am very concerned about the information we are receiving regarding another train accident,” he wrote on social media soon after the crash. “The priority now is to assist the victims and support their families. My full support goes to the emergency teams working on the ground.” His Popular Party canceled all its campaign events around the country.

Here’s what else to know:

Survivor speaks: A passenger on one of the trains described a routine trip, a sudden jolt and an effort to tend to the dead and injured. Read more ›

An earlier deadly crash: In January, a northbound Iryo train derailed, two of its cars falling onto the opposite track, and a southbound Renfe train slammed into the carriages seconds later. An official report on what caused that lethal accident has not been released, but preliminary investigations pointed to a broken rail as the likely cause.

A detailed account: In a news conference, Spain’s transportation minister described the events that he said preceded Wednesday’s crash. Read more ›

José Bautista contributed reporting from the scene of the crash.

World.title: Twice before, Netanyahu was ousted then returned to power.
World.content:
Shira Shapiro, right, a candidate for the Yashar party, meeting with Gadi Eisenkot at a roadside bomb shelter where her son died during the Oct. 7 2023, attack, near Reim, Israel, earlier this month.

Several people whose relatives were killed or taken hostage in the Hamas-led attack on Israel on Oct. 7, 2023, are running for office in Tuesday’s election, the first national vote since the assault, which shook the country’s foundations and ignited its longest war.

The October 2023 assault looms large over this week’s vote. There are sharp divisions over who was to blame for failing to prevent the worst military, intelligence and policy disaster in Israel’s history.

About 1,200 civilians and soldiers were killed that day, according to the Israeli authorities, and roughly 250 were taken hostage to Gaza. Many of the family members of hostages held by Hamas rose to prominence as they campaigned for their loved ones in television interviews and at nationwide protests.

Most of them called for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to take responsibility for the government’s failures of Oct. 7 and to prioritize negotiating the release of the hostages over continued fighting. Others supported Mr. Netanyahu’s right-wing government and urged it to keep up the military pressure on Hamas and Israel’s other enemies.

Parties from across Israel’s political spectrum have recruited candidates from what have become known as the Oct. 7 families. Here are some of the candidates with a chance to win a seat in Parliament:

Shira Shapiro is running with Yashar, the centrist party led by Mr. Netanyahu’s main political rival, Gadi Eisenkot. Ms. Shapiro’s son, Staff Sgt. Aner Shapiro, was on leave from the army on Oct. 7 when he attended the Nova music festival, one of the bloodiest targets of the Hamas-led attack. He took shelter in a crowded roadside bomb shelter and stationed himself by the entrance when gunmen attacked it. As the militants hurled grenades inside, Sergeant Shapiro repeatedly caught the grenades and threw them back out, until he was killed, according to surviving witnesses.

Zvi Mor, the father of a released hostage, Eitan Mor, is running as a candidate for the far-right party Religious Zionism, headed by Bezalel Smotrich. While Eitan was in captivity, Mr. Mor, an educator, founded a forum of right-wing parents of hostages and soldiers who opposed making deals with Hamas and pushed for Israel to defeat the group militarily.

Omri Ronen, a reserve soldier, is running with the left-wing Democrats, led by Yair Golan. His grandmother, Nira Ronen, was killed in her home in Kfar Aza, one of the border communities worst hit in the October 2023 attack, along with her Filipina caregiver, Angelyn Aguirre. Before Oct. 7, Mr. Ronen had been one of the leaders of a grass-roots group of reservists protesting the government’s plan to overhaul the judiciary. He said in a recent television interview that Mr. Netanyahu, whom he called “Mr. Oct. 7,” must go. “The word responsibility has meaning,” he said.

Rafael Ben Shitrit, a former mayor of Beit Shean in northern Israel, is in Yisrael Beitenu, a right-wing opposition party led by Avigdor Liberman. Mr. Ben Shitrit used to belong to Mr. Netanyahu’s conservative Likud party, but abandoned it after his son, Staff Sgt. Elroy Ben Shitrit, was killed in battle on Oct. 7 near the Gaza border. He has been an advocate for an independent state inquiry into what went wrong that day. Mr. Netanyahu has refused such an inquiry, and the opposition parties have pledged to establish one if they are elected.

Sharon Sharabi, also on Yisrael Beitenu’s list of candidates, is the brother of Eli Sharabi, a former hostage who was released from Gaza only to learn that his wife and two teenage daughters had been killed during the Oct. 7 attack. Another brother, Yossi Sharabi, was also taken hostage and killed after 100 days in captivity. Sharon Sharabi campaigned tirelessly for his brothers’ return. When Eli Sharabi was finally released, many Israelis were outraged over how emaciated he looked. “I was shocked,” Sharon said at the time. “I’d been told he would be thin, but I didn’t imagine how thin. It was extreme.”

Tali Gvili, running with Mr. Netanyahu’s Likud party, is the mother of Master Sgt. Ran Gvili, a member of a police counterterrorism unit who was shot and severely wounded in combat on Oct. 7 and then dragged into Gaza. His remains were recovered and returned to Israel in January 2026. The Gvili and Netanyahu families have become close, and the prime minister attended Sergeant Gvili’s state funeral, saying, “Our souls are bound with yours.”

Michal Hirsch Negri is running with Together, a joint slate led by right-wing politician Naftali Bennett and the centrist Yair Lapid. Ms. Hirsch Negri’s son Maj. Roee Negri was killed fighting in Kibbutz Be’eri near the Gaza border on Oct. 7.

Maj. Shahar Varon, a commander in the reserves, is another Together candidate. He fought that day in Kfar Aza, another border community, and later went to fight in Gaza. He was wounded in battle, then went back into Gaza to fight again. “There is life before October 7th, and there is life after,” he wrote recently, adding, “Our government disappeared that morning — but our people showed up instead.”

World.title: Audio reveals exchanges between control centre and drivers before deadly Spain train crash
World.content:
Audio recordings published in Spanish media reveal conversations between train drivers and a railway control centre in the minutes leading up to a deadly train crash that killed at least 69 people and injured dozens.

Officials are investigating the cause of the disaster, which occurred when a train travelling from Madrid to Seville barrelled into a stationary train on Wednesday morning.

Three audio recordings between the control centre in Madrid and two train drivers appear to show that one high-speed train was given clearance to move even though another some 25km (15 miles) up ahead had stalled.

The release of the recordings comes as Spain begins three days of national mourning for one of the worst rail disasters in Europe's modern history.

One train, run by state-owned operator Renfe, had 397 passengers on board. Ahead of it on the same line was a train run by private operator Iryo, with 147 passengers.

A reported issue with the automatic signalling system - a computer failure - had forced all trains to halt on the affected stretch.

But later the Renfe train was ordered to proceed in "error", according to Spain's transport minister.

World.title: Flávio Bolsonaro denies fleeing Brazil after landing in Miami
World.content:
Bolsonaro's arrival in Florida ended days of confusion over his whereabouts, after he was reported to have travelled to Argentina, and then prematurely reported to have already entered the US on Tuesday.

In a statement, Bolsonaro thanked both the presidents of Argentina and the US, and the American public "who share the same values ââas the good people of my own country".

"It was never my intention to leave my homeland, but I know exactly where this is heading," he said. "I departed from a regime of exception so that I could become the leader my people deserve."

He called himself a victim of a coup d'Ã©tat and political persecution, and said his travel to the US was to protect his family.

In the lengthy letter, he also repeated unsubstantiated allegations of "electoral fraud" which he said allowed a "mathematical impossibility" to occur in the election.

On Wednesday, Trump declined to discuss the allegations made in Bolsonaro's letter.

"I won't get involved. It was a very strange election, that's for sure," Trump said. He went on to add that he thought Bolsonaro "and his family were treated very unfairly".

After Bolsonaro won the first round of Brazil's election, Lula won the second round by more than four million votes, which was attributed to significantly higher turnout, and swaying more undecided voters.

The result was confirmed by the president of Brazil's top electoral court, who was appointed by Bolsonaro's father, former president Jair Bolsonaro.

Speculation about Bolsonaro's whereabouts was first triggered by a report on an Argentine news site, which claimed that he had crossed the land border between Brazil and Argentina and then boarded a private plane en route to the US.

Brazilian police took the rumours seriously. Early on Tuesday, they checked border crossings but found no evidence that Bolsonaro had left the country, and Argentine officials said they had no reports of him crossing.

For a little while, it seemed like Bolsonaro may just be keeping an uncharacteristically low-profile after being unexpectedly beaten by his left-wing rival in the presidential run-off vote on Sunday, in addition to a criminal investigation that led to orders that his passports be turned into authorities.

But when he failed to surrender his passports in time to meet a 24-hour deadline on Tuesday, Brazilian authorities cancelled the documents and ordered police to make checks at border posts.

Speculation quickly grew that he'd left the country and Bolsonaro's lawyers said they had no idea where he was.

World.title: Netanyahu's bloc leading Israel election but short of majority, partial results show
World.content:
Partial results from Israel's general election show veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is leading his rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, but is still short of a majority in parliament.

With 85% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies were on track to win 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset. Eisenkot's Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his bloc were set for 48.

Both leaders have said they will try to form a governing coalition.

Arab-led parties, who are on course to win an unprecedented 19 seats, could emerge as kingmakers, but all but one of the Jewish parties have pledged not to work with them.

With between 430,000 and 480,000 absentee ballots from groups including soldiers, diplomats and hospital patients yet to be counted, it could still take a day or two for the final election results to emerge.

Once they are confirmed, President Isaac Herzog will hold consultations with all the political factions and invite the leader whom he believes has the best chance of success to form a government - a process that could take weeks.

If they fail, then ultimately there would have to be another election.

World.title: Carney to push for closer ties at Canada-EU summit in Montreal
World.content:
For decades, Canada-EU summits took place without much fanfare - but that's not the case for this coming two-day meeting in Montreal.

Thursday and Friday's summit will be closely watched for details on how Canada and the European bloc deepen their ties.

Last month, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed "opening the door" to Canada for what she called an "associate membership" - a status that does not currently exist.

The overture came after Prime Minister Carney addressed the European Parliament in Strasbourg, telling EU lawmakers that Canada and Europe were "stronger together" in the face of "geopolitical rupture".

Carney and many EU member states welcome closer ties, but not all are on board with what to call this new relationship.

Some, like Germany, are questioning the "associate member" term, fearing that Canada is getting preferential treatment ahead of other nations who also want in.

According to reports by multiple news outlets, Germany and other nations successfully lobbied to remove mention of the title in a draft statement ahead of the summit, opting instead for softer language that references an "ever closer association".

Germany's ambassador to Canada, Matthias LÃ¼ttenberg, told CTV News on Tuesday that some member states were "a little surprised" by von der Leyen's announcement.

The concept of "associate membership", he added, is something that is not clearly understood as it pertains to Canada.

"Germany has been using the term of associate membership for something completely different, which is the relationship of the EU to Ukraine and potentially Moldova", he said, both of which have been trying to join the bloc for many years.

World.title: Building boom puts 300,000 people in the path of potential Himalayan disasters
World.content:
At least 300,000 people in parts of the Himalayan region could now be living in the path of potential disasters, a new study suggests.

Researchers found that the amount of built-up land in high-risk zones in northern Nepal, parts of south-eastern Tibet and a corner of India's Uttarakhand had grown by about 45% between 2016 and 2023.

In areas particularly threatened by flooding from glacial lakes, development increased even faster, rising by almost 78% over the same period, according to the peer-reviewed study published in Scientific Reports.

The team of scientists behind it said the true number of people under threat could be much higher, as they only analysed a specific territory and not neighbouring areas which face similar risks.

The study was carried out before August's devastating mass floods which left more than 1,400 dead and thousands missing in Nepal. More recently there have been several smaller incidents, including flooding along the Budhi Gandaki river on 11 October that damaged 200 houses, swept away five bridges and left five people missing.

World.title: Death of US actress Hayden Panettiere ruled accidental, ending local police probe
World.content:
The death of US actress Hayden Panettiere has been ruled accidental, ending a local probe into her death, police in South Carolina have said.

The Heroes and Nashville star died in August from the toxic effects of fentanyl, Xanax and several other drugs in her system, at the age of 36.

Citing the medical examiner's report last month that found Panettiere died from a drug overdose, the Greenville Police Department said it had "concluded its investigation" into her death.

The US Drug Enforcement Agency (DEA) reportedly joined a local police probe. It is unclear if that investigation has also concluded. The BBC has contacted the DEA for comment.

"Based on the Medical Examiner's determination and the findings of the investigation, Hayden Panettiere's death has been ruled accidental," police said in a statement.

Authorities, including the DEA, were reportedly investigating the circumstances of Panettiere's death, according to the BBC's US media partner CBS News.

World.title: Details of thousands of US immigration agents leaked in major hack
World.content:
Details of more than 41,000 personnel working for the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including thousands involved in immigration enforcement, have been leaked to the public.

The leak includes names, work addresses and phone numbers of DHS staff, including agents working with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection, along with descriptions of the work they do for each agency.

Wednesday's leak marks the third time in recent weeks that a government agency has been targeted by leaks or hacks.

A DHS spokesperson said the agency is "aware of a potential breach and is actively working to address the situation swiftly and effectively."

"We take all security threats against our employees and officers seriously and will work to ensure all are properly protected," the spokesperson added.

"We will update the public when more information is available."

The seemingly unprecedented breach of employee information was made public online. A group called the Department of Peace accessed the information from DHS, while journalist and cybersecurity researcher maia crimew alongside the website Distributed Denial of Secrets put it online.

The information was put in a database named Icepick.

Most of the agents included, more than 21,000 of them, work for CBP, according to the data. Nearly 6,600 work for ICE.

Other records show agents with Homeland Security Investigations, the Federal Protective Service and even people working for the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency.

The leaked information also included dozens of previously unknown operation names, the agents that led and worked on those operations, and some of the technology they used in their work, including tech provided by Cellbrite and Palantir.

The groups wrote in an online statement that the the leak was not meant to be a directory of every DHS agent. Rather the aim was to replace "anonymity with accountability", according to Emma Best, a co founder of DDoSecrets.

"The leak is extraordinary but deceptive in its simplicity as it identifies the officials responsible for overseeing covert and undercover operations, the government's hunt for leakers and the failed BlueLeaks investigation - along with key personnel in DHS's ever-escalating rendition and deportation programs," Best added.

BlueLeaks refers to a massive leak of US police data in 2020, data from which DDoSecrets also hosted.

A spokesperson for the Department of Peace pointed directly at actions by ICE agents for the group's work to hack DHS records.

"On July 17th, Markwayne Mullin said he was 'turning up the heat'. This is what happens to ICE when you do that," the spokesperson wrote on Wednesday.

Mullin in March became Secretary of Homeland Security.

The Department of Peace said it accessed the DHS agent profiles through a single sign-on service called Okta.

Okta is a popular online security tool that organisations use to ensure that only people with access to internal platforms are logging on to them.

A spokeswoman for Okta said the company is aware of the claims being made, but said: "Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised."

Last month, the FBI was hacked by a group called ShinyHunters, which took personal information about thousands of agents.

In recent days, the Federal Election Commission, which makes public political campaign donation data, was taken offline because of a suspected hacking attempt.

Public backlash to US immigration enforcement has been building as the Trump Administration has pushed a huge increase in arrests and deportations of people suspected of being in the country illegally.

Immigration operations this year have repeatedly turned violent, external, with ICE agents shooting at more than two dozen people and killing at least nine people.

Those killings include the high profile deaths of Alex Pretti and Renee Good, both of whom were shot and killed by ICE agents this year in Minnesota, despite not being the targets of arrests.

Often, ICE agents carry out enforcement actions while their faces are covered by masks and sunglasses. Immigration agents rarely identify themselves, despite being required by law to do so, and US politicians have publicly demanded, external DHS enforces the requirement.

Since President Donald Trump returned to office in 2025, the US has enacted nearly 1 million deportations, external, according to data from the Migration Policy Institute. More than 70% of the deportations have been of people with no criminal record.

World.title: Elon Musk is a 'real genius', Putin says after satellite talks with SpaceX boss
World.content:
Elon Musk is a "real genius", Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Wednesday after revealing the two are in "close" contact about satellite technology.

The remarks came during the Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow, during which Putin discussed Russia's own satellite internet project Rassvet, which provides internet connections to people from satellites.

"He's a genius, a real genius," Putin said of Musk, according to a translation of his remarks by the BBC. "We are in close contact with our American partners, including Mr. Musk."

Starlink is part of Musk's company SpaceX. The company did not respond to a request for comment.

Putin added that it was important for Russia to be in contact with Musk so Rassvet and Starlink satellites do not "interfere with each other in orbit".

"We and our American partners value this mutually, and despite all the political questions, we are working hard," he said.

Starlink has launched roughly 13,000 of its satellites, according to the company. By contrast there are only a couple of dozen Rassvet satellites currently in orbit, according to online satellite trackers.

The Russian Embassy in South Africa said on Wednesday Rassvet is "Russia's Starlink alternative" and "marks only the country's first steps in this field".

"Russia maintains close contacts with the US on space, including with Elon Musk," the embassy wrote.

Putin's comments about Rassvet and Starlink were made as the US and Russia appear to be growing closer, even as it approaches five years since Putin's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Ukraine relied on Starlink internet in its efforts to keep Russia's forces at bay. But its military last week suddenly suffered Starlink connectivity problems, something Musk has admitted SpaceX did intentionally.

US President Donald Trump earlier this month said he'd struck a deal with Russia to import diesel in an effort to lower gas prices that have skyrocketed due to the US war with Iran.

Then Trump waived certain sanctions against Russia that were set to take effect.

Not long after, a US citizen was released from Russian custody, with US envoy Steve Witkoff referring to Putin as a "humanitarian".

Musk was born in South Africa and then immigrated to Canada before settling in the US. All of his business ventures, including Tesla, SpaceX and Starlink, are based in America, with most operating out of California and Texas.

The billionaire, and off and on again trillionaire, has been one of the biggest political allies and financiers of Trump and other Republican US politicians.

World.title: Oshiomhole defends Tinubu’s borrowing plan, says loans will fund infrastructure
World.content:
Adams Oshiomhole, the Senator representing Edo North, has defended President Bola Tinubu’s latest borrowing request, saying the proposed loans are intended to address Nigeria’s infrastructure deficits, not to pay salaries or fund recurrent expenditure.

Mr Oshiomhole, a former governor of Edo State, said the proposed borrowing would help the government invest in critical infrastructure and stimulate economic growth.

He spoke during an interview on TVC’s Beyond the Headline, where he said the president’s request had been formally presented to the Senate and referred to the Committee on Local and Foreign Debts for consideration.

Mr Oshiomhole argued that Nigeria needed sustained investment in infrastructure to achieve economic growth and break what he described as a vicious cycle of underdevelopment.

“I think this is what this additional payment is meant to address,” he said, defending the need for borrowing to finance projects the government could not immediately fund from available revenue.

He said Nigeria could not afford to delay essential investments until it had enough money to finance them entirely from its own resources.

“We are here now and we have to be able to borrow,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The senator also argued that Nigeria’s ability to access loans from foreign sources reflected some level of credibility, adding that borrowing in foreign currencies could help prevent local businesses from being crowded out of the domestic credit market.

He said the government had alternatives: abandon borrowing and slow infrastructure development or obtain long-term loans to finance projects that could expand the economy and generate the resources needed to repay the debt.

“Stop borrowing, stop development, stop funding infrastructure, keep lamenting what they’ve done there, or take the bold step, get long-term loans that are sustainable, grow the economy in a manner that it will generate enough prosperity to settle those loans,” he said.

Mr Oshiomhole stressed that the president’s letter made clear that the proposed loans were not intended to finance salaries, allowances or other recurrent expenses.

He, however, declined to pre-empt the Senate committee’s deliberations, saying the committee would examine the request and present its recommendations to the chamber for debate.

He expressed confidence that the Senate would support the proposal, arguing that lawmakers could not consistently complain about Nigeria’s poor road infrastructure while opposing borrowing intended to repair and expand the road network.

Mr Oshiomhole said Nigeria’s large landmass made it difficult to rely solely on road transportation and argued that infrastructure investment was necessary to connect economic zones, transport finished goods to consumers and move raw materials to industrial locations.

Oshiomhole replies Atiku

The senator also responded to criticism of the borrowing plan by former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, saying the opposition politician was entitled to his opinion.

He said criticism of the government was part of democracy and that opposition lawmakers in the Senate should use their positions to seek explanations about the proposed loans.

Mr Oshiomhole said the government should provide comprehensive answers to questions raised about the borrowing plan but warned that such scrutiny should not obstruct development.

He added that borrowing was not new to Nigeria and said other countries, including the United Kingdom and the United States, also faced debates over rising public debt.

The senator said he was familiar with discussions about public borrowing in other countries and maintained that governments had to make difficult economic decisions to meet their development needs.

He argued that opposition parties in Nigeria often rejected government policies even when they considered some aspects necessary, although he said he did not fault Atiku for questioning the proposal.

Mr Oshiomhole also defended his own record of speaking against government decisions when he disagreed with them, saying his loyalty to the ruling party did not prevent him from criticising policies he considered wrong.

He said accountability remained central to democracy and that the government had a responsibility to explain its intentions to Nigerians.

However, he maintained that the need for explanations should not delay governance or infrastructure development.

Power sector investment

Mr Oshiomhole said reliable electricity was particularly important to the Tinubu administration’s ambition to attract industries and revive manufacturing.

He argued that manufacturers would not return to Nigeria in significant numbers if they continued to depend on generators because of inadequate power supply.

The senator also questioned Atiku’s record on the privatisation of the power sector and criticised the handling of public funds allocated to electricity under the administration in which the former vice-president served.

Mr Oshiomhole alleged that $16 billion spent on the power sector during that period had not delivered the expected results.

He argued that the current government was now faced with the need to borrow to address infrastructure problems that previous administrations had failed to resolve.

Comparing the proposed borrowing with the money spent on power under the former administration, he said inflation and changes in the value of money meant the proposed $22 billion was not worth as much in real terms as the $16 billion previously spent.

Mr Oshiomhole also cited China as an example of a country that achieved sustained economic growth through long-term infrastructure investment, including roads, railways and electricity.

He said such infrastructure was essential to reducing poverty and creating jobs.

The lawmaker said Nigeria’s central challenge is to create enough employment opportunities to ensure that citizens benefit from the economic reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration, which he said the opposition was seeking to reverse.

World.title: Nature is making a comeback, but the world must move faster to meet restoration targets – UN Report
World.content:
A UN report published today finds that 252 million hectares (ha) across 149 countries are being restored, creating more than one million green jobs – the largest documented global restoration effort to date.

To reach 2030 commitments, action must rapidly increase with a particular focus on freshwater, marine and coastal ecosystems, and annual restoration finance must more than quadruple. This investment could generate up to an estimated 32 million new jobs worldwide by 2030.

The report, Nature’s comeback – scaling ecosystem restoration for people and planet, is published midway through the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration (2021–2030). It provides the first-ever comprehensive global assessment of progress against commitments to restore around one billion hectares and the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework target to ensure that by 2030, at least 30 per cent of degraded terrestrial, freshwater, marine, and coastal ecosystems are under effective restoration.

Co-published by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), the UN Environment Programme (UNEP), and the Secretariat of the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), the report was launched at a high-level event during the UN Biodiversity Conference (COP17). The event awarded five outstanding initiatives in China, Colombia, Ethiopia, Italy and the United States as UN World Restoration Flagships – highlighting successful restoration drives around the world.

“Today, we are witnessing the makings of one of the largest movements for nature in recorded history,” said Inger Andersen, Executive Director of UNEP. “Yet, at the halfway point of the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration, we are still not restoring nature at the scale or speed required. By 2030, we must turn inspiring initiatives into systemwide action – shifting to restoration economies that protect what remains and restore what has been degraded.”

The global movement to restore nature extends beyond national programmes to cities, schools, businesses, and community initiatives. Since the start of the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration, its partnership network has grown to more than 300 organizations across all regions.

“Five years into the UN Decade, the message is clear: restoration works,” said FAO Director-General QU Dongyu. “The challenges are to make restoration an integral part of the sustainable management of land, water and natural resources, and to have a coherent transformation of agrifood systems. Healthy ecosystems are vital for better production, better nutrition, a better environment, and a better life for all, leaving no one behind.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Ecosystem restoration is essential for food and water security, climate resilience, jobs, and well-being. Across all ecosystems, Asia accounts for 192.2 million ha of the total documented area under restoration, followed by Africa with 36.3 million ha, Europe with 9.1 million ha, North and Central America with 5.8 million ha, South America with 5.4 million ha and Oceania with 3.2 million ha. These differences do not rank restoration performance – they reflect the scale of restoration activity, regional land area, and capacities in monitoring and reporting.

Research indicates that restoring just 15 per cent of global priority areas could capture and store 30 per cent of carbon dioxide (CO₂) equivalent emissions since the industrial revolution and help avoid 60 per cent of species extinctions. Documented successes among UN World Restoration Flagships include the recovery of species ranging from mountain gorillas in East Africa and jaguars in Brazil, to snow leopards in Kyrgyzstan and Ganges River dolphins in India.

Restoration progress is variable across ecosystems and countries, according to the report. Restoration of terrestrial ecosystems has reached nearly half the global target to have 30 percent of degraded terrestrial ecosystems under restoration by 2030. China reports the largest terrestrial area under restoration (127.4 million ha), while substantial areas are also documented in Mongolia and Kazakhstan.

Progress is far more limited in freshwater, marine and coastal ecosystems, which are also degrading at the fastest rates. Only 11 million ha of freshwater ecosystems and 5.7 million ha of marine and coastal ecosystems across 62 and 46 countries, respectively, are documented as being under restoration. However, momentum is growing: the share of Parties reporting implemented wetland restoration or rehabilitation programmes has risen from 8 per cent to 54 per cent since 2022. The report cautions that the limited reporting for aquatic restoration may result in an underestimation.

Restoring nature for the resilience and wellbeing of people will require sustained political commitment and a more than fourfold increase in annual restoration finance, from US$64 billion to US$296 billion by 2030. The largest estimated annual investment needs are in agroforestry (US$87 billion), restorative reforestation (US$52 billion), peatland restoration (US$44 billion) and seagrass restoration (US$28 billion).

“We cannot expect to fix nature with one hand while we destroy it with the other one,” said Astrid Schomaker, Executive Secretary of the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) Secretariat. “Governments must address the drivers of ecosystem degradation and invest in monitoring mechanisms to ensure the durability of the restoration movement to date.”

Beyond 2030, restoration must be sustained long enough to enable recovery of ecosystem integrity and biodiversity while delivering lasting benefits for communities. Secure tenure, meaningful participation and respect for the rights, knowledge, and leadership of Indigenous Peoples and other rights-holders are essential to durable restoration.

The report argues that the next phase of the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration must move beyond individual projects towards “restoration economies” capable of sustaining ecological recovery, livelihoods, and long-term value at scale.

Data sets underpinning the report were compiled from government-endorsed data submitted through global reporting processes and data reported by restoration initiatives to FAO’s Framework for Ecosystem Restoration Monitoring (FERM).

About the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration

The UN General Assembly has declared 2021–2030 a UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration. Led by the UN Environment Programme and the Food and Agriculture Organization of the UN, together with the support of partners, it is designed to prevent, halt, and reverse the loss and degradation of ecosystems worldwide. It aims to revive billions of hectares, covering terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems. A global call to action, the UN Decade draws together political support, scientific research, and financial muscle to massively scale up restoration.

About the UN World Restoration Flagships

Countries have already promised to restore 1 billion hectares – an area larger than China – as part of their commitments to the Paris Agreement, Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, the Land Degradation Neutrality targets and the Bonn Challenge. With the World Restoration Flagships, the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration is honouring some of the best examples of large-scale and long-term ecosystem restoration in any country or region, embodying the 10 Restoration Principles of the UN Decade. Progress of all World Restoration Flagships will be transparently monitored through the Framework for Ecosystem Restoration Monitoring, the UN Decade’s platform for keeping track of global restoration efforts.

About the UN Environment Programme (UNEP)

UNEP is the leading global voice on the environment. It provides leadership and encourages partnership in caring for the environment by inspiring, informing and enabling nations and peoples to improve their quality of life without compromising that of future generations.

About the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)

FAO is a specialized agency of the United Nations that leads international efforts to defeat hunger. It aims to achieve food security for all and make sure that people have regular access to enough high-quality food to lead active healthy lives. With over 194 Members, FAO works in over 130 countries worldwide.

World.title: JUST IN: Kano anti-drug task force arrests fleeing suspect in Rivers State
World.content:
The Kano State Multi-Agency Task Force on Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking has arrested an alleged notorious gang leader, known as “Malam Keya,” in Port Harcourt, Rivers State.

​Announcing the arrest on Thursday, the Chairman of the Task Force, Muhuyi Magaji, said the suspect has been transferred to Kano to face prosecution.

​According to Mr Magaji, the suspect fled the state after being declared wanted over violent gang clashes that claimed several lives.

“The Kano State Multi-Agency Task Force on Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking has arrested Ishaq Lawan Ibrahim, popularly known as “Malam Keya”, a 27-year-old man from Yelwa in Dala Local Government Area, in Port Harcourt, Rivers State. He is suspected of playing a leading role in the violent gang clashes that have disturbed the peace of parts of Kano State.

“Malam Keya is alleged to be a gang leader who orchestrated and sponsored the violence, fuelling and funding the hoodlums behind attacks that claimed lives and left residents of Dala Local Government living in fear.

“The suspect reportedly fled Kano after the Task Force intensified security operations in communities affected by gang violence, including Jakara, Madigawa, Yalwa, Sanka, Kul Kul, Dogon Nama, Kuka Bulukiya, Dala, Shatsari and Dandalin Turawa. Acting on credible intelligence, operatives tracked him to Port Harcourt, where he was apprehended in an operation led by the Task Force’s Head of Operations, CSP Bashir Gwadabe. He has since been brought back to Kano”, Mr Magaji said.

“Let me assure you that those who bankroll violence should know that no distance, and no hiding place, will protect them. This arrest is only the beginning. We will not rest until peace is fully restored.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the arrest, made outside Kano State, shows the Task Force’s determination to pursue wanted suspects beyond the state’s boundaries.

“The Task Force assures the people of Kano State that it will not relent in dismantling criminal gangs, their sponsors and their drug supply networks.

“The Task Force appreciates the support of the Kano State Police Command, the Rivers State Police Command and all other law enforcement agencies for their commitment to the success of the operation.”

Kano’s war against illicit drugs

The Kano State Government established the Multi-Agency Task Force on Drug Abuse and Illicit Substances as an inter-agency coalition comprising security outfits, regulatory bodies, and civil society groups.

The task force is mandated to interdict, raid, and dismantle major distribution hubs, warehouses, and open markets used for illegal drug sales across the 44 local government areas of Kano State.

It is also mandated to implement strict anti-drug laws, including the immediate confiscation and sealing of properties or structures utilised for storing, packaging, or selling illicit substances.

World.title: ‘No Nigerian asset has been sold to US’ — Alake
World.content:
The Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, has dismissed reports that Nigeria sold $700 billion worth of solid minerals to the United States, insisting that the bilateral agreement between both countries does not involve the sale or transfer of Nigeria’s mineral assets.

Mr Alake made the clarification during the inauguration of the Nigeria-United States Committee on Strategic Cooperation in the Solid Minerals Sector in Abuja.

“There is no sale of any Nigerian asset. There’s nothing exchanging hands,” he said.

The minister explained that the agreement signed by Nigeria and the US was a government-to-government framework designed to connect American investors with Nigerian businesses, rather than transfer ownership of the country’s natural resources to foreign interests.

“We created a platform to facilitate mingling of US investment ventures with Nigeria’s local operators,” he added.

Mr Alake said the partnership was intended to attract capital, promote technology transfer, expand local mineral processing and create jobs as the Federal Government seeks to reduce Nigeria’s dependence on crude oil.

The committee’s inauguration followed the signing of a strategic cooperation framework by Nigeria and the US in New York in September, on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

What the $700bn figure means

The clarification follows the announcement of the agreement, which described Nigeria’s mineral resources as being worth an estimated $700 billion.

The figure refers to the estimated value of Nigeria’s mineral resources, according to the government, not the value of minerals sold to the US or a confirmed investment commitment from the American government.

The framework was signed by Mr Alake and US Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau in New York on 23 September. It provides for cooperation in geological data and exploration, mineral development and processing, infrastructure and technical capacity-building.

The agreement is expected to provide a platform for American investors to partner with Nigerian mining companies and other local operators.

Mr Alake said the government wanted to change a pattern in which resource-rich countries export raw materials while other countries capture more of the value through processing and manufacturing.

“We have the resources, the critical elements the world needs to transit to clean energy. So we are creating a new paradigm: you bring your capital, expertise and technology to match with our natural resources and create a win-win situation. The investor gains, Nigeria gains,” he explained.

He added that the government wanted Nigeria to retain more economic value from its mineral resources through local processing and industrial development.

Local processing takes centre stage

Mr Alake said local processing had become a key requirement for investors seeking mineral titles, as the government sought to discourage the extraction and export of raw minerals without sufficient value addition.

Nigeria has deposits of minerals including lithium, gold, iron ore, limestone and tin. However, the sector remains underdeveloped compared with the country’s oil industry, limiting its contribution to exports, industrial growth and government revenue.

The government has increasingly identified solid minerals as an avenue for diversifying the economy, attracting foreign investment and creating employment outside the oil sector.

Mr Alake said the policy was encouraging investment in mineral-processing facilities, including a lithium processing plant in Nasarawa State that the government has described as one of the largest of its kind in West Africa.

He said the Nigeria-US partnership could help match the country’s mineral resources with the capital, technology and expertise needed to develop a stronger mining industry.

The agreement comes amid global competition to secure critical minerals used in electric vehicle batteries, renewable energy systems and other advanced technologies. Countries are seeking to diversify their supply chains as demand for these materials grows.

Mr Alake charged members of the newly inaugurated committee to identify viable investment opportunities and ensure that the agreement produced measurable outcomes.

He said the committee’s work was important to President Bola Tinubu’s target of building a $1 trillion economy.

The minister said the government was determined to ensure that mineral wealth translated into tangible economic benefits for Nigerians rather than remain an underutilised resource.

In his remarks, the ministry’s Permanent Secretary, Faruk Yusuf Yabo, said the committee would provide a structured platform for turning bilateral discussions into practical cooperation and investment.

Jonathan Baas, an economic officer at the US Embassy in Nigeria, said Washington was prioritising energy, artificial intelligence and critical minerals in its international economic engagements.

He explained that the US was seeking partnerships that would strengthen critical mineral supply chains while allowing resource-producing countries to benefit from the economic opportunities created.

The Managing Director of the Nigeria Solid Minerals Company, Martins Imonitie, also said the committee would coordinate implementation, facilitate investment and monitor progress towards the objectives of the cooperation framework.

Mr Alake said the government would judge the partnership by its ability to generate investment, strengthen local industries and create jobs, rather than by the estimated value of Nigeria’s mineral resources alone.

World.title: U-17 WWC: Five key players to watch as Flamingos face Mexico in Round of 16
World.content:
Nigeria’s Flamingos face a defining test against Mexico in the Round of 16 of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup on Thursday, with a place in the quarter-finals at stake and little room for mistakes.

Head coach Akeem Busari’s side will draw confidence from their impressive 3-1 victory over defending champions DPR Korea, a result that demonstrated their attacking quality and ability to rise to the occasion against elite opposition.

Mexico, however, will present a different challenge. After recovering from an opening defeat to Spain, the North Americans defeated Chile and Australia to secure their place in the knockout stage.

With both teams chasing a quarter-final ticket, individual brilliance could prove decisive. From Nigeria’s goal scorers and creative midfielders to Mexico’s experienced captain and chief provider, these five players could have a major say in Thursday’s showdown.

Oluwakemi Adegbuyi — Nigeria

Adegbuyi has emerged as one of Nigeria’s most important attacking threats in Morocco, showing a knack for finding the right spaces and delivering when the Flamingos need a breakthrough.

The forward scored in Nigeria’s 2-0 victory over Puerto Rico before opening the scoring against DPR Korea, helping set the tone for the memorable win over the defending champions.

Her ability to find scoring positions and finish chances makes her a player Mexico cannot afford to overlook. Against a Mexican defence that conceded three goals during the group stage, Adegbuyi could prove dangerous if Nigeria create opportunities around the penalty area.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The challenge for the Nigerian forward will be to stay sharp in front of goal and make the most of her teammates’ service. In a knockout fixture where chances may be limited, her finishing could be crucial to the Flamingos’ quarter-final ambitions.

Citlalli Reyes — Mexico

If Nigeria are looking for the player who could pose the greatest threat to their hopes, Mexico captain Citlalli Reyes deserves close attention.

Reyes has already demonstrated her importance to the Mexican side, scoring against Chile and netting the decisive goal in their 1-0 victory over Australia. Her contribution in both matches underlines her ability to influence tight contests.

The captain also made history against Australia by recording her 13th appearance at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, becoming the competition’s all-time appearance leader. That experience could be valuable in a high-pressure knockout encounter.

Nigeria’s defensive organisation will be tested if Reyes is allowed to receive the ball freely in dangerous areas. The Flamingos must limit her space, track her movement and prevent her from dictating Mexico’s attacking play.

With her experience and goalscoring instincts, Reyes could become the difference-maker if Mexico find a way through Nigeria’s defence.

Oluebube Umejiaku — Nigeria

Umejiaku has made her presence felt at both ends of Nigeria’s attacking play, contributing goals and creating opportunities for her teammates.

The forward scored Nigeria’s only goal in their opening 2-1 defeat to Poland before finding the net again in the 3-1 triumph over DPR Korea. She also provided the assist for Precious Oscar’s goal against Puerto Rico, underlining her ability to contribute beyond scoring.

Her versatility gives Busari another attacking option. Umejiaku can threaten defenders with her movement while also helping create space and opportunities for those around her.

Against Mexico, her combination of finishing and creativity could be particularly valuable. If the Mexicans concentrate on containing Adegbuyi, Umejiaku’s movement and ability to exploit openings could give Nigeria another route to goal.

The Flamingos will need their forward line to work collectively, and Umejiaku’s contribution could be central to that effort.

Bianka Arredondo — Mexico

While Reyes offers Mexico a direct goalscoring threat, Bianka Arredondo provides another important dimension through her creativity and ability to supply teammates.

Arredondo delivered the assists for Mexico’s first two goals in their 3-1 comeback victory over Chile, helping her side recover after conceding the opening goal.

Her performance highlighted her value as a provider who can create opportunities when Mexico needs a breakthrough. Against Nigeria, her ability to pick out runners and deliver decisive passes could test the Flamingos’ defensive structure.

Nigeria will therefore need to pay attention not only to the players arriving in scoring positions but also to those supplying the final ball. If Arredondo is given time and space to operate, Mexico could find opportunities to penetrate the Nigerian back line.

Restricting her influence could be just as important as keeping Reyes quiet, particularly when Mexico attempt to build attacks through combinations in the final third.

Kanyinsola Rodiat Yusuf — Nigeria

From being a super sub to crashing into the first eleven, Yusuf has become one of the exciting stories of Nigeria’s campaign, making an impact through her attacking contribution, left-footed quality and ability to influence matches from midfield.

The midfielder assisted Umejiaku’s goal against Poland before scoring Nigeria’s third goal in their victory over DPR Korea. Her contribution in that crucial encounter further underlined her growing importance to the team.

Yusuf also offers Nigeria a threat from set pieces, giving the Flamingos another potential source of goals in a contest that could be decided by a single moment.

Her ability to arrive in attacking areas could create additional problems for Mexico, especially if their defensive attention is focused on Nigeria’s forwards. From open play or dead-ball situations, Yusuf has the potential to change the course of the match.

For Busari, having a midfielder capable of both creating and finishing chances provides tactical flexibility. For Mexico, keeping Yusuf under control will be another major assignment.

Five players, one Quarter-Final ticket

Nigeria’s meeting with Mexico promises a contest where individual quality must be matched by collective discipline.

Adegbuyi and Umejiaku will be expected to carry the attacking threat, while Yusuf could offer an additional route to goal from midfield. Mexico, meanwhile, will look to Reyes’ experience and goalscoring ability, with Arredondo’s creativity potentially providing the service needed to unlock Nigeria’s defence.

The Flamingos have already shown what they can achieve by defeating DPR Korea, but the knockout stage brings a different kind of pressure. They must turn their attacking promise into goals while remaining alert to Mexico’s threats.

With the quarter-finals within reach, the performances of these five players could go a long way towards determining which side keeps its 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup dream alive.

World.title: Police probe officer filmed assaulting man in Imo
World.content:
The police in Imo State say they have begun investigation into a viral video showing an officer assaulting a man along the Owerri–Orlu Road in the state.

The police spokesperson in the state, Henry Okoye, said in a statement on Wednesday that the incident happened on Tuesday.

The viral clip

The video clip, which has now gone viral on social media, showed the armed officer assaulting the victim while his fellow officers tried to restrain him.

The officer was subsequently seen attempting to cock his rifle while pointing it at the man.

The man, a motorist, later told the officer’s colleagues that the officer stopped him to check his vehicle documents and then demanded “fuel money”, which he declined, prompting the officer to descend on him.

‘We’ve identified the officer’

In Wednesday’s statement, Mr Okoye, a deputy superintendent of police, said the police in the state have identified the officer as Gabriel Utuh, an assistant superintendent of police.

The spokesperson said the officer was the team leader of the Rapid Response Squad patrol team deployed along the Owerri–Orlu Road in the state.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“The circumstances surrounding the incident are being thoroughly investigated, and appropriate disciplinary measures will be taken against any erring officer,” he said.

Mr Okoye assured residents of Imo State that the investigation would be “thorough, impartial and guided by the principles of accountability and professionalism.”

He dropped a mobile phone number and urged the victim to contact the Command’s Complaint Response Unit to assist with the ongoing investigation.

The spokesperson said the Commissioner of Police in Imo State, Audu Bosso, has reiterated the command’s zero tolerance for unprofessional conduct, abuse of authority, and violations of citizens’ fundamental rights.

The police chief also reaffirmed the command’s commitment to accountability, discipline, and professionalism.

Not the first time

Cases of police brutality, extortion, extrajudicial killings and other unprofessional activities in Nigeria have continued despite sanctions by police authorities, such as dismissal from service.

The latest incident occurred less than three weeks after the police authorities ordered the arrest and detention of a police inspector and two personnel of the Imo State Civil Guard Corps over alleged extortion in the state.

Six months ago, the police in Anambra State arrested and detained six senior officers who allegedly tortured and extorted N200,000 from a trader in Onitsha, the commercial hub of the South-eastern state.

In February, three officers were dismissed over alleged kidnapping, extorting N1.7 million and car snatching in Imo, another state in the South-east.

Last January, police operatives shot dead a private motorcyclist in Ebonyi State.

In November 2024, police operatives from the Crack Squad in Abakaliki, Ebonyi State, shot dead a labourer and critically injured three others in the state.

A similar incident happened in the same Abakaliki in 2018 when a police officer shot and killed a commercial motorcyclist for allegedly refusing to give him a N50 bribe.

In August 2024, police operatives in Bayelsa State extorted N3 million from a Nigerian man at gunpoint.

The victim later petitioned police authorities, and the officers were arrested.

The police operatives later returned the N3 million to the victim, about three weeks later.

World.title: A Forgotten Bag, Four Gunshots: Sheikh Masussuka’s final evening
World.content:
Sheikh Yahaya Masussuka was preparing to leave his home in Dutsin-Ma, Katsina State, on Monday evening when his wife, Fatima, accompanied him outside.

He was going to teach his Almajirai students. But he had forgotten his bag, and she returned indoors to retrieve it.

Then she heard four gunshots.

“Before I knew what was happening, I heard four gunshots. When I came out, I discovered that he had been shot,” Mrs Yahaya told PUNCH.

The cleric was shot outside his residence in Karambanin Ɗan Abba, Bakin Kasuwa. Adamu Abubakar, described by an associate as his close friend, was also killed.

In another part of Dutsin-Ma, Abdulrahim Sabiu was preparing the studio where Mr Masussuka regularly conducted his evening teaching activities.

Gunfire at Karambanin Ɗan Abba

The police said two armed men riding a motorcycle attacked Mr Masussuka and Mr Abubakar on Monday, 26 October.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The police placed the shooting at about 7.30 p.m. But Aliyu Ladan, a neighbour who had known the cleric for approximately 20 years, recalled that it happened around 8.30 p.m., after the Isha prayer.

Mr Ladan told PREMIUM TIMES that he was returning from the roadside when he saw Mr Masussuka coming out and noticed that a vehicle had been started.

He was near the entrance when he heard several gunshots.

Mr Ladan said he looked towards the scene after the shooting subsided but could not identify the attackers. He was approaching from the south, while the gunfire came from the north, and vehicle headlights obstructed his view.

When he reached the cleric, he found him lying on the ground.

He called for assistance and helped lift Mr Masussuka into a vehicle for evacuation to hospital.

Mr Ladan believed the cleric had died before reaching hospital. The police said an attending doctor pronounced Mr Masussuka and Mr Abubakar dead at the hospital.

The studio at Hayin Gada

At Hayin Gada, a neighbourhood where Mr Masussuka grew up and attended school, Mr Sabiu was expecting him that evening.

A longtime student and associate who had worked closely with the cleric for about two decades, Mr Sabiu said he left his companions at approximately 8.20 p.m. to open the studio.

He switched on the air conditioner and prepared for the evening’s activities.

Mr Masussuka was expected between 8.30 and 8.40 p.m., an arrival time that Ahmad Rufa’i, another close associate, said was consistent with the cleric’s usual routine.

Imran Nasarisu, a student, also recalled that the cleric had been preparing to come to the teaching venue.

The studio was in the same neighbourhood as Bani Adam Academy, where Mr Masussuka had studied. His former teacher, Yahaya Bani Adam, still lived nearby.

While Mr Sabiu waited, a student brought news that Mr Masussuka had been shot.

He went first to the cleric’s residence, where people had gathered, before proceeding to the hospital.

At the hospital

Mr Sabiu said he found Mr Masussuka and Mr Abubakar lying motionless when he arrived at the hospital.

Mr Rufa’i, who had also received news of the shooting, went there separately.

He later accompanied Mr Masussuka’s body to Katsina, the state capital. He recalled arriving at approximately 12.30 a.m. and remaining there until around 4 a.m.

An associate familiar with the aftermath also reported that a driver identified as Suleiman and a woman sustained injuries during the incident.

The associate described damage to a Toyota RAV4, including broken glass and apparent bullet impacts.

PREMIUM TIMES could not independently establish the extent of those reported injuries or examine the vehicle. The police’s initial statement did not provide details about additional casualties.

A former pupil, a respected neighbour

When PREMIUM TIMES visited Hayin Gada after the killing, mourners had gathered in the neighbourhood where Mr Masussuka spent part of his early life.

Among those grieving was Mr Bani Adam, his former teacher.

Mr Bani Adam remembered Mr Masussuka as a pupil and spoke of his death in terms of religious acceptance. He said he did not personally suspect anyone of responsibility.

In Karambanin Ɗan Abba, Mr Ladan remembered a man he had known for approximately two decades.

He described the cleric as helpful, compassionate and respectful towards his neighbours.

Mr Ladan said residents were troubled by the shooting, particularly because it occurred within their own neighbourhood.

He also described Mr Abubakar as a scholar and someone regarded as a trusted friend of Sheikh Masussuka.

According to Mr Ladan, Mr Abubakar was said to be from a place called Nasarawa and to have studied with the cleric. But the neighbour acknowledged he did not know Mr Abubakar well and could not personally confirm those details.

For the cleric’s students, the killing interrupted work they had expected him to continue.

Mr Sabiu said Mr Masussuka had completed a Qur’anic commentary known as Tafsir al-Quran bil-Quran and was planning a gathering involving people from different religious backgrounds.

Mr Rufa’i also recalled his ambition to establish a university.

Ansaru’s claim, police investigation

Following the killing, the extremist group Ansaru claimed responsibility for the attack, as previously reported by PREMIUM TIMES.

The claim has not been independently authenticated, and the police have not publicly confirmed the identity of the attackers.

In a statement issued after the shooting, police spokesperson Abubakar Sadiq Aliyu said the Commissioner of Police, Ali Fage, had ordered tactical and operational teams to investigate the killings and pursue those responsible.

President Bola Tinubu also condemned the killings and directed a thorough investigation.

At the time of this report, PREMIUM TIMES had not independently confirmed any arrest in connection with the attack.

At the Hayin Gada studio, Abdulrahim Sabiu had opened the premises and switched on the air conditioner ahead of Sheikh Masussuka’s expected arrival.

The teacher never came.

World.title: Reps summon Navy, Police, Customs, others over recovered assets
World.content:
The House of Representatives has summoned five government agencies to appear before its Sub-Committee on Public Assets on 2 November as part of an investigation into how seized, forfeited, and recovered assets are managed in Nigeria.

The agencies are the Nigerian Navy, Nigeria Police Force, Nigeria Customs Service, Nigeria Immigration Service and the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA).

The committee is seeking to establish a comprehensive record of recovered assets held by government institutions, develop a unified digital registry and identify gaps in the systems for documenting, managing and disposing of such properties.

The chairman of the sub-committee, Ibe Osonwa, who represents Arochukwu/Ohafia Federal Constituency of Abia State, announced the date during the panel’s inaugural meeting in Abuja.

Mr Osonwa said the investigation was necessary amid longstanding concerns about transparency, coordination among government agencies, and accountability in handling assets recovered through law enforcement operations and other statutory processes.

“Across various administrations, questions have persisted regarding transparency, coordination, and the integrity of processes governing assets seized or forfeited through anti-corruption efforts, criminal justice actions, and administrative enforcement,” he said.

The lawmaker said the concerns went beyond administrative shortcomings, warning that the handling of recovered assets had implications for public trust, institutional credibility and the effectiveness of Nigeria’s anti-corruption framework.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“These concerns are not merely technical; they strike at the heart of public trust, institutional credibility, and the effectiveness of Nigeria’s anti-corruption architecture,” he added.

According to him, the sub-committee has been mandated to conduct a comprehensive audit to establish an accurate, verifiable record of assets seized, forfeited, or recovered and held, controlled, or managed by relevant government institutions.

The exercise is expected to establish the status of the assets, clarify their custody and management, and determine how they are eventually disposed of or deployed for public use.

Mr Osonwa identified the proposed unified digital registry as a key component of the investigation, explaining that it would centralise asset records, improve information-sharing among agencies and address inconsistencies and duplication in existing documentation.

The registry would also enable relevant institutions to track assets from seizure or forfeiture through custody, management and eventual disposal or transfer.

The committee plans to review existing accountability mechanisms and recommend reforms to align asset management practices with applicable laws and international best practices.

“The sub-committee has the opportunity to recommend reforms that will close long-standing loopholes, modernise asset management systems, and reinforce Nigeria’s commitment to transparency and responsible stewardship,” Mr Osonwa said.

He added that the ultimate objective was to ensure that assets recovered through lawful processes were managed responsibly and used in ways that benefit the public.

“Our work can help ensure that recovered assets truly serve the public interest—whether through restitution, reinvestment, or national development priorities,” he said.

The chairman formally announced 2 November as the date for the agencies to appear following a motion moved by Omosede Igbinedion and supported by other members of the sub-committee.

“We expect all these agencies: Nigerian Navy, Nigeria Customs Service, the Nigeria Immigration Service, the Nigeria Police and NMDPRA, and see them here on the 2nd of November,” he said.

The agencies are expected to provide information on their respective roles in the seizure, recovery, custody and management of assets, as well as the procedures they use to document and account for such properties.

Mr Osonwa urged sub-committee members to approach the assignment with diligence, objectivity, and a strong sense of national responsibility.

He expressed confidence that the investigation would produce recommendations to strengthen transparency, improve coordination among government institutions and promote accountability in the management of recovered assets.

World.title: Breaking: Court sacks Uzodinma as APC senatorial candidate for Imo West
World.content:
Governor Hope Uzodimma

…orders INEC to recognise ex-Gov Okorocha

By Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja

The Federal High Court in Abuja on Thursday nullified the emergence of Governor Hope Uzodinma as candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) for the Imo West Senatorial election slated for January 16, 2027.

The court, in a judgment delivered by Justice Obiora Egwuatu, held that evidence before it established that Governor Uzodinma was not the valid winner of the primary election the APC conducted in the senatorial zone on May 18, which was monitored by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

According to the court, it was a former governor of the state, Senator Rochas Okorocha, who garnered the highest number of votes cast at the primary election and therefore ought to have been nominated by the party.
