Consequently, Justice Egwuatu ordered INEC to forthwith recognise Senator Okorocha and publish his name as the authentic candidate of the APC for the senatorial poll.

It further issued an order barring Governor Uzodinma from presenting himself as the candidate of the APC for the election.

World.title: Iran Guards says three tankers on fire after hitting mines in Hormuz
World.content:
Vessels transit the Strait of Hormuz off Bandar Abbas in southern Iran on August 10, 2026. The US President signalled on August 9 that he was prepared to let economic pressure mount against Iran, apparently backing away from more military strikes after Tehran issued a list of demands for opening the Strait of Hormuz. His remarks came after Iran issued over the weekend a list of conditions to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which has remained largely closed since the start of the Middle East war in late February. (Photo by ATTA KENARE / AFP) /

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said on Thursday that three oil tankers had caught fire after hitting mines while attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz.

“Over the past 24 hours, three violating oil tankers exploded and caught fire after striking mines while attempting to pass through the unauthorised southern route of the Strait of Hormuz,” the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said in a statement.

The vessels had “switched off all their radar and navigation systems” and disregarded warnings from the IRGC navy, the statement said.

It was not immediately clear when the incidents occurred or which flags the tankers were flying.

Since the outbreak of the war on February 28, Iran has severely restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil and gas consumption.

The United States has in response imposed a blockade on Iranian ports.

Iran’s armed forces have repeatedly accused US Central Command (CENTCOM), which oversees US military operations in the region, of encouraging vessels to use a southern corridor near the Omani coast that Tehran considers unauthorised.

“The IRGC Navy states that the unauthorised route through the Strait of Hormuz is mined, and that vessel owners and crews are responsible for transiting these routes and should not pay attention to CENTCOM’s delusions on social media,” the statement said.

Earlier on Thursday, the British maritime agency UKMTO said it had received a report of a ship on fire in the strait but gave no details about the cause or any casualties.

It was not immediately clear if it was one of the three ships referred to by the Guards.

The organisation also said it had captured a US reconnaissance drone during an operation in the Strait of Hormuz in a separate statement.

“The IRGC Navy announced that its electronic warfare unit had successfully captured a US MQM-170 drone during an offensive operation in the western Strait of Hormuz,” the statement said.

World.title: ECB President Christine Lagarde to step down in February 2027
World.content:
(FILES) European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde addresses a press conference on the Eurozone’s monetary policy, at the central bank’s headquarters in Frankfurt am Main, western Germany, on June 11, 2026. Christine Lagarde is to step down as President of the ECB on February 7, 2027, it was announced on October 30, 2026. (Photo by Kirill KUDRYAVTSEV / AFP)

European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde will step down in February 2027, several months before her term expires in October next year, the Frankfurt-based institution said Thursday.

“European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde today informed the Governing Council and the president of the European Council Antonio Costa that she will step down from her position on 7 February 2027,” the ECB said in a statement.

AFP

World.title: NFF warned me against inviting Mikel, Enyeama, Emenike — Oliseh
World.content:
By Ayobami Okerinde

Former Super Eagles coach, Sunday Oliseh, has revealed that the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) warned him against inviting John Obi Mikel, Vincent Enyeama and Emmanuel Emenike to the national team when he took charge, describing the trio as players who were causing problems for the federation.

Oliseh, speaking on The Play Zone Podcast, however, said he regretted not heeding the warning, recalling his efforts to engage the players individually and resolve issues surrounding their involvement with the national team.

“I regret not having listened to the NFF. Because when I took over the job, the first thing NFF told me was to stop inviting three of them (Mikel, Enyeama and Emenike) because they were chaotic to the NFF,” he said.

Oliseh recalled travelling from Belgium to France to meet Enyeama, who was playing for Lille at the time, saying he held discussions with the former Super Eagles captain and clarified matters with him.

He said he also travelled to London at his own expense to meet Mikel and Victor Moses, who were both playing in England at the time, but was disappointed when Mikel failed to attend the scheduled meeting.

“I did the same thing for Obi Mikel. With my own money, not the NFF money, I went to the UK, sent a message to the clubs, sent a message to him (Mikel), sent message not only to him but also to Victor Moses, gave them an appointment at a bar that was accessible in the heart of London, with my assistant coach, for two of them to come and have meeting.

“Now, of the two of them, who did not come to the meeting? Obi Mikel did not come to the meeting. Victor Moses came. Obi Mikel did not even respond to the WhatsApp message,” he said.

The former midfielder suggested that Mikel might have considered himself bigger than the national team coach because he was playing for a major club.

“Maybe because he’ll say, ‘I play for this big club now,’ but you see, that’s why they say sometimes Sunday (Oliseh) is direct. Where did you play that I did not play? What did you play that I did not play?

“Even though the coach was not a footballer or not as big as you, the fact that they’ve given him that title ‘national team coach’, means you have to respect the position he’s holding,” Oliseh added.

He described Mikel’s failure to attend the meeting as one of the biggest insults he had experienced but said he did not take the incident personally.

According to Oliseh, Moses used the meeting to explain the issues troubling him about the national team, including some experiences Oliseh said he could relate to.

Oliseh also spoke positively about Emenike, saying his experience working with the former striker contradicted what he had initially been told about him.

He described Emenike as a gentleman and a respectful player, adding that he was among the greatest footballers he worked with and also credited Emenike’s influence as an important factor in Nigeria’s triumph at the 2013 Africa Cup of Nations.

Current Super Eagles lack quality

In a separate remark on the podcast, Oliseh attributed Nigeria’s recent struggles in football to a decline in the quality of players compared with previous generations.

“The reason why we are failing is so obvious that I am embarrassed when I hear people don’t talk about it.

“We are failing because we are not good enough,” he said.

Oliseh argued that earlier generations of Nigerian players competed at a higher level in European football, which, in his view, distinguished them from the current crop of internationals.

He cited former Nigerian stars including Finidi George, Rashidi Yekini, Emmanuel Amuneke, Victor Ikpeba, Taribo West, Celestine Babayaro, Ben Iroha and Tijani Babangida as examples of players who featured for prominent European clubs during their careers.

Oliseh referenced clubs such as Ajax Amsterdam, Borussia Dortmund, AS Monaco, AC Milan, Inter Milan and Chelsea while making his comparison.

He challenged listeners to identify current Super Eagles players at clubs with realistic ambitions of winning the UEFA Conference League, Europe’s third-tier club competition.

“Which of the Nigerian players in the national team now is playing at a team that starts this season to aspire to win the Conference League?” he asked.

“I’m not even going to Champions League or E. Conference League, which is the smallest European title,” Oliseh said.

World.title: Tell Nigerians your real destination, APM challenges Tinubu
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu

By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja

The Allied People’s Movement, APM, has challenged President Bola Tinubu to disclose his actual destination, insisting that he should remain in Nigeria to pray for the country and tackle the hardship facing citizens.

The party argued that Tinubu should address Nigeria’s mounting problems at home rather than embark on a trip, it questioned, alleging that the announced lesser Hajj pilgrimage should not serve as a cover for other activities.

In a statement, APM National Publicity Secretary Abubakar Yusuf questioned the purpose of the President’s trip, insisting that the pilgrimage should not be used to distract from the challenges confronting Nigerians.

“Lesser Hajj involves prayer and supplications, but not an opportunity to do the unusual or as a cover to do other things,” Yusuf said.

Accusing Tinubu’s administration of worsening the hardship in the country, the APM spokesman said the president should stay back and address the problems facing ordinary Nigerians.

“You cannot pray for the problems you have inflicted on ordinary Nigerians, rather than staying here to resolve the heavily burdened, self-contrived problems of the citizens,” he said.

Yusuf also invoked the popular ‘Andrew, check out’ expression, urging Tinubu not to leave the country.

“Let Mr President not behave like ‘Andrew’ of those days, saying President Bola Ahmed Tinubu should not check out,” he said.

Looking ahead to the 2027 presidential election, Yusuf claimed Tinubu could struggle to secure the required 25 per cent of votes in 12 selected states, challenging the president to pay attention to his electoral prospects.

The APM spokesman expressed confidence that the party’s presidential candidate, Seyi Makinde, would defeat Tinubu in 2027, describing him as a workaholic and energetic contender poised to challenge the President’s political dominance in the South-West and across the South.

World.title: ‘This abuse must end’ – Sowore reacts to remand of Doris Ogala
World.content:
Doris Ogala and Chris Okafor

Human rights activist, Omoyele Sowore, has condemned the remand of actress Doris Ogala at the Kirikiri Correctional Centre pending the hearing and determination of her bail application over alleged cyberbullying, cyberstalking and attempted extortion of Pastor Chris Okafor.

Ogala was arraigned Wednesday on three counts by the Office of the Attorney-General of the Federation before Justice Akintayo Aluko of the Federal High Court in Lagos on allegations bordering on the publication of intimate photographs, dissemination of allegedly false electronic messages and threats against the cleric.

The prosecution counsel, Tolulope Mokolu, told the court that between September 2024 and March 2026, Ogala published nude and intimate photographs of Okafor on her social media accounts without his consent. He alleged that the publication was capable of causing annoyance, embarrassment, emotional distress and injury to the cleric’s reputation.

In his reaction on Facebook, Sowore accused the police of weaponising the Cybercrimes Act to serve the interest of “influential figures”.

“Once again, the Nigeria Police Force has deepened its weaponization of the Cybercrimes Act! What kind of society are we becoming? How could anyone be arraigned simply over allegations of having an affair with a pastor? And how could the police actually take such a matter before a Federal High Court judge?

“Even more troubling is that the case has reportedly been brought before Justice Aluko of the Federal High Court in Lagos, a judge whose handling of cases involving pastors raises serious concerns about judicial impartiality. The perception that the police and judiciary are being used to settle personal scores and protect influential religious figures must be confronted.

“The Nigeria Police Force has no business turning private relationships into criminal prosecutions or deploying the Cybercrimes Act as a weapon of intimidation,” he wrote.

Sowore noted that Ogala, as the governorship candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC) in Abia State, deserves the full protection of her constitutional rights, due process, and a fair hearing.

“The police must stop criminalizing private disputes, and the judiciary must never become an instrument of religious influence or personal vendettas. This abuse must end!” he added.

Ogala’s case was adjourned until October 30, 2026, for the hearing of her bail application.

World.title: Alwan Hassan’s comment on appointment scandal not about Tinubu’s ministers – Felix Morka
World.content:
APC National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka.

The National Publicity Secretary of the All Progressives Congress, Felix Morka, has denied allegations that ministers in President Bola Tinubu’s administration paid billions of naira to secure their appointments.

Morka said the ministers were selected based on competence, insisting that no such payments took place under the current administration.

He spoke on Arise News on Wednesday while responding to comments by Alwan Hassan, a spokesperson for the APC Presidential Campaign Council, who alleged that some ministers paid billions of naira to secure their positions and later sought to recover the money after assuming office.

Morka said he had spoken privately with Hassan, who clarified that his comments referred to practices predating the APC-led administration rather than the current government.

“Since that interview, I have had a moment to speak with Alwan to also just, out of curiosity, understand what he was thinking when he made those comments. He explained that what he was referring to was not really about this administration, but he was speaking in a historical context,” Morka said.

“When he came back and said this thing predated the APC, that suggested to me that his frame of thought was really located not in the present, but really in the past.”

He acknowledged that Hassan’s remarks were open to different interpretations, including the suggestion that officials paid for their appointments.

“However, what he said left a lot of ambiguity, which some have suggested that he was speaking about appointments,” Morka said.

The APC spokesman distinguished between lobbying for political appointments and paying money to secure them, describing the latter as unacceptable.

“In all democracies, lobbying for appointments is not something unusual. In the United States, there are firms that contract to lobby for individuals to get appointments to office. Those are usual things that happen in the background prior to appointments,” he said.

“But I think the concern here is when lobbying becomes monetized, where people pay money to authorities or to individuals to influence, to procure appointments. That I think is what is odious, what is really wrong.”

Morka categorically rejected the allegation that ministers in Tinubu’s government paid billions of naira to obtain their positions.

“I can tell you without equivocation that there’s no such thing. It didn’t happen. Our ministers were selected on the basis of the competence,” he said.

He added that Hassan had expressed regret over how his comments were framed and told him that he had intended to discuss the issue in a historical context.

“What I’m saying is that the individual who made these comments, as I told you, I’ve had conversations with him, he’s clarified for me to my satisfaction that he was mud-slung in a moment of — he didn’t frame all of that. It sounded unequivocally clear,” Morka said.

Explaining their conversation, he added: “I had a discussion with him because I was curious to know, ‘did you really mean to say this?’ He said, ‘No, no. That’s not what I meant to say. I may have come up wrong. But actually, what I meant to say was to situate this problem, this thematic, in historical context.’ He said that to me.”

World.title: Mbappe, Real Madrid and La Liga face long road to redemption in China
World.content:
(FILES) Real Madrid’s Spanish forward #10 Kylian Mbappe reacts during the Spanish league football match between Elche CF and Real Madrid CF at Martinez Valero Stadium in Elche on September 15, 2026. Kylian Mbappe was dropped on October 27 by two major brands in China after a video circulated online in which the French football star apparently joked about former leader Mao Zedong. (Photo by JOSE JORDAN / AFP)

Kylian Mbappe, Real Madrid and La Liga have apologised for the superstar striker’s comments about Mao Zedong, but the damage to their reputation in China won’t be easily or quickly repaired, experts say.

The France captain, one of the best footballers on the planet, is at the centre of a major row after a video emerged this week of him appearing to make fun of former leader Mao.

Mbappe talked about being amused by an internet meme of his face photoshopped onto “some guy, think he’s a Chinese dictator”.

Mao remains officially revered as the hero of the communist revolution and founder of the People’s Republic of China.

He is blamed by historians for millions of deaths, but publicly mocking him is taboo, and Mbappe’s remarks saw him become the latest foreign sports figure or entity to infuriate Beijing.

Major Chinese brands cut ties with the 27-year-old, and Spanish top-flight matches will be pulled from state television broadcaster CCTV.

Chinese state media and social media users lined up to lambast Mbappe, although they were left in the dark about what exactly he said.

China has the world’s second-biggest economy and can be hugely lucrative, and within two days the striker, his club Real Madrid, and La Liga all apologised.

A spokesman for China’s foreign ministry said the Beijing government took Mbappe’s apology “seriously”.

– ‘Serious damage’ –

So is that the end of the matter?

“Viewed from a calm, objective and emotion-free standpoint, this is clearly a very damaging incident,” Yan Qiang, a veteran sports commentator, told AFP.

“It causes serious damage to the image of La Liga and Real Madrid in China.

“In the age of the mobile internet things blow up on social media quickly and emotions run high.

“An apology does not necessarily mean the end of the story.

“It’s better to have an apology than no apology at all, but it’s definitely not the end of the story.”

The Mbappe furore and fallout is not an unfamiliar tale.

Various overseas sports leagues or players have found themselves in hot water for comments on topics that are politically sensitive to China.

China effectively cut ties with the NBA in 2019 after then-Houston Rockets general manager Daryl Morey tweeted his support for Hong Kong protesters.

NBA executives said Morey had the right to freedom of expression. In contrast, La Liga immediately distanced itself from what Mbappe said.

The NBA, which along with football is the most popular sport in China, was wiped from CCTV for more than a year.

NBA pre-season matches only returned to China last year.

Australian National University lecturer Debby Chan called the NBA case — and now Mbappe — an illustration of China’s consumer nationalism, where online sentiment and state media converge into “a spiral of outrage”.

NBA commissioner Adam Silver said the league lost “hundreds of millions of dollars” over the split.

– No way back? –

Spanish football also has a lot to lose.

A source within La Liga told AFP that China and the United States alone finance the “majority” of international broadcasting rights, which were valued at 748 million euros ($834 million) for the 2024-25 season.

According to the Real Madrid-affiliated newspaper Marca, the Madrid club generates between 10 and 15 percent of its sales of jerseys and merchandise in China.

Real Madrid also counts Chinese companies among its main sponsors, with Hisense, sports betting firm Kaiyun Sports, and Linglong Tire all featuring prominently.

Adam Zhang, founder of the Beijing-based Key-Solution Sports Consulting, said showing fast and heartfelt remorse was the first step.

“This will influence the decision on whether to continue the broadcast ban and, if so, for how long,” he told AFP.

Sports commentator Yan cast doubt on whether the reputation of Mbappe, whose face has adorned drinks bottles and advertising campaigns in China, can ever fully recover.

“Judging by commercial sponsorships and big ad campaigns he appeared in during the World Cup, he has a huge influence in China,” he said.

“If that influence can’t be sustained there can be no talk of commercial interests, and La Liga and Real Madrid will definitely be badly affected.”

Yan said it was “genuinely hard to predict” what happens next.

“In the short term, I’m certainly not optimistic,” he added.

“If they want to repair their image and the relationship, their future actions and behaviour will be key.”

World.title: Edugist Launches Global First Journalism Beat to Tackle Foundational Learning Crisis
World.content:
Funmi Ogundare

Edugist, an African education newsroom and innovation lab, has launched a dedicated journalism beat on foundational literacy and numeracy (FLN) to strengthen accountability and address the growing crisis of children leaving primary school without basic reading and counting skills.

The Foundational Literacy and Numeracy beat, described by the organisation as the first journalism beat globally dedicated exclusively to the issue, will investigate education policies, government spending, research outcomes and classroom realities affecting children’s acquisition of foundational learning skills.

The initiative comes amid concerns that nearly nine in 10 children in low-income African countries cannot read with understanding by age 10, despite attending school, while an estimated 617 million children globally remain below minimum proficiency levels in reading and Mathematics.

In Nigeria, the majority of children reportedly complete primary education without acquiring the foundational skills required for further learning.

Founder of Edugist, Elvis Boniface, said the initiative was designed to bridge the gap between education research, policymaking and classroom practice, while ensuring that investments in foundational learning produce measurable results.

“Africa has been talking about learning outcomes for decades, but the conversation has largely stayed in conference rooms and donor reports,” Boniface said.

He explained that years of education reporting and the organisation’s involvement in early childhood education development had exposed persistent gaps between research findings, government policies and the experiences of teachers and learners.

“The FLN beat exists to close that gap, to be the journalism layer that the entire FLN ecosystem has been missing,” he stated.

The launch comes as governments and international development organisations increase investments in foundational learning across Africa and other parts of the global south.

In March 2025, the World Bank approved $500 million in HOPE-EDU financing for Nigeria to support education reforms, including improvements in foundational learning.

Other initiatives, including the Foundational Learning Compact, UNICEF’s Foundational Learning Action (FLA) tracker and Teaching at the Right Level Africa, are also working to improve learning outcomes across the continent.

However, Boniface noted that increased funding and policy interventions must be accompanied by independent reporting to track implementation, assess results and ensure that resources reach the children who need them.

“The new beat would extend beyond education sector stakeholders to focus on the millions of children whose learning needs remain unmet.

“We are not launching a beat for the FLN community alone. We are launching it for the 250 million children across the global south who are sitting in classrooms right now and still cannot read. Every policy decision, every research finding, every dollar spent, it either reaches those children or it does not. Our job is to report on why,” the founder stressed.

The FLN beat, he noted, will focus on government policies and budget accountability, evidence of what works in improving learning outcomes, teachers’ experiences in underfunded classrooms and the challenges faced by communities whose children lack essential learning skills.

Edugist, he said, also plans to publish an annual state of FLN in Africa report to document progress, setbacks and persistent challenges in foundational literacy and numeracy across the continent.

As part of the initiative, he also announced Learning Changes Everything, a monthly podcast bringing together researchers, policymakers and classroom teachers to discuss practical solutions to the foundational learning crisis.

The inaugural episode, titled, ‘Can Nigeria Reach Every Child Before Grade 4? ‘, will feature a J-PAL Africa education researcher, the Edo State Commissioner for Education and a grade two teacher from Kano State.

The podcast will be available on Spotify, Apple Podcasts and other major platforms.

World.title: Akpabio Appeals to North to Support Tinubu’s Re-election Bid
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Senate President, Senator Godswill Obot Akpabio, has urged Nigerians, particularly stakeholders across Northern Nigeria, to give their overwhelming support to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and his administration, calling for collective backing for his re-election bid.

He noted that sustained public engagement and support for the administration’s programmes would be crucial to advancing its development agenda.

Akpabio made this appeal while receiving a prestigious Award of Excellence in recognition of his leadership and contributions to Nigeria’s democratic and legislative development at his office in Abuja.

The Senate President, who was honoured by a northern organisation, the Arewa Revival Project (ARP), expressed his appreciation for the recognition, describing it as an encouragement to continue working towards the unity, stability and development of the country.

Akpabio, however, assured the youth of Northern Nigeria of his commitment to supporting initiatives that promote their empowerment, education, skills acquisition, entrepreneurship and economic inclusion.

He stressed that young people must be given meaningful opportunities to participate in national development and contribute to building a stronger Nigeria.

He further called for sustained cooperation among the Federal Government, state governments, community leaders and youth organisations to expand opportunities for young Nigerians, particularly those in the North.

He emphasised that investing in the potential of young people was essential to promoting peace, tackling insecurity and achieving sustainable development.

Presenting the award to Akpabio during a brief ceremony in Abuja, the Project Coordinator of the Arewa Revival Project, Hon. Muttaka Ahmed Ibrahim, said the recognition underscored Arewa’s commitment to celebrating distinguished public service, promoting national unity and encouraging leadership that advances peace, development and the welfare of Nigerians.

Hon. Ibrahim said the award was a mark of appreciation for Akpabio’s contributions to democratic governance and national development.

He also emphasised the need for stronger collaboration among political leaders, community organisations and other stakeholders to address the challenges facing Northern Nigeria, particularly those affecting its young people.

The organisation congratulates the Senate President on receiving the Par-Excellence Award and expresses the hope that the recognition will further strengthen collaboration towards building a peaceful, inclusive and prosperous Nigeria.

World.title: Fowokan Bags Continental Award for Drive Towards Youth, Women Empowerment
World.content:
The Initiative for Positive Influence on African Youth (IPIAY) has conferred a prestigious double honour on the Deputy Vice-President (DVP) of the Chartered Institute of Taxation of Nigeria (CITN), Dr. Titilayo Fowokan, recognizing her as 2026 Pan-African Golden Woman of the Year, alongside her induction as a five star General.

The award ceremony, which held in Abuja, celebrated Fowokan’s years of dedication to youth empowerment, leadership, women and community development across the continent.

In a statement, IPIAY said the recognition reflects its commitment to celebrating individuals whose leadership and contributions support positive change among African youths and promote the development of communities across the continent.

It added that it found Fowokan worthy of the honour having met the standards in areas of leadership, commitment to youth empowerment and contributions to African women and communities over the years.

Reacting, Fowokan described the honour as a call to greater responsibility, pledging to do more across the continent.

“This is a call to more responsibilities of getting African youths out of addiction and vices that have made them a threat to the continent. Certainly, it serves as a reminder to stand alongside the younger generation so they can become the pride of the world. As the youths make a difference and cause positive change in Africa, it transcends other continents,” she expressed.

On her commitments following the recognition, Fowokan identified mentorship, protection of vulnerable people and support for disadvantaged communities as key areas of focus.

“These will require my time and resources as I trust God for his divine enablement,” she added.

The event drew leaders, well-wishers, and youth advocates who praised Fowokan’s consistency in championing causes that elevate women and enable the younger generation.

Organizers noted that her remarkable track record makes her a true role model for a brighter African future.

World.title: UNICEF, IHS Inspect Rivers Oxygen Plant, Seek Solar Power to Boost Production
World.content:
Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) and IHS Towers have inspected the medical oxygen plant at the General Hospital, Eleme, Rivers State, amid calls for solar power installation and additional oxygen cylinders to boost production and ensure sustainability.

The inspection provided an opportunity for the partners to assess the facility’s operations, identify challenges and explore ways to strengthen its capacity to meet the growing demand for medical oxygen in Rivers State and neighbouring states.

During the inspection Wednesday, UNICEF Health Specialist at its Enugu Field Office, Dr. Ifeyinwa Anyanyo, noted that the oxygen plant was established through a partnership involving the Nigerian and Canadian governments, IHS Towers and UNICEF.

Anyanyo further noted that the initiative was part of efforts to address gaps in access to medical oxygen exposed by the COVID-19 pandemic, which prompted the establishment of oxygen plants across different geopolitical zones of the country.

She acknowledged the efforts of the Rivers State Government in managing the facility but noted that there was room for improvement and expansion.

Speaking, the Chief Medical Director of the Rivers State Hospitals Management Board, Dr. Bright Ogbonda, said the plant, inaugurated in August 2023, had significantly improved access to medical oxygen for healthcare facilities in the state and beyond.

He disclosed that the facility was operating below capacity, largely because of inadequate power supply and a shortage of oxygen cylinders.

Ogbonda said: “The plant is not connected to the national grid and relied entirely on diesel-powered generators, making production expensive and limiting its output.”

He called on UNICEF, IHS Towers and other partners to support the installation of solar power and connection to the national grid, stressing that solarisation would significantly reduce operating costs, increase production and improve the plant’s financial sustainability.

According to him, the plant has a lifespan of about 15 years, making it necessary to build sufficient financial reserves to replace the equipment when required and support the establishment of additional facilities.

Ogbonda also identified inadequate oxygen cylinders as another major constraint, explaining that: “Some cylinders supplied to hospitals remained with customers who lacked their own containers, limiting the plant’s ability to serve other facilities.”

He said the management had procured about 50 additional 40-litre oxygen cylinders, which had helped ease the problem, but more were still required.

The medical director added that the plant supplied oxygen at one of the lowest prices in Rivers State, attracting customers from Bayelsa, Imo and other neighbouring areas.

He explained that the facility was established primarily to ensure access to affordable medical oxygen rather than maximise profits.

On security, Ogbonda said measures, including closed-circuit television cameras, reinforced doors and night security, had been introduced to protect the plant against vandalism.

He, however, called for additional security support to safeguard the wider hospital premises.

The plant’s senior operator, ThankGod Epelle, said the facility had an installed production capacity of 18 cubic metres per hour but currently produced about 20 cylinders of 40 litres daily because of power constraints.

Epelle said the high cost of diesel consumed a significant portion of the plant’s revenue, preventing it from meeting the growing demand from public and private hospitals.

He also appealed for solar power and additional cylinders to improve production and distribution.

The oxygen plant was established following a nationwide assessment of medical oxygen needs across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, and was handed over to the Rivers State Government as part of efforts to strengthen healthcare delivery.

World.title: Tompolo Seeks another Term for Tinubu  to Consolidate Reforms
World.content:
High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, has declared support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election, saying the president means well for Nigeria and deserves another four years to consolidate his administration’s reforms.

Tompolo spoke at the inauguration of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in Imo State, where he donated 30 vehicles to support grassroots mobilisation for Tinubu’s re-election.

Represented by the Managing Director of Tantita Security Services Limited, Chief Kestin Pondi, Tompolo said the vehicles and other resources were provided to support Governor Hope Uzodimma and the movement’s campaign activities across the state.

He described Tinubu as a courageous leader who prioritised Nigeria’s interests by embarking on economic reforms from the beginning of his administration in May 2023.

“Our President, President Bola Tinubu, is a very courageous man. A man who puts Nigeria first. A man who loves Nigeria more than he loves himself.

“A man who loves Nigeria more than the office that he is vying for. When he came into office, he did not do the normal calculations that politicians usually do. He came in and said that he wants to reform Nigeria,” Tompolo said.

Relaying Tompolo’ message, Pondi said: “Your Excellency, we have come with vehicles. We have come with resources. These vehicles you have seen, there are 30 of them. We brought them to Imo State to support you in your cause to re-elect President Bola Tinubu.”

He said the movement would work with the governor and other political leaders to take the President’s campaign to households and communities across the state.

Pondi added that the newly inaugurated chapter would be available to support campaign activities whenever required.

“Your Excellency, the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in Imo State is at your beck and call. Anytime you need them, call them. Give them instructions. Tell them how you want them to campaign,” he said.

Speaking at the event, Governor Uzodimma commended Tompolo for providing resources to support the campaign, describing the movement as an important partner in efforts to secure another term for the President.

Uzodimma said his assessment of the Tinubu administration’s performance had convinced him that the President should be given another term to complete his programmes.

“When we preach the Gospel about the All Progressives Congress(APC) government of President Bola Tinubu, we started, we were not many. But as the days go by, the efforts and activities of the government begin to trickle in. Nigerians begin to see the man called Bola Tinubu in his true colour,” he said.

The governor acknowledged that the administration had made progress but still had outstanding tasks to accomplish, adding that continuity would enable Tinubu to complete his work.

“We have assessed the achievements of President Bola Tinubu. And we have seen the good things he brought. We have also seen so many things he is also yet to do.

“And we decided to lead the crusade that will enable him to complete his good work. We have taken that decision,” Uzodimma said.

He described Tompolo as a man whose contributions and resources had helped advance the campaign for the President’s re-election.

Uzodimma also praised the door-to-door strategy, saying it would enable campaigners to communicate the achievements of the Renewed Hope Agenda directly to Nigerians.

“We are partners in progress. We work with you. We do the work. We elect the President,” he said.

Earlier, the National Coordinator of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Sunday Asuku, urged Nigerians to remain patient with the administration, arguing that the economic difficulties associated with its reforms would give way to long-term benefits.

Asuku said Tinubu had laid a foundation for economic development in the past three and a half years and should be allowed another four years to build on it.

“The message we must tell today is simple and short. Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, has sent us to make you understand that things might be rough, but Nigeria is on the right trajectory,” he said.

He maintained that economic reforms often came with temporary difficulties but argued that they were necessary to achieve lasting prosperity.

“Where there is reform, we are expected to go through some pains. But it is a pain that guarantees long-term prosperity. And we can get through for sure,” Asuku said.

He also challenged opposition politicians to explain their records in public office, urging Nigerians to examine their past performances before making electoral decisions.

Asuku called on voters to turn out en masse on January 16, 2027, to vote for Tinubu, adding that the movement would take its message from door to door, town to town and community to community.

In his remarks, Imo State APC Chairman, Chief Austine Onyedebelu highlighted the Federal Government’s economic reforms and the state government’s infrastructure projects, urging party members to take the campaign directly to residents.

He cited the removal of the petrol subsidy, foreign exchange reforms, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund and the increase in the national minimum wage to N70,000 as measures introduced by the Tinubu administration.

World.title: Dagogo: Govt Borrowing Must Be Subjected to Transparent Legislative Scrutiny
World.content:
A former member of the House of Representatives and member of the African Democratic Congress, Dr. Farah Dagogo, in this interview speaks on the constitutional limits of economic policy entrenchment, external loans being taken by the President Bola Tinubu’s government, and sustainable alternatives to a blanket petrol subsidy regime. Adedayo Akinwale brings excerpts:

Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has indicated that the Federal Government intends to pursue a law-backed economic policy framework to prevent future administrations from reversing petrol subsidy removal and tax reforms. What is your position on this proposal?

With due respect, I believe this proposal requires careful constitutional consideration. There is an important distinction between providing a sound statutory foundation for economic policies and attempting to make those policies permanently irreversible by future governments. Under Sections 4, 58 and 59 of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999, legislative powers are vested in the National Assembly and the State Houses of Assembly within their respective constitutional jurisdictions. These provisions also establish the legislative procedures through which bills become law at the federal and state levels.

Where the National Assembly has the requisite legislative competence, it may enact laws governing taxation, petroleum regulation and other matters within its constitutional jurisdiction. Such laws provide legal certainty, establish enforceable obligations and create institutional frameworks for implementation.

However, the fact that a policy has been enacted into law does not make it constitutionally immune from subsequent amendment or repeal. The objective of economic reform should therefore be to establish clear, coherent and predictable rules that encourage investment, strengthen public institutions and promote long-term economic stability. It should not be to remove the lawful legislative discretion of future governments or deny future elected representatives the ability to respond to changing economic circumstances.

Can an Act of the National Assembly then permanently prevent a future government from reversing these policies?

No ordinary Act of the National Assembly can permanently deprive a future National Assembly of its constitutional power to amend or repeal that legislation.

A valid law remains binding until it is amended, repealed, invalidated by a competent court or otherwise ceases to have effect in accordance with the law.

An incoming administration cannot lawfully disregard an existing statute merely because it disagrees with the policy behind it. Equally, a future legislature may amend or repeal an ordinary statute through the constitutionally prescribed legislative process.

That is an essential feature of representative democracy and the rule of law. Consider the Petroleum Industry Act, 2021. It establishes a statutory framework for the petroleum industry, including provisions relating to petroleum pricing and market regulation. Those provisions have legal force, but they are not constitutionally irreversible. The National Assembly may amend the Act in accordance with the applicable legislative procedure.

The same principle applies to taxation. Nigeria’s 2025 tax reform legislation, including the Nigeria Tax Act, 2025 and the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025, provides a statutory basis for significant changes to the country’s tax system.

The new framework took effect from January 1, 2026 in respect of the relevant provisions scheduled to commence on that date. Nevertheless, these laws remain subject to constitutional requirements, judicial interpretation and future legislative amendment. The fundamental distinction is between giving a policy the force of law and making it impossible for a future government to change it. The former is constitutionally permissible within the legislature’s competence; the latter cannot ordinarily be achieved by passing a conventional statute. If the government seeks genuine constitutional entrenchment, it must comply with the applicable amendment procedure under Section 9 of the Constitution, including the required legislative majorities and approvals of State Houses of Assembly, as applicable.

Even constitutional amendments must remain consistent with the Constitution’s own amendment requirements and other applicable constitutional limitations.

My position is that policy continuity should be secured through institutional credibility, transparent implementation, effective oversight, broad stakeholder consultation and demonstrable public benefits—not through an attempt to permanently bind the democratic choices of future administrations.

In a constitutional democracy, no administration should treat its policy preferences as permanently binding on its successors. Equally, no succeeding administration should disregard valid laws at will. Both the executive and the legislature must operate within the Constitution and the rule of law.

President Bola Tinubu has requested National Assembly’s approval for a supplementary external borrowing plan of approximately $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion for 2026–2027. Is the proposed borrowing justified?

The question must be examined from two distinct but related perspectives: economic justification and legal compliance. The reported request, presented to the National Assembly on Tuesday, 27 October 2026, covers proposed external financing for projects and programmes in infrastructure, power, transportation, agriculture, healthcare, education, water supply, security, employment generation and public financial management reforms. The proposal has been referred for legislative scrutiny.

The scale of the proposed financing is substantial, and that alone makes rigorous scrutiny indispensable. However, neither the size of the borrowing nor the government’s stated development objectives is sufficient, in isolation, to establish whether the proposal is economically justified. Borrowing can be a legitimate instrument of national development. Economies require significant investment in electricity, transport infrastructure, healthcare, water systems and other productive assets. Where a project delivers long-term economic and social benefits, financing it over time may be more appropriate than attempting to fund the entire cost from current revenue.

External borrowing may also be justified where the financing terms are competitive, the repayment profile is manageable and the projects generate sufficient economic returns or measurable public benefits. However, borrowing must not become a substitute for fiscal discipline, improved domestic revenue mobilisation, expenditure efficiency or responsible debt management. Before this proposal can be considered prudent, the government must demonstrate that the expected benefits justify the full cost and risks of the financing.

Critical questions must be asked such as, what specific projects will receive the funds? How much is allocated to each project, and what is the implementation timetable?

Also, we need to determine: who are the lenders? What are the interest rates, commitment fees, arrangement fees, grace periods, maturities, repayment schedules and other conditions? The economic and social returns must be spelt out.

What measurable improvements in productivity, employment, revenue generation, public services or poverty reduction are expected from each investment? Is the debt sustainable?

Can Nigeria meet the resulting repayment obligations without undermining essential public expenditure or creating excessive pressure on future budgets?

What is the Foreign-exchange exposure? Since the loans are denominated in foreign currencies, what would happen to debt-service costs if the naira depreciates significantly? Another is alternative financing? Has the government and its advisers compared the proposed loans with domestic financing, concessional development finance, public-private partnerships, improved revenue collection and the reprioritisation of existing expenditure?

Our Implementation capacity is also an area of concern. Do the relevant ministries, departments, agencies and state-level partners have the capacity to execute the projects efficiently and prevent cost overruns, delays and procurement abuses? These are not procedural formalities. They are central to determining whether borrowing will produce sustainable development or leave future generations with substantial liabilities and inadequate public assets.

What about the question of previous approvals?

I believe that is another matter that deserves particular attention: the relationship between this request and earlier borrowing approvals. Public reporting indicates that Senate President, Senator Godswill Akpabio, referred to the borrowing programme’s appearance in previous budgetary and borrowing arrangements. That observation makes reconciliation essential, but it does not, by itself, establish that the current request is duplicative or unlawful.

The National Assembly must establish whether the proposal represents entirely new financing, the implementation of previously approved borrowing, an extension or restructuring of an existing programme, or an additional approval for financing already contemplated in an earlier plan. The government should publish a reconciliation schedule showing the original approvals, amounts committed, funds drawn, undisbursed balances, outstanding obligations and any additional financing now being requested.

So my position is straightforward: Nigeria may legitimately borrow for development, but every borrowing proposal must be justified project by project, assessed against the country’s repayment capacity and subjected to transparent legislative oversight.

What legal principles govern the proposed external borrowing, and what should the Senate and the House of Representatives do before granting approval?

The first principle is that a presidential request for legislative approval does not, in itself, establish that every aspect of a proposed borrowing programme complies with the law. Equally, a large borrowing request is not automatically unconstitutional merely because of its size. The legal assessment must focus on the applicable statutory requirements, the terms of the proposed facilities, the purposes for which the funds will be used, the relevant appropriations and authorisations, and the procedures followed by the government.

Section 21 of the Debt Management Office (Establishment, etc.) Act, 2003 provides that the terms and conditions of external loans must be laid before and approved by a resolution of the National Assembly before the Minister of Finance may approve or obtain them, subject to the Act’s applicable provisions.

Section 44 of the Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2007 also establishes requirements concerning the stated purpose of borrowing, cost-benefit analysis, prior authorisation and the application of borrowed funds to long-term capital expenditure. These provisions make it clear that borrowing must be supported by more than a general statement of development intentions. The government must demonstrate the purpose, legal authorisation and economic rationale for the proposed financing.

The National Assembly should therefore insist on these safeguards before reaching a final decision.

The Debt Management Office and the Ministry of Finance should present updated projections covering debt service, government revenue, foreign-exchange exposure and the effects of adverse economic scenarios.

The assessment should consider the implications of lower oil revenue, weaker economic growth, higher interest rates, currency depreciation and unexpected expenditure pressures.

The executive should demonstrate that the proposed borrowing satisfies the relevant provisions of the Constitution, the Debt Management Office Act, the Fiscal Responsibility Act, applicable appropriation legislation and any other governing legal requirements. My position is that the Senate and the House of Representatives should not approve the programme solely on the strength of the government’s assurances or the importance of the sectors listed.

World.title: DICON-D7G Urges FG to Boost Local Defence Manufacturing
World.content:
John Shiklam in Kaduna

The Managing Director of DICON-D7G, Mr. Osman Chennar, has called on the federal government to intensify support for local defence manufacturing and technology transfer to reduce Nigeria’s reliance on imported military equipment.

Chennar made the call in a statement yesterday in Kaduna as the organisation participated in and sponsored the ongoing African Defence Industries Exhibition (AFRIDEX) in Lagos.

He warned that dependence on foreign suppliers could leave the country vulnerable to supply chain disruptions and delays in the delivery of military equipment, with possible implications for military operations.

He said: “No nation can achieve genuine strategic autonomy if its critical military capabilities remain heavily dependent on external supply chains.

“Nigeria must develop the capacity to manufacture, maintain, and sustain the equipment required by its Armed Forces.”

The statement said local defence production must extend beyond the assembly of imported equipment to the development of indigenous technologies, skilled manpower, and sustainable manufacturing capabilities.

“Technology transfer must translate into practical industrial capacity, enabling Nigerian engineers and manufacturers to acquire the expertise required to produce, maintain, and upgrade military equipment,” the statement added.

Chennar said strategic partnerships were critical to bridging the gap between military requirements and domestic production capacity.

He described AFRIDEX as a platform for bringing together government institutions, manufacturers, investors, and researchers to explore opportunities for local production and industrial cooperation.

The statement said: “Building a strong defence industry requires coordinated efforts involving government institutions, private manufacturers, universities and technology companies working towards clearly defined national security objectives.”

Chennar also called for increased government support and private sector investment in defence research, manufacturing infrastructure, and technical training.

According to him, sustained investment would enable local manufacturers to develop competitive products, create skilled employment, and retain a greater share of defence expenditure within the domestic economy.

“Indigenous defence manufacturing is not only a security priority; it is also an opportunity to stimulate industrial growth, develop technical expertise, and create employment for Nigerians,” he said.

The organisation said increased domestic production could enhance military readiness by reducing reliance on foreign suppliers for spare parts, maintenance, and equipment support.

It added that stronger local manufacturing could also enable Nigeria to supply defence products to other African countries, subject to applicable quality standards and export requirements.

“Nigeria has the potential to become a significant contributor to Africa’s defence industrial development. Achieving this requires sustained investment, innovation, and partnerships that strengthen local production capacity,” he stressed.

The statement maintained that defence self-reliance did not imply isolation from international partners but required mutually beneficial relationships capable of delivering technology transfer and long-term industrial development.

World.title: Abia Community Demands Suit Withdrawal over N1.3bn Road Project
World.content:
The Niger Data Mobilisation Team and indigenes of Nkpa community in Abia State have issued a 72-hour ultimatum to Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, and his former campaign Director-General, Trump Eke, to withdraw a defamation suit against public interest advocate Darlington Agoha over his criticism of the execution of the Nkpa Road project.

The group, led by Dixon Uwakwe, gave the ultimatum in Umuahia, accusing the plaintiffs of using litigation to intimidate a citizen who raised questions about a Federal Government-funded infrastructure project.

The dispute centres on the Nkpa Road project, reportedly financed with N1.3 billion from the Federal Government’s Ecological Fund. The community alleged that despite the substantial public funding, sections of the road remained incomplete and some completed portions had deteriorated, raising concerns about the quality and value delivered to residents.

Uwakwe said the community’s intervention was driven by the need for accountability over public expenditure and not merely the legal dispute involving Agoha.

“Mr. Darlington Agoha’s only crime was daring to demand basic accountability and transparency from the leadership of our constituency,” the group said in a statement.

The community alleged that Agoha had faced legal pressure for about two years after questioning the quality of work on the road, describing the defamation action as an attempt to discourage citizens from demanding explanations over publicly funded projects.

Counsel to Agoha, Vincent Nwabueze, also described the suit as an attempt to intimidate citizens who had raised concerns about the road project.

Nwabueze alleged that the contractor had been fully paid despite the road allegedly remaining incomplete, saying the condition of the road continued to impose hardship on residents.

However, Eke defended the decision to pursue the case, insisting that the allegations considered defamatory should be determined by the court.

“The matters that we feel are defamatory are before the court. It is left to the court to decide whether or not he has defamed me and the person of the Deputy Speaker,” Eke said.

He acknowledged Agoha’s right to protest against what he considered poor infrastructure delivery but maintained that he also had a right to seek legal redress if he believed his reputation had been damaged.

Responding to the 72-hour ultimatum, Eke said the community was entitled to express its position but insisted that the court would ultimately determine the dispute.

“They have a right to issue an ultimatum. It is part of our democratic culture. You will always have your say. The court will have its way,” he said.

The controversy has consequently shifted attention beyond the defamation suit to questions surrounding the implementation of the Nkpa Road project and the accountability of public funds allocated to it.

The community is demanding that the lawsuit be withdrawn and that concerns over the road’s execution be addressed transparently.

The allegations concerning the project and the parties remain contested, while the defamation suit is before the court for determination.

World.title: Acting police minister moves to give Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi powerful new role
World.content:
KwaZulu-Natal police commissioner Lieutenant-General Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi is in line to become the next Hawks boss after Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia sought Cabinet approval for his appointment. Image: X

KwaZulu-Natal police commissioner Lieutenant-General Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi is in line to become the country’s next Hawks boss.

Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia has submitted a memorandum to Cabinet seeking approval to appoint Mkhwanazi as national head of the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation (DPCI).

The Ministry of Police confirmed the move on Thursday, 29 October.



Mkhwanazi takes on high-profile investigations

Mkhwanazi made headlines in July 2025 when he exposed alleged political interference, corruption and links between senior police officials and criminal syndicates.

His allegations sparked the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry and a parliamentary investigation.

Cachalia also brought Mkhwanazi into the investigation into the murders of women in Ekurhuleni in September.



He joined Crime Intelligence head Lieutenant-General Dumisani Khumalo in assisting a national investigative team led by Lieutenant-General Hilda Senthumule.

By early October, police were investigating 12 cases involving murdered women in Ekurhuleni. Investigators had resolved three cases and identified persons of interest in three others.

Police have not established whether the killings are linked.



Cabinet to decide on Hawks appointment

Cachalia has invoked Section 17CA of the South African Police Service Act, which requires Cabinet’s concurrence before the minister appoints a national Hawks head.

The ministry said Cabinet would consider the memorandum at its earliest available sitting.

The appointment forms part of Cachalia’s Police Reset Agenda, which prioritises the fight against organised crime and corruption.



“The appointment of a National Head is important in ensuring strong leadership, strategic direction and operational effectiveness in addressing these crimes,” the ministry said.

World.title: South Africa’s busiest tourist border crossings
World.content:
Stats SA has revealed which South African border posts welcomed the most tourists in September 2026. Image: file

South Africa’s biggest tourist gateways aren’t all airports.

In fact, the latest tourism figures show that the country’s busiest tourist entry points are actually major land border crossings, reflecting the huge role neighbouring countries play in South Africa’s tourism industry.

Stats SA recorded 835 380 overnight tourists entering South Africa in September 2026. Of these, 627 230, or 75.1%, arrived by road, compared with 208 146 by air and just four by sea.



The 10 busiest tourist border crossings

Looking specifically at road-based tourist arrivals, these were the busiest ports in September 2026:

Rank Border crossing Tourists 1 Lebombo 180 429 2 Beit Bridge 143 675 3 Maseru Bridge 52 318 4 Ficksburg 51 684 5 Oshoek 41 854 6 Groblers Bridge 25 454 7 Caledonspoort 18 738 8 Golela 16 887 9 Jeppe’s Reef 14 516 10 Kosibay 9 959

The figures come from Stats SA’s September 2026 tourism data on tourist arrivals by port of entry.

Lebombo is way out in front

The Lebombo border post was by far the busiest tourist road entry point during September.



It recorded 180 429 tourist arrivals, putting it more than 36 000 tourists ahead of Beit Bridge in second place.

Lebombo connects South Africa with Mozambique, and its high ranking corresponds with Mozambique also being the country’s biggest source of tourists during the month.

Mozambique recorded 182 751 tourists in September, according to Stats SA.



Lebombo’s tourist numbers were also up 3.8% year on year, from 173 765 in September 2025 to 180 429 in September 2026.

Beit Bridge comes in second

The Beit Bridge crossing between South Africa and Zimbabwe recorded 143 675 tourist arrivals.

That made it the second-busiest tourist road entry point in the country.



However, its numbers were slightly lower than the same month in 2025, when 148 641 tourists entered through the crossing, a decline of 3.3%.

Zimbabwe was South Africa’s second-biggest source of tourists in September, with 178 966 overnight tourists recorded.

How do the border crossings compare with airports?

The dominance of the road network is particularly striking when compared with South Africa’s airports.



Among tourists arriving by air, OR Tambo International Airport was the busiest entry point, with 144 132 tourist arrivals.

Cape Town International Airport followed with 61 832. By comparison, Lebombo alone recorded 180 429 tourist arrivals by road. This reflects the different travel patterns of South Africa’s tourism markets.

Some 90.6% of overseas tourists arrived by air, while 92.5% of SADC tourists arrived by road.



Among tourists from other African countries outside SADC, 86.4% arrived by air.

Stats SA cautions that its border data measures movements rather than unique people. This means the same person can be recorded more than once if they cross the border multiple times during the month.

Stats SA also notes that some ports have missing data because of network coverage issues, although the Department of Home Affairs is working to improve coverage.



Nevertheless, the figures provide a useful snapshot of where international tourists are entering South Africa, and show just how important the country’s land borders remain to its tourism industry.

World.title: Soweto derby survey | Kaizer Chiefs or Orlando Pirates: Who will win?
World.content:
Saturday, 31 October will see the next installment of the Soweto derby between Orlando Pirates and bitter rivals Kaizer Chiefs at the FNB Stadium. Image: Kaizer Chiefs website

Saturday, 31 October will see the next installment of the Soweto derby between Orlando Pirates and bitter rivals Kaizer Chiefs at the FNB Stadium.

Kick-off is at 15:30.

The build-up to the match has predictably dominated local football discussions this week.



READ | Warning to fans attending Soweto derby

History

The match will be the 61st Soweto derby league match since the professional era kicked off in the 1996/97 season.

Incredibly, of the previous 60 matches, Kaizer Chiefs and Orlando Pirates have each won 18 matches, while 24 clashes ended in stalemates.

Equally incredibly, only one of the last 15 matches has ended in a draw – and that was the most recent match in April 2026.

Unbeaten

Heading into the match, both sides are unbeaten in the league after eight matches.

The Buccaneers are in second place in the standings, while the Glamour Boys are in fifth. Eight points separates the sides.



Take 30 seconds to fill in the form below and let us know who you think will emerge victorious this weekend.

World.title: Soweto Derby: All-time H-2-H record between Pirates vs Chiefs
World.content:
Orlando Pirates host Kaizer Chiefs at FNB Stadium in the first Soweto Derby of the season on Saturday afternoon.

Kick-off is at 15:30.

The two Soweto giants head into this titanic clash on the back of winning their previous games by a three goal-margin.



Chiefs beat TS Galaxy 3-0 in the Last 16 of the Carling Knockout Cup while Pirates also eased past Milford FC by the same scoreline.

SOWETO DERBY: ALL-TIME HEAD-TO-HEAD RECORD BETWEEN ORLANDO PIRATES AND Kaizer Chiefs

Now, this historic encounter between Orlando Pirates and Kaizer Chiefs will be played for the 185th time since January 1970.

In the previous 184 matches across all competitions since then, Amakhosi still have have the edge over their arch-rivals.

However, it is important to note that the Buccaneers have had the better of Chiefs in recent years.

Of the 184 previous matches, Chiefs won 75 to Pirates’ 50 while the other 54 matches ended in draws.

Five of the 184 matches were abandoned for various reasons with the last being the 11 April 2001 match where there was a stampede at Ellis Park Stadium.



During this period, Chiefs have scored 234 while Pirates are sitting on 204 goals scored. Amakhosi legend Ace Ntsoelengoe contributed the most goals (19).

WHO IS YOUR MONEY ON?

World.title: Bulls captain cleared of foul play
World.content:
This past weekend Bulls stalwart Marcell Coetzee received a yellow card following an incident involving Ulster lock Ben Donnell during a URC clash at Loftus.

However, after the game Coetzee was cited, alleged to have breached Laws 9.20(a) and 9.20(b), which prohibit dangerous play at a ruck or maul, including charging into an opponent without binding and making contact above the shoulders.

It led to a customary disciplinary hearing, but the good news for Coetzee and the Bulls is the fact that it was deemed that a yellow card was sufficient.



Bulls captain free to play

This weekend the third-placed Bulls – who have made a strong start to the season – will be careful not to underestimate the 14th-placed Scarlets after they put up a competitive performance against the Stormers last weekend.

It will be a big boost for the Bulls to have their skipper available, with a statement from the URC explaining the disciplinary outcome.

“The citing commissioner in charge reported Marcell Coetzee for an act of foul play in the 43rd minute of the game under Law 9.20(a) and 9.20(b) – Dangerous play in a ruck or maul. (a) A Player must not charge into a ruck or maul. Charging includes any contact made without binding onto another player in the ruck of maul. (b) A Player must not make contact with an opponent above the line of the shoulders.



“The Panel overseeing the disciplinary hearing Ben Rutherford (Chair – Ireland), Declan Goodwin and Chris Morgan (Wales), reviewed the incident and agreed that an act of foul play had occurred, the clean out was principally shoulder to body.

“The head contact was incidental and low force, corroborated by the evidence of both the Player and his opponent and medical team. The degree of danger was therefore low in accordance with the World Rugby Head Coach Process and the correct outcome was a yellow card, as issued by the Match Officials on the day.

“The Citing Complaint was not upheld and the Player is free to play this weekend.”



Match information

Bulls v Scarlets

Date: Saturday, 31 October 2026

Venue: Loftus Versfeld, Pretoria

SA Time: 17:00

Referee: Eoghan Cross

TV: SuperSport

World.title: Wandile Duba has unfinished business with Orlando Pirates
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs forward Wandile Duba will be eager to continue his impressive form when Amakhosi take on Orlando Pirates in the Soweto Derby on Saturday.

The 22-year-old attacker has scored six goals across all competitions this season, making him Chiefs‘ leading goalscorer.

His performances have also highlighted his growing confidence and improved finishing under coach Fernando Da Cruz.



Duba, popularly known as AK47, has become a key attacking outlet for Amakhosi, using his pace, direct running, and willingness to take on defenders to trouble opposition defences.

Why Duba Could Trouble Pirates

Duba already showed what he can do against Orlando Pirates in the previous Soweto Derby.

The young attacker used his strength to get past the Buccaneers’ defence before delivering a cutback for Pule Mmodi, who finished neatly to give Chiefs the lead.



Amakhosi couldn’t hold on to their advantage as Pirates found an equaliser 10 minutes later, and the match ended in a draw.

On Saturday, Pirates’ defence will once again have to be alert to Duba’s threat. His pace and ability to run directly at defenders could create problems, particularly if he finds space behind the Buccaneers’ backline.

The Chiefs forward has also shown greater confidence on the ball, taking on opponents and looking to make things happen in the final third. If Pirates allow him time and space, he could make the most of those opportunities.



Duba’s determination is another quality that could work in Chiefs’ favour. The attacker is known for his competitive nature and will be desperate to make his mark in one of South African football’s biggest fixtures.

Despite his growing influence, Duba is still searching for his first goal against Orlando Pirates. With the spotlight firmly on the Soweto Derby, he will have extra motivation to break that duck.

The outspoken winger heads into the highly anticipated encounter on the back of an impressive hat-trick against TS Galaxy in his previous match. That performance will further boost his confidence as he prepares to face the Buccaneers.



If Duba carries that scoring touch into Saturday’s clash, Pirates could have a difficult afternoon trying to contain one of Chiefs’ most dangerous attacking players.

Will Duba be on the scoresheet on Saturday?

World.title: Warning to fans attending Soweto derby
World.content:
Football fans heading to Saturday’s Soweto derby between Orlando Pirates and Kaizer Chiefs at FNB Stadium have been urged to plan their journeys carefully. Image: Orlando Pirates website

Football fans heading to Saturday’s Soweto derby between Orlando Pirates and Kaizer Chiefs at FNB Stadium have been urged to plan their journeys carefully, with road closures and traffic restrictions set to affect access to the venue.

The highly anticipated Betway Premiership clash kicks off at 15:30, with stadium gates opening at 10:00.

Tickets have sold out, and a full house is expected.



READ | Football legend Thierry Henry to attend Soweto derby

To manage the anticipated crowds, the stadium precinct will operate as a vehicle exclusion zone, with private motorists required to have valid parking tickets or authorised access permits to enter designated areas.

Spectators are encouraged to arrive before 12:00 and consider public transport to avoid delays.

Soweto Derby road closures

Road closures and traffic restrictions will come into effect from 10:00 on Saturday.

Key traffic control points will include:

N1 South off-ramp and N17

Nasrec Road

Rand Show Road

Crownwood Road

Booysens Reserve Road

Soweto Highway, between Mentz Street and the N1 North on-ramp, will be reserved for Rea Vaya and Gautrain buses.



Motorists who are not attending the match are advised to avoid the stadium precinct and use alternative routes where possible, including the N1, M1 and N12 highways and Main Reef Road.

Traffic arrangements will also be adjusted after the final whistle to help vehicles leave the area.

Where to park for the Soweto Derby

Spectators planning to drive to the match have several designated parking options.

Parking facility Cost per vehicle Johannesburg Expo Centre, Expo 1–8 R80 Premium parking, Expo Centre Gate 1 R250 IPROP parking at Booysens Reserve Road and Crownwood Road checkpoint R80

Expo Centre parking can be booked in advance through the MyTicket app or at www.myticket.co.za, subject to availability.

Limited parking tickets may also be available at designated checkpoints, with payment by credit or debit card.

IPROP parking is available only at the specified Booysens Reserve Road and Crownwood Road checkpoint and is subject to capacity. Spectators using this facility will have access to a free return shuttle to the stadium.

Importantly, a match ticket alone does not grant permission to drive through the road closures. Motorists must have the appropriate parking ticket or access permit.

Public transport options and prices

Fans who want to avoid driving into the stadium precinct can use several public transport services.

Johannesburg Stadium Park & Ride

The Johannesburg Stadium Park & Ride facility offers free secured parking and return Rea Vaya transport to FNB Stadium.

Spectators whose match tickets do not include transport can purchase return transport for R60 per person.

Gautrain match-day shuttle

A dedicated Gautrain match-day shuttle will operate between Park Station and FNB Stadium from 09:00 to 19:30.

Return bus transport costs R25 per person when purchased on match day. This excludes Gautrain train fares and station parking.

Rea Vaya services

Rea Vaya will provide return transport from designated stations, including:

Ellis Park

Library Gardens

Thokoza Park

Dobsonville

Return match-day transport costs R60 per person.

Fans who have already purchased match tickets that include transport will not need to pay again for the transport covered by their packages.

Transport-only tickets do not include admission to the match, and no additional match tickets will be sold at FNB Stadium.

E-hailing, residents and match-day safety

E-hailing vehicles must use the designated Transportation Hub for passenger drop-offs and collections.

Residents who need to travel through the vehicle exclusion zone must present their event-specific access passes.

Soweto derby spectators are also urged to follow instructions from traffic officers and event marshals, keep emergency routes clear and avoid stopping in moving traffic lanes to collect passengers.

Traffic officers’ instructions will take precedence over GPS and navigation applications.

Standings

Heading into the Soweto derby clash, Orlando Pirates are in second place in the standings with 22 points after eight matches, thanks to seven wins and a draw.

They trail log leaders Mamelodi Sundowns by a single point and have a game in hand.

The Buccaneers have conceded just one goal this campaign to date.

Meanwhile, Kaizer Chiefs are in fifth place with 14 points after eight fixtures. Amakhosi are also unbeaten, but have only won three and drawn five matches to date.

World.title: These are the 10 countries sending the most tourists to South Africa
World.content:
From neighbouring countries to major overseas markets, these were South Africa’s biggest sources of tourists in September. Image: canva

South Africa welcomed more than 835 000 overnight tourists in September 2026, with neighbouring African countries continuing to dominate the country’s tourism numbers.

According to the latest figures from Statistics South Africa (Stats SA), 835 380 overnight visitors arrived in South Africa during Tourism Month.

The figures show just how heavily South Africa’s tourism market relies on its neighbouring countries, with several SADC nations recording far more arrivals than even the country’s biggest overseas markets.



The top 10 countries sending tourists to SA

Mozambique was comfortably South Africa’s biggest source of tourists in September, followed by Zimbabwe and Lesotho.

Rank Country Tourists 1 Mozambique 182 751 2 Zimbabwe 178 966 3 Lesotho 127 152 4 Eswatini 74 261 5 Botswana 38 672 6 USA 27 825 7 UK 22 305 8 Malawi 19 729 9 Germany 17 627 10 Namibia 13 923

The figures are based on tourists’ country of residence, rather than their nationality.

TWO AFRICAN COUNTRIES lead the way

Mozambique and Zimbabwe alone accounted for more than 360 000 visitors in September. Mozambique recorded 182 751 tourists, while Zimbabwe contributed another 178 966.

Lesotho was third with 127 152, followed by Eswatini with 74 261 and Botswana with 38 672.

Together, Mozambique, Zimbabwe and Lesotho accounted for 74.1% of all SADC tourists visiting South Africa during the month.

Overseas markets look very different

The United States was South Africa’s biggest overseas source market in September, with 27 825 tourists.



It was followed by the UK with 22 305 and Germany with 17 627.

Other major overseas markets included Australia, the Netherlands, France, Brazil, Canada, India and Switzerland. However, the overall picture remains heavily weighted towards Africa.

Of the 835 380 tourists recorded in September, 659 613 came from SADC countries, representing 79% of all tourists.

Overseas tourists accounted for 161 753, or 19.4%, while visitors from other African countries outside SADC accounted for 13 225, or 1.6%.

While Mozambique and Zimbabwe provided the largest numbers, Lesotho recorded one of the strongest increases among the major SADC markets.

The number of tourists from Lesotho increased by 21.9% year on year, rising from 104 339 in September 2025 to 127 152 in September 2026.

Brazil was the only overseas market in the top 10 to record a notable increase, rising by 9.1% year on year to 6 035 tourists.

Most tourists came for a holiday

Tourism also remained overwhelmingly leisure-driven. Stats SA found that 97.5% of tourists were in South Africa for holiday purposes.

The category includes vacations, visiting friends and relatives, shopping and other personal reasons such as attending weddings.

Business accounted for 2.1% of tourists, while study accounted for 0.3% and medical treatment for less than 0.1%.

One important caveat is that Stats SA’s border figures measure movements rather than unique individuals. Someone who crosses the South African border multiple times during the month can therefore be counted multiple times.

The September figures also show that South Africa’s tourism industry continues to have a very strong regional base, with neighbouring countries supplying the vast majority of its international tourists.

World.title: LGE 2026: Knysna residents call for urgent water and sanitation upgrades
World.content:
