KNYSNA - Housing shortages and persistent sewage spills are among the biggest challenges facing residents in Knysna ahead of the 2026 Local Government Elections.

Resident Jovan Maritz says the lack of housing over the past 15 to 20 years has forced people to build homes in areas not equipped to accommodate them, placing additional strain on an ageing sewage infrastructure.

Maritz says the municipality’s sewerage pipes have not kept pace with the town’s growth, with infrastructure in some areas reportedly last upgraded during apartheid.

“All the political parties that have governed Knysna are part of the problem. They always make the surface look good here in Knysna, but underneath, it is absolutely rotten,” Maritz says.

Water shortages are another major concern. Maritz says the community went without water for three months and alleges that water supplies are sometimes interrupted during storms, while water tankers appear in the area.

Residents want reliable access to clean running water, urgent upgrades to sewage infrastructure and more housing.

Maritz also expressed concern about the health risks posed by sewage spills, particularly for children, warning of the potential spread of diseases such as cholera.

Despite the challenges, Maritz says there is little faith that the upcoming elections will bring immediate change. Instead, they hope the community will unite and hold the incoming leadership accountable during its first 100 days in office.

“At the end of the day, we forget this is our tax money that they are using to help us. They are public servants, and they seem to forget that,” Maritz says.

World.title: Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi tipped for top Hawks post
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia has initiated the process to appoint KwaZulu-Natal Police Commissioner Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi as the national head of the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation (DPCI), commonly known as the Hawks.

Cachalia has submitted a memorandum to Cabinet seeking approval for the appointment. The document is expected to be presented at the earliest opportunity during a Cabinet meeting.

The Police Ministry said the appointment is intended to ensure leadership for the unit, which investigates serious priority crimes, including organised crime and corruption.

“The DPCI plays a critical role in South Africa’s fight against organised crime, corruption, and other serious priority offences. This is a priority for the Police Reset Agenda,” the ministry said in a statement.

“The appointment of a National Head is important in ensuring strong leadership, strategic direction and operational effectiveness in addressing these crimes,” it added.

World.title: E.coli concerns in parts of Knysna lagoon
World.content:
KNYSNA - E. coli levels in parts of the Knysna Lagoon remain a concern, with monthly water testing highlighting the impact of sewage flowing from nearby settlements into rivers and the lagoon.

Beverley Pothier of the Greater Knysna Business Chamber says testing at specific points around the lagoon shows that the leisure areas have not been significantly affected.

However, higher levels of concern have been identified where rivers flow into the lagoon, carrying pollution from upstream settlements.

READ | Water quality alert lifted in Bezuidenhout Valley after tests

Pothier says active campaigns are under way to tackle the problem at its source, with efforts focused on addressing sewage pollution upstream to prevent further contamination downstream.

“There are E. coli measurements done every month at specific spots around the lagoon," she said

"It's not impacted very much in the leisure portions of the lagoon, but particularly where the rivers do meet the lagoon, we are seeing an inflow coming from various settlements that feed into the river that are then coming through to the lagoon.

“But there are some active campaigns working at ensuring that upstream is sorted so that downstream doesn't land up with the sewage in the lagoon or the E. coli in particular.”

World.title: Samsung logs record quarterly profits despite investor AI jitters
World.content:
SEOUL - Massive demand for AI chips delivered record quarterly profits to South Korea's Samsung Electronics on Thursday, but shares fell as investors questioned the resilience of the global tech boom.

Samsung is the world's largest maker of memory chips -- components in short supply as advanced types are snapped up for use in data centres powering artificial intelligence.

The company posted July-September operating profit at 107.4 trillion won ($80.5 billion) -- up more than 780 percent on-year.

It marked the first time any technology company had reported quarterly operating profit over 100 trillion won, Samsung said.

Net profit jumped more than 510 percent from last year to 75.1 trillion won, while sales reached 195.3 trillion won.

The global race to build data centres to train and run chatbots, image generators and other AI tools has turbocharged the fortunes of Samsung and other chipmakers, despite concerns that the sector may be overvalued.

Samsung shares fell more than five percent on Thursday morning.

Investors were disappointed by a miss of market expectations for operating profit by the semiconductor division, according to Bloomberg News.

The company's memory business achieved "another record-breaking quarter by managing its product mix, with a focus on AI products, amid capacity constraints," Samsung said in a statement.

"Strong demand momentum for servers led to higher market prices across all applications."

- 'Unprecedented growth' -

Demand-driven shortages of advanced memory chips known as HBM, used in AI systems alongside other data-crunching semiconductors, has caused their price to spike.

Dilin Wu, research strategist at Pepperstone, said strong earnings from Samsung and South Korean industry rival SK hynix were "a reminder that the AI memory boom is still very real, despite all the concerns we've seen around the broader AI trade".

"Chipmakers are benefiting directly from the AI investment boom, while the companies buying their chips are still trying to prove they can earn a decent return on all that spending," she told AFP earlier this week.

With sky-high expectations for stellar results, record profits may not be enough to reassure market players.

"Ultimately, investors want to know whether there's still another leg to this memory upcycle, or whether we're getting close to peak earnings," Wu said.

Samsung predicted Thursday that it would continue to feel the benefits of the AI boom.

Chief financial officer Park Soon-cheol told an earnings call the company expects "unprecedented growth in memory demand in 2027, driven by accelerating competition to build AI infrastructure and the expansion of personal AI agents".

"On the supply side, however, we expect difficulties in expanding... output in a short period of time through new capacity additions," he said.

Chip companies focusing their efforts on profitable HBM has also fuelled shortages of the less glamorous computer memory components used in everyday consumer electronics -- driving up the price of smartphones and laptops.

- Shareholder returns -

Samsung on Thursday detailed plans to return up to 110 trillion won to shareholders this year, including 30 trillion won in cash dividends, following an August announcement.

Record profits driven by booming demand for AI memory chips have fuelled calls for greater shareholder returns, particularly after shares in tech giants such as Samsung tumbled from their June record highs amid concerns over US tech firms' AI spending.

The announcement comes a day after SK hynix also announced plans to return 60 trillion won to shareholders, following the completion of a 40 trillion-won shareholder return programme.

Such shareholder returns "would allow the benefits of earnings growth to translate into greater shareholder returns," said Kim Dong-won, head of KB Securities' research centre.

"With record profits and undervaluation coexisting, the largest-ever expansion of shareholder returns would be a decisive opportunity to address the company's undervaluation and serve as a key driver of a reassessment of its market value," said Kim.

World.title: Bangladesh presses India before Ganges water treaty expires
World.content:
NEW DELHI - With a 30-year Ganges water-sharing treaty with India expiring in December, Bangladesh fears failure to strike a new deal could deepen water shortages, threatening tens of millions of livelihoods.

In Bangladesh's parched Barind region, 72-year-old Bikash Soren remembers when the Ganges river flowing in from neighbouring India carried large boats past his village year-round.

"For almost three months a year, you hardly see the river flowing," the Protestant priest said.

Two farmers killed themselves last season, he added, after dwindling water levels left their rice and wheat crops in tatters.

Shrinking flows in the Ganges have also slashed fish catches in the river, known in Bangladesh as the Padma.

World.title: Antonelli ready to rewrite the Formula One record books in Mexico
World.content:
MEXICO CITY - Kimi Antonelli will take his place in Formula One’s record books as the youngest champion and Italy’s first since 1953, barring a wild swing of unexpected misfortunes amid a fiesta atmosphere at this weekend’s Mexico City Grand Prix.

The runaway leader of the drivers’ championship needs to finish ninth or better in his Mercedes to take the title aged 20 years and 68 days, lowering the record held by Sebastian Vettel by more than three years.

Almost more remarkably, he will also succeed Italy's last champion Alberto Ascari, who won for Ferrari in 1953, after a gap of 73 years during which his country has become synonymous with Formula One.

After winning the United States Grand Prix last Sunday, his two remaining title rivals team-mate George Russell and Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton are 123 and 124 points adrift respectively and can only prevent the seemingly inevitable by winning and hoping Antonelli finishes 10th or worse.

Such an outcome is highly unlikely.

Antonelli has won nine races of this year’s 18 to date. In his last 11, he has scored nine podium finishes, one fifth and one 15th place – only his second non-points-scoring race in 18 outings that began with a second-place in Australia followed by five wins.

World.title: Hollywood producer Kennedy to head LA28 Olympic ceremony plans
World.content:
LOS ANGELES - Oscar-nominated film producer Kathleen Kennedy was named on Wednesday to oversee preparations for the opening and closing ceremonies at the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games in Los Angeles.

Kennedy, 73, an eight-time Academy Award nominee whose first film producing credit came on Steven Spielberg's 1982 classic "E.T. The Extra-Terrestrial", will serve as head of ceremonies and content.

She will executive produce the opening and closing ceremonies, which will take place at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum and SoFi Stadium.

"Kathleen is a legend. She is one of Hollywood's all-time greats, with a rare gift for storytelling," LA28 chairperson and president Casey Wasserman said in a statement.

"When the stars align to focus the world's attention on Los Angeles for the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games, I can't think of anyone better to conjure the magic of Hollywood than Kathleen."

Kennedy, whose other film credits include "Jurassic Park" and "Schindler's List" and the most recent instalments of the "Star Wars" franchise, said she and her husband, fellow producer Frank Marshall, had been longtime Olympic fans.

"The Olympics have been a touchstone in my life," Kennedy said. "My husband...and I have attended virtually every Games since Los Angeles in 1984, and sport remains one of the great unifying experiences we share," she said.

The Olympic Opening Ceremony is scheduled for July 14, 2028, with the Closing Ceremony on July 30.

The Paralympic Opening Ceremony is scheduled for August 15, with the Closing Ceremony at the Coliseum on August 27.

In a separate announcement on Wednesday, Olympics organisers revealed that the official slogan for the 2028 Games would be "Stars Align" in a nod to Los Angeles's status as the world's entertainment industry capital.

"Los Angeles is the place where dreams take flight, and the Olympics show us what's possible when the world unites," Wasserman said in a statement. "We can't wait for the stars to align in 2028 so we can share this moment with everyone."

World.title: On the ground in Knysna: What residents want from local government
World.content:
eNCA reporter Kevin Brandt takes us behind the scenes on his second day in Knysna, where residents continue to grapple with water and sanitation challenges ahead of the 2026 Local Government Elections.

Level 2 water restrictions are in place, limiting municipal water use to essential needs and business activities.

The town is also facing political instability and governance challenges.

World.title: Former USIU student sentenced to death over colleague's murder, Sh100,000 ransom demand
World.content:
When Duncan Livingstone Kimathi (R) and his accomplice were presented in court after their arrest in 2012. [Courtesy]

A former United States International University (USIU) student, Duncan Livingstone Kimathi, has been sentenced to death for the murder of fellow student Sarah Akello Aruwa in June 2012.

High Court Judge Justice Kanyi Kimondo handed Kimathi the death sentence on Thursday after finding that the murder was premeditated and involved an abduction and ransom demand targeting the deceased’s family.

World.title: Not so fast! Court blocks Bomas expansion
World.content:
Contractors hired are barred from clearing vegetation, cutting trees, excavating, grading, fencing, constructing routes, and undertaking any works at the disputed site. [File, Standard]

The Environment and Lands Court has blocked the government from continuing with the construction of a car park inside the Nairobi National Park.

Justice Grace Kemei, in her ruling, said that the contractors hired are barred from clearing vegetation, cutting trees, excavating, grading, fencing, constructing routes, and undertaking any works at the disputed site.

World.title: Kikuyu PCEA church loses 2.7-acre illegally acquired land
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Justice Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent. [Courtesy, EACC]

The Presbyterian Church of East Africa (PCEA) has lost its 2.7-acre piece of land to a school.

This is after the Environment and Lands Court at Thika established that the land under the church's Ruguthi Women's Guild was a school playground and was illegally allocated.

Presiding Judge Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property, and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent.

According to her, the land had been reserved for use as a playground by Kanyiha, Lusigetti and Njumbi Primary Schools.

The verdict follows a case filed by the Law Society of Kenya, with the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) participating as an interested party.

In a statement on Monday, EACC's head of Corporate Affairs and Communication Stephen Karuga said the anti-graft agency presented evidence demonstrating that the land had been reserved for public use and therefore, any allocation to third parties was irregular. Justice Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent. [Courtesy, EACC]

"Our investigations established that the land was set aside in 1957 by the former County Council of Kiambu for use as a school playing field," Karuga said, adding, "the investigations further revealed that there was no letter of offer or acceptance, no evidence of payment of rent rates and no proof that the Women's Guild had paid any consideration to the council for the land."

According to Karuga, the judgement safeguards a vital public facility used by more than 1,300 pupils, ensuring that the playground remains available for learning, sports and recreation for the current and future generations.

As a result, the judge said the allocation, transfer and registration of the land LR. NO KARAI/350 and subsequent issuance of a title deed in 2001 was unprocedural, illegal, null and void.

"An order of Mandamus is hereby issued directing the 3rd respondent, the Land Registrar, Kiambu Chief Land Registrar, to forthwith cancel and revoke the Title Deed and all register entries in respect of the land issued to the 1st respondent on Dec 6, 2001, or at any subsequent date," the Judge said.

The judge further ordered that the said parcel of land be handed over to the Board of Management of the two schools and the Education Ministry.

"An order of permanent injunction is hereby issued restraining the 1st respondent, whether by herself, her church officials, agents, servants, assigns or anyone claiming through her, from entering into, taking possession of, fencing, depositing construction materials upon, transferring, charging, developing or in any other manner dealing or interfering with the land," she ordered.

World.title: Sakaja protests release of 14 suspects linked to Eastleigh collapsed building
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court. [GPS]

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja has protested the release of suspects linked to the collapsed building in Eastleigh.

While pushing for the county to have prosecutorial powers, Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court.

Sakaja in statement posted on his X account (formerly Twitter) said City Hall had taken enforcement action against those involved after establishing change of user from a residential property to a commercial had been approved.

According to Sakaja, architectural plans required to authorise construction had not been approved.

The Governor said County officers arrested the suspects and handed them over to Kamukunji Police Station because county governments no longer hold prosecutorial powers they previously held.

“We enforced the law and arrested those involved. However, because we do not have prosecutorial powers, the suspects were handed over to Kamukunji Police Station. They were reportedly released on a cash bail of Sh50,000 without being taken to court,” Sakaja said.

“We want the police to explain why the suspects were released without being presented in court and why construction was allowed to continue. These are serious questions that must be answered,” he added.

A police occurrence book entry from Kamukunji Police Station indicates that 14 suspects were booked into custody on June 17, 2026, over the alleged offences relating to contravention of city planning laws.

Enforcement action and arrests were made severally by the county officials and most recently in July after failing to comply with the enforcement order below. However the suspects were released on a 50k bail at Kamukunji police on the very same day. Prosecution of the same was also denied. We have repeatedly asked for the resumption of the power to prosecute such violations of such county and county related laws after this was taken away from County governments in 2024 (one such letter to the office of the DPP is attached). Meanwhile, several such cases have either been rejected by prosecutors (who are independent of the County), dismissed by the justice system or have had minimal fines imposed. Fining a developer 50k for an illegal development with hundreds of millions without orders to stop and remove the offensive development is completely unreasonable. I raised this in the Senate a fortnight ago and we shall keep pushing for a review of this position. All of these instances, where enforcement action has been curtailed, blocked or interfered with, will be published to the public. October 25, 2026

The entry, recorded under OB No. 98/17/06/2026, names the suspects and states that they were booked by Nairobi City County officers before being placed in police cells.

A separate Kenya Police Service record indicates that 10 suspects were subsequently released on a cash bail of Sh50,000.

The entry, recorded at 9.44pm, states that the release was carried out on the instructions of the Officer Commanding Station (OCS), identified in the record as C.I. Onyapidi, through Corporal Awadh.

The record references receipt number 2039434 and states that the suspects left the station without complaints.

However, the documents do not, on their own, establish the specific charges against the suspects, the legal basis for the bail arrangement or whether they were subsequently presented in court.

The discrepancy between the 14 suspects recorded as booked into custody and the 10 named in the release entry also raises questions about the subsequent status of the other suspects. Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court. [GPS]

Sakaja said a June 2025 enforcement notice adds another dimension to the questions surrounding the property and the enforcement of planning regulations.

The notice, issued by Nairobi City County over alleged construction works undertaken without the required development permission, cited the Physical and Land Use Planning Act, 2019, and county by-laws.

It directed the recipient to stop the works and remove the development described as illegal, warning that the County could undertake the required action and recover the costs if the directives were not followed.

The notice also provided for an appeal to the County Physical and Land Use Planning Liaison Committee.

Sakaja clarified that approval to change a property’s use from private to commercial-cum-residential does not amount to approval of architectural plans authorising construction.

He said the County approved the change of use but did not approve the architectural plans, yet construction proceeded.

I have seen some people peddling a fake approval document alleging that the Eastleigh development was approved. It is telling that this is the same document that the Eastleigh developer used to get NCA approval. They allege that the development was approved in January of 2024. This is not true. The application for development as shown below was made in November of 2024, it could not have been approved in February of the same year. Also, there is a difference between a change of user approval and a development approval. The developer applied for change of use from residential to residential & commercial in August of 2024. Change of user was approved in October of 2024. Development approval has never been granted. The developer went on to build with impunity and without building approvals despite enforcement action by the county and arrests. — Sakaja Arthur Johnson (@SakajaJohnson) October 25, 2026

“If the building had been approved for construction, I would have named the officers who approved it so that action could be taken against them,” he said.

Sakaja, in his argument, said the current arrangement creates a gap between enforcement and prosecution, leaving counties dependent on other agencies after taking action against alleged offenders. Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court. [GPS]

Under his proposal, appropriately authorised county prosecutors would be able to pursue qualifying county offences through the courts, subject to the law and the constitutional authority of the Director of Public Prosecutions.

He said county prosecutors previously had a better understanding of technical offences involving planning, construction and other county regulations, enabling them to handle such cases more directly.

“We want to be able not only to enforce regulations and make arrests, but also to take offenders to court and prosecute them. When counties had prosecutorial powers, we had prosecutors who understood the nature and seriousness of county offences and could ensure that appropriate legal action was taken,” he said.

World.title: Pregnant woman rescued from collapsed Eastleigh building
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya Red Cross workers after rescuing a man who trapped in the rubble.

A pregnant woman was on Saturday evening rescued from the multi-storey building that collapsed in Nairobi’s Eastleigh estate on Friday, October 23 and rushed to the Kenyatta National Hospital (KNH) for treatment.

She is the second person to rescued as earlier in the afternoon the Kenya Red Cross society announced the rescue of a man from the ill-fated building.

The man was also taken to KNH for treatment with the society saying that the rescue followed hours of work put in by the search and rescue multi-agency team.

“After hours of painstaking work alongside multi-agency partners, our search and rescue teams in Eastleigh brought a trapped man out of the rubble,” said Red Cross.

The rescue comes even as the fate of six people who were reported missing on Friuday remains unknown with rescue teams still continuing with the search at the site of the collapsed building along Yusuf Haji Avenue.

The society said that 66 of the 67 construction workers who were at the site had been traced and accounted for but the search continues for people who may have been near the site of the collapsed building.

The development comes as police announced that they had launched a manhunt for the for the owner and contractor of a building.

Police spokesperson Muchiri Nyaga said that officers had launched a probe in collaboration with relevant bodies to establish the cause of the collapse and determine criminal liability.

“Any individual or entity found culpable of negligence or of violating building regulations will face the full force of the law,” he said in a statement.

Nyaga called on members of public to stay completely clear of Yusuf Haji Avenue and 9th Street to give access to heavy excavators, specialised canine units and rescue personnel to perform their duties.

Earlier Saturday, at least 31 families reported their relatives missing as coordinated rescue efforts entered their second day.

No deaths have been reported so far.

The National Construction Authority (NCA) on Friday evening identified the developer, contractor, architect and structural engineer listed for the collapsed building.

The Authority has faced scrutiny over its oversight role, as Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja said the project had failed to comply with construction guidelines.

He said the county had forwarded relevant information to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations for further investigation.

In a statement, the NCA said the building was registered on July 30, 2025, as a proposed development on 9th Street in Eastleigh.

It identified 9th Street Plaza Limited as the developer and Stromax Holdings E.A. Limited as the contractor.

Emmanuel Mwangi Maina was listed as the project architect, while Joseph Muturi Mugu was named as the structural engineer.

World.title: Several feared trapped in Eastleigh building collapse
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

What was supposed to be a usually busy Friday afternoon in Eastleigh's 9th Street turned chaotic after an 18-floor building that was under construction came down, tumbling.

By Friday evening, rescue operations were still ongoing, with cries from people believed to have been trapped being heard from a distance as bulldozers and rescuers continued the search operation.

Two victims, a man and a woman, who were injured in the building had been rescued and rushed to hospital as the search continued.

Asha Jilo, one of the witnesses, said the building collapsed around 1:09 pm just after the afternoon prayers.

"Immediately after the building collapsed, we started contacting some people we know who work there, one of them was still available on the phone until around 3 pm, when his phone went offline," Jilo shared

On Fridays, Eastleigh is usually a hive of activities, being the main market day, but all the businesses were shut as police were battling rowdy youths, some of them believed to be opportunists.

The building, whose height was said to be about 15 floors, had not been cleared for occupation as required, raising questions about why the investors had allowed it to be taken.

It is said that the ground and first floors were already occupied by businesses, raising fears that the number of victims could be high. Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

At the time of the collapse, it is said that some construction workers were busy on the upper floors.

Governor Johnson Sakaja, who visited the scene after the collapse, was still gathering information about the building. The first priority was about saving lives.

“The building that collapsed is around 16 floors, and we have got information about the building, but what is more concerned right now is for us to save lives,” said Sakaja

Adding, “Equipment has already been mobilized, excavators and breakers, so we can be able to remove the big debris and save lives,’

The Governor said some developers engage qualified professionals to secure construction approvals before dismissing them and disregarding approved plans and safety standards.

He urged professional bodies to strengthen oversight, investigate such cases and take appropriate disciplinary action, stressing that developers must comply with approved designs, engage qualified personnel and obtain occupation certificates after safety inspections.

Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

Nairobi Regional Police Commander Issa Mohamud, who was at the scene, said that, according to reliable information, several people were trapped inside the debris, inside the big boulders, and the rescue effort is ongoing.

The city police boss said investigations will be carried out to ascertain who is responsible for any negligence.

“If there will be any death, that is negligence by murder. Whoever is the owner, whoever authorized the building, all of them will be charged properly. But that will come after thorough investigation is done,” he warned

Adding, “We will not excuse anybody on this matter. This has become now and then, and we will make sure that people face the law accordingly for any criminal negligence,”

World.title: Ruto hands over COMESA chairmanship, pushes for levy to fund regional programmes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President Ruto and Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa during the handover of the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa chairmanship at the bloc’s 25th Summit of Heads of State and Government in Harare, Zimbabwe, on Thursday, October 22, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has handed over the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) chairmanship to Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa.

Ruto took over the one-year chairmanship from Burundi’s President Évariste Ndayishimiye at the 24th COMESA Summit in Nairobi on October 9, 2025.

His tenure focused on using digital technology to deepen regional integration, expand trade and promote inclusive growth.

He handed over the role on Thursday, October 22, during the 25th Comesa Summit of Heads of State and Government in Harare, Zimbabwe, where he urged the regional bloc to fast-track a market levy to finance its programmes and institutions.

“We cannot be ambitious in our plans and timid in our financing. Every programme we agree upon must be matched by the resources to deliver it. Otherwise, our communiqués will promise what our budgets cannot pay for,” Ruto said.

He urged the Comesa Secretariat to fast-track Article 168 of the COMESA Treaty, which provides for the Comesa Market Levy, as the organisation seeks sustainable and predictable financing.

The treaty establishes the levy to generate resources for financing the bloc’s activities.

Ruto said officials from finance ministries, central banks and other relevant agencies would meet to consider a draft COMESA Resource Mobilisation Strategy aimed at strengthening member states’ ownership of regional programmes and finding new ways to raise funds.

He called on member states to make financing central to their discussions, warning that the bloc’s institutions and integration agenda would depend on their ability to fund agreed commitments.

“Can we finance what we commit, and deliver what we finance?” he asked.

Ruto also urged African countries to channel more of their domestic financial resources into African institutions rather than leaving funds in foreign accounts while development projects lack capital.

He said Africa holds more than $4 trillion in domestic financial assets, arguing that regional financial institutions could mobilise more of these resources to support trade, infrastructure and development.

Ruto named the Trade and Development Bank (TDB), the African Trade and Investment Development Insurance (ATIDI) and ZEP-RE among the institutions that could mobilise capital for regional priorities.

He urged African governments to place more reserves with these institutions, finance more projects through them and support their bonds and guarantees.

The outgoing Comesa chairperson said the bloc needed stronger regional value chains and more trade among member states as global supply chains faced disruption and protectionism returned.

“Regional integration is no longer a dream we discuss. It is an economic and strategic necessity,” he noted.

Ruto said Comesa’s economic growth rose from 5.6 per cent in 2024 to 6.4 per cent in 2025, while inflation fell from 31 per cent to 13.2 per cent.

Exports among member states increased by 10.5 per cent to $14.7 billion, their highest level between 2020 and 2025, while exports to global markets rose by 6 per cent to $212 billion, he said.

He argued that African countries needed to process more raw materials locally instead of exporting them and importing finished products.

“To every partner who seeks our minerals, our markets and our young workforce, our offer is clear: invest with us, process with us, build with us,” Ruto added.

He called for partnerships based on mutual benefit and equal treatment, saying African countries should have a greater role in determining how their resources and markets contribute to economic development.

World.title: Judge certifies fresh bid to jail Sakaja, Charles Kerich over Sh76.7m debt as urgent
World.content:
Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja. [File, Standard]

The High Court has certified as urgent a fresh application seeking to have Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja, former Finance Executive Charles Kerich and two other county officials jailed over an alleged breach of a court-approved payment plan in a Sh106.7 million legal fees dispute.

Justice Francis Gikonyo certified the application by Kwengu & Company Advocates seeking to reinstate a three-month jail sentence previously imposed on Kerich and hold Sakaja, current Finance County Executive Committee Member Ibrahim Auma Nyangoya and Chief Officer for Finance Asha Abdi accountable for the alleged failure to pay Sh76.7 million.

World.title: Egypt, World Bank to boost investment and exports
World.content:
Investment and Foreign Trade Minister Mohamed Farid said on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, Egypt is cooperating with the World Bank Group to develop an investment promotion strategy aimed at maximizing the economic impact of foreign investment, strengthening productive capacity and boosting exports by directing investment toward development-priority sectors and activities linked to global value chains.

Farid made the remarks during a session titled “The Role of the Private Sector in Financing Development in Developing Countries” at the 2026 World Investment Forum, organized by the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) in Doha, Qatar, with the participation of officials, experts and representatives of financial and development institutions.

He said the strategy seeks to identify priority sectors and opportunities within value chains to direct investment toward activities that enhance production capacity and exports, strengthen links between major projects and local suppliers and manufacturers, and capitalize on manufacturing opportunities related to renewable energy projects.

Farid noted that attracting long-term private investment requires clear and stable economic policies, streamlined investment procedures, licensing and approvals, and leveraging Egypt’s network of trade agreements to give investors access to wider regional and international markets.

He stressed the importance of preparing bankable projects by completing technical and economic studies, developing financial models, identifying risks and building institutional capacity, particularly in infrastructure, water and energy.

He added that developing domestic capital markets and providing investment guarantees and risk-mitigation mechanisms are essential to mobilizing savings and diversifying development financing, particularly amid high global interest rates, competition for capital and a shift toward fast-growing sectors such as artificial intelligence.

On Africa, Farid called for greater integration of capital markets, harmonized regulations and disclosure requirements to facilitate cross-border investment in public offerings and broaden the investor base.

He also stressed that harmonizing standards, rules of origin and trade procedures under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) would support industrial integration, help African companies expand into new markets and attract more investment.

Farid concluded that strengthening the private sector’s role in development financing requires an integrated framework based on stable economic policies, identifying production and export opportunities, preparing projects for financing, developing financial markets and deepening economic integration among African countries.

World.title: Egypt, Turkey discuss regional de-escalation efforts
World.content:
Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty and his Turkish counterpart Hakan Fidan discussed regional developments and efforts to de-escalate tensions during a phone call on Wednesday, October 28, 2026.The call came as part of ongoing consultations between the two countries, both bilaterally and through the R4 quadrilateral ministerial mechanism, which also includes Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, the Egyptian Foreign Ministry spokesperson stated.

Abdelatty stressed the need for concerted efforts to promote calm and prioritize de-escalation amid continued uncertainty in the region, which has witnessed alternating signs of military escalation and efforts to pull back in recent days, Zaki added.

The two ministers agreed to maintain close consultation and coordination and continue their efforts to prevent further crises in the region.

World.title: Egypt offers condolences to Spain over deadly train accident
World.content:
Egypt expressed its condolences to Spain on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, following a train accident near the town of Urda that reportedly left dozens dead or injured.

In a statement, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation, and Egyptian Expatriates expressed solidarity with the Spanish government and people following the accident.

Egypt also extended its condolences to the families of the victims and expressed sympathy with the Spanish people.

World.title: Egypt committed to supporting sustainable development in Uganda – Irrigation Minister
World.content:
Minister of Irrigation and Water Resources Hani Sewilam affirmed deep-rooted relations between Egypt and Uganda and Egypt’s commitment to further strengthening bilateral cooperation, building on development projects already implemented to serve citizens and support sustainable development efforts in Uganda. Sewilam made the remarks during a meeting with Uganda’s Minister of Water and Environment Kahinda Otafiire on the sidelines of the ninth Cairo Water Week, where the two ministers discussed ways to enhance cooperation in water resources and issues of mutual interest.

Sewilam stressed the importance of continued cooperation in integrated water resources management, implementing water conservation projects and improving water use efficiency, as well as expanding training and capacity-building programs and exchanging technical expertise to strengthen the capabilities of Ugandan professionals in water management.

He also underscored the importance of benefiting from Egypt’s regional pooled financing mechanism, launched to support water projects in Nile Basin countries. He expressed Egypt’s readiness to coordinate with Uganda to identify priority areas of cooperation and projects that address development needs and serve shared interests.

On Nile Basin issues, Sewilam emphasized the importance of preserving the Nile Basin Initiative as the umbrella platform bringing together all basin countries.

He highlighted the need to strengthen cooperation and coordination among Nile Basin countries on the basis of mutual trust, transparency and consideration of shared interests, in a way that promotes sustainable development and mutual benefits without harming any country.

Sewilam expressed his hope for continued coordination with Uganda to support bilateral and regional cooperation in the coming period.

World.title: Top Arab leader says he’s ready to support opposition bloc, urges Eisenkot to “be brave”
World.content:
A top Arab political leader said he is prepared to help the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot form a minority government in order to oust Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

“If they want us to help, we will be there in order to help,” Ahmad Tibi, the head of the Joint List’s parliamentary faction, told CNN in an interview. “We want to support the candidate of the opposition. It is important. It should be done.”

Tibi said his coalition is not looking to join an Eisenkot-led government and would not be seeking any ministerships. He said their only demand is that the next government commits to combating crime impacting the Arab community and stop the demolition of Bedouin homes, which have risen under Netanyahu’s government.

Tibi’s Joint List and Raam, another Arab-majority party, are projected to win a record 19 seats in Israel’s 120-seat parliament after Palestinian citizens of Israel turned out in record numbers – nearly 80 percent – to vote on Wednesday.

Major opposition parties have ruled out forming a government with the Arab parties, but their political support from outside could provide Eisenkot with the tacit support he needs to form a minority government.

Tibi said doing so will require Eisenkot and his coalition to “be brave” in the face of Netanyahu’s condemnation of any attempt to form a government with the help of Israel’s Arab parties.

Tibi said he has received hundreds of calls and messages since the initial exit polls came out, including from a “significant figure” in the opposition bloc, although not from Eisenkot himself.

He said he conveyed a message that the Joint List is “ready” and “willing” to help pave the way for a different government but stressed it would only be possible if “they are brave” enough to do it.

World.title: Netanyahu is the ultimate survivor. But can he survive this time?
World.content:
Jerusalem — In a political career that has spanned more than three decades, Benjamin Netanyahu has been written off too many times to count, only to prove the obituaries were penned prematurely. In a political career that has spanned more than three decades, Benjamin Netanyahu has been written off too many times to count, only to prove the obituaries were penned prematurely. Israel’s election results this week appear to give the prime minister’s opponents a chance to end his run, but in the country’s ruthless political system, it’s no guarantee.

By Wednesday night, most votes had been counted. But there is no clear winner for Israel’s top post, setting up weeks — possibly months — in which Netanyahu’s political survival remains on the line.

With the vote counting nearing its conclusion, Netanyahu’s Likud party remains the largest party in the 120-seat parliament, known as the Knesset, with an estimated 26 seats. But his right-wing bloc has lost its majority, set to win only 53 seats, short of the 61-seat majority needed to govern.

Netanyahu hasn’t won. But he hasn’t lost, either — at least not yet. Now, he has to stop his rivals from building their own government, and he may survive again.

The Arab parties

On paper, the opposition holds roughly 67 seats, but that arithmetic is fractured by ideological, national and personal rivalries. Netanyahu’s main challenger, Gadi Eisenkot, won 21 seats, but the Jewish opposition parties total only 48, well short of victory. To reach 61, they would need the support of two Arab parties, Raam and the Joint List, which are projected to win a record 19 seats between them. Analysts say that record turnout by Arabs or Palestinian citizens of Israel was in part a backlash to four years of a far-right national security minister under whom crime in the Arab community soared.

This is where the math gets complicated. Raam is an Islamist party that draws heavily from Israel’s Bedouin community. Its leader, Mansour Abbas, became the first Arab politician to join an Israeli government following the country’s 2021 election. The Joint List, projected to be the bigger Arab party, combines several smaller parties: the Communist Hadash, secularist Taal and nationalist Balad factions.

On Wednesday, Yair Golan, leader of the left-wing Democrats party, called on his partners to count the Arab parties as part of the bloc, rejecting what he called Netanyahu’s “racist division between Jewish and Arab votes.” But two of Eisenkot’s right-wing allies, Naftali Bennett and Avigdor Liberman, have opposed any government that depends on the Arab parties. (They have not issued a statement on the issue since polls closed.)

The Joint List said Wednesday that it was ready for political cooperation and willing to do “do everything in its power to bring Netanyahu’s rule to an end.”

What will Netanyahu do?

A source close to Netanyahu said his main post-election goal is to delegitimize and therefore prevent the Jewish-Arab political cooperation that could send him home.

“He is very concerned about a minority government,” the source said. Netanyahu even plans to pressure individual opposition lawmakers not to cooperate with the Arab parties. After campaigning against them throughout the election, Likud issued a statement Wednesday accusing the Arab parties of “stealing the election” through bribery, threats, violence and forgery, echoing election fraud claims from his closest ally, US President Donald Trump. The Central Elections Committee said Wednesday it was examining the complaint, but the committee had already dismissed thousands of complaints from the different parties on election day.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu speaks to supporters at the Likud party’s election-night event on October 28 in Jerusalem. Chris McGrath/Getty Images

Netanyahu plans to “neutralize this possibility by all means,” the source told CNN, “including launching an attack on Iran or enlisting President Trump to intervene in Israeli politics on his behalf.”

The opposition fears that Netanyahu could use a security crisis to stall or block a new government. Before the election, Netanyahu had pressed Trump to launch a joint attack on Iran, but Washington held off, partly because Israeli military chief of staff Eyal Zamir warned it could disrupt the vote. An Israeli security source told CNN the operational plans are ready and awaiting Trump’s approval, possibly after the US midterms.

“There is no way to know what Netanyahu will do,” an opposition source told CNN. “We are aware that he may try to push for another escalation.” Another source said that Netanyahu “will do everything he can not to leave the prime minister’s office, including domestic and external chaos.”

Eisenkot, a former Israel Defense Forces chief of staff, called on Israel’s security chiefs Tuesday night to remember that “Netanyahu is a caretaker prime minister, without a mandate and without public confidence.” Speaking to supporters shortly after exit polls were published, Eisenkot declared that the public “has chosen change.”

In his first reaction to the updated results since Tuesday night’s speech, Eisenkot said he remains committed to “bringing change to Israel.”

What comes next

The numbers can still change. By Wednesday evening, the Central Elections Committee is expected to finish counting most ballots. Attention now turns to double-envelope ballots from home by soldiers, prisoners, hospital patients and staff, diplomats abroad and voters with disabilities. The committee estimates there are between 430,000 and 480,000 double envelopes, enough for over 10 seats. They are counted separately in a special verification process, with final results expected Thursday.

Then the political maneuvering begins in earnest.

The next step runs through President Isaac Herzog, whose post-election role is pivotal. His job here is to consult with all elected parties on the candidate they recommend as prime minister, before picking the one he believes is most likely to secure a 61-seat majority. This is not necessarily the leader of the largest party but the one with the most plausible path to a coalition.

Eisenkot is likely to collect more recommendations than Netanyahu, since the Arab parties are expected to back him.

Then the clock starts ticking.

The chosen candidate has 28 days — and a possible 14-day extension — to negotiate with other parties over cabinet posts, budgets and policies in order to form a government. If he fails, the mandate passes to another candidate for another four weeks. If he fails, too, the Knesset gets a short window to put forward an alternative candidate. If that fails, the country goes to automatic elections.

Netanyahu, as caretaker prime minister, has a built-in advantage. If Eisenkot receives the mandate first — and fails — all he needs to do is wait for his time to pass. And if Israel finds itself headed for new elections, Netanyahu will remain caretaker for months.

Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot addresses his supporters at an election-night rally after the first exit polls were announced, in Tel Aviv early October 28. Maya Levin/AFP/Getty Images

Eisenkot’s options

Eisenkot isn’t out of options entirely.

Even without forming a government, the opposition could still leverage its parliamentary majority to replace the Knesset speaker and other key positions. That could limit Netanyahu’s ability to govern and even enable the opposition to advance legislation.

But Eisenkot, a retired lieutenant general, isn’t on his preferred battlefield. Netanyahu’s coalition remains incredibly loyal, and he doesn’t have to worry in any real way about defections. The same cannot be said for Eisenkot. His diverse coalition is far less ideologically aligned, and even the tiniest step could splinter the bloc and send the country back to elections.

For now, the focus is on Herzog, whose role is even more important given the current deadlock. With neither bloc holding a clear majority, he may try to push Netanyahu and Eisenkot to form a unity government.

“We must do everything to avoid another round of elections,” Herzog said Wednesday. He called on party leaders to come to consultations with an “open mind.”

World.title: Why the US has become a political base for Brazil’s Bolsonaro allies
World.content:
Three days after losing Brazil’s presidential election on Sunday, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro arrived in Miami, joining other prominent allies of the Bolsonaro political movement who have sought refuge in the United States while facing legal troubles back home.

The defeated candidate reportedly crossed into Argentina with his wife and two daughters on Tuesday, then boarded a private plane that stopped in Ecuador before landing in South Florida. He left after a Supreme Court order, issued the day after the election, required him to surrender his passports and barred him from leaving Brazil. Justice Alexandre de Moraes, who has a long history of legal battles with the Bolsonaro family, issued the order citing a “concrete risk” that the senator would flee.

On Friday, on the American conservative podcast Louder with Crowder, his brother Eduardo Bolsonaro had suggested that Flávio should leave Brazil if he lost to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, citing concerns about the investigations he could face once his Senate term ends.

In a video posted Monday, Flávio Bolsonaro addressed his brother’s comments and promised to comply with the Supreme Court order, citing political persecution. His Senate term ends on January 31, 2027, leaving him out of elected office for the first time in 24 years.

Flávio Bolsonaro is currently under investigation by the country’s highest court for alleged acts of corruption and money laundering.

Upon arriving in the US, he released a three-page statement on Wednesday, declaring himself the “leader of Brazil,” despite losing Sunday’s runoff to Lula. He repeated unsubstantiated claims of electoral fraud, said it had not been his intention to leave the country and vowed to lead the Brazilian opposition from the United States.

“I want to make it clear: I did not flee Brazil. I left for Brazil,” he wrote, describing himself as a victim of political persecution and thanking US President Donald Trump and Argentine President Javier Milei for their support in his departure plans.

A growing political base abroad

In the United States, Flávio Bolsonaro joins a growing list of prominent figures in the Bolsonaro movement who have relocated there while facing legal trouble in Brazil.

Eduardo, a former congressman, moved to the US in early 2025, saying he was the target of political persecution, and received permanent residency in July. Brazil’s Supreme Court has since sentenced him to four years and two months in prison for coercion, finding that he lobbied US officials to pressure the judges overseeing his father’s coup case. Moraes ordered his arrest this month.

Former intelligence chief and congressman Alexandre Ramagem slipped out of Brazil through Guyana in September 2025, while the Supreme Court was still trying him for his role in the plot to overturn the 2022 election, and arrived in the US the day he was convicted. US immigration authorities detained him in Florida in April and released him two days later. His allies say he has applied for asylum.

Conservative commentators Allan dos Santos and Paulo Figueiredo have also built platforms in the US while facing legal disputes in Brazil.

Their cases differ, but together they suggest that the US has become more than a refuge for Bolsonaro allies. It is also a political base, with ideological allies, access to influential conservatives and a network of Brazilian supporters.

“Exile is no longer isolation,” said Teresa Cristina Schneider Marques, a political scientist at PUCRS (Pontifical Catholic University of Rio Grande do Sul), who researches “Bolsonarismo” in the US. “With social media and the media, it has become a strategy for international and transnational projection.”

Why the United States?

The US is home to the largest Brazilian community abroad, with about two million people, according to estimates from Brazil’s Foreign Ministry. That community has historically leaned conservative. Brazilian voters in the US backed the right-wing candidate in the 2010, 2014, 2018 and 2022 runoffs, according to Brazilian electoral data. This year they backed Flávio Bolsonaro, who won nearly 63% of their valid votes in Sunday’s runoff.

The ties go beyond the ballot box. Connections between Brazilian conservative elites and American political figures deepened during the overlapping presidencies of Jair Bolsonaro — Flávio’s father — and Trump, whose movements share nationalist and socially conservative positions.

After Jair Bolsonaro lost the 2022 election, thousands of his supporters stormed Brazil’s Congress, Supreme Court and presidential palace on January 8, 2023, in an attack that drew comparisons to the January 6, 2021, assault on the US Capitol. As legal pressure mounted, several prominent figures in his movement left for the United States.

Since then, Marques said, the movement has worked to “domesticate the cause” on three fronts, persuading American society to adopt it as its own.

The first is Washington, where allies have sought to influence US policy toward Brazil. The second is the media: Eduardo Bolsonaro and Figueiredo, among others, have used American podcasts, conservative outlets and social media to argue that Brazil’s judiciary is persecuting the right.

The third is the Brazilian diaspora.

“The diaspora plays an important role in spreading narratives, but also in translating them,” Marques said, “not just in English, but also adapting political messages so they resonate with American audiences.”

Groups such as Yes Brasil in Florida and the Congresso Conservador Brasileiro in Massachusetts bring together supporters, Brazilian politicians and the immigrant community, and can act as intermediaries with American conservative circles.

The result is a division of labor: prominent figures gain access to institutions and influential allies, while ordinary supporters spread the message among the Americans and Brazilians around them.

The ultimate aim is to win American support and use it to pressure Brazilian institutions, a tactic scholars call the “boomerang effect” — in which political movements turn to international allies to influence decisions at home.

A powerful ally in the White House

Trump has repeatedly criticized Brazil’s judiciary over its treatment of Jair Bolsonaro, who was sentenced to more than 27 years in prison for the coup plot. That support has had concrete consequences. Last year, Trump imposed tariffs of up to 50% on Brazilian products, explicitly citing Jair Bolsonaro’s prosecution, and his administration sanctioned Brazilian judicial authorities.

More recently, a Reuters investigation published ahead of Sunday’s runoff election, described efforts by two senior State Department officials to help the Bolsonaro family return to power, including measures intended to pressure Lula’s government.

Trump has questioned the legitimacy of Brazil’s election, without providing evidence of fraud, pointing to a last-minute Supreme Court decision to extend voting by two hours, until 7 p.m., following reports of transportation problems. At a campaign rally in Texas on Tuesday, Trump also compared Brazil’s election to his longstanding allegations of electoral cheating by Democrats.

US President Donald Trump waves goodbye after speaking during a midterm campaign rally at Lubbock Memorial Civic Center in Texas on October 27. Kent Nishimura/AFP/Getty Images

Trump confirmed Wednesday that the US allowed Flávio Bolsonaro to enter the country. “Well, I’m not going to make a comment about that, but I know that we gave him a pass to come into the country, so we’ll see,” Trump told reporters before departing for Ohio.

A Trump adviser had told CNN Tuesday that the president had approved allowing Flávio Bolsonaro into the United States, and US officials confirmed that the administration would issue visas to the senator and his family.

It is unclear what visas they received or whether Flávio Bolsonaro will seek asylum. Permission to enter does not mean someone qualifies for asylum or is shielded from extradition.

Marques argued that, for Trump, welcoming Bolsonaro allies has political value: their claims of persecution fit a narrative, shared across the global right, that portrays leftist governments as authoritarian.

Granting asylum implicitly accuses another country of persecution, she noted.

But Marques said that narrative is harder to sell about Brazil than about Venezuela or Cuba. “Lula ends up being a stone in the shoe of the global right,” she said. “Lula is respected abroad and submitted to the courts when he was jailed in 2018, which makes him hard to cast as an authoritarian.”

Brazil’s President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, the Workers’ Party candidate for re-election, speaks after winning the presidential runoff in Sao Paulo, on October 25. Amanda Perobelli/Reuters

His reelection has also energized left-wing leaders abroad, who see his comeback victory as a possible turning point after a series of right-wing electoral gains. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, for instance, celebrated Lula’s win as an inspiration ahead of Spain’s November 29 election, declaring: “What happened in Brazil will happen in Spain. The comeback of global progressivism has just begun.”

Marques suggested that a current US welcome carries less weight than it once did. “It would be one thing for the Obama administration to receive someone from Brazil as persecuted. It’s another for the Donald Trump administration.”

Nor is that protection necessarily permanent; a successive US administration might take a different view of the matter than Trump does.

A risky strategy for Brazil’s right?

Flávio received nearly 60 million votes in Sunday’s runoff, a sign of the right’s continued strength, and his sudden departure caught his own party off guard.

Rogério Marinho, the senator who coordinated Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign, said Tuesday that party leaders had not been told of his travel plans.

With Jair Bolsonaro serving his sentence under house arrest and Flávio and Eduardo abroad, some on the right are already looking to alternatives.

“I think it’s a somewhat risky move, particularly the way Flávio did it,” Marques said. She sees exile as a deliberate political strategy, but unlike Eduardo, who presented his move as a political choice, Flávio Bolsonaro left immediately after a court order restricting his travel, feeding the perception that he fled to avoid prosecution. “The way it was done raised the costs of that strategy,” she said.

The episode could give other conservative leaders an opening to distance themselves from the family, she said, though Brazil’s right has repeatedly struggled to build an identity independent of Jair Bolsonaro. “The big question now is how long the right will allow itself to remain tied to Bolsonarismo.”

She also finds the persecution narrative hard to sustain at home, since the movement’s allies won a large share of Congress this month.

Having Flávio and Eduardo in the US could strengthen the family’s international influence. But it also presents a striking paradox: the movement’s three most prominent figures are trying to shape Brazil’s political future while two face legal risks if they return to the country, and the third, Jair Bolsonaro, remains under house arrest.

Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro disembarks from a plane after arriving at Opa-locka Executive Airport near Miami, Florida, on October 28. Eva Marie Uzcategui/Reuters

Marques expects the fight to play out on the international stage. Brazil could seek Flávio Bolsonaro’s extradition, she said, setting up a prolonged dispute over whether he is a fugitive or a dissident, along the lines of the Julian Assange or Edward Snowden cases.

“Just as Bolsonarismo is trying to make this boomerang effect work with the right, the left will do the same,” she said. “Now the question is which way it will come back.”

World.title: Russia and US discussing sanctions relief for Moscow’s sovereign wealth fund, Kremlin aide says
World.content:
The Trump administration and the Kremlin are discussing the possible lifting of US sanctions on Russia’s multibillion-dollar sovereign wealth fund, Russian state media quoted a Kremlin aide as saying, in what would be another US concession to Moscow in negotiations to end its war in Ukraine.

Russian President Vladimir Putin’s foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov told reporters that talks with the United States to lift sanctions on the state-owned Russian Direct Investment Fund have been “going on for some time,” Russian state news agency TASS reported on Wednesday.

“What the outcome will be, I do not know,” he added.

The fund’s CEO and presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev was actively engaging American officials on lifting the sanctions, Ushakov said.

The Biden administration imposed the sanctions in the wake of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, calling it a “known slush fund” for Putin and his inner circle.

CNN has reached out to the White House and US Department of State for comment.

The New York Times first reported on Tuesday that the Trump administration was considering lifting the sanctions.

President Donald Trump has defended recent concessions made to Russia on sanctions, which have triggered criticism from both sides of the aisle in Washington and driven a wedge between the US and its Western allies.

Earlier this month, Trump announced a deal to allow Russian diesel exports to global energy markets and waived a further slate of sanctions related to Russian fossil fuel sales that had only just been signed into law.

The forestalled legislation would have imposed tariffs of up to 100 percent on, among other things, goods brought into the US from the five largest importers of Russian crude oil or gas, the sale of which is crucial to funding the Kremlin’s war machine.

The US-Russia diesel deal involves suspending fuel export sanctions for six months to allow for diesel sales at market prices, but experts have cast doubt on the impact it will have on global diesel markets.

Russia banned exports of diesel in early July, after Ukrainian drone strikes on its refineries triggered widespread fuel shortages across the country.

The White House is trying to relieve pressure on oil and diesel prices in the US ahead of crucial midterm elections next week.

Trump has also said his decision to waive some sanctions on Russia was to keep Moscow at the negotiating table.

“I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine, and don’t want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table,” Trump wrote in a Truth Social post on October 18.

Trump has blamed high global fuel prices on Ukraine, and heaped pressure on Ukrainian President Volodymr Zelensky to halt strikes on Russian refineries even as Russia continues its attacks on Ukraine’s towns, cities, and energy infrastructure.

There is growing anxiety in Kyiv and Europe that the Trump administration will make further concessions to Moscow in an effort to get Putin to agree to a peace deal.

Zelensky recently told NBC’s “Meet the Press” that the waivers strengthened Putin’s war against Ukraine while Moscow was failing on the battlefield.

Kyiv has long advocated for tougher sanctions on Russian energy exports.

Last week, Putin said the Kremlin would be ready to resume trilateral Russia-US-Ukraine peace talks after mid-November, at the request of US special envoy Steve Witkoff who met the Russian leader in St. Petersburg. During the talks, Putin expressed interest in restoring economic cooperation with the US.

World.title: Liberia: EPA Boss Dr. Yarkpawolo Accepts Global Donor Advocacy Role as GEF Seeks Increased Funding for Environmental Protection
World.content:
Dr. Yarkpawolo’s anticipated engagement with donors is expected to highlight the importance of translating international environmental commitments into financial support capable of producing measurable improvements in vulnerable communities. His decision to accept the advocacy responsibility also reflects an emphasis on strengthening cooperation between environmental financing institutions and countries experiencing the consequences of climate change, biodiversity loss and environmental degradation

YEREVAN, Armenia – The Executive Director of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Dr. Emmanuel King Urey Yarkpawolo, has accepted an invitation to spearhead advocacy for increased financial contributions to the Global Environment Facility (GEF), positioning the country to play a greater role in international efforts to mobilize resources for biodiversity conservation, climate resilience and environmental protection.

By Selma Lomax, [email protected]

The decision followed a high-level meeting Thursday between Dr. Yarkpawolo and the newly appointed Chief Executive Officer and Chairperson of the GEF, Diego Mesa Puyo, in Yerevan, Armenia, where world leaders, environmental experts and policymakers are participating in the 17th Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP17).



During the discussions, the GEF leadership invited the Liberian environmental official to engage directly with international donors and development partners to encourage stronger financial commitments to the institution, which supports environmental projects in developing countries.

Dr. Yarkpawolo accepted the invitation, taking on an advocacy responsibility that could strengthen Liberia’s participation in global environmental financing discussions while highlighting the difficulties confronting countries with significant natural resources but limited financial capacity to protect them.

The engagement comes amid growing international concern over inadequate financing for biodiversity conservation, climate adaptation and sustainable natural resource management, particularly in developing countries where environmental degradation continues to threaten livelihoods and economic development.

Liberia, home to a substantial portion of the remaining Upper Guinean tropical rainforest, has consistently emphasized the importance of international financial assistance in protecting its forests, wildlife habitats and other natural resources while pursuing economic development.

Dr. Yarkpawolo’s anticipated engagement with donors is expected to highlight the importance of translating international environmental commitments into financial support capable of producing measurable improvements in vulnerable communities.

His decision to accept the advocacy responsibility also reflects an emphasis on strengthening cooperation between environmental financing institutions and countries experiencing the consequences of climate change, biodiversity loss and environmental degradation.

The Liberian environmental official is expected to draw attention to the country’s conservation responsibilities, particularly the challenge of protecting tropical forests while ensuring that rural communities have access to sustainable livelihood opportunities.

Dr. Yarkpawolo said: “Countries like Liberia are protecting environmental resources that are important not only to our people but to the entire world. However, conservation cannot succeed on commitments alone. We need stronger financial partnerships, predictable funding and practical investments that allow vulnerable communities to protect nature while improving their livelihoods.”

Beyond the donor mobilization discussions, Thursday’s meeting provided an opportunity for Dr. Yarkpawolo to brief the GEF leadership on Liberia’s

ongoing environmental initiatives and identify priority areas requiring additional international support.

Among the projects discussed was the Strengthening Agricultural Resilience through Transformational Livelihood Adaptation in Liberia (SARTLA) initiative, which has received its first disbursement of funding.

The project is designed to strengthen the ability of agricultural communities to withstand climate-related challenges while promoting livelihood adaptation and improving resilience among vulnerable populations.

Agriculture remains an important source of employment and household income across Liberia, particularly in rural communities where families depend heavily on farming for their survival.

However, changing rainfall patterns, flooding, soil degradation and unpredictable weather conditions continue to create difficulties for farmers, threatening agricultural productivity and household food security.

The SARTLA initiative is intended to help address some of these challenges by supporting adaptation measures that strengthen agricultural livelihoods and reduce vulnerability to environmental shocks.

During the meeting, Dr. Yarkpawolo provided updates on the project’s financing progress, underscoring the importance of sustained support for initiatives designed to protect vulnerable communities against climate-related threats.

The discussions also focused on a proposed US$10 million Urban Resilience Project, which Liberia is seeking to advance as part of broader efforts to address environmental risks affecting urban communities.

The proposed project comes as several urban settlements in Liberia continue to experience flooding, drainage problems, environmental pollution and infrastructure challenges associated with rapid population growth and unplanned development.

In Monrovia and surrounding communities, seasonal flooding remains a recurring concern, often disrupting transportation, damaging properties and exposing residents to health and sanitation risks.

Environmental experts have repeatedly emphasized the need for investments in drainage infrastructure, improved urban planning and climate-resilient development to reduce the vulnerability of densely populated settlements.

The proposed Urban Resilience Project could provide an opportunity to strengthen Liberia’s response to these challenges if the necessary financing is secured and the project moves into implementation.

Although no new funding approval for the proposed initiative was announced during Thursday’s meeting, its inclusion in the discussions demonstrated Liberia’s interest in expanding cooperation with the GEF to address emerging environmental challenges.

Another important component of the engagement centered on Liberia’s priorities under the ninth replenishment cycle of the Global Environment Facility, known as GEF-9. The replenishment process is important because it determines the financial resources available to support future environmental projects across eligible countries.

For Liberia, access to GEF financing remains significant because domestic resources alone are insufficient to address the country’s extensive environmental protection and climate adaptation needs. The country faces the difficult responsibility of preserving globally important ecosystems while responding to economic pressures, infrastructure deficits and the development needs of communities dependent on natural resources.

Its forests provide habitats for endangered wildlife species, support biodiversity conservation and contribute to broader international efforts to address climate change.

At the same time, forest-dependent communities require sustainable economic opportunities that can reduce pressure on natural resources without undermining their livelihoods.

The EPA Executive Director’s anticipated donor advocacy could therefore reinforce Liberia’s position that environmental financing must go beyond international declarations and provide practical assistance to communities confronting environmental threats.

Such assistance could include strengthening agricultural resilience, improving urban environmental management, supporting biodiversity conservation and building the institutional capacity required to implement environmental programs.

He added: “My commitment to engaging donors is driven by the urgent need to close the financing gap confronting developing countries. We must demonstrate that every investment in biodiversity conservation, climate resilience and sustainable development is an investment in the future of humanity. Liberia is prepared to play its part, but international solidarity must be reflected in concrete financial support.”

The GEF chief welcomed the updates presented by Dr. Yarkpawolo and expressed confidence in continued support for Liberia’s environmental protection and climate resilience efforts.

Mr. Mesa Puyo’s response highlighted the continuing relationship between Liberia and the international financing institution, which has supported initiatives aimed at addressing environmental degradation and strengthening national capacity to manage natural resources.

The Global Environment Facility serves as a major international financing mechanism for projects addressing biodiversity loss, climate change, land degradation, international waters and pollution.

Its financial contributions are particularly important to developing countries seeking assistance to implement environmental commitments under international agreements.

Thursday’s meeting also produced another significant development, with Dr. Yarkpawolo extending an invitation to the GEF chief to visit Liberia and personally assess projects supported by the institution.

Mr. Mesa Puyo accepted the invitation, creating an opportunity for future engagement with government institutions, project implementers and communities benefiting from GEF-supported interventions. Although a date for the proposed visit was not disclosed, the planned engagement could allow the GEF leadership to observe the implementation of environmental projects and better understand the challenges confronting beneficiary communities.

The visit could also provide Liberia with an opportunity to present additional financing needs and demonstrate how international environmental investments contribute to community development and ecosystem protection.

For Dr. Yarkpawolo, the proposed visit represents an opportunity to strengthen the connection between decisions made by international financing institutions and the realities experienced by communities implementing environmental projects.

Direct interaction with project beneficiaries could help demonstrate the benefits of existing investments while identifying gaps that require additional financial and technical support. Such engagement is particularly important in Liberia, where environmental challenges frequently intersect with poverty, limited infrastructure, agricultural dependence and inadequate access to essential services.
