World.title: K-Pop Band BTS Cuts Fan Walk in São Paulo
World.content:
Estádio do MorumBIS in São Paulo, where BTS plays three nights. File photo.

BTS, the South Korean pop group, skipped the part of its São Paulo show that fans love most: the walk through the crowd during the song “IDOL”. Our BTS São Paulo live updates hub tracks the three-night run.

Key Facts What happened: At the 28 October opener, BTS did not make its usual walk near the crowd during “IDOL”.

At the 28 October opener, BTS did not make its usual walk near the crowd during “IDOL”. Why: No official reason has been given; some fans guessed the floor was too crowded.

No official reason has been given; some fans guessed the floor was too crowded. Next: Shows on Friday 30 and Saturday 31 October start at 8:00 p.m. in São Paulo (7:00 p.m. ET).

Shows on Friday 30 and Saturday 31 October start at 8:00 p.m. in São Paulo (7:00 p.m. ET). Scale: All three shows are sold out at MorumBIS, a São Paulo stadium holding about 84,000.

The Walk Fans Did Not Get

BTS opened its three-night São Paulo run at Estádio do MorumBIS on Wednesday, 28 October 2026. During “IDOL”, the seven members did not make the usual walk through the lower stadium area.

The walk had been part of the show at earlier stops on the “ARIRANG” world tour, the group’s current stadium tour. Some attendees said the floor looked too crowded for the movement, but that remains unverified, and no organiser has said the venue was oversold.

Online reaction split. Some fans criticised the change, while others backed dropping the walk if crowd conditions made it a safety risk.

Fans Also Reported Entry Problems

Fans also reported closed gates and some ticket holders left outside on opening night, in heavy rain. No response from the promoter, Live Nation Brasil, had been published.

The opener was BTS’s first Brazilian show in seven years, since its May 2019 shows at Allianz Parque, another São Paulo stadium.

What Happens Next

The remaining concerts are on Friday, 30 October, and Saturday, 31 October 2026, at 8:00 p.m. Brasília time (BRT, UTC−3), which is 7:00 p.m. Eastern Daylight Time. Gates open at 4:00 p.m. BRT on both nights.

The venue’s capacity is reported at about 84,400 per night, so roughly 250,000 people across the three sold-out shows. A cinema live viewing of the 30 October show is promoted in more than 80 countries and regions, with screening times varying by market.

Fans on the MorumBIS pitch before an earlier stadium concert. File photo, not from the BTS show. Photo: Fronteira, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

Roads, Maps and Screens

São Paulo’s traffic authority, CET (Companhia de Engenharia de Tráfego), began road restrictions around MorumBIS at 11:00 p.m. on 27 October. A second phase runs from 11:00 p.m. on 29 October until 1:30 a.m. on Sunday, 1 November.

Procon-SP, the state consumer-protection agency, pressed Live Nation Brasil over screens and visibility. The state prosecutors’ office questioned seating maps that showed standing zones called Pit 1 and Pit 2, and on 26 October the promoter said the structure matched the official map shown when sales opened, and that the production format was standardised across South America.

What It Means for US Readers

US fans can follow the 30 October show through the cinema live viewing; check local listings for the time. The two remaining shows start at 7:00 p.m. ET, so they fall in the US evening.

The question to watch is whether the promoter or the group explains the missing walk before Friday. A calm, crowd-safe show on the next two nights would end the row quickly.

What Is Not Known

BTS, Live Nation Brasil and MorumBIS have not said why the walk was cut. Nothing confirms that the floor was oversold or that any safety limit was breached.

It is also unclear whether the walk returns on 30 or 31 October. We found no prediction-market price for the São Paulo shows.

World.title: Brazil Brewer Ambev Profit Falls 10%
World.content:
Draught beer at a Brazilian Oktoberfest. (Photo: gustavo.kunst, CC BY-SA 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons)

Brazil Markets · Company Earnings · Ambev

Published Thursday, 29 October, 6:15 a.m. ET · Source: Ambev earnings release, filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission

Key Facts The number. Profit fell 10.2% to R$4.37 billion (US$816 million), against a year-earlier figure lifted by a one-off gain.

The core business. Normalized profit, which strips out one-offs, rose 14.3% to R$4.39 billion (US$821 million).

The cash. The board approved buying back up to 190 million shares, about R$2.9 billion (US$540 million).

Still unknown. How fast Ambev will buy; the plan runs until 28 April 2028.

Brazil’s Ambev sold pricier beer and still reported a smaller profit. The brewer, whose shares trade in New York as ABEV, earned R$4.37 billion (US$816 million) in the third quarter, down 10.2% from a year earlier.

The drop is largely a one-off effect, because a year earlier the profit included a gain of R$885 million (US$165 million) from selling operations, according to Ambev’s cash-flow statement. Our guide to Brazil’s economy covers the household spending behind these sales.

Why Reported Profit Fell While Core Profit Rose

Ambev publishes two profit numbers. The reported figure counts everything, while “normalized” profit removes one-off items so investors can compare quarters.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

On the normalized measure, profit rose 14.3% to R$4.39 billion (US$821 million), from R$3.84 billion (US$718 million) a year earlier. Net financial costs fell to R$312 million (US$58 million) from R$1.09 billion (US$203 million), which helped.

Taxes pushed the other way. Ambev’s income-tax bill rose to R$882 million (US$165 million) from R$350 million (US$65 million).

In Plain English Normalized profit: profit with one-off items removed.

profit with one-off items removed. EBITDA: earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, a rough gauge of operating cash earned.

earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, a rough gauge of operating cash earned. Organic growth: growth after stripping out currency moves and company purchases or sales.

growth after stripping out currency moves and company purchases or sales. Hectolitre: 100 litres.

Fermentation tanks inside a brewery. File photo. Photo: "Beer brewing tanks" by SteveStrummer, via Wikimedia Commons, CC0.

Higher Prices Drove the Sales Gain

Net revenue rose 3.6% to R$21.6 billion (US$4.04 billion), or 7.6% on an organic basis. Volume grew only 0.8% on an organic basis, so price and mix did the work.

Revenue per hectolitre climbed 6.8% organically. Normalized EBITDA rose 3.0% to R$7.27 billion (US$1.36 billion), with a margin of 33.7%, down 0.2 points as reported but up 0.4 points organically.

Premium and Lighter Beers Carry the Growth

Premium brands grew volume in the mid-teens, Ambev said. Ambev’s “Balanced Choices” range of lighter options grew by more than 90%, and alcohol-free beer by more than 30%.

Michelob Ultra, a low-calorie beer, and Stella Artois Pure Gold, a gluten-free one, more than doubled in volume when counted together. Mainstream volumes, the cheaper core of the market, fell by a low single-digit percentage.

Chief executive Carlos Lisboa said the quarter “built on the progress we achieved in the first half of the year.” Net revenue grew in every business unit.

Where Volume Grew and Shrank

Brazil soft drinks and other non-alcoholic drinks: +3.6%.

+3.6%. Central America and the Caribbean: +2.3%.

+2.3%. Brazil beer: +0.5%.

+0.5%. Canada: −1.0%.

−1.0%. Latin America South, including Argentina and Chile: −1.4%.

A Buyback of Up to 190 Million Shares

Ambev’s board approved the repurchase programme on 28 October, mainly so the shares can be cancelled. Cash from operations rose 11.0% to R$7.68 billion (US$1.44 billion).

What It Means for US Readers

US investors hold Ambev through ABEV, an American depositary receipt, a US-traded certificate that stands for shares listed in Brazil. Earnings arrive in reals, so the dollar value of the profit depends on the exchange rate, about 5.35 reals per dollar on 29 October (from the market-data provider RT); our real-to-dollar guide explains the swings.

Buybacks and rising prices can support a share price, but they do not prove demand is growing. For context on the wider market, see our Brazil stock market guide and our earlier look at how Ambev traded volume for margins.

What Is Not Known

It is not yet clear whether premium growth can keep offsetting weak mainstream sales, or how quickly Ambev will buy back shares. Trading in New York had not begun when we published, and executives discuss the results on a call at 11:30 a.m. ET today.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why did Ambev’s profit fall in the third quarter?

Reported profit fell 10.2% to R$4.37 billion (US$816 million) because the year-earlier figure included a gain of R$885 million (US$165 million) from selling operations. On Ambev’s normalized measure, profit rose 14.3%.

How much will Ambev spend on share buybacks?

The board approved on 28 October a programme to repurchase up to 190 million shares, about R$2.9 billion (US$540 million) at that day’s closing price. The plan runs until 28 April 2028.

Sources: Ambev third-quarter 2026 earnings release and quarterly financial statements, filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on 29 October 2026; exchange rate from market-data provider RT.

World.title: Sánchez Trails Feijóo by 7 Points in Polls
World.content:
Alberto Núñez Feijóo, the PP leader, in Santander in 2023. File photo.

Spain heads into its 29 November general election with the conservative Partido Popular (PP) ahead in most polls and in prediction markets. Our Spain Election 2026 hub tracks every development.

Key Facts Vote: Spain elects its 350-seat Congress and the Senate on Sunday, 29 November 2026.

Spain elects its 350-seat Congress and the Senate on Sunday, 29 November 2026. Polls: The latest NC Report poll, taken 22 to 24 October, put the PP at 32.9% and the Socialists at 25.8%.

The latest NC Report poll, taken 22 to 24 October, put the PP at 32.9% and the Socialists at 25.8%. Split: The state-run CIS survey, Spain’s public pollster, has the Socialists ahead, 34% to 22.2%.

The state-run CIS survey, Spain’s public pollster, has the Socialists ahead, 34% to 22.2%. Prediction markets: Kalshi, a US-regulated exchange, gave PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo 78.0% to become prime minister (5:24 a.m. ET, 29 October).

This story is part of our coverage of the Spain Election 2026. Dates, times and how to follow it are in our guide. Latest: Spain's Housing Costs Outrun Wages in 2026

Why the Right Leads Most Polls

Spain’s two big parties are the PP and the governing Spanish Socialist Workers’ Party (PSOE) of Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez. Vox, a nationalist conservative party to the PP’s right, comes third in every recent survey.

NC Report, a Spanish polling firm, surveyed voters from 22 to 24 October. It put the PP at 32.9%, PSOE at 25.8% and Vox at 19.0%.

SocioMétrica, another Spanish firm, found a similar picture in fieldwork on 10 and 11 October. It had the PP at 32.6%, PSOE at 26.2% and Vox at 18.8%.

GESOP, a third firm, was less kind to the PP in a poll ending 8 October. Even so, it placed the PP first at 28.7%, with PSOE at 26.1% and Vox at 18.9%.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What Prediction Markets Say

Kalshi, a prediction exchange regulated in the US by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), asks who will be prime minister after the vote. At 5:24 a.m. ET on 29 October (10:24 a.m. in Madrid), Feijóo stood at 78.0%, Sánchez at 13.0% and Vox leader Santiago Abascal at 3.0%.

A second Kalshi market asks whether PP and Vox together will win at least 50% of the vote. It priced that at 40.0%.

The prime-minister market had traded 32,715 contracts. These prices are bets, not polls, and can move within minutes of news.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Why the State Survey Disagrees

The Centro de Investigaciones Sociológicas (CIS) is Spain’s state-run public opinion institute. Its October barometer, based on more than 5,000 interviews from 1 to 6 October, put PSOE at 34%, the PP at 22.2% and Vox at 17.1%.

That is a gap of nearly 12 points in the opposite direction from the private polls. Nothing we could verify explains it yet, so the size of any lead remains unsettled.

What Is Not Known

We found no verified report of a new official result, court ruling or change to the 29 November timetable. The final seat split, the smaller regional parties and the question of who can reach the 176 seats needed for a Congress majority all remain open.

It is also unclear whether the CIS gap reflects method or a real late shift in the campaign. Prediction markets and private polls agree on direction, but both can be wrong.

What It Means for US Readers

A PP-led government would replace a left-led one in one of the euro area’s biggest economies. Spain’s weight in European Union budget and migration debates would shift with it.

American investors and newsrooms increasingly watch exchanges such as Kalshi and Polymarket for early signals. Spain offers a live test of how real-money odds track polls a month before a vote.

Congress is due to meet on 23 December, so a new government could take shape quickly after the vote.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is ahead in Spain’s election polls?

The conservative Partido Popular (PP) leads most private polls. NC Report’s 22 to 24 October survey shows the PP at 32.9% against 25.8% for the Socialists (PSOE), but the state-run Centro de Investigaciones Sociológicas (CIS) shows PSOE ahead.

What do prediction markets say about Spain’s election?

On Kalshi, a CFTC-regulated US exchange, Alberto Núñez Feijóo had a 78.0% implied chance of becoming prime minister at 5:24 a.m. ET on 29 October. These are bets, not polls.

Sources: NC Report, SocioMétrica and GESOP polls; Centro de Investigaciones Sociológicas (CIS) October barometer; Kalshi markets; Spain’s Official State Gazette (BOE).

World.title: El Niño Soaks Tanzania Safari Season 2026
World.content:
TANZANIA · TRAVEL GUIDE

Key Facts Holidays Wednesday, 9 December; Friday, 25 December; Saturday, 26 December. No public holiday falls in November.

Weather Above-average short rains are forecast into January 2027, driven by El Niño, a Pacific Ocean warming pattern.

Entry costs Visa US$100; mandatory insurance worth US$44 on the mainland from Thursday, 1 October; Zanzibar has its own.

US advisory Level 2, Exercise Increased Caution, since mid-October 2026; embassy security alert issued Wednesday, 28 October.

Football Africa Cup of Nations, Africa’s top football event: qualifiers Monday, 9 to Tuesday, 17 November.

Tanzania has three public holidays before the new year, and the rainy season shapes every safari and beach plan. Here is what a US visitor needs for November and December 2026.

In Plain English Zanzibar: an island group off the Tanzanian coast that runs many of its own affairs inside the Tanzanian union.

an island group off the Tanzanian coast that runs many of its own affairs inside the Tanzanian union. Short rains: Tanzania’s October to December rainy season, called vuli in Swahili.

Tanzania’s October to December rainy season, called vuli in Swahili. El Niño: a warming of the Pacific Ocean that shifts rain patterns across the world.

a warming of the Pacific Ocean that shifts rain patterns across the world. TANAPA: Tanzania National Parks Authority, the state agency that runs the main parks, including the Serengeti and Kilimanjaro.

Tanzania has three public holidays left in 2026: Independence Day on Wednesday, 9 December, then Christmas and Boxing Day. Christmas falls on Friday, 25 December and Boxing Day on Saturday, 26 December.

The State Department rates Tanzania Level 2, Exercise Increased Caution, and the US Embassy issued a security alert on Wednesday, 28 October. Entry costs a US citizen US$100 for the visa plus the shilling equivalent of US$44 for compulsory insurance.

The short rains also run into January 2027, with above-average rainfall forecast. This guide covers holidays, weather, safari and Zanzibar access, costs, safety and what is still unknown.

Tanzania Public Holidays in 2026 and Early 2027

The Dar es Salaam Stock Exchange, the national stock market, publishes a list of Tanzania’s 2026 public holidays. It shows no holiday between Nyerere Day, named for the first president, on Wednesday, 14 October and Independence Day.

We never share your email.

Independence Day on Wednesday, 9 December marks the end of British rule on the mainland in 1961. The Public Holidays Act lists it as Independence and Republic Day, so expect government offices and many businesses to close.

Christmas Day is Friday, 25 December and Boxing Day is Saturday, 26 December, both on the 2026 list. The Public Holidays Act gives a day in lieu for weekend holidays, but the list shows no such day.

New Year’s Day is Friday, 1 January 2027, and Zanzibar Revolution Day is Tuesday, 12 January 2027. The Public Holidays Act sets both dates.

Short Rains and the Safari and Zanzibar Season

The Tanzania Meteorological Authority, the national weather service, issued its October to December rainfall outlook on Tuesday, 18 August 2026. It expects mostly above-average to average rain, driven by a strong El Niño.

Rains were due to start in the first or second week of October in Dar es Salaam, Zanzibar, Arusha and Kilimanjaro. They are expected to end in January 2027, with a rise in rainfall expected in November.

The authority warns that floods may make wildlife move and can damage roads, bridges and railways. It advises regular infrastructure inspections and says heavy rain periods may bring floods and landslides.

Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times →

The official Zanzibar tourism website calls June to October the best time to visit, in the dry season. TANAPA also names June to October as the best time for the wildebeest migration in the Serengeti.

TANAPA lists January and February as the calving season, when the herds give birth, and says nothing about November or December. No official migration timing is therefore given for the short-rains months.

Plan a wet-weather backup for any December trip, and ask operators about road, bridge and airstrip conditions before you pay. Keep deposits in US$ refundable where you can, because floods can cut routes at short notice.

Kilimanjaro and Serengeti Access

TANAPA said in late September 2026 that a wildfire had closed the Lemosho and Londorosi routes on Mount Kilimanjaro. Reports of a reopening in October could not be confirmed on a TANAPA page, so check route status before you book.

Ask your operator to confirm in writing that your chosen route is open before you fly. Mountain conditions can change at short notice in the rains.

TANAPA’s visitor guide says Arusha is the most common entry point, with regular flights to the Seronera airstrip in the Serengeti. It adds that a road safari may take seven to eight hours.

Park fees change by year, and the tariff file on the TANAPA site covers 2023/24 only. Ask your operator for the 2026/27 fee in writing before you pay.

Getting to Tanzania From the United States

A US citizen needs a passport valid for at least six months, with one blank page, the State Department says. Only passports with an M or F sex marker are accepted for entry.

Tourists need a one-year multiple-entry visa costing US$100, and can apply online for an e-visa before travel. The State Department says US citizens can also buy a tourist visa on arrival.

Visitors must present a round-trip ticket and be ready to show enough funds, the State Department says. A yellow fever certificate is needed if you arrive from a country with the disease, including after a 12-hour layover or longer.

Tanzania keeps UTC+3 all year, so it is eight hours ahead of New York from Sunday, 1 November. That is when US clocks go back.

No nonstop flight from the United States to Tanzania could be confirmed, so plan for at least one connection. The main gateways are Julius Nyerere International in Dar es Salaam, Kilimanjaro International near Arusha and Abeid Amani Karume International in Zanzibar.

The State Department advises using the high-speed ferry to Zanzibar and buying tickets online or inside the ferry terminal. Tickets should show your name, travel date and class of travel.

Compulsory Travel Insurance

Government Notice No. 256 of 2026, the Insurance (Inbound Travel Insurance) Regulations, requires most foreigners entering mainland Tanzania to hold a policy. The finance minister signed it on 31 August 2026, and it was gazetted on Friday, 4 September.

The premium is the Tanzanian shilling equivalent of US$44, and the policy lasts up to 92 days with multiple entries. A foreigner without a valid policy shall be denied entry, but it can be bought before travel or at the entry point.

The regulations carry no start date, but a finance ministry notice, reported by travel-industry sources, set Thursday, 1 October 2026. The National Insurance Corporation, the state insurer, now calls the cover mandatory for every foreign visitor to the mainland.

The cover must include emergency medical treatment, evacuation, repatriation and lost luggage. The National Insurance Corporation, or a partner insurer, must issue it.

Residents of East African Community and Southern African Development Community states are outside the definition of foreigner. US visitors are not exempt.

Zanzibar has required its own cover from the Zanzibar Insurance Corporation, the island’s state insurer, since Tuesday, 1 October 2024. A Zanzibar government advisory dated Monday, 5 August 2024 gives up to 92 days of cover and states no price.

Events and Football Dates

The Confederation of African Football (CAF), Africa’s football governing body, runs the Africa Cup of Nations. Its qualifiers have matchdays three and four from Monday, 9 to Tuesday, 17 November 2026.

Tanzania, Kenya and Uganda co-host the finals, which open on Saturday, 19 June 2027 and end on Saturday, 17 July 2027. The draw placed Tanzania in a qualifying group with Nigeria, Madagascar and Guinea-Bissau.

The Sauti za Busara music festival runs from Friday, 19 to Sunday, 21 March 2027 in Stone Town, Zanzibar, its organiser says. Early bird tickets are on sale, but the organiser’s page lists no prices.

For concerts, summits and trade fairs in the commercial capital, see the Rio Times guide to Dar es Salaam in November. No other November or December event for visitors could be confirmed with an organiser.

Safety and the US Advisory

The State Department now rates Tanzania Level 2, Exercise Increased Caution, lowered from Level 3, Reconsider Travel, in mid-October 2026. The US Embassy in Tanzania lists crime, terrorism, health, unrest, arbitrary law enforcement and targeting of gay and lesbian people as risks.

The embassy issued a security alert on Wednesday, 28 October 2026, for the anniversary of the 29 October 2025 election violence. It warns of a possible heavy security response to gatherings, with roadblocks, checkpoints and internet blackouts, and tells Americans to avoid them.

On Tuesday, 9 December 2025, police banned planned Independence Day protests and deployed heavily. The government urged people to mark the day at home.

The State Department’s country page warns that immigration officers may deny entry to gay, lesbian and bisexual travelers, including in Zanzibar. It says those admitted may be targeted, harassed or charged with unrelated offenses.

Enrol in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP), the State Department’s alert service for Americans abroad, before you travel. Keep copies of your passport, your visa grant notice and your insurance certificate.

What It Means for You

Book with flexible terms, because the short rains can close roads and the embassy warns of unrest. Budget about US$144 per adult for the visa and insurance before flights, ferries, park fees and tours.

If you travel around Wednesday, 9 December or Christmas, expect closed offices and heavier security, and avoid any crowd or protest. Buy the government insurance before departure and keep the certificate with your passport.

What Is Not Known

Tanzania’s own November fixtures, venues and kick-off times in the Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers were not confirmed. Ticket sales for the 2027 finals were not found either.

It is not known whether Monday, 28 December will be a day off, as the list shows no day in lieu. Plans for marking Independence Day on Wednesday, 9 December, and any protest calls, were not found.

The 2026/27 TANAPA park tariff and Kilimanjaro route status after the wildfire were not confirmed on official pages. Flight routes from the United States and the ferry fare from Dar es Salaam to Zanzibar were not confirmed either.

The regulations list no children’s rate, and it is unclear whether one policy covers both the mainland and Zanzibar. The finance ministry notice setting the 1 October start could not be opened.

The exact date of the US advisory cut, reported as Friday, 16 October 2026, was not shown on official pages. The full Level 2 advisory text could not be opened, so its area-specific warnings are not listed here.

Related Coverage

Read the Rio Times Tanzania explained pillar and the guide to who runs Tanzania’s economy. The Tanzania news hub and the Zanzibar city page cover the wider picture.

Plan more with the report on the US$44 travel policy and the Kilimanjaro fire routes report. Music fans can see Sauti za Busara 2027.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the public holidays in Tanzania in December 2026?

Independence Day is Wednesday, 9 December, Christmas is Friday, 25 December and Boxing Day is Saturday, 26 December. No public holiday falls in November.

Is Tanzania safe for American visitors?

The State Department rates Tanzania Level 2, Exercise Increased Caution, citing crime, terrorism, unrest and health risks. Read the full advisory and enrol in STEP before you book.

Do Americans need a visa and insurance for Tanzania?

US citizens need a tourist visa costing US$100, available online or on arrival. Mainland Tanzania also requires inbound travel insurance worth US$44 from Thursday, 1 October 2026, and Zanzibar has its own cover.

Is November or December a good time for safari or Zanzibar?

Both months fall in the short rains, and the weather authority expects above-average rain into January 2027. Official sites name June to October as the best season, so plan a wet-weather backup.

Sources: Dar es Salaam Stock Exchange, Public Holidays of Tanzania 2026; Public Holidays Act, Tanzania; US Embassy in Tanzania, Travel Advisory notice (Level 2); US Embassy in Tanzania, Security Alert (28 October 2026); US State Department, Tanzania country information; Tanzanian Embassy in Washington, visa information; Government Notice No. 256 of 2026, Insurance (Inbound Travel Insurance) Regulations; National Insurance Corporation inbound travel insurance portal; Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar, Travel Advisory No. 1 of 2024; Tanzania Meteorological Authority, Vuli 2026 rainfall outlook (18 August 2026); TANAPA Serengeti page; TANAPA Serengeti visitor guide; TANAPA tariff page; Zanzibar tourism website; Confederation of African Football, AFCON 2027 dates; Sauti za Busara festival (all accessed 29 October 2026).

World.title: Argentine Oil Firm Vista Lifts Output 33%
World.content:
ARGENTINA · EARNINGS

Key Facts The company Vista Energy, listed in New York as VIST, drills for shale oil in Vaca Muerta, Argentina’s main shale basin.

What happened Third-quarter output rose 33% to 169,023 barrels of oil equivalent a day.

The catch Net income fell 7% to US$293.5 million because 2025 included a one-off acquisition gain.

Why it matters Adjusted EBITDA, a cash-profit measure, jumped 78% to US$841.5 million on higher output and prices.

A drilling rig at night near Añelo, in Argentina’s Vaca Muerta shale region (file photo)

Vista Energy pumped a third more oil and gas in Argentina’s shale country than a year earlier, and its cash profit jumped even faster. The company, which is listed in New York (NYSE: VIST) and Mexico City and drills mostly in Argentina, published its third-quarter results after markets closed on Wednesday 28 October 2026.

Vaca Muerta is a huge shale formation in Neuquén province and Argentina’s main source of new oil. Vista produced 169,023 barrels of oil equivalent a day, 33% more than in the third quarter of 2025 and 8% more than in the second quarter.

Background on the company is in our Vista Energy company profile. Related coverage includes Chile’s plan to ship Vaca Muerta cargo to Asia.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Argentina ranks 4th of 14 with 61.2 points. Strongest pillar: future resources (68); weakest: economic relationships (23). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (B-); inflation of 42%; public debt at 80% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Output and Prices Both Rose

Oil output was 147,126 barrels a day, up 34% on the year. Vista said 13 percentage points of the 33% growth was organic, from 91 new wells connected in 12 months, and 20 points came from assets bought from Equinor, the Norwegian energy group.

Those assets, stakes in the Bandurria Sur and Bajo del Toro blocks, counted for a full quarter this time instead of two months. The company connected 25 net new wells in the quarter.

We never share your email.

The average price Vista received for its oil was US$84.2 a barrel, 30% above a year earlier and 6% below the second quarter. Brent, the global benchmark, averaged US$91.3 a barrel in the quarter against US$96.7 in the second.

Total revenues were US$1.234 billion, up 75% on the year and 7% on the second quarter. Exports made up 72% of net revenues, or US$854.2 million.

Heavy equipment on the outskirts of Añelo, the hub of Vaca Muerta (file photo) Photo: Gervacio Rosales, CC BY 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons

Why Net Income Fell 7% While EBITDA Jumped

Adjusted EBITDA, a measure of cash profit before interest, tax and depreciation, rose 78% to US$841.5 million. The margin was 68%, one point higher than a year earlier.

Net income was US$293.5 million, down 7% from US$315.3 million. The 2025 figure included a one-off US$288.1 million gain from buying the La Amarga Chica block, and without it net income grew more than tenfold.

Income tax expense also rose. Vista booked US$211.8 million in the third quarter against US$116.5 million in the second.

Adjusted net income, which Vista calculates without one-off items, rose to US$240.1 million from US$155.5 million. Earnings were US$2.6 a share, against US$3.0 a year earlier.

Cash, Debt and Drilling

Vista spent US$459.7 million on capital projects, mostly drilling and completing Vaca Muerta wells. It drilled 22 net wells and completed 28 in the quarter.

Free cash flow, the cash left after investment, was US$334.2 million. The company also spent US$55.4 million buying back its own shares.

Gross debt was US$3.642 billion and net debt US$2.857 billion. The net leverage ratio, net debt divided by yearly adjusted EBITDA, was 1.12 times, down from 1.83 times a year earlier.

The cost of lifting oil out of the ground was US$4.7 a barrel of oil equivalent, 6% above a year earlier. Vista attributed that to slightly higher costs in peso-denominated goods and services.

What It Means for You

For US investors, Vista is a leveraged bet on Argentine shale and on Brent. All of its oil sales are priced on export-parity formulas tied to international prices, so a lower Brent trims revenue even as volumes rise.

The New York shares closed at US$72.27 on Wednesday 28 October, up 1.0% before the results came out. Vista’s webcast for investors takes place on Thursday 29 October at 9:00 a.m. Mexico City time.

What Is Not Known

The results release gives no production or spending forecast for the fourth quarter. It is also not yet known how the shares will react once US trading opens on Thursday.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much oil does Vista Energy produce?

Vista produced 169,023 barrels of oil equivalent a day in the third quarter of 2026, up 33% on the year. Oil alone was 147,126 barrels a day.

Why did Vista’s net income fall 7%?

The 2025 figure included a one-off US$288.1 million gain from buying a block. Net income was US$293.5 million against US$315.3 million.

How much did Vista earn before interest, tax and depreciation?

Adjusted EBITDA was US$841.5 million, up 78% on the year, with a 68% margin. Revenues were US$1.234 billion.

Where can US investors buy Vista Energy?

It trades on the New York Stock Exchange as VIST and on the Mexican stock exchange as VISTA. The New York shares closed at US$72.27 on 28 October 2026.

Sources: Vista Energy 2026 third-quarter results, Form 6-K, Securities and Exchange Commission, 28 October 2026; Vista Energy investor relations; New York Stock Exchange closing prices, 28 October 2026.

World.title: Mexican Store Giant Femsa Profit Jumps 81%
World.content:
MEXICO · EARNINGS

Key Facts The company FEMSA, based in Monterrey, owns OXXO, Mexico’s convenience-store chain, and trades in New York under the ticker FMX.

What happened Third-quarter net income rose 81% to 10.57 billion pesos (about US$567 million).

The catch A loss that did not repeat and a currency gain explain much of the jump.

Why it matters OXXO Mexico store traffic rose 3.5%, which the CEO called its best in over two years.

Power Index Mexico ranks 2nd of 14 in Mexico ranks 2nd of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 71.4 points (October 2026 edition).

Monterrey, the northern Mexican city where FEMSA is based (file photo) Photo: Daniel Escobedo, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

Shoppers came back to OXXO in the third quarter, and its owner FEMSA reported a much bigger profit. FEMSA, a Monterrey-based conglomerate that also runs a health division and fuel stations and holds a stake in Coca-Cola FEMSA, released the results on Wednesday 28 October 2026.

Consolidated net income rose 81% to 10.57 billion pesos (about US$567 million), on revenue up 9.8% to 235.6 billion pesos (about US$12.64 billion). This article converts pesos at 18.64 per US$, the spot rate on 28 October 2026.

Its bottler, in which FEMSA holds a stake, is covered in our report on Coca-Cola FEMSA’s third quarter. More Mexican business news is in our Mexico hub.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Mexico ranks 2nd of 14 with 71.4 points. Strongest pillar: economic relationships (90); weakest: state capacity & security (46). Alignment group: Hedging. Watch21 homicides per 100,000; organised crime at 7.7 of 10. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Why Profit Jumped 81%

Most of the jump came from the absence of last year’s loss, not from sales. In the third quarter of 2025 FEMSA recorded a 3.15 billion peso (about US$169 million) loss from discontinued operations, linked to the sale of its logistics business Solistica.

A non-cash currency gain of 1.12 billion pesos (about US$60 million) also replaced a 1.26 billion peso loss (about US$68 million) a year earlier. The company said the peso’s depreciation against the US dollar drove the swing, because FEMSA holds US dollar cash and investments that gain peso value when the peso weakens.

Income from operations, the profit from running the businesses before interest and tax, rose 9.9% to 19.92 billion pesos (about US$1.07 billion). Adjusted EBITDA, a cash-profit measure, rose 12.9% to 34.83 billion pesos (about US$1.87 billion).

Profit attributable to FEMSA shareholders was 6.81 billion pesos (about US$365 million), more than 2.8 times the 2.42 billion pesos of a year earlier. That works out to US$1.10 per American depositary share (ADS), the form in which US investors hold the stock.

OXXO Mexico Draws More Shoppers

OXXO Mexico revenue rose 10.3% to 86.65 billion pesos (about US$4.65 billion). Same-store sales, which strip out new openings, rose 9.2%, helped by a 5.5% higher average ticket and 3.5% more store traffic.

Coca-Cola FEMSA delivery trucks in Mexico City (file photo) Photo: Gobierno CDMX, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons

Chief Executive José Antonio Fernández Garza-Lagüera said customer traffic delivered “its strongest performance in more than two years”. He credited stronger execution in most regions and promotions on categories that bring people into stores.

Profit grew more slowly than sales. OXXO Mexico’s operating income rose only 5.8% to 8.04 billion pesos (about US$431 million), because gross margin fell 1.2 percentage points to 44.8%.

The company pointed to a demanding comparison base and to price adjustments in categories meant to draw traffic.The chain had 24,759 stores at the end of September, up 702 in 12 months.

Spin by OXXO, its payments app, had 11.7 million active users, up 17.3%.

It produces, markets, and distributes Coca-Cola trademark beverages in Mexico, Guatemala, Nicaragua, Costa Rica,…

Where Growth Is Still Weak

Americas & Mobility, which groups OXXO outside Mexico with fuel sales, grew revenue 18.1% to 29.47 billion pesos (about US$1.58 billion). Its operating income fell 75.9% to 170 million pesos (about US$9 million), mainly because OXXO Brazil’s losses now enter the consolidated results and fuel margins in Mexico stayed under pressure.

OXXO’s operations in Chile, Peru and Colombia improved.Health operating income fell 63.2% to 319 million pesos (about US$17 million), including a non-cash 430 million peso (about US$23 million) provision tied to winding down Colombia’s institutional business.

Europe’s operating income fell 24.8% to 531 million pesos (about US$28 million) on revenue that was down 5.2% in pesos, or up 4.0% excluding currency effects.The chief executive described the Mexican consumer as soft and Brazil as volatile, and warned of tougher year-on-year comparisons ahead.

Cash for Shareholders and the Share Price

FEMSA entered an accelerated share repurchase, a deal in which a bank buys the shares up front and delivers them over time, for up to US$280 million of its ADSs. Final settlement is expected before the end of 2026.

Net debt, which counts lease obligations and excludes Coca-Cola FEMSA, was 95.2 billion pesos (about US$5.11 billion), or 1.19 times adjusted EBITDA. The ADS closed at US$123.70 on Wednesday 28 October, 0.5% below Tuesday’s close.

What It Means for You

For US holders of FMX, the headline profit flatters the quarter. The cleaner signals are the 9.9% rise in operating income and the recovery in OXXO Mexico traffic, set against weak margins in Brazil, Colombia and Europe.

Mexico’s statistics office INEGI publishes its first estimate of third-quarter economic growth on Friday 30 October 2026, the next read on the consumer. Banxico, the central bank, announces its next interest rate decision on Thursday 5 November 2026.

What Is Not Known

The results release gives no full-year forecast, so it is unclear how much of the traffic recovery management expects to hold. It also does not explain the small dip in the ADS on Wednesday.

More: Mexico news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much did FEMSA earn in the third quarter of 2026?

Consolidated net income rose 81% to 10.57 billion pesos (about US$567 million). Profit attributable to shareholders was 6.81 billion pesos (about US$365 million), or US$1.10 per ADS.

Why did FEMSA’s profit jump 81%?

Last year’s 3.15 billion peso loss from discontinued operations did not repeat, and a 1.12 billion peso currency gain replaced a loss. Operating income rose 9.9%.

How is OXXO Mexico performing?

Revenue rose 10.3% and same-store sales 9.2%, with store traffic up 3.5%. Operating income grew only 5.8% as gross margin fell, which the company tied to a tougher comparison base and price adjustments.

Where can US investors buy FEMSA?

It trades on the New York Stock Exchange as FMX through ADSs. The ADS closed at US$123.70 on 28 October 2026.

EGYPT · TRAVEL GUIDE

Key Facts Film festival Cairo International Film Festival runs Wednesday, 11 to Friday, 20 November 2026.

Pyramids race Giza Plateau race: 5K on Friday, 11 December; 10K and half marathon Saturday, 12 December.

Museum tickets The Grand Egyptian Museum sells tickets only at tickets.gem.eg; check the foreign adult price at checkout.

Holidays No Egyptian public holiday is known for November or December; Coptic (Orthodox) Christmas is Thursday, 7 January 2027.

Visa and advisory The online e-visa costs US$30 single entry; US State Department advisory pages differ on Level 2 or 3, so check before you book.

What it means for you Book the e-visa at least 7 days ahead and check the live US advisory before you pay for anything.

No Egyptian public holiday is known before Coptic Christmas. Its winter calendar is full of festivals and races.

In Plain English Nile cruise: a boat trip along the river between Luxor and Aswan in southern Egypt.

a boat trip along the river between Luxor and Aswan in southern Egypt. E-visa: an entry permit you buy online from the Egyptian government before you fly.

an entry permit you buy online from the Egyptian government before you fly. Travel advisory: the US State Department’s four-level warning scale, from Level 1 to Level 4, “Do Not Travel”.

the US State Department’s four-level warning scale, from Level 1 to Level 4, “Do Not Travel”. Giza Plateau: the desert site outside Cairo that holds the Great Pyramids.

No Egyptian public holiday is known for November or December 2026, so winter trips revolve around festivals and races. The main dated events are a film festival from Wednesday, 11 November and a Pyramids race on 11 and 12 December.

US visitors need an e-visa, which the government portal prices at US$30 for one entry. The US State Department, Washington’s foreign ministry, shows conflicting levels for Egypt, so check its live advisory before you book.

The Winter Season at a Glance

Egypt’s clocks go back at the end of October, and the country then sits at UTC+2. From Sunday, 1 November it is 7 hours ahead of US Eastern time.

The Egyptian pound traded at about EGP 56.09 per US$1 on 28 October, the rate used in this guide. Museum hours differ by weekday, so check them before you go.

Cairo International Film Festival, 11 to 20 November

The festival’s own website lists the 47th Cairo International Film Festival for Wednesday, 11 to Friday, 20 November 2026. It lists a Cairo Industry Days programme, a New Wave programme and an extended reality strand called Cairo’s XR.

The pages read name no screening venues. Ticket prices and the sales channel had not been published there either.

The Cairo International Jazz Festival lists Thursday, 5 to Saturday, 7 November 2026 on its official site. The site does not name a venue or show prices, so check its ticket page before you plan around it.

Both events fall after US clocks go back, so Egypt is 7 hours ahead of New York. Check each organiser’s page, because programmes can change.

Grand Egyptian Museum Tickets and Hours

The Grand Egyptian Museum near the Giza pyramids sells tickets only at tickets.gem.eg, which calls itself the only official ticket website. This guide could not confirm the current foreign adult price at the museum or Egypt’s tourism ministry, so read it at checkout.

On Sunday to Tuesday, Thursday and Friday, the complex opens 8:30 am to 7:00 pm, with galleries 9:00 am to 6:00 pm. On Wednesday and Saturday, it stays open to 10:00 pm, with galleries to 9:00 pm.

The last entry is one hour before the galleries close. Tickets are single-entry, non-transferable and non-refundable, according to the museum’s booking site.

Bags larger than 40 by 40 centimetres go to storage, and flash, tripods, selfie sticks and drones are banned. Some free or discounted categories exclude Fridays and public holidays, so check eligibility first.

Pyramids Half Marathon, 11 and 12 December

The Pyramids Half Marathon takes place on the Giza Plateau on Friday, 11 December and Saturday, 12 December 2026, its organisers say. The 5K runs on Friday, and the 10K and 21.1K half marathon run on Saturday.

The organisers say the race pack includes access to the Giza Pyramids complex and the required Tourism Police permit. Runners must collect it at the official race expo before the event.

Registration fees, the closing date and the start times were not confirmed at the organiser. Read them on the official sign-up page before you plan flights.

A further race follows in January: the 34th Egyptian Luxor Marathon is on Friday, 8 January 2027 at Hatshepsut Temple. Its organiser lists fees from EUR 80 (about US$89) for international runners.

Nile Cruises Between Luxor and Aswan

A Nile cruise is a boat trip along the river between Luxor and Aswan in southern Egypt. This guide found no official season calendar, fare list or boat count, so treat claims about peak months as unconfirmed.

Compare operator terms carefully, and confirm the boarding port, the included meals and the temple entry fees in writing. Ask whether a change of cabin or itinerary is allowed before you pay a deposit.

Holidays and Closures

No Egyptian public holiday is known for November or December 2026, but no official cabinet list was found. The Danish embassy’s closing list, which mixes Danish and Egyptian holidays, shows none either.

Coptic Christmas, celebrated by Egypt’s Orthodox Christians, falls on Thursday, 7 January 2027. Egypt’s prime minister can announce a paid holiday at short notice, as he did for Sinai Liberation Day in April.

Check the prime minister’s announcements in the days before any date you rely on. This guide did not confirm whether 25 December is a day off.

Getting There From the US

US citizens need a passport valid for six months and an e-visa, priced at US$30 for one entry. Multiple entries cost US$65, and the portal says to apply at least 7 days before departure.

Pay by card on the government portal, and print the approval, which the portal lists among entry requirements. This guide did not verify US flight routes, so confirm them with your airline.

Agree taxi fares before you start any ride. Read the State Department advisory again a few days before you fly.

Safety and Costs

The State Department’s pages disagree on Egypt’s overall level, so check the live advisory before you book. Its advisory page shows Level 3, “Reconsider Travel”, while a US embassy alert of 29 March 2026 says Level 2.

Both pages say “Do Not Travel” for Northern and Middle Sinai and parts of the Western Desert. The advisory page adds border areas and gives terrorism as its reason for Level 3.

Importing any drone into Egypt is banned, and photographing police stations or military barracks is illegal. Egyptian law treats dual US-Egyptian nationals as Egyptian citizens, which limits what the US embassy can do if they are detained.

Only one amount here needs conversion: the Luxor Marathon fee of EUR 80 (about US$89). Rates used are EGP 56.09 per US$1 and EUR 0.897 per US$1, as of 28 October.

What It Means for You

If you plan a winter trip, buy the e-visa early and book museum tickets on the official site. Check the price at checkout, because this guide could not confirm the current foreign adult fee.

If you want a Nile cruise, compare operator terms in writing before you pay a deposit. Add the film festival or race only after checking each organiser’s ticket page.

What Is Not Known

The Cairo film festival’s screening venues, ticket prices and programme were not on the organiser’s pages read. The Cairo Jazz Festival’s venue and ticket prices were also not published on its official site.

Registration fees, the closing date and the start times for the Pyramids Half Marathon were not confirmed at the organiser. No official Nile cruise season dates, fares or number of operating boats were found at a government source.

The current foreign adult price at the Grand Egyptian Museum was not confirmed at the museum or the tourism ministry. No cabinet list of 2026 holidays was found, and the State Department’s pages disagree on Egypt’s level.

Related Coverage

Read the Cairo International Film Festival guide and the Pyramids Half Marathon guide. The Grand Egyptian Museum ticket story covers museum admission.

See what to do in Cairo in November and the Egyptian Luxor Marathon guide. The Egypt visa guide, the Cairo city page and the Egypt news hub give more background.

Frequently Asked Questions

What public holidays does Egypt have in November and December 2026?

No Egyptian public holiday is known for November or December, though no cabinet list was found. Coptic Christmas is Thursday, 7 January 2027.

When is the Cairo International Film Festival 2026?

The festival’s website lists Wednesday, 11 to Friday, 20 November 2026. Venues and ticket prices were not published on the pages read.

How much does the Grand Egyptian Museum cost for foreigners?

This guide could not confirm the current foreign adult price at the museum or the tourism ministry. Buy only at tickets.gem.eg, the museum’s official website.

Is Egypt safe for US visitors?

The State Department’s pages disagree: its advisory page shows Level 3, while a March 2026 embassy alert says Level 2. Both say Do Not Travel for Northern and Middle Sinai; check the live advisory before you book.
