The DFFE said the exporter applied for the required licence on 27 July 2026. The application covered the removal, possession, collection, transport, export and acquisition of five protected trees. However, the department rejected it on 31 July. “The application was rejected because a criminal investigation into the matter is under way. The department will not issue a licence retrospectively to legitimise actions that appear to have been unlawful,” the department said.

On 8 August, the exporter appealed against the decision. The department said the appeal was currently under review by the official responsible for such matters.

Asked whether the applicants had complied with the relevant regulations, the DFFE said they had failed to meet the requirements of the National Forests Act. According to the department, the trees came from the local municipality of Lephalale in Waterberg District, Limpopo province, and were intended for export to Georgia.

The department has launched criminal proceedings in the case. Under the law, the offence carries a fine or a prison sentence of up to three years.

The DFFE has not disclosed the names of those facing criminal proceedings, nor has it identified the owner of the trees or the exporter. The department explained that possessing, collecting, removing, transporting, exporting, buying or selling protected trees constitutes a Category 1 offence.

The plan to transport the baobabs to Georgia has also raised concerns among environmentalists. Dr Sarah Venter, founder of the Baobab Foundation, said that although it was technically possible to uproot baobabs and transplant them elsewhere, the record of their survival in Georgia was discouraging.

“Unfortunately, the survival rates of these trees in Georgia leave much to be desired,” Venter said.

The Kenyan case: eight baobabs transplanted to Georgia dried up and died

The investigation currently under way in South Africa echoes an earlier attempt to transport baobabs from Kenya to Georgia, an incident that attracted international attention in 2022.

On 24 October 2022, The Guardian reported that Kenyan farmers had sold baobabs growing on their land to a group led by Georgian national Giorgi Gvasalia. The plan involved uprooting eight trees and transporting them to Georgia.

In November that year, Kenya’s Ministry of Environment suspended a foreign company’s licence to uproot baobabs, citing several violations. The ministry also instructed the Kenya Forest Service to stop the trees from being moved.

The ministry said uprooting baobabs required the appropriate permit and a transparent process demonstrating how relocating the trees would benefit the public. It concluded that the established requirements had not been met in this case. In April 2023, the Environment Committee of Kenya’s National Assembly, the lower house of parliament, launched an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the export of baobabs from the Kilifi region to Georgia.

The eight uprooted trees remained in that condition for almost two years and eventually died.

According to Georgia’s Dendrological Park, workers had uprooted the trees in 2021, but various obstacles delayed their transport to Georgia until October 2023. They planted the baobabs in the ground on 8 November 2023.

“These African giants spent almost two years uprooted, in natural conditions entirely unsuitable for them and without proper care. Unfortunately, the stress took its toll: six to seven months after they were planted in Georgia, all eight baobabs had died,” the park said.

Investigators in South Africa must establish who owned the trees and who arranged their removal from the country, under what circumstances these protected plants were uprooted, and who bears responsibility for the attempt to transport them to Georgia.

World.title: Uzbekistan eyes Gulf markets for CRAFERS confectionery exports
World.content:
Photo: the Ministry of Investment, Industry and Trade of Uzbekistan

BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 29. Uzbekistan is exploring opportunities to increase confectionery exports to Gulf countries as part of efforts to expand production at CRAFERS, a local confectionery manufacturer, and strengthen its presence in international markets as Deputy Minister of Investment, Industry and Trade Ibrokhim Ergashev reviews industrial projects in Tashkent on Thursday.

According to the Uzbekistan's Ministry of Investment, Industry and Trade, Ergashev visited several production facilities in the capital to assess their operations, the progress of ongoing projects and plans for further development.

During a visit to the CA-EXPORT & INTERNATIONAL TRADE CENTER project in Tashkent’s Yangihayot district, discussions focused on increasing trade volumes, involving domestic manufacturers in export activities and promoting Uzbek products in international markets.

The project is being developed on a 55,000-square-meter site. Participants also discussed establishing direct communication channels between local producers and foreign buyers to facilitate business partnerships and expand access to export markets.

Ergashev also visited the CRAFERS confectionery factory in the Mirzo Ulugbek district, where discussions centered on expanding production capacity and increasing exports to Gulf countries.

Moreover, the parties considered ways to improve access to financial resources and upgrade engineering and utility infrastructure to support the factory’s operations and future growth.

World.title: Azerbaijan, Wonderful sign MoU to expand AI use in public sector (PHOTO)
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 29. A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on cooperation in the field of artificial intelligence (AI) solutions and related digital technologies has been signed between the Ministry of Digital Development and Transport and Wonderful, a company that provides an AI operating system for large enterprises and organizations of strategic importance.

This was announced in a report by the Ministry of Digital Development and Transport.

According to the information, the document establishes a framework for cooperation to explore the implementation of AI solutions, based on the Wonderful platform, within ministries, government agencies, and state-owned enterprises. The primary objective is to improve the delivery of public services, making them faster, more accessible, and better aligned with the needs of citizens and business entities, while simultaneously ensuring that government institutions operate more efficiently and on a larger scale.

The parties envision the creation of a shared AI platform, equipped with management and oversight mechanisms, designed to serve citizens, business entities, and government institutions. The platform is planned to be hosted on Azerbaijan’s "Government Cloud" (G-Cloud). Within this framework, the parties will jointly identify application areas with high-impact potential and explore opportunities for the broader implementation of successful solutions across the public sector.

The signing ceremony held in Baku was attended by Deputy Minister of Digital Development and Transport Rashad Hasanov, Chairman of the Board of the Innovation and Digital Development Agency (IDDA) Farid Osmanov, and a delegation led by Bar Winkler, Co-founder and CEO of Wonderful. The delegation also included Omer Perez, the company’s Managing Director for Central and Eastern Europe, and Vitaly Gordon, General Manager for the Caucasus and Central Asia.

Hasanov said that the true value of AI is measured by its potential to enhance the efficiency of public administration and improve public access to government services.

"Through our collaboration with the company Wonderful, we aim to explore the implementation of solutions that can make public administration more efficient, agile, and accessible. This partnership also aligns with the priorities of the 'Action Plan for Accelerating Digital Development (2026–2028)' and is part of our broader efforts to ensure that technological progress delivers tangible benefits to citizens, businesses, and the economy as a whole," the deputy minister noted.

Winkler emphasized that they view Azerbaijan as a strategic and long-term partner.

"Our goal is to support the government, citizens, and strategically important organizations in meeting their needs within the field of artificial intelligence. In addition to our partnership, we are pleased to be expanding our local team and operations in Baku, as well as accelerating the adoption of artificial intelligence across the country," he said.

Initial areas for AI implementation

Following the signing of the memorandum, a round table on AI was held, involving the Innovation and Digital Development Agency and several government institutions. The meeting focused on the development and implementation of pilot projects across priority areas.

Wonderful showcased the capabilities of its unified platform by demonstrating AI solutions tailored to the needs of the participating government institutions. The presentations covered areas such as verifying residency-related applications, validating import documentation, providing an anonymous assistant in the Azerbaijani language for families, offering voice-based support for "mygov" services, and assisting public transport passengers.

These solutions are aimed at simplifying existing processes across various service sectors, making services faster and more accessible, and increasing citizen satisfaction.

Strengthening local capacity and expanding operations in Azerbaijan

The parties have agreed to cooperate on strengthening local capacity, exchanging knowledge and experience, and developing relevant skills.

Wonderful plans to invest in Azerbaijan for the long term, which includes establishing a local legal entity in Baku, recruiting local professionals, and providing training to Azerbaijani specialists. As an initial commitment in this regard, the company has already hired its first employee in Azerbaijan. This step marks a concrete beginning toward building a local team and establishing long-term operations in the country.

The objective is to ensure that AI solutions contribute to Azerbaijan’s long-term national digital development goals. The cooperation also envisages supporting the development of Azerbaijan’s domestic information and communication technology (ICT) industry and enhancing the international competitiveness of the technology sector.

Laying foundation for widespread application of AI in public sector

Initial collaboration with government agencies aims to lay the groundwork for the broader application of AI within Azerbaijan’s public sector. In this context, the initiative includes exploring opportunities to scale the implementation of successful solutions across other government institutions.

The memorandum aligns with the objectives of the "Artificial Intelligence Strategy of the Republic of Azerbaijan for 2025–2028" and the "Action Plan for Accelerating Digital Development for 2026–2028," as well as with the measures being implemented by the ministry to foster a modern, citizen-centric, and data-driven public sector.

World.title: Azerbaijan Airlines and Sea Breeze announce 100 winners of joint lottery (PHOTO)
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 29. The grand prize winner of the “Sky and Sea” (“Səma və Dəniz”) lottery, jointly organized by Azerbaijan Airlines and Sea Breeze for members of the AZAL Miles loyalty program, has won an apartment in the Park Lane residential complex at Sea Breeze Resort.

According to the announcement of the Press Service of Azerbaijan Airlines CJSC, a total of 100 winners were selected following an electronic draw held on September 28 and broadcast live. In addition to the grand prize — an apartment in the Park Lane residential complex — the prize pool included flight miles, ABB–AZAL Miles Co-brand Infinite and Platinum cards, annual memberships at Crocus Fitness Baku, and gift vouchers for the Aghalarov Rest restaurant chain.

The campaign ran from July 8 to September 8, 2026. During this period, participants earned chances to win through flight ticket purchases, earning and redeeming miles, and other eligible transactions specified in the lottery terms and conditions. To participate in the draw, AZAL Miles members were required to confirm their participation through their personal accounts.

The full list of winners is available on the official Azerbaijan Airlines website.

World.title: KazMunayGas plans to raise marketable gas output to 4.5 bcm by 2030
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 29. Kazakhstan's national oil and gas company KazMunayGas (KMG) plans to increase its annual marketable gas production from 2.4 billion to 4.5 billion cubic meters by 2030, while raising annual liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) production from 1.3 million to about 1.5 million tonnes, according to the company.

KMG Deputy Chairman of the Management Board Asset Magauov outlined the company's key gas and petrochemical projects at the ENERGY TRENDS: Gas & Petrochemicals conference in Astana.

Magauov noted that in line with instructions from the President of Kazakhstan, KMG is working to increase gas production and expand its gas processing capacity. Priority projects include the second phase of development of the Rozhkovskoye field in the West Kazakhstan region, the Zapadnaya Prorva project in the Atyrau region, and the development of the Central Urikhtau field in the Aktobe region.

He said that KMG is applying a cluster-based approach to these projects, which involves processing gas at existing gas processing plants located near the fields. The approach is intended to accelerate project implementation, optimize costs and make use of existing production capacity.

Another strategic area for KMG is the development of the petrochemical industry. The company is continuing to build a petrochemical cluster focused on the deep processing of hydrocarbon feedstock and the production of higher-value-added products.

According to him, major projects are underway in the Atyrau region, including a polyethylene plant, a gas separation complex and main pipelines for transporting ethane and propane.

In September 2026, installation of an ethylene fractionation column more than 100 meters tall was completed at the site of the future polyethylene plant. The equipment was manufactured by Kazakhstan's AtyrauNefteMash.

As of October 2026, construction progress at the polyethylene plant had exceeded 41%, while the gas separation complex was 32% complete. Construction of the main pipelines had reached approximately 9%.

"Implementation of strategic projects in the gas industry and petrochemicals will help strengthen energy security, develop domestic industry and increase Kazakhstan's export potential," Magauov said.

World.title: Zacharia blames media for troubled stint as White House press secretary
World.content:
Former White House press secretary Katie Zacharia has broken her silence 10 days after her abrupt departure from the administration.

Ms Zacharia's legal credentials came under scrutiny after a truncated first press briefing raised questions over her suitability for the position.

It all seemed to come crashing down for Ms Zacharia after two appearances on Fox News, where she admitted she had failed the bar exam.

Katie Zacharia only answered three questions from conservative-leaning news outlets at her first White House press briefing. (AP: Julia Demaree Nikhinson)

In a media appearance at the time, US President Donald Trump told reporters he had advised her to reconsider the position, bringing her tenure after just five days in the office.

The pair appeared to part ways cordially, with Mr Trump accusing the media of treating her "pretty nastily".

Ms Zacharia later penned an op-ed for the New York Post saying the "call" to serve the president was an "honor" she was proud of.

"I've always wanted to work for President Donald Trump," she wrote.

"Being back in California feels like an interlude, a temporary pause between the work that matters most," she wrote.

Katie Zacharia was asked about her legal credentials before heading to Alaska. (Reuters: Kevin Lamarque)

Appearing on Piers Morgan Uncensored this week, Ms Zacharia doubled down on her loyalty to Mr Trump and did not rule out working for his administration if the opportunity arose again.

"I would love to work for the president again," Ms Zacharia told Morgan on Wednesday, local time.

She said she had since returned to her home state of California, where she plans to continue to "fight" for Mr Trump, whom she described as a "force of nature" and an "incredible president to serve".

Loading Instagram content

When Morgan asked about the firestorm after her first press briefing and the backlash over the misrepresentation of her legal credentials, Ms Zacharia blamed the media for leading the public down a "red herring trail" that distracted attention from Mr Trump ahead of crucial midterm elections.

As she continued to pledge her loyalty to Mr Trump, Morgan accused her of being a "robot".

"Has Donald Trump got some program plugged into you to make you say all of this?" he asked.

The United States goes to the polls next week, where voters will decide which major party will control the House of Representatives and the Senate for the remainder of Mr Trump's administration.

Trump is very unpopular in the US Donald Trump wants American voters to "pretend" he's on the ballot these midterm elections. Voters don't need to be reminded how much they dislike him.

Ms Zacharia, a staunch supporter of Mr Trump since his first term in office, told Morgan that initial polling showed the Senate race would be "tight" and the House would prove to be an "uphill battle".

In the lead-up to the midterms, Mr Trump has drawn criticism for attempting to block alleged non-citizens from voting in California.

Meanwhile, he has continued to host rallies around the country, recently addressing Ms Zacharia's departure from the White House at one such event.

"She was a perfect, beautiful woman when she walked into that press room," he told the crowd.

He blamed the media for "scaring" the former press secretary, telling the crowd that he told her there were easier ways to make a living.

Mr Trump has yet to appoint the next press secretary, having earlier said he had no plans to do so until after the midterms.

ABC

World.title: Darwin man who ran over partner during argument to spend five months in jail
World.content:
A 63-year-old man will spend five months in jail after running over his partner during an argument, leaving her with multiple skull and facial fractures, at a caravan park just outside of Darwin at the beginning of the year.

The sentencing judge said the incident left the woman with "horrendous" life-threatening injuries, including brain bleeds, that left her in hospital for months and faced with a long process of recovering her ability to walk.

Christopher Morley pleaded guilty to dangerous driving and breaching a domestic violence restraining order earlier this month after spending a little over four months in jail on remand.

On Thursday morning, before sentencing in the Northern Territory Supreme Court, he also pleaded guilty to the summary charge of driving under the influence of drugs.

Christopher Morley pleaded guilty to dangerous driving and breaching a domestic violence order earlier this month. (ABC News: Pete Garnish)

According to the agreed facts, Morley and his then-partner were drinking at the Oasis Caravan Park in Virginia when the pair got into a verbal argument.

Earlier that day, Morley had texted his daughter saying the victim had threatened to burn the caravan down unless he paid her $1,500 — a threat the victim denied when speaking to the daughter at the time.

In another message to his daughter, Morley said the victim was drinking, refusing to leave and talking to another male at the bar.

The court heard the incident occurred earlier this year at the Oasis Caravan Park in Virginia. (ABC News)

In handing down his sentence, Justice Stephen Southwood said the victim had walked in front of Morley's Range Rover Discovery as he was trying to leave and "faced the vehicle head-on".

"As the offender accelerated the vehicle, the victim reached out in front of her and placed both hands on the centre of the vehicle," he said.

He said Morley then accelerated forwards, pushing the victim backwards, causing her to lose her balance and fall under the front passenger side of the car.

"The offender then continued to drive for approximately 10 metres before coming to a stop," Justice Southwood said.

Justice Stephen Southwood says Christopher Morley misrepresented the incident to police when they arrived. (Supplied: NT Supreme Court)

The court heard Morley called Triple Zero (000) immediately, but made false statements to police when they arrived.

"The offender suggested that the victim had jumped out in front of the car in an act of self harm. That is not correct," Justice Southwood said.

He said Morley had also told police he was only driving 5km/h, when in fact it was closer to 10km/h, and that his vehicle's dash camera was not working, although it was.

The court heard Morley's blood alcohol level was at 0.045, and that he tested positive for benzodiazepine, amphetamines and another substance at the time of the incident.

The judge took Christopher Morley's criminal history into account during sentencing. (ABC News: Pete Garnish)

In handing down his sentence, Justice Southwood said Morley's criminal history could not be ignored.

The court heard the victim had taken out a domestic violence order against Morley two years prior, after he assaulted her.

In 1990, he spent a month in prison for a separate assault, and was later fined after damaging property and resisting police.

In 1991, he was sentenced to three months jail for breaching an intervention order.

The Supreme Court heard the victim had previously taken out a domestic violence order against Christopher Morley, following an assault. (ABC News: Tristan Hooft)

While Morley's defence counsel had previously submitted their client was attempting to leave the situation in question voluntarily, an argument Justice Southwood accepted, the judge said the "very serious injuries" sustained by the victim were "significant".

"The volatile domestic situation preceding the offending explains but does not excuse it," he said.

"They should have adhered to the domestic violence orders in place and none of this would have happened."

Morley was sentenced to two years and three months in jail, suspended after nine months and backdated, leaving him with five months' remaining jail time.

He was also ordered to pay a $194 fine and disqualified from driving for six months.

World.title: Cigarette likely cause of catastrophic Hong Kong fire, report finds
World.content:
The Hong Kong government was partially responsible for a catastrophic fire that killed 168 people, a report has found.

The fire at Wang Fuk Court in November 2025 engulfed several residential tower blocks and was the world's deadliest residential building blaze since 1980.

On Thursday Hong Kong chief executive John Lee announced the resignation of Housing Secretary Winnie Ho, the first official to stand down over the inferno.

Loading...

The press conference marked the release of a 1,000-page independent report that detailed wide-ranging governance and supervisory failings in Hong Kong's building renovation system.

The report found that the "fire was most likely caused by a glowing source, likely a cigarette, which ignited paper materials on the flat roof outside".

"As chief executive and head of the government, I am deeply saddened," Mr Lee said.

"I would like to apologise to the affected residents and the general public."

The report said that four government bodies "should bear part of the responsibility for the high casualties caused by this tragic fire". It found that the housing department "should bear a greater share of responsibility".

The flames engulfed bamboo scaffolding across multiple buildings at the Wang Fuk Court housing estate. (Reuters: Tyrone Siu)

More than 30 hearings before a judge-led committee were held since March during the inquiry into the blaze.

The committee heard that almost all fire safety measures failed that day because of "human errors".

In July the committee's leading counsel Victor Dawes told a hearing that the disaster "was preventable but not prevented, and foreseeable but not foreseen".

The fire sent shockwaves across Hong Kong and the world. (Reuters: Tyrone Siu)

The apartment complex was a home to more than 4,600 people, 1,700 of them over the age of 65.

Of those who died, 114 were aged 65 or older.

Authorities have filed charges, including manslaughter, against seven individuals and two companies and arrested at least 35 people.

Mr Lee said a steering committee had been established to oversee changes, which will include laws to criminalise bid-rigging across the construction industry, with fines of up to HK$10 million and 10 years' imprisonment.

Reuters/AFP

World.title: WBBL season gets underway with Thunder thumping of Renegades
World.content:
Anika Learoyd has carved out a career-best innings as the Sydney Thunder began its WBBL campaign with a convincing six-wicket win over the Melbourne Renegades in the season opener.

Learoyd made 48 off 37 balls after off-spinner Georgia Voll (4-26) did most of the damage in the first match of a double-header at Junction Oval today.

The Melbourne Stars host the Hobart Hurricanes in the night game.

In at first drop, after Voll made 25 off 18, including the Thunder's only six of the match, Learoyd hit nine boundaries and put on 62 with Heather Knight in a match-winning third-wicket partnership.

The pair took 28 runs from the power surge, putting the Thunder within sight of victory.

Knight (29 not out off 22 balls) and Nadine de Klerk (12no off six) finished the job, guiding their team to 4-140 with 18 balls to spare.

Learoyd admitted feeling "really nervous" batting near the top of the order, but will take confidence from starting the season with a strong performance.

Earlier, Voll's four wickets and hand in a run-out were crucial in restricting the Renegades to 9-138 from their 20 overs.

Renegades opener Hayley Matthews gave her side a strong start, blasting 45 from 30 balls before holing out in the deep.

Matthews put on 56 for the first wicket with Courtney Webb (22 from 24), and Georgia Wareham made a handy 23 from 19, but a late-innings collapse ended their chances.

The Renegades lost 5-2 in seven balls through the 17th and 18th overs as Voll wreaked havoc.

AAP

World.title: Businesses hoping for 'salvation' from Sydney's new metro line
World.content:
After two years of economic pain, the small businesses along Sydney's Southwest Metro line are breathing a sigh of relief and hoping customers will return in droves.

The first passenger service on the new line will depart Bankstown Station early on Friday morning.

The opening comes after more than two years of commuters being forced onto replacement buses to allow for the 130-year-old heavy rail T3 Bankstown line to be converted.

The 10 stops from Marrickville to Bankstown have been transformed — automatic platform doors have been installed and tracks and corridors have been upgraded.

Business operators along the route are relieved that the interruptions are finally over. The Sydenham to Bankstown extension took more than a year longer than initially forecast.

A number of staff have been let go from Casablanca. (ABC News: Charle McLean)

Talia Gill, the owner of vintage shop Casablanca near Marrickville station, has been weighing up whether she should close her doors for good.

When the station closed in 2024, commuters and people visiting the popular food hub were forced to go through Sydenham, causing a major drop in foot traffic on Illawarra Road.

Within a month Ms GIll had to let almost 10 staff go.

"They all rallied around me and said, 'We'll work for free, let's all save Casablanca', but it really became apparent that, you know, I was not going to be able to," she said.

'A lot of those people felt like my children, you know? It was really sad because it was such a new business."

The pain was only meant to last for 12 months, but a combination of industrial action and the complex challenge of retrofitting modern metro infrastructure to 130-year-old curved train platforms saw the construction timeline double.

Ms Gill is hoping the long-awaited reopening of Marrickville station will be her passion project's "salvation".

"I have definitely hung on to Casablanca not for rational reasons. Like, anyone with any kind of business sense would tell me I was crazy," she said.

"This is the last hope."

Nora Lee says she has lost 40 per cent of her customers this year. (ABC News: Charlie McLean)

Ms Gill's neighbour, Nora Lee of Vanessa's Hair Design, has also been feeling the pain.

"We lost 40 per cent of our customers this year," she said.

"I'm wishing and dreaming and really want to see what they [customers] look like tomorrow."

Camaraderie from adversity

Businesses have struggled during the constuction of the line. (ABC News: Charlie McLean)

Ms Gill said there was also an element of fear when she thought about the metro opening.

"We've waited for this moment for so long and it's exciting," she said.

" But it's also like, shit, what if it doesn't turn around our business? "

Regardless of how things play out in the coming months, Ms Gill said she was grateful the experience had brought her closer to her fellow business owners on Illawarra Road.

"When we started to face adversity, we started to drop into one another's places and say, 'How are you doing? Have you been really quiet?'" she said.

"And there was this camaraderie that would never have occurred otherwise, and, you know, that's a lovely thing and that will endure now."

Transport Minister John Graham and Member for Canterbury Sophie Cotsis acknowledged the patience of business owners and their staff.

The NSW government said new and improved public spaces along the corridor were also designed to provide more welcoming connections between stations.

The MetroWay shared path is also in the works, in a bid to further invite foot traffic.

The planned 13.8-kilometre walking, running and cycling shared path is in the procurement stage and will be designed to run parallel to the Southwest Metro.

Farewell to pink buses

Pink train replacement buses have been a source of irritation for commuters. (ABC News: Charlie McLean)

Commuters in Sydney's inner and south-west suburbs are also optimistic about Southwest Metro, and thankful to be saying goodbye to the pink buses that have been irritating them for the last two years.

The buses meant some commuters faced lengthier travel times.

University student Afifa said she would miss the pink trim of the buses but not the delays they brought to her commute.

"To go to uni right now it takes me like an hour and 10 minutes. And I've checked out the metro and it should take me like 24 minutes," she said.

"So I can sleep in a lot more in the mornings."

Member for Summer Hill Jo Haylen joined residents in farewelling the train replacement buses.

"Inner Westies are so excited to say goodbye to the pink buses and say hello to the new metro," she said.

World.title: Child care sector faces further changes after shocking abuse exposed
World.content:
A proposed national childcare commission will be discussed at a meeting of education ministers next week, as the government faces renewed calls for changes following a Four Corners investigation into Australia's child care system.

Early Childhood Education Minister Jess Walsh told Senate estimates the commission could provide greater national oversight and strategic planning for the $20 billion sector, amid an oversupply of centres in some areas and shortages in others.

"We think a commission could assist with better strategic planning," she said.

Senator Walsh was also grilled about gaps in supervision rules, including why workers who have not completed their qualifications could be left alone with babies.

The questions follow Four Corners exposing shocking CCTV footage of a 13-month-old boy being smothered, kicked, hit and shaken 55 times by a trainee childcare worker, Edwina Ling, inside a Far North Queensland centre.

"Can you explain how a worker studying towards a qualification can be left alone with babies?" Greens deputy leader Steph Hodgins-May asked.

Steph Hodgins-May questioned how Edwina Ling could be left alone with babies before she had finished her childcare qualification. (ABC News: Adam Kennedy)

Senator Walsh said state ministers had ordered a review of how the "working towards" rules applied and in what circumstances. She said an update would be provided next week.

"We have asked for a review into how working towards qualifications applies and in the circumstances where it may apply. That review is underway. We will be updated on it at the next education ministers meeting, and it's an important part of the work," Senator Walsh said.

"That service [Injinoo] has responsibilities to ensure that child was adequately supervised and that child was clearly not adequately supervised."

Childcare worker's violence captured on CCTV Behind the doors of a small childcare centre, a worker went on a violent spree. Parents are still searching for answers.

Senator Walsh said there was also broader work underway on adequate supervision in early childhood services.

She told the committee CCTV would be discussed at next week's meeting of education ministers following a trial involving 300 services.

CCTV proved critical in the Injinoo case. Ling originally denied hurting the children and told parents it was another child responsible for the cuts and bruises, but when she was told the footage showed it was her, she pleaded guilty to 82 assaults.

Read more about Australia's childcare crisis Explore the ABC's investigation into Australia's childcare sector, revealing what goes on behind closed doors.

Senator Hodgins-May pressed Senator Walsh on the government's new funding enforcement powers, asking why Little Zak's Academy and Only About Children remain absent from the Commonwealth's enforcement list despite significant compliance histories.

"What does a large provider actually have to do before the Commonwealth intervenes?" she said, pointing to 25 staff ratio breaches last year.

Analysis of the country's 26 largest long-daycare providers found that half of Little Zak's centres had enforcement action in the past two years, the highest proportion of the 26 largest providers analysed.

For Only About Children, another big for-profit provider, the figure was 27 per cent, or one in four.

Matt O’Sullivan said governments needed to rebuild trust in child care. (ABC News: Adam Kennedy)

Liberal senator and Shadow Childcare Minister Matt O'Sullivan said there had been a "massive distrust and breakdown" in confidence in the child care sector and governments needed to do everything possible to rebuild that trust.

Ling was jailed in June for four years with a one-year non-parole period.

Queensland District Court Judge Dean Morzone KC described her offending as "monstrous, cruel and sadistic" and "a gross breach of trust".

The Injinoo Child Care Centre was closed after losing funding.

World.title: Alcoa ordered to stay further away from Perth's drinking water supply
World.content:
US mining giant Alcoa will have to stay further away from Perth's drinking water sources amid heated debate about the potential impact its bauxite mining could have on waterways.

The temporary order by the state government forms a key part of a broader environmental assessment for Alcoa's mining operations in jarrah forest south-east of Perth.

The miner has been operating there for more than six decades but is only now being scrutinised by the state's Environmental Protection Authority for the first time.

Alcoa's mining footprint between 1984 and 2022. (Supplied: Google Earth)

That scrutiny would ordinarily require works to stop, but an exemption granted by the government in 2023 allowed operations to continue under certain conditions in an effort to "safeguard local jobs".

A new "enhanced" order was issued today, in what the government described as an effort to "ensure Alcoa is meeting government and community expectations".

Environment Minister Matthew Swinbourn said the new conditions would strengthen protections for drinking water and black cockatoo habitat while recognising the miner created jobs for locals.

Endangered cockatoos are offered increased protections in the changes. (ABC News: Phil Hemmingway)

The new rules will ban Alcoa from mining within 50 metres of black cockatoo nesting trees and other significant trees, up from 10 metres currently.

The miner will also be required to survey areas where it plans to mine to identify those trees, provide the government with their locations and mark the area around the trees in which work is prohibited.

Do you know more? Contact Keane Bourke on encrypted email. Please note you will need your own encrypted email account, such as Protonmail, to ensure end-to-end encryption.

Greens environment spokesperson Jess Beckerling said the changes were welcome but in many cases did not go far enough.

"While a 50-metre buffer is better than a 10-metre buffer, it still doesn't guarantee the survival of these critically important trees," she said.

Intense debate over water

Alcoa will not be able to mine within two kilometres of any water reservoir, up from one kilometre previously.

That's a sticking point advocated for by the Water Corporation, in an effort to protect Perth's drinking water supply.

Alcoa holds a vast minerals lease, stretching from east of Perth down to south of Collie in WA's South West region.

Over the years Alcoa's operations have moved closer to Serpentine Dam, raising concerns, although there is no evidence the company has ever impacted drinking water.

Intense back-and-forth discussions between the company, state government and Water Corporation emerged in documents related to the EPA's assessment process.

A wide aerial shot of Alcoa's operations encroaching around Serpentine Dam, a major water supply in Perth's south-east. (Supplied: Nearmap)

Documents released under Freedom of Information laws to online publication Boiling Cold revealed the Water Corporation had also asked for a ban on mining in steep terrain.

"Slopes greater than 16 per cent have been identified as impacting erosion in rehabilitation areas and mine site failures," the utility warned.

In a 2025 internal drinking water assessment, Alcoa said it would generally only clear areas with less than a 16 per cent slope, but where that could not be achieved it would prepare a drainage management plan.

Further conditions possible: Premier

In a statement, an Alcoa spokesperson said it welcomed the government's decision and was focused on meeting "evolving community expectations".

"We are committed to operating in line with our stringent operational requirements which provide strong protections for the environment," they said.

The company said it employed around 4,000 people in WA with around 60 per cent living in the Peel and South West regions.

Alcoa's headquarters in Perth. (ABC News: Cason Ho)

Premier Roger Cook indicated further, more stringent conditions, could be imposed in future.

"We'll continue to work with Alcoa around modernising their state agreement which will further bring them into a modern environmental protection regime," he said.

"This latest move is about making sure the instruments that we have available to us today are effective and relevant in relation to their current mining activity."

Protests have sparked at times against Alcoa's proposed mining expansion. (ABC News: Phoebe Pin)

The Conservation Council of Western Australia's Matt Roberts said the government should instead be focused on closing down the mine.

"What we're seeing is slightly stricter conditions that will enable and continue the destruction of the jarrah forest, the world's only jarrah forest, that cannot be rehabilitated back to the state that it is in at the moment," he said.

"What we're not seeing is a move towards what it means to end mining in the jarrah forest, which is the leadership that we need from the government at the moment."

World.title: Police search launched for man swept away in Central Australia flooding
World.content:
Northern Territory Police are searching for a 60-year-old man believed to have been swept away in floodwaters near the remote Aboriginal community of Santa Teresa, south of Alice Springs, late yesterday.

In a statement, a police spokesperson said aboutaround 6:50am today, officers received a report that a man had been swept off the roof of a vehicle that had "become stuck in floodwater" near Phillipson Bore Road at about 7pm.

"The vehicle contained a man and a woman and had become stuck in a creek, forcing the two occupants to seek refuge on the roof," the spokesperson said.

" The man was subsequently swept off the roof and has not been seen since. "

The police spokesperson said the woman was able to walk back to Santa Teresa, where she reported the man missing to police this morning.

"The Search and Rescue Section has been deployed to search for the man, including resources from Santa Teresa and Alice Springs Police Stations, along with drone support and police divers," the spokesperson said.

Santa Teresa, in Central Australia, has a population of about 700. (ABC News: Xavier Martin)

Santa Teresa/Ltyentye Apurte is a remote Aboriginal community located about 80 kilometres south of Alice Springs.

The incident comes after a series of severe weather warnings — including for heavy rainfall, damaging winds and hail — were issued across Central Australia in recent days.

'Huge' rainfall in the area

The head of Santa Teresa's Atyenhenge Atherre Aboriginal Corporation, Ellie Kamara, said the road to the community had been severely damaged by rain in recent days.

She said about 45.5 millimetres of water had fallen near the community since Sunday.

"That's huge for us," she said.

Ms Kamara said she had been trying to return home to the community from Alice Springs on Tuesday night, but had to be collected by someone in a large troop carrier vehicle to make it back on the damaged road.

"The water in the creeks comes up really quickly, depending on where the rain is, and [on Tuesday night] nearly every single creek along the road came up," she said.

" The volume of rain must have been huge, and right along the road. "

Police are urging anyone who may have seen or heard from the missing 60-year-old man to contact police on 131 444.

World.content:
NationalNSWCity life The inner Sydney school where the gates are opened to everyone Julie Power October 29, 2026 — 10:00pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. It was a moment when old knees felt young again. A bit like the ABC’s Old People’s Home for 4 Year Olds, Green Square Public School and Community Spaces’ new multi-generational choir began on Monday when seniors sang with the school’s junior choir and executed a few knee-bending dance moves. Green Square resident Kathleen Hii with Green Square Public School librarian Yvette Lewington, who lives locally, with her daughter in the large multi-purpose play area. Wolter Peeters The school, in one of the most densely populated neighbourhoods in Australia, is for children by day. But its grounds, basketball court and meeting rooms, managed by Sydney City Council, are for everyone on weekends, holidays and after 6.30pm on school days. That’s prompted many in the community – neither grandparents nor parents of students – to volunteer at the school, too.



Principal Nicole Molloy said it was the first authentic community shared facility that she’d experienced. “We don’t close our gates at 3pm every day and keep people out. They’re welcomed in,” Molloy said. Now celebrating its first birthday, the project by architects BVN, developed with advice from Molloy and other teachers, has won the Daryl Jackson Award for Educational Architecture from the 2026 Australian Institute of Architects. Green Square Public School and Community Spaces designed by BVN Architects has just won the most important award in Australia for educational architecture. Wolter Peeters AIA jury chair Adam Haddow said in “a time of societal paranoia and public distrust, good architecture is about trusting people”. Green Square was designed to include people, not exclude them. Haddow hailed projects that are left open for public use where “occupants assume that someone is not going to come and tag a building or burn it down”.



It was architecture that assumed most people were good, wanted to live in great places, connected to their friends, family and the people around them. Local Kathleen Hii, 75, a member of the new choir and who started a playgroup for the community, said they hadn’t realised the Beatles’ song Here Comes the Sun had moves the children knew. “Sun sun sun, full squat, then rising,” Hii said. BVN co-chief executive Ali Bounds and Green Square Public School and Community Spaces foundation principal Nicole Molloy in the award-winning campus. Wolter Peeters They were a bit hard on the seniors’ knees. But something magical happened, some intergenerational transmission of knee oil, and Hii said they had young knees again. “We walked out of there [on Monday] after singing feeling two inches taller,” she said. BVN co-chief executive and architect Ali Bounds said they had turned the original brief upside down. Initially, the multipurpose play area with a full-size basketball court was planned for the top floor. But they moved it to the ground floor next to the community spaces – where it was easily accessible – to avoid the public traipsing through the classrooms destined for 600 students when full.



Bounds said there were often teenagers waiting outside after 6pm asking, “‘When’s the gate opening?’ And that happens most days.” Hii said the school and its shared facilities had given the community a sense of belonging. “It is the magnet, it is the conduit.” Related Article Architecture ‘Looks like the Opera House’: Why Ray Hadley’s new apartment is a winner Many seniors now read to the young students. “I joke about rent a grandma,” said Hii, adding many of the children she read to were born overseas. “One child was from Mongolia, another from mainland China … None had a grandparent here.” The NSW government announced in September that every new public school will share facilities with the community outside school hours, and more than 200 have already undertaken to do so.



Premier Chris Minns said, “I’ve never been a fan of locking up school grounds to the public. I want kids and families to be able to use the grounds outside of school hours.” Many schools fear vandalism, and about 1200 schools have large security fences to keep people out. Molloy said some people had feared the school would be damaged or graffitied. “I’ve not had a single issue because it’s special to everybody.” EA House designed by Bokey Grant won the national award for residential housing in 2026. Clinton Weaver The community had developed a real ownership of the space. “Because it’s theirs seven days a week. We’ve been here a year, and the place is well looked after and loved, and not just by us.”



Green Square’s walls are covered in a fine tensile mesh designed to make children feel safe without feeling imprisoned. It is also covered in a web of brick slips that provide privacy from the apartments that surround the school in every direction. Just as the ground floor spaces and rooms can be used in different ways, Molloy and other teachers wanted the school’s classrooms to adapt. Furniture was designed to be moved, rooms have large dividers, small spaces for groups, outdoor meeting areas and large wet spaces for art. New Sydney Fish Market | 3XN GXN in association with BVN Architecture and Aspect Studios Rasmus Hjortshøj Other national winners include: Sydney Fish Market by 3XN in association with BVN and ASPECT Studios, which won for commercial architecture

Fraser McReight has won the John Eales Medal as Australian rugby’s best player of the year after his international teammates recognised his consistently excellent performances for his country this season. McReight received the game’s highest honour at the Rugby Australia awards in Sydney on Thursday night, while 21-year-old inside centre Faitala Moleka was crowned Wallaroos Player of the Year and Reds star Treyvon Pritchard named rookie of the year. Fraser McReight has been recognised by his peers for Rugby Australia’s highest honour Getty Images The John Eales medal is based on votes submitted by Wallabies players after every Test match. McReight joins a long list of outstanding back-rowers to have won the award since it was established in 2002, including David Lyons, Phil Waugh, George Smith (twice), Rob Valetini (twice), David Pocock (twice) and former captain Michael Hooper, who won the award a record four times. Like Hooper, McReight has played some of his best rugby when the Wallabies are under the greatest pressure. A ferocious competitor at the breakdown, McReight has also developed an accomplished all-around game, establishing himself as one of the best openside breakaways in world rugby.



McReight was also recognised for his outstanding defensive performances – particularly in the 16-point defeat to France in Brisbane in July, in which he scored two tries as well as making 19 tackles, with the award for Defender of the Year. McReight has also become the first Queensland Reds player to claim a John Eales medal since former Wallabies fullback Chris Latham 20 years ago. The late Peter Meagher who has been recognised by Rugby Australia for his outstanding service to the game. Meagher family Brisbane Junior Rugby Union Western Region chair Paula Watkins was honoured with the inaugural Peter Meagher Spirit of Rugby Award, in recognition of her dedication and tireless support for the community game. Meagher, a much-loved figure in the Randwick rugby community, was one of 15 people tragically killed in the terrorist attack at Bondi Beach last year while taking photographs of the Hanukkah festival as a volunteer.



“Rugby Australia decided to honour Marzo”, who held a longtime association with Randwick rugby club, by rebranding the award previously named after Nick Farr-Jones in his honour. National team captains Isabella Nasser and Henry Hutchison took home the Shawn Mackay Awards for the Women’s and Men’s Sevens Player of the Year, respectively. 2026 Rugby Australia Awards - winners list John Eales Medal - Fraser McReight

Wallaroos Player of the Year - Faitala Moleka

Shawn Mackay Award for Men’s Sevens Player of the Year - Henry Hutchison

Shawn Mackay Award for Women’s Sevens Player of the Year - Isabella Nasser

Swyftx Super Rugby Pacific Player of the Year - Jock Campbell

Santos Women’s Rookie of the Year Award - Amelia Whitaker, Wallaroos

Junior Men’s Player of the Year - Edwin Langi, Australia U20 and NSW Waratahs

Junior Women’s Player of the Year - Waiaria Ellis, Wallaroos and NSW Waratahs

Joe French Award for Outstanding Contribution to Rugby - Craig Robberds, ACT Rugby

Andrew Cole Community Match Official of the Year - Julius Ambat, NSW Rugby First-time winner Nasser led the Australian Women’s team to the World Championship title while Hutchison, who last achieved this accolade in 2021, guided the Men’s side to their first tournament win since 2023 when they claimed gold in Valladolid. Japan-bound fullback Jock Campbell won the Super Rugby Pacific Player of the Year title after an outstanding year for the Reds, while ACT Brumbies and Wallaroos captain Siokapesi Palu Sekona was named Super Rugby Women’s Player of the Year. Amelia Whitaker was also named women’s rookie of the year after her first season for the Wallaroos.



Australian U20 and NSW Waratahs prop Edwin Langi won Junior Men’s Player of the Year for his performances across the year in both programs, while 19-year-old Waiaria Ellis picked up Junior Women’s Player of the Year after shining on the international stage. Referee of the Year Award was awarded to the experienced Nic Berry, who has taken charge of 41 Tests over the last ten years since retiring from playing professional rugby. World.title: Inside the Cottesloe home that won big at the National Architecture Awards
World.content:
PropertyNewsArchitecture Inside the Cottesloe home that won big at the National Architecture Awards Indigo Lemay-Conway October 29, 2026 — 10:00pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 Gift this free article Share full article with anyone — no subscription needed to read it. It won't deduct your gift credits. Learn more Share article as gift Share A A A

A uniquely designed coastal home inspired by an iconic West Australian hiking track took out one of the top prizes at the National Architecture Awards on Thursday. Officer Woods Architects claimed the Robin Boyd Award – the best new residential architecture house – for their Eric Street dual residence in Cottesloe. The Cottesloe house is a maisonette design which looks like a big house but contains multiple dwellings. Robert Frith/Acorn Photo Owners Donna Dransfield and Tony York said the design of their home focused more on outside living than indoor floorspace and was inspired by the Bibbulmun Track – one of the world’s great long-distance walk trails, stretching 1000 kilometres from Kalamunda in the Perth Hills, to Albany on the south coast. “We really wanted a house where you don’t walk in the front door, and you’re in a house,” Dransfield said.



“We wanted a house where the outdoor area was part of the house and the living space, so you’re always in and out, and you can live out there, but you can come in to access something.” Dransfield walked the Bibbulmun Track with her daughter and then again with her son, and said the six weeks spent trekking the trail and sleeping in huts made them want to design their house with the bedrooms separate from the main residence. The kitchen in the upstairs dwelling of the Eric Street house. Robert Frith/Acorn Photo “You’re always outside, and you do it for so long that then you get used to that, and it’s such a beautiful way of living, and sleeping at night, smelling the trees,” she said. “So I think for me, that was a big part of how I’d like to live. Wouldn’t it be nice if you could live like that?”



A walk through of the property reveals its balance between public engagement and privacy. The kitchen and dining zones face the street and ocean, while the living and sleeping areas retreat around a sheltered, north-facing courtyard. Upstairs, two pavilions – the living quarters and bedrooms – and a post-swim sauna frame a pair of protected outdoor spaces, including a breezy entertaining deck and a terrace, buffered by deep planters. Overhead, intersecting skillion roofs provide deep solar shading while channelling rainwater into on-site soakwells to recharge the local aquifer. Officer Woods describes the Eric Street property as “a useful residential model”. “A single house with a broad range of possible occupations, set up for future horizontal subdivision – an adaptable hybrid which allows for long-term flexibility,” they say.



“Its design embraces the idea of the ebb and flow of life, accommodating multiple mutable lives, comings and goings, changes in circumstances and the varying spatial requirements related to each.” In between the bedroom and living areas is a patio area that can be completely enclosed or open depending on the weather. Robert Frith/Acorn Photo The property is split into two separate dwellings – the top is the couple’s main residence and the bottom is frequently used as an Airbnb and has generated $150,000 in income so far – but they have completely different designs. Architect Trent Woods describes the bottom house as “more conventional” in design while the upstairs is “two separate pavilions in a garden”. “It’s what you might see in a semi-detached, it’s got a shotgun plan of bedroom, bedroom, loungeroom, like a terrace house,” Woods said.



“The internal square metreage for the house upstairs, is 137 square meters, which is extremely modest in this day and age. “And to get two houses at that level, it’s unusual to privilege the garden over the internal space, which is something Tony and Donna really wanted to do, to make those gardens and make all those connections.” York said the project came in at $2.2 million and replaced their former 1930s single-storey house they had lived in since 2001. “The house was really dark and really cold, and we were completely overshadowed by the building to the west of us, and we were below everything around us,” he said. “Part of the brief for this place was definitely we want a lot of sunlight. We want to be able to see the sky.”



The couple now have ocean views. Jury members said the simple planning of the house was a “great model for future housing” and one of the reasons for its win. The bedrooms in the upstairs dwelling are completely separate from the living areas. Robert Frith/Acorn Photo “At Eric Street in Cottesloe, Officer Woods Architects has created a dual residence on the site of a single-family home,” they said. “A series of indoor and outdoor spaces is woven together to provide the perfect balance of outlook and privacy, with distant views to the beach and carefully mediated connections to the neighbourhood.



“Eric Street provides a great model for future housing, with a modest but assured architectural approach balanced with skilful planning that allows for dual occupancy for extended family or to sublet as a secondary residence.” Officer Woods also took out the Marshall Clifton Award at the WA Architecture Awards for new residential architecture earlier this year.

World.title: Shell shocked on the Sunshine Coast
World.content:

“Those who’ve been traumatised by the bogong moth invasion (C8), should spare a thought for some of us up here on the Sunshine Coast tackling a far creepier calamity: lawn prawns,” claims Mary Carde of Parrearra (Qld). “We’ve had so much rain that these land-dwelling crustaceans are fleeing the saturated garden and slinking under doorways onto a much drier surface, then die within a couple of hours due to lack of moisture, leaving a sea of husks to be vacuumed up.”

“Apropos of Michael Britt’s item re price per-unit (C8), my mother taught me to do that, using mental arithmetic, 65 years ago,” claims Sally Deves of Kingston (ACT). “Nothing new!”

On the advice of Rev Dr John Bunyan of Campbelltown, there will be no further talk of an alternative Halloween (C8): “C8 is no place for religious controversy but the idea of honouring Martin Luther is appalling. Luther called for the expulsion of Jewish people and the destruction of their homes and synagogues, with centuries-long consequences. His proposals were implemented by the Nazis to whom he was a hero. Kristallnacht in Germany (and the neo-Nazi demonstration outside State Parliament) coincided with Luther’s birthday. The Lutheran Churches, I think unhappily, retain his name but have repudiated this aspect of his writings.”

VoVogate continues, and Daniel Low of Pymble thinks Ted Richards (C8) “may be right. The company is putting fewer and smaller VoVos in the packs and increasing the plastic spacers to make it seem the same size. However, I’d say he’s lucky if there are less because the flavour has also diminished. I was bought a packet for my 19th Birthday (I’m a leaper) two years ago, and it wasn’t the taste of my childhood.”

Tony Tucker of Leichhardt digresses, but not without credence: “Of course Iced Volvos, er, VoVos, have gotten smaller. Remember what happened to Waggon Wheels? Speaking of wheels, that’s something that has gotten larger. Look at how the size of Raptors, Renegades, Rangers, Rebels, Rams, Ringos and Rongos has grown in the testosterone-infected world of the AWD ute!”

World.title: Your fast guide to the US midterms and how they work
World.content:
WorldNorth AmericaUS midterms Your fast guide to the US midterms and how they work Madeleine Heffernan October 29, 2026 — 7:50pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

On November 3, Americans will head to the polls for midterm elections that could have big ramifications for the second half of Donald Trump’s presidency. All seats in the US House of Representatives and a third of those in the Senate come up for grabs. The results will determine whether the Democrats can neuter Trump’s agenda or if he will maintain his grip on America until the presidential election in November 2028. Donald Trump’s approval rating has slumped from 47 per cent to 32 per cent. AP Photo/Alex Brandon The elections, which are on track to be America’s most expensive ever, are being fought on everything from the cost of living to the war on Iran, artificial intelligence and data centres, abortion rights, the immigration crackdown, and, of course, the president himself.



How do the midterms work? The US midterms take place on the Tuesday after the first Monday of November, as stipulated in a law passed 181 years ago. They are held midway between presidential elections to determine the make-up of Congress, which comprises both the House of Representatives (which has two-year terms) and the Senate (six-year terms). For a majority, Republicans and Democrats need to win 218 House seats and 51 Senate seats. Fairfax Media The Trump administration narrowly controls Congress. In the House of Representatives, the Republicans hold a five-seat majority, with 219 seats (including an independent who votes Republican) against the Democrats’ 214. In the Senate, Republicans have 53 seats versus the Democrats’ 47 (including two independents who vote Democrat). Come November, all 435 seats in the House (the lower chamber of Congress) are up for grabs. In addition, a total of 35 Senate seats (the upper chamber) are in play, which comprises a third of all Senate seats, plus two seats vacated by prominent Republicans JD Vance (who became vice president) and Marco Rubio (who became secretary of state). In addition to Congress, 36 out of 50 states will have gubernatorial elections on the same day.



Who’s expected to win? To take control of the House, the Democrats need to pick up at least six more seats (218 seats in total); in the Senate, they need to win a net four seats (51). Polling suggests Democrats are on track to win the House easily, and possibly the Senate. Senator Jon Ossoff is expected to win Georgia for the Democrats. AP Photo/J. Scott Applewhite That’s largely because the unpopular war on Iran and high inflation have pushed Trump’s popularity to the lowest point in his political career. Trump started his second term with an approval rating of 47 per cent, but the latest Reuters/Ipsos poll found his approval rating had slumped to 32 per cent. The same poll found 43 per cent of registered voters planned to vote for the Democrats in these midterms, and 35 per cent for the Republicans – the biggest lead for the Democrats this year.



The Democrats winning control of both houses would frustrate Trump’s agenda for the final two years of his presidency, plus revive the party ahead of the 2028 presidential campaign. “A win is now measured based on how many seats Democrats pick up rather than getting to a balance or status quo,” says Cory Alpert, who worked in the Biden-Harris administration. Related Article US midterms On the road in Ohio: Why Trump is on the defensive in this crucial state Alpert expects young Democrat senator Jon Ossoff to beat Republican Mike Collins in the battleground state of Georgia, and Democratic nominee Roy Cooper to defeat Michael Whatley in North Carolina. “I think races in Texas, Ohio, Alaska, and Michigan are all toss-ups, which in this environment probably favour the Democrat in the race. Florida, South Carolina, Kansas, Iowa and Nebraska are on my watch list for potential flips. “If we see any of those flip on the night, it’s a Democratic wave election.”



Which seats matter the most? Texas is a key battlefield, with former teacher and seminarian James Talarico hoping to become the first Democrat elected to the US Senate from the conservative state since 1988. Talarico, dubbed “Talafreako” by Trump, is up against the president-endorsed state Attorney-General Ken Paxton. “If Talarico wins, it’s a banner year for Democrats,” Alpert says. “If Paxton wins, the margin will tell us a lot.” In the swing state of Michigan, epidemiologist and Democrat progressive Abdul El-Sayed – nicknamed “Mohamed” by Trump – is up against Republican Mike Rogers for a Senate seat. Emma Shortis, a senior researcher at The Australia Institute think tank, says former president Joe Biden’s support of the Netanyahu government in Israel is “one of the key fault lines of the Democratic Party. The result in Michigan will tell us a lot about the ideological make-up and political momentum of the party ahead of the next presidential election.” Democrat James Talarico would make history by winning Texas these midterms. Bloomberg It’s lawyers at 10 paces in Alaska, a state Trump won in 2024. This time around, Democrat Mary Peltola is up against incumbent Republican senator Dan S. Sullivan and a similarly named unaffiliated candidate called Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. There is also another long-shot candidate named Gerald Heikes.



Last week, the US Department of Justice filed a lawsuit requesting Alaska not to certify its Senate results if Peltola wins, arguing that having two Dan Sullivans on the ballot threatened the “integrity” of the vote count. Peltola’s team responded by asking a federal court to dismiss the Trump administration’s lawsuit, describing it as baseless and raising “profound constitutional concerns”. Ohio is home to a hotly contested Senate race, with incumbent Republican Jon Husted neck and neck with Democrat Sherrod Brown. But it’s the battle for the Ohio governorship that has produced international headlines. In an attack ad, Republican Vivek Ramaswamy featured the estranged mother of his Democratic rival, Amy Acton, who was allegedly molested by her stepfather as a child. (The mother called her daughter a liar). The New York Times called it the “most ruthless ad of the midterms”. Then there’s Maine, which has something of a maverick streak when it comes to politics. The Democrats initially picked oyster farmer Graham Platner to take on veteran Republican senator Susan Collins, until an allegation of sexual assault (which Platner denies) killed his candidacy. Former Maine Senate president Troy Jackson is trying to snatch the Senate seat from his five-term Republican rival Collins. Get a note directly from our foreign correspondents on what’s making headlines around the world.

World.title: These films blew up the box office. Now you can finally watch them at home
World.content:
From Obsession to Hokum, these horror box office hits are perfect for a cosy, spooky night in this Halloween.

Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

In the words of Mean Girls’ Gretchen Wieners, horror is so fetch right now. From YouTuber breakouts like Obsession and Backrooms to nostalgic blockbuster hits like Scream 7, the genre is firing on all cylinders, especially among Gen Z. It has massively boosted the box office, contributing more than $1.82 billion in the US alone, just shy of last year’s record of $2.02 billion. And the year’s not over yet. With Halloween just around the corner, it’s the perfect time to catch up on the buzziest horror offerings – many of which are now available to stream at home. Grab the popcorn and prepare to be spooked. One thing is clear after watching Obsession: Be careful what you wish for. Focus Features via AP Obsession (HBO Max) This year delivered several stellar horror titles, but Obsession arguably led the pack. Directed by 27-year-old YouTuber Curry Barker, the film follows Bear (Michael Johnston), a typical “nice guy” who can’t get over a crush on his co-worker Nikki (Inde Navarrette). So, naturally, he wishes on a cheap novelty toy, asking it to make her love him more than anything in the world. This, of course, goes horribly wrong. The once self-assured Nikki turns into what can only be described as a psychotic love monster – one who will go to any lengths, even inflicting violence upon herself and others, to make Bear happy. Related Article YouTube How this 20-year-old went from building worlds in Minecraft to making Hollywood movies After making waves at last year’s Toronto International Film Festival, the movie quickly picked up steam at the box office, grossing more than $739 million globally off a tiny $1.06 million production budget. Critics gushed over the film’s timely take on gender relations, and suggested Barker (along with Backrooms′ Kane Parsons) heralded a YouTuber horror revolution. It did so well, in fact, that Barker already has three upcoming features in line, including Anything But Ghosts starring Breaking Bad’s Aaron Paul and a Texas Chainsaw Massacre remake for A24. It also made Navarrette an overnight star, one potentially worthy of Academy attention.



Chiwetel Ejiofor is caught in the Backrooms, a film that came from internet mythology. A24 Backrooms (Stan*) Just over a week after Obsession came Backrooms, another horror from a former YouTuber that left audiences both stunned and energised. Directed by 21-year-old Kane Parsons, the film adapts the director’s popular online series, which in itself was inspired by a viral creepypasta about an infinite, yellow liminal space. A down-and-out furniture store owner (Chiwetel Ejiofor) stumbles into this mysterious realm, leading his therapist to follow in an attempt to save him. Unnerving, claustrophobic and anxiety-inducing, the film developed solid word-of-mouth, especially among younger audiences, eventually becoming A24’s highest-grossing release of all time. Welcome to the Great Hall of Scream Queens, Rachel McAdams. AP Send Help (Disney+) Finally, Sam Raimi (The Evil Dead) has returned to his unhinged comedy-horror roots. Send Help takes a genuinely terrifying premise – crash-landing on a remote jungle island with your pompous nepo baby boss – and turns it into a darkly hilarious tale that eventually has you begging the characters to just eat each other. Starring Rachel McAdams (The Notebook) and Dylan O’Brien (Teen Wolf), this film may not have blown the box office away, but it still delivered some of the best dark comedy performances of the year, especially from McAdams who proved herself a surprisingly solid scream queen. Exit 8 is simple, yet deeply unnerving.



Exit 8 (Amazon Prime Video) Horror films based on popular video games can be hit-and-miss, but Exit 8 was definitely a hit. Its simple premise follows a man who becomes trapped in an endless underground station and must use any anomalies in the environment to help guide him out. Beyond its respect for the source material, audiences praised the film for its use of eerie liminal space and its deeper exploration of personal guilt. Despite only receiving a limited release, the Japanese film’s average earnings per-theatre became the third-highest of any movie in the US top 10, even surpassing the buzzy Zendaya and Robert Pattinson film The Drama. Once again, it was Gen Z who flocked to cinemas to see it. Jane Schoenbrun’s Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma is mind-boggling in the best possible way. Madman Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma (Mubi) After her 2024 film I Saw the TV Glow, anyone with an interest in surrealist horror had their eye on Jane Schoenbrun. The director’s latest release somehow got even weirder, placing Hannah Einbinder (Hacks) and Gillian Anderson (Sex Education) in an abandoned summer camp where their characters, both actors, attempt to reboot an indie slasher. It’s bloody, dreamlike and slightly meta, paired with pertinent underlying messages around desire and queer identity. In other words, it’s peak Schoenbrun. The dumb writer climbs into the dumb waiter. What could possibly go wrong? Roadshow Hokum (Rent or buy on YouTube, Apple TV or Amazon Prime Video)



A supernatural folk-horror starring Adam Scott and a creepy bunny man? It’s a recipe for success. Damian McCarthy’s tale sends a jaded horror writer (Scott) on a journey to Ireland where he plans to scatter his parents’ ashes. However, his hotel is haunted by a 400-year-old witch who he eventually confronts while searching for a missing hotel employee. Somehow both cosy and terrifying, this film creates slow burn dread like few others, building to some of the most frightening jump scares I’ve seen in a while. It also helps that Scott (Severance) is a master at playing a grumbling anti-hero. Ralph Fiennes returns as a scientist conducting weird experiments. Sony Pictures 28 Years Later: The Bone Temple (Amazon Prime Video) No horror list would be complete without a zombie flick – and this one just happens to be utterly brilliant. Following last year’s 28 Years Later, Nia DaCosta’s instalment of the acclaimed franchise focuses on a cult led by the megalomaniacal psychopath Jimmy (Jack O’Connell), who’s intent on offering uninfected people as satanic sacrifices. It’s incredibly grisly, crushes your faith in humanity (as all good zombie movies should) and offers one of the most twisted villains in contemporary horror history. It also contains a scene in which Ralph Fiennes rocks out to an Iron Maiden song while pretending to be the devil. Cinematic gold. Loading Leviticus (HBO Max from October 30) One of the best horrors of the year was made on our own doorstep. Leviticus is Australian director Adrian Chiarella’s debut feature about a closeted country boy who outs his love interest in a jealous rage, resulting in a sick form of conversion therapy that inadvertently summons an evil entity that mimics those you desire most. The film quickly became a breakout hit, developing major word-of-mouth buzz for its handling of queer trauma and religious repression. But unlike other recent films critiquing religious dogma, this one has much more heart.



Related Article Australian film ‘Did homophobia become OK again?’ Backlash inspires breakthrough horror film Scream 7 (Paramount+) Nostalgia is still alive and kicking. Scream 7 brings Ghostface back to terrorise the residents of Pine Grove, including original scream queen Sidney Prescott (Neve Campbell) and her teenage daughter. To keep it fresh, the killer uses AI deepfakes to manipulate its victims. How timely. Though far from a critical hit, the film smashed the box office, grossing nearly $309 million worldwide – the highest earnings in the franchise’s 30-year history. Undertone may well be the scariest movie ever heard. AP Undertone (Amazon Prime Video) This eerie debut film from director Ian Tuason offers a horrific spin on the current deluge of podcasts. Undertone follows a pregnant paranormal podcaster who discovers 10 anonymous audio recordings which piece together a disturbing story involving a folklore demon that preys on infants. Having originally been conceived as an immersive 250-page audio-cue script, some critics claimed this was the scariest movie they’d ever heard. Audiences clearly agreed, with the film grossing 43 times its production cost globally. *Stan is owned by Nine, the publisher of this masthead.

World.title: ‘In tears’: Jubilation after council scraps plan to turn football club’s home ground into car park
World.content:
NationalNSWSydney councils ‘In tears’: Jubilation after council scraps plan to turn football club’s home ground into car park Emily Kaine October 29, 2026 — 7:30pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Liverpool Council has dropped a controversial plan to redevelop the home ground of a grassroots football club after locals warned it would drive children away from sport. The council master plan would have razed three fields of green space to make way for a car park at Ireland Park, which the Liverpool Rangers have called home for more than 63 years. Junior players during a training session at Ireland Park. Wolter Peeters Club president Matt McMah had warned the redevelopment would force him to significantly cut the number of junior teams and increase fees for registration and uniforms. Parents with multiple children registered at the Rangers said they would have no choice but to withdraw their youngsters. Nearly 1000 people signed a petition calling on the council to overturn the decision.



Related Article Sydney councils Controversial redevelopment of playing fields to drive kids out of sport, locals warn After an internal report by council acknowledged the plan’s impact on club participation and income, councillor Zeli Munjiza put forward a motion to rescind approval of the plan. Fifteen committee members from the Rangers watched as a revote was conducted at Wednesday night’s council meeting. One cheered from the gallery when the plan was scrapped. While the park will still be upgraded, the Rangers will not lose any playing space. The club will retain all of its fields and Ireland Park will gain a cricket pitch, a walking and cycling track, an outdoor gym and an off-leash dog park.



Labor MP for Liverpool Charishma Kaliyanda, formerly a councillor, had been a vocal critic of the 2024 plan. “I was really glad to see that the majority of councillors have listened to the feedback from the community,” she said. The Valmas family called the decision to scrap the 2024 plan “a huge win” for the community. Wolter Peeters “This is a good outcome for the community, where a masterplan that incorporates and delivers more for the community will be progressed.” Rangers secretary Vira Valmas said she was “relieved” to hear council had dropped the plan.



“It is a huge win for the entire community,” she said. “As both a committee member and a parent of juniors at the club, we see every week how much Ireland Park means to families.” McMah said the Rangers would now be able to “continue to grow as a club”. Liverpool Rangers players at their home ground of Ireland Park. Wolter Peeters “I had committee members in tears, they were that excited. This is like a second family for a lot of us. Every time you walk through the gates of Ireland Park, it’s not just going to a soccer club. It’s like coming to a second home.” Start the day with a summary of the day’s most important and interesting stories, analysis and insights.
