If Democrats win majorities in the House and Senate, Musk and his companies could be the subject of congressional investigations.

The link between a law firm that has worked with Musk and officials involved in purported “election integrity” activities is not surprising. For years, Musk has pushed the racist great replacement theory, which posits that minorities are systematically replacing white people in the US and in Western countries around the world. Election denialism—rooted in the unfounded theory of widespread voting by undocumented immigrants—is part of that racist theory of demographic societal change.

Musk has continually pushed election conspiracies that align with Trump’s false claims of election fraud, and this year, he’s doubled down. Musk has been a major disseminator of election misinformation this cycle, and recently boosted the false story that Texas US senate candidate James Talarico had been committed to a psychiatric facility in Ohio. America PAC has also spread inaccurate information about mail-in ballots.

The Association of State and Local Election Officials was first registered on June 17 by Michael Garcar as a nonprofit in Texas. At the time, Garcar was an attorney at Lex Politica, which was expanded after its lead lawyer, Gober, helped launch Musk’s America PAC. Gober has represented Musk’s and America PAC’s political interests in court cases in Wisconsin and Pennsylvania.

Tech.title: Liquid Glass Finally Makes Sense on the iPhone Duo
Tech.content:
Apple rarely admits a mistake. But when it unveiled new versions of its operating systems this summer, it came close.

“With all major design updates, there’s a natural process where we take a bold leap forward, and then we continue to iterate,” said Apple's human interface designer, Shubham Kedia, during a predictably sleek keynote video. “Our team really appreciates your feedback, and we considered it deeply as we refined the new design.”

Not quite “Sorry, everyone, we messed up,” but for Apple, practically an apology tour. The subject was Liquid Glass, Apple’s most divisive interface design since at least iOS 7. Apple's Vision Pro mixed-reality headset (which itself flopped) inspired the translucent design language, and the company brought it to millions of other Apple devices.

The result was a mess—at odds with Steve Jobs’ famous line, “Design is not just what it looks like and feels like. Design is how it works.” Liquid Glass started obsessed with gloss and effects, despite promises it would bring your content to the foreground. Yet Apple’s own press release showed interfaces with illegible text. Worse, users found constant reflections and flickering color shifts distracting, and a lack of clarity across devices hurt accessibility.

But iOS 27, alongside updates to Apple's other software platforms, signaled a shift in priorities after Kedia’s mea culpa. Kedia spoke of reincorporating design cornerstones in what was, if not quite a U-turn, then at least a rediscovery of a core principle: how it works. Instantly, interface elements across Apple devices gained greater clarity and structure, making it easier to tell apps' components from content. The most obvious change, though, was a slider.

Thinking Differently

Courtesy of Apple

Apple said it tuned Liquid Glass to diffuse complex content more effectively, keeping elements legible when above imagery and text. But it also acknowledged that not everyone wants the same thing—some users might prefer a more tinted look, and others “would like Liquid Glass to be even more clear.” You can now decide for yourself with the Liquid Design slider in Settings. For a company known for being opinionated, such bet-hedging was surprising but not unwelcome. Choice isn’t a bad thing, and now users had more of it.

“I immediately pushed that slider all the way to the most tinted setting, and pretty much all the legibility issues vanished,” Ben Rice McCarthy, an indie developer behind popular apps like Obscura and Indigo, tells WIRED. McCarthy has long criticized Liquid Glass. Now? Not so much.

“Liquid Glass introduced a lot of issues without adequate solutions, but this year’s operating systems solved or improved a lot of them,” McCarthy says. “There’s the adaptiveness of the interface. Buttons can grow into menus. Controls merge and divide like cells as you transition between views. Toolbars can expand and contract smoothly as the view changes size.”

Tech.title: Touchscreen MacBook Pro Hands-On: Apple Finally Lets Us Swipe the Screen
Tech.content:
Surpassed only by the iPhone Duo, this year’s most anticipated Apple announcement is its launch of both a 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro with an OLED touchscreen display — the company’s last-to-the-party use of both technologies in one of its laptops. And despite the awful “PROLED” name, it’s more than just a fancy new display. It’s a complete design overhaul that, at least on paper, brings its feature set up to the front of the class for professional content creation, albeit with the same processor options and ports as the other MacBook Pros.

Aside from a screen that brings its capabilities more in line with the Studio Display XDR, the new model adds:

Touch support

The iPhone’s Dynamic Island

A 16TB configuration

Improved speakers with Dolby Atmos support and better mic

A thinner and lighter design

Genlock support

It doesn’t come cheap, though; as predicted, you pay a $400 premium over the standard models. The 14-inch M5 Pro model starts at $2,899 compared with $2,499 for the same non-OLED version, and the M5 Max model begins at $4,499 compared with $4,099. If you want to upgrade to 16TB, you have to bump to the M5 Max — that’s a minimum buy-in of $11,499 with only 36GB of memory. Preorders started on Wednesday, and systems are slated to start shipping Nov. 6.

One of the most popular changes won’t be the whizzy features, but the drop in weight to 3 pounds for the 14-inch model (down from 3.4 pounds) and to 4 pounds (down from 4.7 pounds) for the 16-inch. Also, while Apple updated its sound system to deliver better bass and incorporated Dolby Atmos support to its spatial audio, one of the more notable enhancements is the claimed improvements to the sound when the MacBook is closed.

Hands-on impressions from Executive Producer Bridget Carey

From my brief moments with the laptop, I can tell the touchscreen is something you may use as a supplemental feature — a quick zoom here, a drag-and-drop there. But even if you don’t see yourself needing to poke a screen, the vibrant OLED display is a noticeable leap in quality.

I was expecting to see rows of smudged up screens on demo tables. Yes, there are plenty of Apple staff with polishing cloths to give it a quick buff between tests, but my screens were not looking too smudged up after dragging my fingers around. It’s also less reflective — so those true blacks can be enjoyed without it light reflections getting in the way.

I got a chance to see Apple’s display side by side with another Windows OLED Touchscreen, the Lenovo Yoga 9i. It was no contest — the new MacBook Pro was far superior with a more vibrant display, and it kept the detail even in extremely bright light, plus it was less reflective.

Apple brought back the illuminated logo on the cover. Bridget Carey/CNET

I was worried it might be a little hard to control certain aspects of MacOS with a clumsy finger, but it was able to accurately pick up on my touch. Controls would enlarge when I wanted to screen or expand a window, to make sure I pressed what I intended, and I quickly got used to dragging and locking windows to the sides. You have to do it with a little swivel in your hips and a flick of the wrist.

An impressive screen

A lot of the traditional advantages of OLED over alternatives like IPS with array backlights — such as a wider color gamut and true blacks — are less pronounced than they used to be.

That’s even more true for the current MacBook Pro’s mini-LED-backlit Liquid Retina XDR screens: They already deliver excellent deep blacks and 100% P3 gamut coverage, along with great color accuracy sufficient for prosumer creative work.

But the PROLED XDR screen sounds top-notch. While I take Apple’s claim of a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio with 10,000,000 grains of salt — the arithmetic ratio of peak brightness to minimum black isn’t really meaningful, especially beyond about a million — the display has an expanded gamut that covers the Adobe RGB color space and more of Rec. 2020, a space for mastering video.

The latter is still only 80%, but at the moment, that’s the best you can get in a laptop display.

Tara Brown/CNET

Peak brightness is also similar to the desktop display at 2,000 nits. As with the current screens, though, you can set the SDR brightness only up to 1,000 nits; above that, it’s automated to compensate only for bright sunlight. That can get frustrating for people like me who find auto- brightness distracting.

The display can do 1,000 nits full screen in both SDR and HDR, though. Microsoft’s recently shipped Surface Laptop Ultra also hits 2,000 nits, the first Windows laptop that does, but uses mini-LED.

Oddly, Apple still quotes a 1-nit minimum brightness spec, similar to its mini-LED screens, though OLED’s native minimum is a lot lower: Theoretically, it’s zero, but professional colorimeters have measured it a lot lower. That may be because Apple has adopted it as a standard, and possibly clamped it, to tonally match its mini-LED models.

Apple also refers to its panel technology generically as “tandem OLED,” which is a little annoying, since there is a raft of tandem OLED types. But it is “state of the art!”

The letdowns

There are a couple of potential disappointments, though. For one, the battery life is unchanged. While the MacBook Pro’s battery life has always been good, it’s clear that the OLED display didn’t provide any power savings, or at least savings that weren’t spent elsewhere in the system.

Touch looks like the biggest mixed bag, though. The hardware is only a small aspect of the implementation; operating system interfaces like those of iOS and iPadOS are built around considerations like your finger is bigger and fatter than a cursor. Simply porting the mobile interfaces to a laptop isn’t necessarily a solution, either.

Playing a keyboard on a touchscreen that can’t open wide? Bridget Carey (that’s her hand) says, “You should not play piano like a doofus, finger stabbing the screen.” Tara Brown/CNET

We use laptops in part because a hardware keyboard is sometimes the best input choice, and even navigating the mobile devices via touch can get annoying, so those interfaces don’t necessarily translate optimally.

The point is, a lot is riding on how Apple has adapted MacOS for touch. For instance, the Touch Bar floundered in part because it felt grafted on rather than integral to the OS’ interface, as well as arguably superfluous.

And since Apple didn’t launch the capability with MacOS 27 at its developer conference, WWDC, this year, it sounds like the applications will be behind. That’s not something you beta test on a pro-level production system. Pros rely heavily on muscle memory. It should really have launched with a MacBook Air.

Plus, to adapt to touchscreen use, Apple had to stiffen the hinge — poking the screen makes that necessary — and add image stabilization to the webcam in case you poke the screen during video calls.

Apple seemed like it was really stretching to find meaningful uses for touch. Playing piano on a screen that forces your hand to an awkward angle? No thanks. The one application that sounded like it might be OK was for developers to simulate mobile app interfaces.

I was also kind of hoping for increased refresh rates beyond 120Hz or the ability to manually set it above 60Hz. Apple seems to position ProMotion as a power-saving technology rather than for gaming. Apple also seems to think 60fps is a great frame rate, so it’s not surprising.

Tech.title: Daylight Saving Time Ends on Sunday. Get Ready to Change Your Clocks
Tech.content:
It’s almost time to change your clocks. Daylight saving time ends at 2 a.m. local time on Sunday, when clocks across most of the US move back to 1 a.m. The timing lines up neatly with Halloween: Trick-or-treaters on Saturday still get the later sunset, and the extra hour of sleep arrives overnight. Phones and computers update on their own, but oven, microwave and car clocks usually don’t. Here’s what else to know about the switch, including which states skip it — and when the clocks spring forward again.

The time shift is notorious for disrupting sleep patterns and schedules. Some politicians are advocating for the abolition of time changes and the permanent adoption of daylight saving time, or DST. The House passed the Sunshine Protection Act in July, but it still needs Senate approval and the president’s signature to become law — meaning that, for now, we still have dark winter hours coming.

If you, too, dislike how early it gets dark each day through winter, just remember that brighter evenings will return in mid-March.

More from CNET

When does daylight saving time end?

Daylight saving time in the US ends at 2 a.m. local time Sunday. It will return at 2 a.m. local time on March 14, 2027. The end of DST is when we “fall back,” whereas in March, we “spring forward.”

The US isn’t alone in observing daylight saving time. Check out this list of other countries that use DST, along with their start and end dates.

Daylight saving time vs. standard time

The official US time website shows where time zone boundaries are located. Time.gov/Screenshot by CNET

The exact start dates for daylight saving time and standard time float a little. DST kicks off on the second Sunday of March and ends on the first Sunday of November with the return of standard time.

We spend about eight months of the year in DST. We can thank the Uniform Time Act of 1966 for bringing some order to what had been a complicated history of time changes in the US.

“Motivated by transportation improvements, this act mandated standard time within the existing time zones and established a permanent system of uniform DST, including the dates and times for twice-yearly transitions,” the Bureau of Transportation Statistics states in a history of time zones.

The country’s time zones date to the railroad boom of the late 1800s. DST formally entered the chat in 1918, but its application was inconsistent until 1966. The country tried year-round daylight saving time in January 1974 under President Richard Nixon to address the energy crisis. It didn’t go over well. Congress and President Gerald Ford restored standard time in October 1974.

If you truly hate time changes, then consider moving to Arizona (except for the Navajo Nation) or Hawaii. Those states are on standard time all year long, and their residents don’t have to deal with the physical and mental health impacts of the change. Puerto Rico, Guam, the Virgin Islands, American Samoa and the Northern Mariana Islands also skip DST.



Sleep experts seek year-round standard time

Organizations such as the National Sleep Foundation, the American Academy of Sleep Medicine and the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms are united in calling for permanent standard time, saying it’s better for human biology.

“There’s a mismatch between the outside world and our internal clocks during daylight saving time that can result in some negative health consequences,” says Joseph Dzierzewski, senior vice president of research and scientific affairs at the National Sleep Foundation.

Dzierzewski cites mental health concerns and upticks in cardiovascular events and drowsy driving. He also calls out safety issues with young children walking to school or sitting at bus stops in the dark. Those safety issues were a big reason why permanent DST didn’t last in 1974.

Will we ditch these time changes for good?

Time changes aren’t popular. An October 2024 YouGov poll (PDF) of more than 1,100 US adults found that 63% would like to see the changing of the clocks eliminated. Only 17% wanted to keep time changes, and 20% weren’t sure.

Efforts to end the time changes have so far failed to pass into law. The bipartisan Sunshine Protection Act, which would have made daylight saving time permanent, passed the Senate in 2022 — the new version of the bill passed the House earlier this year and was sent on to the Senate to review in July.

While many people agree on eliminating time changes, the schism between daylight saving time and standard time remains. Standard time may have a bit of an image issue compared to DST.

“Part of the issue is that people associate daylight saving time with summer. People love summer, right?” Dzierzewski said. “But the simple fact of the matter is, it would still be summer if we were on permanent standard time.”

President Donald Trump criticized time changes in a 2024 Truth Social post: “The Republican Party will use its best efforts to eliminate Daylight Saving Time, which has a small but strong constituency, but shouldn’t! Daylight Saving Time is inconvenient and very costly to our Nation.”

Bills and resolutions at the state level haven’t had real-world impacts yet. Politicians are still split on whether they want permanent daylight saving or standard time. Dzierzewski is hopeful that permanent standard time will win out.

“This is the first time in several years where I’ve seen more legislation introduced at a state level in support of permanent standard time as the solution,” he said.

If you’d like to see time changes end and want to advocate for either daylight saving or standard time, contact your state and national representatives and express your opinion.

"You're in a better situation to cope with the effects of the clock change if you have good sleep health generally." Joseph Dzierzewski, senior vice president of research and scientific affairs at the National Sleep Foundation

Adjust your body clock to daylight saving time

Daylight saving time is happening, so now it’s a matter of figuring out how to deal with it. It’s not just about the day of the time change.

“You’re in a better situation to cope with the effects of the clock change if you have good sleep health generally,” Dzierzewski said. He recommends exposure to bright light in the morning, physical activity during the day, eating meals at regular times and practicing a relaxing wind-down routine at night.

The majority of Americans struggle to get the National Sleep Foundation’s recommended 7 to 9 hours of sleep for most adults. A CNET survey found that more than half of US adults use some method to cope with sleep-related challenges. Check out some expert-backed tips for improving your sleep quality.

“If you’re doing these healthy sleep behaviors, you’re probably more resilient to some of these changes,” Dzierzewski said. “If you have poor sleep to begin with, you’re probably going to feel it a little bit more.”

Establishing a better sleep routine can take time. There are two things you can do in direct response to the time change. Dzierzewski suggests adjusting your bedtime and wake-up time gradually ahead of the change. For example, you could shift your schedule by 15 minutes per day and ease yourself into DST. He also recommends getting a good dose of bright morning light on the day of the time change to help set your internal body clock.

Think of DST as another kind of wake-up call, one that can motivate you to evaluate your sleep routine and quality and make positive changes. Start with these six simple habits. And don’t forget to change your clocks. Do it the night before, and you won’t have to worry about it later.

Tech.title: You Can Spend Nearly $15K on Apple’s New Touchscreen MacBook Pro. Why?
Tech.content:
The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display, announced on Wednesday and available on Nov. 6, brings touchscreen control to Apple’s most premium laptop. Pricing starts at $2,899 for the entry-level M5 Pro with the smaller 14-inch display, or $3,399 for the 16-inch model, before any applicable education discounts.

If you go ham on Apple’s preorder configurator and max out the processor, memory and storage, the price balloons to an eye-watering $14,549. That’s wild, especially in today’s economy. Will anyone actually spend that?

Fully loading the M5 MacBook Pro

Let’s see what it means to reach that top-tier configuration of the new touchscreen laptop, starting with the larger, more expensive 16-inch PROLED XDR model at $3,399. Color doesn’t affect price, so take your pick of silver or space black.

More from CNET

The first upgrade you’ll pay for is Nano-texture glass, an antireflective glass finish physically etched at the nanometer scale to diffuse ambient light and eliminate glare, for an additional $150.

Then, stepping up from the M5 Pro’s 20-core GPU to the M5 Max’s 35-core GPU brings the total to $4,949. Bumping to the even more potent 40-core GPU adds another $300, while unlocking horsepower for complex tasks like gaming, video editing and AI-driven operations such as machine learning and coding. (In our testing, CNET found that the Max 40-core is the best fit for pro creatives who work with 8K or raw video, data scientists and intensive users of generative AI imaging and video.)

Next comes memory and storage, which is where things get really expensive. Our starting M5 Max configuration comes standard with 48GB of unified memory and 2TB of storage, but we can pump those numbers considerably. Upgrading to 128GB of memory adds $2,000. Going for 16TB of storage adds $7,000, the most expensive upgrade on the list, roughly doubling the price of the machine.

Pricey high-capacity memory and storage were par for the course long before the RAMpocalypse, but the current AI-fueled spike in RAM and solid-state storage prices has made things worse.

“It’s so expensive because 16TB drives cost a fortune, as does 128GB, and professionals have been paying those workstation prices for years,” Lori Grunin, CNET senior editor for computers and gaming hardware, told me.

Maxing the RAM boosts bandwidth and performance, allowing the Mac to more easily work with the massive files used in high-resolution video, complex 3D models, large datasets and complex mathematical equations. The extra terabytes of storage mean more and larger files can be saved to the device, since neither the MacBook’s memory nor storage can be upgraded after purchase.

All in, our fully loaded MacBook Pro M5 Max with 16-inch PROLED XDR Display comes to $14,549.

Grunin said she’d want more for the money. “For that price, I’d expect the M5 Ultra chip,” she said. “But I don’t think they can put the Ultra in a laptop yet.”

The top-spec MacBooks are aimed at companies that can absorb the high costs of high-capacity storage and memory. Apple

These upgrades aren’t for everyday people

So who buys a laptop that costs more than a used car? Is this just a flex for the super-rich?

“It’s for people who don’t have to pay for it,” said CNET Managing Editor Joshua Goldman.

Configured-to-order, powerful mobile workstations like these are most commonly bought through enterprise procurement by companies, startups and institutions — so the employer is paying, not the individual. Think engineering and architecture firms, Hollywood VFX and post-production houses or AI, machine learning and data science teams. They have big budgets, can put the extra digital horsepower to use and can easily absorb the exorbitant price.

For context, Grunin pointed me to a Dell Precision workstation that I was able to trick out to over $18,000. Five-figure enterprise-scale machines from HP or Lenovo are also not out of the question.

Yes, there will be well-heeled individuals buying at this level, but they’re a relatively small slice of the pie. More likely, the majority of the new touch-enabled MacBook Pros sold will be at still-expensive but easier-to-fathom prices.

Tech.title: Reddit Is Adding ‘For You’ and ‘Following’ Feeds
Tech.content:
Reddit is giving users new ways to sift through its billions of posts. The move follows recent platform changes that eliminated RSS feeds and limited access to the site’s classic desktop layout, Old Reddit.

In a blog post published on Wednesday, Reddit says it will introduce For You and Following tabs, similar to those used on TikTok. The new tabs will roll out to Reddit users worldwide over the next few weeks.

The two feeds will work differently. For You is a discovery feed that recommends posts from subreddits you follow, but adds posts the algorithm believes will relate to your interests. The Following tab is made up strictly of posts from subreddits you’ve already joined. Switching between them might give you a choice between a broader view of what’s on Reddit and one made up only of what you’ve curated for yourself as your interests.

More from CNET

The two new feeds, the company said, are part of its experiments to help people “more intentionally explore Reddit.”

User pushback against Reddit’s previous platform changes highlights a growing frustration with the site’s design evolution. These updates target RSS feeds, third-party API access, and Old Reddit availability, features long favored by users seeking alternatives to the default interface.

To keep browsing post archives, external apps must now transition to Reddit’s official developer platform or risk losing access entirely. Reddit reports that it is currently helping migrate roughly 14,000 apps to the new framework.

According to the company, the stricter policies are a necessary response to the rise of AI-driven bot traffic, which has surged dramatically and strained server infrastructure.

Tech.title: A Touchscreen MacBook Pro Just Invites More Filthy Fingerprints
Tech.content:
I had to suppress a shudder at the thought of how smudgy the touchscreen display on the new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR is going to get. Unlike every other Apple laptop, you can directly tap and swipe on this new MacBook Pro screen like an iPad or iPhone. I try to rarely even brush the screen of my laptop, and yet it still ends up with its share of oily smudges.

To be clear: It’s not like I’m reaching into a bucket of greasy fried chicken when typing away at my MacBook Pro. But even with normal use, skin oils build up on the keyboard. Shutting the laptop brings those oily keys directly into contact with the glass, stamping the display with a ghostly grid of gunk.

Ages ago, I would slip a microfiber cloth between the screen and keyboard whenever I shut my laptop, but I eventually gave that up. Now, I regularly wipe it down with a screen-cleaning spray called Whoosh, recommended to me by an Apple Store employee.

More from CNET

The new MacBook Pro gets the same oleophobic coating, a surface treatment meant to minimize fingerprints, as found on iPad, iPhone and the announced HomeView. We’ll have to see if it’s any more or less successful on the large PROLED XDR display when we test it out.

The least Apple could have done was include its $9 Polishing Cloth for free, but the cloth remains a separate accessory purchase.

A touchscreen Apple laptop has been inevitable since the first iPad — heck, even the first iPhone — which has trained a generation that screens are meant to be tapped, swiped and pinched. Apple even tested a laptop touch interface with the Touch Bar on MacBook Pros for several years before finally giving up. People I love and respect nonetheless send a shiver down my spine when they stab their laptop screen — or worse, touch my screen — to point out something.

I’ll take the MacBook Pro’s Touch Bar over a touch screen. Sarah Tew/CNET

Am I oversensitive to fingerprints on a screen? Most definitely. But I know I’m not the only one.

As a photographer, I want to see my photos on the best possible screen, and this one is certainly Apple’s premium laptop display. Because it’s OLED, the blacks should be truly black, and colors look extremely vibrant. Apple says its 2,000-nit brightness makes it easy to use in bright light, and it has a wider color gamut that covers both P3 and Adobe RGB color spaces.

But I also want to know that when I’m using software to remove errant dust spots from my images, I’m not clicking the same area four times because the spot is actually a smudge on the glass.

So. Much. Screen. Contact. (And are musicians really going to reach for the screen like this? I’m skeptical.) Apple

Could I buy the new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR and never touch the screen? Probably. But that feels like paying extra for a feature I wouldn’t use, even though the improvements are rolled in. You can’t get the OLED quality without the touchscreen.

And making it a touchscreen display invites more skin-to-glass contact. The question is whether I’d be able to keep my paws off the screen when I just want to zoom in on a map or dismiss a notification.

For the time being, a touchscreen Mac isn’t high on my list of features. But as I type this, I am realizing my display is once again in serious need of a good cleaning.

Tech.title: The MacBook Pro OLED Isn’t the Touchscreen Mac I Was Looking For
Tech.content:
I’ve been on a mission for a decade and a half to see that Apple fuses its iPad and Mac lines into something that would be the best of both worlds. I’ve been told that iPads and Macs would never merge, and that touch would never come to Macs. Well, Macs have touchscreens now, or at least one of them; the awkwardly named “MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display” is the very first, arriving Nov. 6.

I’ve been reviewing iPads for years, and I also specialize in reviewing new forms of computing, such as VR/AR headsets and AI-enabled wearables. My hope is that these devices would evolve into true computers that could replace my laptop.

iPads have come awfully close, but the OS and app compatibility still creates a slight divide, meaning certain pro apps and browser tools don’t work the same way. But iPads have the form, the touchscreens, the transforming designs, the modular accessories and support for the wonderful Pencil. I argued earlier this year that the MacBook Neo, with a similar-to-iPad price and an iPhone/iPad-level chipset, showed how close Macs and iPads are getting. I can see a connecting thread, and it excites me.

More from CNET

I say all this because the new MacBook Pros, which I haven’t tried myself, add touchscreens but barely do anything at all to the laptop’s design itself. Instead of folding back or even flat, the screen hinge merely tilts to standard laptop angles and hangs in place while you touch the upright surface.

While Apple is pitching the new MacBook touch features as a great way to interact with MacOS, it doesn’t look, at first glance, that MacOS has evolved to accommodate touch input in truly transformative ways…or in workflows that already perform wonderfully on iPhones and iPads.

Clearly, to me at least, Apple is on a transformation path. The iPhone Duo fuses parts of iPhone and iPad and aims to augment the phone experience with that of a tablet. Similar opportunities lie ahead for Macs and iPads: sure, you may not want MacOS as it exists now on an iPad, but I’d definitely want a touch-evolved MacOS fusion to live on an iPad that could transform into every Mac/iPad need I desire. Would that be worth a higher price? Sure.

The touchscreen MacBook Pro we’re getting at the end of 2026 isn’t that computer. It’s not something most people can afford, anyway, at $2,899 and up. But when I think of touch on a Mac, kids and families using it come to mind. Or, drawing with the Apple Pencil, which you can’t do on this touchscreen MacBook. Or having it be a useful way to access apps that currently live on iPads and iPhones and could, in a pinch, run on the Mac. For iMacs, it could be fun. For convertible MacBooks, it could redefine what a Mac is relative to an iPad.

All I can think of is, what if this Mac could fold back and work with Apple Pencil? Tara Brown/CNET

This feels like a foot in the door for Apple, and an odd one at that. The name “MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display” doesn’t even reference touch at all, and Apple’s marketing seems to underplay the touch-on-Mac debut. The real star of the show is the new OLED display, which truly is a pro feature for a MacBook. The touch extras feel like they’re added in as a bonus.

Now, it all could end up feeling better and more useful than I’m thinking right now. And yes, I’ve often reached up to my MacBook Air to touch the screen, especially after working on an iPad for a while. Almost all the other computers in 2026 have touchscreens, anyway, even in laptop form.

But with all the promises iPads already deliver on for touch, Macs deserve better. And I’m hoping 2027 is when Apple really gets into a transformative discussion about how touch-enabled Macs, and all existing and future iPads, can evolve next. The future Apple computer I’m envisioning doesn’t exist yet, but it’s getting close. And I’m optimistically thinking Apple can address it soon, but as always, you never know.

Tech.title: Google Debuts New AI Models, Genie 4 and Gemini 4 Carbon: What You Need to Know
Tech.content:
Google is back with another new frontier AI model, just two weeks after its last release. The new large language model is dubbed Gemini 4 Carbon, the company announced on Wednesday. And if you’re a fan of world models, there’s good news there, too: Google’s latest, Genie 4, also debuted this week.

Gemini 4 Carbon is the most advanced the company has released. It surpassed its own Gemini 4 Argon model and competitors like OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra on benchmarking tests designed to assess a model’s overall capabilities. But Google is pitching the model as one meant for cybersecurity experts. Google says Gemini 4 Carbon is good at detecting and patching vulnerabilities — a skill we’ve already seen can uncover major problems, as with last week’s PHP vulnerabilities affecting a majority of the world’s websites.

Google’s other new AI model this week is Genie 4. This is a world model, which can simulate real and imagined physical worlds. Whereas chatbots predict the next word in a sentence, world models are grounded in the physics of a digital universe. They’re useful for things like robotics and video game design. Genie 4 will introduce a new capability: audio. Developers will be able to add background noise and dialogue to their AI worlds. You may have heard of two AI bigwigs, Fei-Fei Li and Yann LeCun, building world models in their respective start-ups.

More from CNET

Neither of these new models, Gemini 4 Carbon nor Genie 4, is available to the general public yet. Right now, only select cybersecurity experts have access to Gemini 4 Carbon. Google declined to answer a question from CNET about when we can expect access to open up, but if we go by previous releases, it may be as soon as one to two weeks from now. Google says it is actively engaging with the US government’s review process. You can join the waitlist for Genie 4 now.

Google ended 2025 as a major player in the AI industry, but it hasn’t kept up with its peers in the so-called “AI race.” Gemini 4 Argon was the company’s first new frontier model in 11 months — a long time in an industry that sees new models seemingly every week.

But public appetite for AI has changed a lot since 2025. Fears around AI have risen, as has public backlash against AI infrastructure projects such as data centers. While fears about AI contributing to human extinction are often overblown or actually give tech companies more power, other fears about AI leading to mass job losses, misinformation and deepfakes are alive and well.

Tech.title: Dead Island 2, Tomb Raider Remastered and More Come to All PlayStation Plus Subscribers in November
Tech.content:
Halloween traditionally marks the last day of spooky season, but PlayStation Plus subscribers can keep the ghoulish, monstrous vibes going right through November. On Nov. 3, all subscribers will be able to play Dead Island 2, Monster Train and a plethora of Tomb Raider games.

PlayStation Plus, which is Sony’s version of Xbox Game Pass, offers a large, constantly expanding library of games. Subscribers can choose from the Essential, Extra and Premium tiers, each with unique perks and benefits. Starting at $11 per month, the plans give subscribers access to monthly games and rewards, and each month, all subscribers can access a handful of games at no additional charge.

Here are the games all PlayStation Plus subscribers can play starting on Nov. 3.

More from CNET

Dead Island 2

The city of angels is more like the city of the dead in this first-person zombie survival game. You’ll fight the undead around LA, take on quests and meet quirky characters along the way. This sun-drenched, pulpy game is a bloody good time.

Monster Train 2

The monstrous deck-building roguelite is back with more clans, playstyles and monsters to fight with. You’ll be commanding clans of demons and former angels to oust powerful beings known as Titans who have seized heaven. To defeat them, you’ll have to journey through hell, heaven and beyond in order to bring them down before they destroy the world.

Tomb Raider 4, 5 and 6 Remastered

This collection of games includes remastered versions of Tomb Raider: The Last Revelation, Tomb Raider: Chronicles and Tomb Raider: The Angel of Darkness. You still play as the archeologist/adventurer Lara Croft as she uncovers mysteries and prophecies from the ancient world and today.

For more on PlayStation Plus, here’s what to know about the gaming service and other games you can find on PS Plus now.
